### D-134 — T-117: sync phase 4 (the finish) over Phase3Outcome — the counted verdict and MAIN-027 derived, retention and journal inside the one finish transaction, and their refusals never fail the run — 2026-11-21

Problem: T-117 turns §9.4 phase 4 into code: stamp the `unchanged`
projects (step 1), apply BKP-003's retention (step 2), write the
counted `success`/`partial`/`failed` verdict with `finished_at`
(step 3, the empty run "success with a message"), update MAIN-027's
overall last-success time (step 4), reset `sync_running` and send
`state://dirty` (step 5), and journal the run (§7.7 LOG-001…004).
Five points were open: where MAIN-027's time lives (the spec names no
column); whether retention/journal failures fail the run; what the
journal's closed vocabularies say about a `partial` run; which
instant stamps the `unchanged` projects; and how the phase relates to
the flag whose reset is step 5's first word.

Solution: `eunomia_store::sync_runs::finish_run` +
`last_success_finished_at` + `src-tauri/src/sync_phase4.rs` (the
phase), with `lib.rs` mod blocks (the D-130 anchor).

- _MAIN-027 is derived, not stored._ §9.4 phase 4 step 4's own words
  ("the `finished_at` of the last run with the `success` status")
  name a query, not a cell: `finish_run` writes verdict and
  `finished_at` in ONE UPDATE, so that write IS the update mechanism,
  a `partial`/`failed` finish moves nothing, and
  `last_success_finished_at` (`ORDER BY started_at DESC, id DESC` —
  the D-054 runs order) is the single read. LOG-007's "overall"
  sentence and §9.4's "the UI shows Last attempt: partial" both
  consume it; no `settings` row, no second column.
- _`finish_run` counts, the phase remembers nothing._ The verdict is
  derived from a GROUP BY over the run's `sync_run_projects` rows —
  `success` iff written+unchanged == total (the EMPTY run is the
  all-of-them case and carries §9.4's message in the row's free-text
  `details`, the one home the schema offers; the journal's
  `Details` is closed and message-less, D-051); `failed` iff
  written+unchanged == 0; else `partial`. A `not_started` row at
  finish time matches no arm honestly — phases 1–3 own every
  transition — so it is the typed `Sql` refusal (the module's
  zero-row carrier), the run stays `running`, and the startup
  `interrupted` recovery owns the corpse. Scoped to
  `status = 'running'`: re-finishing, an aborted run, an unknown id
  refuse (the `mark_project_skipped` ruling). `error_code` is
  cleared: no §10 code names a phase-4 outcome, and the per-project
  rows carry their own.
- _One transaction, then one seam._ Steps 1–3, the retention sweep
  and the journal inserts ride ONE `Db::run` write transaction (the
  phase's rows read → unchanged stamps through
  `projects::record_last_synced` with the row's own frozen DB-020
  fingerprint, D-130/D-133's form → `backup_retention::apply` with
  `keep` read in the same transaction, the D-054 precedent →
  `finish_run` → the D-051 entries), so a finished run and everything
  its summary claims commit or vanish as one set. Only AFTER the
  commit does the injected `dirty` seam run (production closes it
  over `dirty_recalc::recalc_and_emit` — D-121's after-sync point;
  the recalculation must observe the committed stamps); a refused
  pass is reported in the outcome, at-least-once to the next trigger.
- _Retention and journal refusals never fail the run_ (BKP-003,
  §7.7): retention is housekeeping "after the run finishes", not a
  verdict step — D-122 already reports filesystem failures instead of
  raising them, and this phase extends the posture to the service's
  own refusals (a refused mark → `StorageError::Sql`, an unreadable
  `backup.retention` cell): the reason lands in
  `RetentionReport::failures`, the verdict commits, the next run
  converges (the already-removed files stay removed; `ok` records
  retry). The journal is the same sentence: a refused insert costs
  the Activity window its entry, not the sync its verdict
  (`JournalReport::failures`). Both reports are the outcome's facts
  for T-118's log lines — never `Err`. What IS `Err`: store failures
  of the read/stamp/finish and the broken-chain invariants
  (`Phase4RowUnsettled`, `Phase4FingerprintMissing` — the phase-3
  family, class-only), every one leaving the run `running`.
- _The unchanged stamps are the written form._ §9.4 phase 4 step 1
  says "updated" without an instant of its own; the ruling: the
  run's one finish instant (the injected `now`, DB-002 — phase 3's
  twin) and the row's frozen fingerprint, exactly the rule phase 3
  stamped the `written` projects under, so both verdicts of one run
  agree on what "synced" means. `updated_at` stays untouched (a
  stamp is not an edit, D-133).
- _The journal dictionary._ D-051's two sync members: one
  `sync.run_finished` (entity `sync_run`) and one
  `sync.project_result` per project. The closed vocabularies force
  one ruling each: a `partial` run is the warn/skipped chip (the run
  completed deliberately short of full success — the precise
  outcomes live in the per-project entries; there is no "partial"
  `result` member and inventing one is a D-051 change, not a phase
  choice), `failed` is error/error, `success` info/ok; per project,
  written/unchanged → ok (a written project carries its target path
  in `Details::File`, LOG-001…004's file-write rule), skipped →
  warn/skipped with the §10 code, failed → error/error with the code
  and the refused path. All entries are `Visibility::User`; each
  successful insert is mirrored once through `logging::action_logged`
  (D-051's call-once rule — its own facade tests own the mirror
  policy).
- _The flag is not the phase's._ §9.4 phase 4 step 5's "Reset
  `sync_running`" is the RAII drop of the `SyncGuard` inside the
  caller's `Phase0Outcome` (D-123): phases hold it BY holding that
  outcome, and the `sync_run` command (T-118) releases it by dropping
  it — documented in the phase's module docs, not re-implemented.
  The phase needs `Phase3Outcome` only for the run id: every fact it
  writes derives from the run's committed rows (D-130's
  read-the-fingerprint posture, carried to the whole finish).

Tests: store — 5 in `tests/sync_runs.rs` (success with counters +
MAIN-027 moved, over stale planted outcome cells the finish must
clear; partial and failed over one database with the
partial-after-success MAIN-027 pin; the empty run's message;
the unsettled-row/re-finish/aborted-run refusals with the row left
`running`; the derived read's `started_at DESC, id DESC` ordering
against a later-started/earlier-finished discriminator). src-tauri —
6 unit in `sync_phase4.rs` (the two journal shape tables, the
details table incl. the non-§10-code and missing-path degradations,
the DB-002 stamp twin, the class-only refusals, the liveness probe
over a real connection) + 11 in
`sync_phase4_tests.rs` over the full real chain (phases 0–3 driven
for real, mock harness): the success path (unchanged stamp == the
written form — the run's instant, the row's own fingerprint,
fingerprints of DIFFERENT builds asserted apart; counted success;
MAIN-027; the 3-entry dictionary; dirty seam exactly once, reading
the COMMITTED verdict; nothing
swallowed), retention applied inside the finish (one real copy from
phase 2 + two older planted through the record writer over real
files, keep=2 → the oldest leaves the disk, `pruned` record, verdict
untouched), the retention FILESYSTEM refusal (a directory squatting
on the `.bak` name: reported, record keeps `ok`, verdict `success`),
the retention SERVICE refusal (a trigger ABORTing the pruned-record
UPDATE: `apply → Err(Sql)` swallowed into the report, verdict
`success`, the D-122 delete-first residue pinned — the file left the
disk before the mark refused), the unreadable `backup.retention`
cell (out-of-range plant: the limit is not applied, the class-only
report names the setting, verdict `success`), the partial run over
TWO real runs (the second loses a project to a deleted folder and
re-stamps its unchanged project at the second instant; MAIN-027
keeps the first success; the partial journal chips), the failed run
(both writes refused through phase 3's seam; nobody stamped; MAIN-027
unknown), the empty run (message, one journal entry, dirty seam
still runs), the unsettled row (SQL-planted `not_started`:
class-only `Phase4RowUnsettled`, run `running`, nothing journaled),
and the missing fingerprint (SQL-planted NULL `build_hash` on an
unchanged row: `Phase4FingerprintMissing`, nothing stamped — the
phase-3 family's mirror), and the second finish (a finished run and
an aborted run both refuse `Phase4RunNotRunning` with the first
verdict and journal verbatim). Mutation check: M1 verdict arms swapped →
the partial/failed store test red; M2 unchanged stamps skipped →
both stamp tests red; M3 the keep value bypassed → both retention
tests red; M4 MAIN-027 ordered by `finished_at` → the ordering pin
red; M5 the per-project journal INSERTs skipped → the three tests
asserting non-empty journals red (the empty run's summary entry
comes from the unmutated summary insert); M6 the dirty seam moved
before the transaction → the five seam-observing pins red (the seam
reads `running`/`None` before the commit); M7 the step-A run-state
check widened to accept success/aborted → the second-finish test
red. All green after revert.
Untested by injection (recorded): the journal insert's own `Err`
arm's REPORT SHAPE — the liveness half is pinned by the probe's unit
test, the swallow line's text is code-reviewed; a genuine FATAL
SQLite class (I/O, full disk, OOM, interrupt) landing AT a swallow
point and yielding `Phase4TransactionLost` has no injection seam in
this harness (the managed `Db` owns the connection; the classes
cannot be aimed at one statement), so that integration leg rests on
the unit-pinned predicate and code review; the empty-run
message's text has no spec literal to oracle (§9.4 says only "with a
message") — the constant is the single owner and a wording change is
a conscious edit here.

Follow-ups for the board (the orchestrator cards them): the
ARCHITECTURE.md row for `sync_phase4` (outside this task's allowed
list, the D-132/D-133 precedent); T-118's log lines consume
`RetentionReport`/`JournalReport`/`DirtyReport`.

### D-135 — The §12.2 load benchmarks: the eunomia-load workspace member, criterion 0.8.2 pinned minimal, the T-101/T-112 passes mirrored behind pin tests, and both budget rows measured inside their budgets — 2026-11-21

Problem: T-137 turns §15.1's Load row ("Section 12.2 metrics on sets
M and L — criterion benchmarks and e2e scripts") into the criterion
half: benchmarks for the two §12.2 budget rows — building one project
with up to 1000 items (≤ 20 ms) and the dirty recalculation over all
of set L (≤ 500 ms) — on the D-109 generator's data. Six points were
open: where such benchmarks can even live (the generator's halves
refuse an edge: the store stays file-system-free, the fs layer stays
database-free, so neither crate can host the composition D-109 named
"the benchmark crate"); which criterion version and features enter
the graph (a new dependency — D-035's discipline, the card's sanction
to record it); what exactly one measured iteration is for each row
(the card cuts the emit seam but leaves the shape to the task);
whether the src-tauri Cargo.toml needs touching; what "the reference
machine" means when CI runs no benchmarks; and how a third spelling
of the D-064/D-121 mirrors (after `dirty_recalc.rs` and
`sync_phase0.rs`) can be kept from drifting.

Solution: `benches/eunomia-load`, a new workspace member (the
"benchmark crate" D-109 predicted; `src-tauri` untouched, and no
library crate gains an edge) — a harness lib plus two bench targets.

- _Where it lives, and why a member._ The harness needs
  `eunomia_fs::temp_repos` (roots) feeding
  `eunomia_store::data_sets::generate` (rows) into an
  `open_db`/`run_migrations` database, plus `eunomia-core`'s build
  seams — a composition no existing crate can host without breaking
  D-109's no-edge rule (a store dev-dependency on fs would create
  exactly the edge that entry's design refuses, dev-only or not). A
  bench-only member keeps every production build graph clean while
  `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` still lints the harness.
  Root `Cargo.toml` gained the members entry only.
- _criterion pinned `=0.8.2`, minimal features._ The card and §15.1
  name criterion; 0.8.2 (2026-02-04) is the current line of the
  demonstrably maintained series (the D-035 precedent for choosing by
  maintenance), MSRV 1.86 against the workspace's 1.99 toolchain.
  `default-features = false` with `cargo_bench_support` only: no
  plotters (no plot generation — the console report and
  `target/criterion` data are the deliverable, the card's "disable
  plot generation"), no rayon, no async/csv/html extras. The exact
  pin follows the tauri-specta precedent for tooling every task
  runs. New to the lockfile: 21 external crates — criterion itself
  plus 20 transitive (alloca, anes, anstyle, cast, ciborium + -io/-ll,
  clap + builder/lex, criterion-plot, crunchy, either, half,
  itertools, oorandom, page_size, tinytemplate, zerocopy + -derive) —
  `cargo deny check`
  green in all four categories (licenses: Apache-2.0 OR MIT at the
  root; advisories/bans/sources unchanged posture). The bench profile
  is the workspace's release-inherited one (opt-level 3, LTO,
  codegen-units 1, `panic = "abort"`); no profile overrides were
  added and `cargo bench` builds and runs under it as-is.
- _What one iteration measures._ The build row
  (`project_build/one_project_1000_items`): one read transaction for
  the ALG-001 snapshot (SYS-005's shape) plus the whole T-112 build
  slice of the one project — §9.2 body over the scoped chunk, ALG-030
  managed text, §9.4 target path, DB-020 hash. The dirty row
  (`dirty_recalc/full_pass_set_L`): the full T-101 pass minus its UI
  plumbing (the card's seam) — one read transaction carrying the
  snapshot **and** the stored hashes together (D-105), then the
  chunked verdicts: per chunk of 25 (D-121's constant, mirrored) a
  fresh scoped mini-snapshot, per project the build slice plus
  DB-021's `is_dirty`; the chunks spread over parallel threads
  (production: `spawn_blocking`; the bench: `std::thread::scope`, the
  same one-task-per-chunk, collected-in-chunk-order shape without an
  app handle) and collected in `sort_order`. The diagnostic
  `dirty_recalc/snapshot_read_set_L` isolates the read transaction
  half. Fixtures are generated in setup only — `TempRepos::create` +
  `generate` + a migrated `open_db` database under a self-cleaning
  `TempDir`; stored hashes stay `NULL` (the honest startup pass every
  dirty verdict of which reads true — D-121's probe measured the same
  state).
- _The single-project profile._ `ONE_PROJECT_1000_ITEMS`: data set
  L's library (1000 instructions, 100 headings, 3 variants per
  instruction) with one project carrying **all** 1000 assignments —
  the §12.2 row's premise read as its upper limit ("up to 1000
  items" is reachable only by assigning the whole library; the named
  sets' per-project densities are M's 40 and L's 200). Parameterized
  through `DataSetSpec`, so the profile is a documented constant, not
  a generator change.
- _The third mirror cannot drift silently._ The mirrors
  (`managed_text`, the 25-chunk scoping, the pass compositions) are
  the harness lib's public API and are pinned by six tests: the
  managed text against `build_content`'s real output (A and C, the
  file minus its marker tail; B against the body — `build_content`
  refuses B by design), the chunk scoping against an independent
  full-snapshot `build_body` spelling on a boundary-crossing fixture
  (57 projects → 25+25+7), and the parallel pass against the
  sequential one id-for-id with DB-021 verified in both directions
  (never-synced dirty, stored-matching-hash clean). Both oracle
  chains were mutation-verified red: joining the managed parts with
  a single break fails the `build_content` pin; unscoping a chunk's
  assignments fails the equivalence and verdict tests (the
  mini-snapshot's own validation refuses the foreign project's row).
- _The reference machine, honestly._ §12.2's budgets are checked "on
  a reference machine (4 cores, 16 GB RAM, SSD)" and CI runs no
  `cargo bench` (verified against `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — the
  crate is linted and compiled there, never run). The ruling: the
  benchmark report is produced by whatever machine runs
  `cargo bench -p eunomia-load`; the numbers below are that report
  on this 8-core box (the same class D-121 measured on), and the
  §15.5 release gate remains a rerun on the actual 4-core reference
  machine — recorded as open, not silently assumed equal.
- _Measurements (bench profile, this 8-core box, under unrelated
  load)._ `project_build/one_project_1000_items`: **12.19 ms**
  [12.06, 12.35], 50 samples — inside the ≤ 20 ms budget.
  `dirty_recalc/full_pass_set_L`: **383.4 ms** [380.7, 385.7], 10
  samples — inside the ≤ 500 ms budget (T-101's precedent measured
  480 ms; D-121's whole-pass range 430–545 ms).
  `dirty_recalc/snapshot_read_set_L`: 297.0 ms [295.2, 300.9] — the
  read transaction is ~77 % of the pass, so the parallel compute
  half is ~86 ms (D-121's sequential ~210 ms over the same 20
  chunks); the store's snapshot read, not the build, owns the dirty
  row's cost — the same attribution D-121's read-split probe made.
  No optimization was needed or performed; both rows landed inside
  their budgets on the first honest composition. One measurement
  condition the numbers carry: the fixture database lives under the
  system temp directory (the `TempDir` house pattern), which on this
  machine is `tmpfs`, and criterion's steady-state iterations read it
  fully page-cache warm — §12.2's premise is an SSD-backed data
  directory and a startup pass, so the release rerun on the actual
  4-core reference machine must include a cold-cache startup pass
  before the row is called confirmed (round-1 review's P3-1; the
  rerun was already recorded open).

Testing: the pin/composition suite — 8 in `tests/mirror_pins.rs`
(the `build_content` pins, the chunk-scoping equivalence, the
parallel-vs-sequential and DB-021 direction pins, and the three the
round-1 review added: the read-half pin, the no-assignments

### D-111 — Platform-true facts in tests: OS error codes and canonical path expectations — 2026-11-21

Problem: two Windows-only CI failures in a row (runs 44864444674,
44865217431), both invisible on the Linux dev machine and both in
test expectations, not production code. (1) The T-069 fault-injection
test injected `io::Error::from_raw_os_error(28)` ungated: on Unix 28
is ENOSPC (std maps it to `ErrorKind::StorageFull`), on Windows it is
`ERROR_OUT_OF_PAPER` — so the production `StorageFull` classification
was right to refuse `DiskFull` and the test failed. (2) Four T-074
IPC tests built expected paths with `std::fs::canonicalize`, which
prepends the `\\?\` verbatim prefix on Windows, while every command
returns the DB-030 canonical form (dunce, no prefix); the first run's
leg aborted at (1) before reaching them, masking (2) for one round.

Solution — two rules for every test that states a platform fact:

- A raw OS error is a platform statement. When a test injects or
  asserts one, it must either gate by platform (`#[cfg(unix)]` /
  `#[cfg(windows)]` with the platform's code — ENOSPC 28 vs
  `ERROR_DISK_FULL` 112, both `StorageFull` in std) or use
  `io::Error::new(ErrorKind::…)` when only the kind matters.
- A canonical-path expectation is built with
  `eunomia_fs::paths::canonicalize` (the DB-030 form the commands
  return), never `std::fs::canonicalize` — the two diverge by the
  verbatim prefix on Windows and are identical on Unix, which is
  exactly why Linux runs cannot catch it.

Service commits 799163f (T-069) and 430bf22 (T-074) carry the fixes;
subagent briefs for tasks with IPC/fs tests quote these two rules.

### D-109 — The §12.2 data set generator: repository-driven fill in one transaction, determinism defined over a stabilized view, and the two-crate split (store fill / fs temp Git roots) — 2026-11-20

Problem: T-136 needs the M and L benchmark databases of spec §12.2
(M: 50 projects, 200 instructions; L: 500 projects, 1,000
instructions, 100 headings, 3 variants per instruction, 100,000
assignments — the confirmed upper-limit scenario) plus the temporary
Git folders the future sync benchmarks will write into, produced
deterministically for T-137+. Open questions: where the generator
lives (the store cannot create folders, the fs crate cannot write
rows, and no new crate/dependency edge is allowed); what
determinism can even mean when the repositories own the id and
timestamp columns (UUIDv7 `new_id`, wall-clock `now_utc` — D-031);
how the L assignments spread; and what "generate again into the same
database" means.

Solution: two modules, one per crate, composed by the benchmark
consumer.

- **Store side — `eunomia_store::data_sets`.** `DataSetSpec`
  (projects / headings / instructions / variants-per-instruction /
  assignments-per-project) with the consts `M` and `L` carrying
  §12.2's exact numbers (M: 50/0/200/1/40 → 2,000 assignments; L:
  500/100/1000/3/200 → 100,000). `generate(&mut Connection, &spec,
&[ProjectRoot])` fills an **empty** database through the
  repositories' own create methods only — `projects::create`,
  `create_item`, `create_variant`, `assign` — inside one transaction
  it owns: the standalone-connection seam for benchmarks and
  fixtures, which is why it takes `&mut Connection` and cannot be
  composed under `Db::run` (D-037's executor composition stays the
  app layer's). Integrity is the repositories' guarantee, not a
  generator re-implementation: dense `position`/`sort_order` come
  from the append semantics, DB-010 from the constructive
  main-variant rules, D-02 from `assign`. Typed refusals before the
  first write: `NotEmpty`, `NotEnoughRoots`,
  `AssignmentsPerProjectTooHigh`, `InstructionsRequired`,
  `VariantsRequired`; repository/transaction failures roll the whole
  run back (empty database → a retry converges: the idempotency
  semantics are "fresh fixture or rejection", not merge — pinned by
  a duplicate-path-key rollback test).
- **Determinism = the stabilized view.** No RNG exists to seed —
  every value is a pure function of the profile counts and the row
  ordinal. The contract is defined over what the generator cannot
  control stripped away: `stabilized(conn, base)` reads the ALG-001
  collections back through the repositories with ids mapped to
  creation ordinals, timestamps dropped, and the base prefix
  stripped **by component count** (components split on `/` and `\`,
  empties ignored) from both `path` and `path_key`. Component
  counting — not text-prefix matching — is what makes the rule
  platform-true: DB-030's keying re-spells separators, NFC and case
  (folded keys on Windows/macOS) but never changes component
  structure, so one count strips both columns everywhere (round-1
  review's P1: a single text prefix silently never matches a folded
  `path_key`). Two runs with the same profile and equally named
  roots produce **equal stabilized views** while their raw ids
  differ — pinned as the falsifiable determinism test, with folded
  key spellings in the fixture roots and both the negative half
  (without `base`, the views differ: the stripping is part of the
  definition) and a unit pin of the strip's spelling-agnosticism.
- **The L spread.** Project `p`, assignment `k` → instruction
  `(37·p + k) mod 1000`, variant `(p + k) mod 3`. Distinctness needs
  no coprimality (round-2 review's correction: `k < 200 ≤ 1000`
  alone makes the k-window injective, so no stride check exists);
  37 is purely the spread constant — a hop big enough that
  consecutive projects' windows interleave across the whole library
  instead of stacking into bands. Coverage: all 1,000 instructions
  appear, ≈100 assignments each (90–110 exactly, by the formula).
  The closed form is recomputed in the tests by hand — never through
  the module's helpers — over all 100,000 L pairs and all 2,000 M
  pairs. Layout: headings partition the instructions into near-equal
  consecutive groups (exactly 10×100 for L; the 4/3/3 remainder
  branch and the empty-heading edge pinned separately), heading
  levels cycle `2..=6`, all rows active (§12.2 measures the plain
  upper-limit scenario). Variant names run `Main`, `Compact`,
  `Detailed`, then numbered `Alternative 03`… — distinct NOCASE
  names for any variant count (a cycling scheme would collide on the
  §6.9 active-sibling uniqueness). Variant texts are sized for
  §12.2's sync premise (≈52 characters average → a fully assigned
  set-L project builds ≈10 KB). `set L` also reads back through
  `build_snapshot::read` — the whole ALG-001 graph validates, so
  T-137 benchmarks start from a snapshot the sync pipeline accepts.
- **fs side — `eunomia_fs::temp_repos`.** `TempRepos::create(count,
label)` lays out `<tempdir>/<label>/repo-<i:04>` with a minimal but
  real `.git` (`HEAD`, `config`, `objects/`, `refs/` — git's own
  validity set; the scan's ALG-052 probe and `git rev-parse` both
  accept it), canonical paths + DB-030 keys ready for
  `ProjectRoot`, auto-removed with the guard (the crate's idle
  `tempfile` dependency's first staging use). Labels are validated as
  one safe component (no separators, no `..`) so nothing escapes the
  guard's cleanup. The two crates keep no edge between them —
  benchmarks compose (`TempRepos` → roots → `generate`), the store
  stays filesystem-free, fs stays database-free. Group directory
  stored canonical (macOS `/var` → `/private/var`), roots always
  canonical so `path`/`path_key`/scan root spellings agree.

Tests: 5 unit + 7 integration in `tests/data_sets.rs` (M sizes,
invariants and stabilized collections with M's distribution; L
sizes/distribution/snapshot — the one heavy L fill, ≈25 s in a debug
build; determinism both halves with folded key spellings; typed
rejections writing nothing; heading layout edges 4/3/3 and 1/1/1/0/0
with variant names beyond the third; the duplicate-key mid-fill
rollback; stabilized corrupt-cell propagation through the
`ignore_check_constraints` seam) and 2 unit + 4 integration in
`tests/temp_repos.rs` (naming, unsafe labels, layout, canonical
keys, the scan finding every root, teardown, empty fixture).

### D-110 — vue-i18n 11 with the in-repo `eunomia/no-raw-ui-text` lint gate; pipe plurals as UI-020's "ICU plurals" — 2026-11-20

Problem: UI-020 (spec §11.5) requires vue-i18n with an `en.json` catalog
of dotted feature keys, pluralization ("ICU plurals"), and — per the
card's acceptance criteria — a linter or test that catches a template
string that is not going through a key. Three decisions were open: the
vue-i18n version, the plural format reading, and the enforcement
mechanism (`vue/no-raw-text` was suggested, but eslint-plugin-vue 10.12.1
ships no such rule — verified against the installed package's 256-rule
list; the rule of that name lives in `@intlify/eslint-plugin-vue-i18n`,
an extra dependency outside the card's vue-i18n-only allow-list).

Solution (T-142):

- **Dependency.** `vue-i18n@^11.4.23` (dependencies) — the current v11
  stable line on the registry (`latest` dist-tag), peer `vue ^3.0.0`,
  `node >= 22` (the repo pins node 22/pnpm 12). v12 is alpha-only; v9/v10
  lines carry `legacy9`/`legacy10` dist-tags. Composition API mode
  (`legacy: false`), one instance in `src/i18n/index.ts`, installed in
  `main.ts`; components use `useI18n()`, no global `$t` reliance.
- **Catalog and keys.** `src/locales/en.json`, nested namespaces per UI
  feature reached as dotted paths (UI-020's `project.settings.title`
  convention): `app.*` for the shell today (title, version line,
  tagline, logo alts, tracked-projects plural), later screens add their
  own namespaces. The catalog generic (`MessageSchema = typeof en`)
  feeds vue-i18n's key autocomplete only — its `t()` accepts any string,
  so unknown keys are NOT a compile error; typo protection is behavioral:
  a catalog-coverage test asserts every `t('…')` literal in `.vue`
  templates exists (`te(key)`), and App.spec pins the rendered tagline
  and alts (a missing key renders as the literal key string, warned
  only). `en` is the single locale and the fallback; NFR-004…006's
  backend error texts will resolve against this same catalog when their
  `message_key` consumers land.
- **Plurals.** vue-i18n's pipe-separated plural forms (`zero | one |
other` for English, `{count}` interpolation, count passed as the
  plural choice) — vue-i18n's CLDR plural-rule message format, which is
  the tool-native reading of UI-020's "ICU plurals"; adopting ICU
  MessageFormat syntax literally would need an extra message-compiler
  dependency outside the allow-list. The working UI-visible example is
  the tracked-projects line in App.vue: count from `projects_list`
  through the ipc facade, rendered with
  `t('app.trackedProjects', { count: n(projectCount) }, projectCount)` —
  the explicit numeric argument selects the plural form, `n()` formats
  the interpolated count.
- **The lint gate.** A custom rule, `eunomia/no-raw-ui-text`
  (`src/i18n/no-raw-ui-text.ts`, registered in eslint.config.js for
  `**/*.vue`): a template text node containing any Unicode letter or
  digit is a violation — punctuation/symbols are layout — and so is the
  literal of a user-facing attribute (`alt`, `title`, `placeholder`,
  `label`, `aria-label`, `aria-placeholder`, `aria-description`,
  `aria-roledescription`, `aria-valuetext`, `aria-braillelabel`,
  `aria-brailleroledescription`, plus `value` on submit-style inputs,
  where the browser renders it as the control's label) and an
  interpolation or bound expression that shows bare literal copy —
  `{{ 'Save' }}`, `{{ 'Sa' + 've' }}`, ``{{ `Save` }}``,
  `{{ t('k') + ' — Beta' }}`, `:title="'Save'"`: only `+`
  concatenations, template literals and lone literals are walked, and
  everything inside a `t`/`n`/`$t` call counts as translation data, so
  comparisons (`x === 'en'`) and filter calls never fire; bound key
  expressions (`:alt="t('…')"`) are the sanctioned form. A copy prefix
  around an interpolation (`v{{ version }}` — text-node half — or
  ``{{ `v${version}` }}`` — expression half) is caught too, which is
  why the version line moved into the `app.versionLine` message with a
  `{version}` placeholder. Options `ignorePattern`/`ignoreText` exist
  for the day a genuinely text-like literal needs an exemption. Known
  limit, accepted: copy computed in `<script setup>` and rendered via
  `{{ label }}` is invisible to this template-only rule, and so is copy
  smuggled through non-copy expression shapes (method calls returning
  literals, ternary arms); the catalog-coverage test catches the typo
  half, and a script-side scan would be its own rule if real screens
  start doing it. eslint.config.js
  imports the rule with an explicit `.ts` extension — Node's type
  stripping (default since Node 22.18; CI floats `node-version: 22`,
  local is 22.23) loads it at lint time, and vue-tsc checks the rule
  file itself (under `src/`); the config file belongs to no tsconfig
  project, so its import is unchecked wiring (verified end to end:
  eslint red on a planted raw string, green after removal).
- **The keyed/unkeyed boundary.** Not keyed, by design: mock-layer and
  fixture data (`src/ipc/**` — project names, journal actions, error
  message keys — data the UI renders, not UI chrome), the generated
  `src/bindings.ts`, `index.html` (plain HTML, no Vue template; the
  window title is Tauri's), URLs, CSS classes, and code identifiers.
  The rule scans `.vue` templates only, which matches that boundary.
- **Tests.** `src/i18n/no-raw-ui-text.spec.ts` pins the rule red/green
  with ESLint RuleTester (the card's "red example": a raw template
  string must fail; also the copy-prefix, attribute-literal,
  expression-literal and submit-input `value` cases, plus both exemption
  valves and a non-matching `ignorePattern`) and the eslint.config.js
  wiring (rule present at error severity for `**/*.vue`, guarded by a
  `@ts-expect-error` import of the JS config — no declaration file by
  design); `src/i18n/i18n.spec.ts` pins nested keys, named
  interpolation, the 0/1/2/5 plural forms, the `n()`-formatted count at
  the message level, and the catalog coverage over every `t('…')`
  literal in `.vue` templates; `App.spec.ts` mounts through the i18n
  plugin and proves the plural line end to end over the mock facade with
  exactly 1/2/5/0 active projects, an active-vs-archived counting case
  (3 rows, 2 archived → "1 project tracked"), and the rendered tagline
  and alts (per-test `resetMockState` worlds). The T-141
  mock layer is untouched — all its suites stay green; e2e assertions
  (title, heading text, `v\d` version line) keep holding because the
  keyed rendering produces the same strings.

Review: two rounds — findings and fixes in `.opencode/reviews/t142-round*.md`
(owner-local). Round 1 (deepseek-v4.1-flash): no P0/P1; 2 × P2, 5 × P3,
all applied. P2-1 — the "typed catalog" claim was false (vue-i18n's `t`
accepts any string, so a key typo passed lint, typecheck and every
test): the claim is corrected here and in `src/i18n/index.ts`, and the
real guards added (the catalog-coverage `te()` test and the tagline/alt
assertions in App.spec). P2-2 — the rule missed string literals inside
template expressions (`{{ 'Save' }}`, `:title="'Save'"`): the
`VExpressionContainer` literal case added with red/green pins; the
script-side constant remains a documented known limit. P3s applied:
`aria-valuetext`/braille attributes and submit-input `value` joined the
attribute set (with text-input/option non-cases pinned); the
`ignorePattern`/`ignoreText` exemption valves are tested (including a
non-matching pattern); the plural tests gained an archived-rows case
that separates counting active from counting everything; the eslint
config comment now states the real Node floor (type stripping default
since 22.18) and drops the incorrect `allowImportingTsExtensions`
rationale (the config belongs to no tsconfig project); the count
interpolates through the composer's `n()` ("1,000 projects tracked",
pinned). Declined: reconciling spec §12's dangling NFR-004…006 IDs —
`docs/spec.md` is outside this task's file scope (a docs card material).
(T-250 reconciliation: the IDs are now defined — spec §12.5; the
requirement is the §7 error envelope and UI-020's `message_key` +
`params`, the catalog above serves it, and the first consumer landed
as D-113.)
Round 2 (hy4-flash-free): no P0/P1/P2; 4 × P3, all applied. The
submit-input `value` check compared the element's source-cased
`rawName` (an uppercase `<INPUT type="submit">` slipped by) — it now
compares the parser's lowercased `name`, with an uppercase red pin;
the expression gate only fired on literal roots (`t('k') + ' — Beta'`,
`'Sa' + 've'`, `` `Save` `` passed clean) — the visitor now walks the
narrow copy-only shapes (`+` chains, template literals, lone literals,
skipping `t`/`n`/`$t` call subtrees), with red pins for all three forms
plus `` `v${version}` `` and green pins for comparisons/filters; the
catalog-coverage scan read raw sources (a `t('…')` mention inside a
comment counted as a usage) — comments are stripped before matching and
the raw-scan intent plus its false-negative surface (aliased `t`,
dynamic keys) documented in the spec; D-110's plural call form was a
wrong shorthand (`t(key, n)`) — it now quotes the real expression.

### D-137 — The target-file watch service: parent-directory watches under the "one watch per file" rule, the ALG-033 verdict through the real builders, and the closed-list reading of §5.7 — 2026-11-21

Problem: T-102 turns spec 5.7 into code (SYS-007…009, OUT-014,
MAIN-028, T-F13): watch the target files of active, available
projects, debounce 300 ms, compute "externally modified" by ALG-033,
report deletions separately, and never write. Seven points were open:
what mechanical watch satisfies "one watch per file"; which files a
project contributes under scheme C; what the ALG-033 "new side" is
for each scheme; when `file_deleted` is honest; how subscriptions
learn about availability without touching T-079's file; how the
future sync pipeline (T-118) reuses the pass; and the T-F13 criterion
without a sync pipeline.

Solution: `eunomia-fs/src/watcher.rs` (mechanics) +
`src-tauri/src/file_watch.rs` (semantics, the D-112 service shape),
wired in `lib.rs`.

- _The watch sits on the parent directory._ SYS-007's "one watch per
  file" is honored as a per-file guarantee (each target file is
  observed individually, name-filtered; no file is watched twice; no
  tree walk), while the notify watch itself is a non-recursive watch
  on the file's parent: inotify watches inodes, the app's own §9.5
  write-then-rename and every editor's atomic save replace the inode,
  and a file-pinned watch would go silent exactly on the external
  edits it exists to catch (pinned by the atomic-rename-over test).
  Directories are deduplicated — the SYS-010 watch-budget posture —
  and `set_files` is the idempotent full-set convergence: an
  unwatchable root leaves the converged set (`watched_files()`) with-
  out an error, and the next call retries it.
- _The watch set follows D-080's closed list._ One file per project
  through `target_file_name(scheme, base_name)`: A|B →
  `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md`, C → `<STEM>.project.md` (the spec 1.2
  §5.7 parenthetical read as the write-target list — D-080 already
  maps `(Scheme, BaseName)` onto exactly this list; the scheme-C main
  file is not edited, so it is not watched).
- _The verdict goes through the production builders, not mirrors._
  A/C: the ALG-033 new side is `build_content`'s output minus the
  probe marker tail it was handed — the builder IS the oracle, no
  hand-rolled join (the dirty service needed a mirror because it
  builds markerlessly; the comparison wants exactly this strip). B:
  the side is `assembly_b::assemble` of the CURRENT file minus the
  inserted marker line (the splice's own re-parse brackets the
  block), so an edit OUTSIDE the markers does not flag the project —
  the build preserves the outside, and the file follows itself; not
  UTF-8 or broken markers can never match (E_NOT_UTF8 /
  E_MARKERS_INVALID live in the sync's future).
- _`file_deleted` is gated on a recorded sync._ A missing target with
  a stored hash (DB-024; `NULL`/empty ≡ never, D-068) is SYS-009's
  hint; a never-synced project without a file is not "deleted"
  (OUT-005 creates it — the flag would mark every fresh column). A
  pre-existing differing file IS externally modified regardless of
  sync history (SYS-008's literal reading). The two flags are
  mutually exclusive in the verdict.
- _Subscriptions learn availability through T-079's event, truth
  through its own probes._ `listen_availability` subscribes to
  `state://project-availability` (registered in `lib.rs` BEFORE the
  startup recheck is spawned — the session's first verdicts cannot
  miss it) and drops a Refresh permit; every pass then probes the
  folders itself (the D-084 probes, on the blocking pool), so no
  stale cache ever gates a watch or a verdict. SYS-010's backend
  errors land as a Refresh too — the "re-check everything once"
  degrade, no crash.
- _The bus is the serializer, so there is no ticket guard._ Unlike
  dirty's D-121 (direct awaits can overlap the service task), every
  pass here — startup, availability-triggered, debounced, after-sync —
  runs on the single service task; `refresh_after_sync` does not run
  a pass of its own but awaits one through an ack channel (the
  D-112/no-new-dependency shape: a capacity-1 `tauri::async_runtime`
  channel, since tokio's `sync` feature would be a new-feature owner
  decision this task does not carry). Recovery mode is answered in
  the seam itself (`managed_db`) — waiting for an ack from a service
  that is never spawned in that mode would hang. The diff contract is
  D-112's third instance over a clean baseline: first observation
  reports modified/deleted projects, both directions are changes,
  empty diffs are silent, emit-then-record is at-least-once, full
  passes prune leavers, debounced partial passes merge (the rest of
  the world was not re-read).
- _T-F13 proven to the honest half._ The criterion test runs the full
  watch chain: a synced scheme-A project, an external std write, the
  debounced re-read, and the `state://file-changed` event with
  `external_changed` — plus the display-only pin (the file still
  holds the external bytes after the pass) and idempotence. The
  "next sync overwrites" half is simulated: the pipeline's own write
  (real builder bytes) + hash store + `refresh_after_sync` clears the
  flag through the same wire. T-118 readiness: the seam exists,
  awaits, and returns the diff; backups and the overwrite are the
  pipeline's.

### D-139 — The SYS-010 watch limit made testable: the WatchBackend seam, the mid-set refusal battery, and the extracted dispatch for the overflow half — 2026-11-21

Problem: T-103 proves the watcher's SYS-010 halves. The overflow
half was BELIEVED wired since T-102 (an event-stream `Err` batch →
one `Backend` event → the consumer's full re-check), and the
refused-watch half (a watch the backend will not arm → the file
leaves the converged set, visible through `unwatched_files()`) is
wired and even tested — but only through a MISSING root. Two facts
stayed unprovable: the inotify limit refuses an EXISTING healthy
directory mid-set (some watches already live, the rest refused),
and no fixture can exhaust `fs.inotify.max_user_watches` on demand.
D-137 recorded exactly this gap as its follow-up (7) (round-1 P3-7:
"the fault-injection feature does not reach notify's stream today"
— and the armed-fault discipline is thread-local, while notify's
events arrive on notify's own thread). Round 1 of this task's
review then showed the belief itself was half wrong (the addendum
below): inotify's queue overflow never reaches the `Err` arm.

Solution, two seams in `watcher.rs` (the atomic.rs precedent: a
callable seam whose production value is the real thing and whose
test value is a fake — `free_space`'s shape, not a cfg-gated fault
point):

- _`WatchBackend` (the arming seam)._ The two calls `set_files`
  makes — arm/disarm one non-recursive directory watch — moved
  behind a public trait with a class-only `WatchRefused` error
  (mirrors `WatcherInitError`; the convergence never branches on
  the reason, so the type carries a diagnostic string and nothing
  else). Production `NotifyBackend` wraps the same debouncer;
  `TargetWatcher` became generic with `NotifyBackend` as the
  default, so `TargetWatcher::new`'s signature is unchanged (the
  frozen app layer compiles untouched) and `with_backend` is the
  tests' way in. The fake (`LimitBackend`, tests/watcher.rs)
  refuses arming from a chosen call number on — persistent until
  the test lifts the plan, exactly a kernel limit — and logs every
  arm call. The battery: a mid-set hit leaves the later
  directories unwatched (exactly them, through the seam) while the
  already-converged directory KEEPS its convergence — the map's
  evidence rule (a genuinely LIVE watch's re-arm cannot be refused
  by the watches limit at all, the kernel updates the existing
  mark without allocating; the refused re-arm of a converged
  directory stands for the lost-watch-plus-limit shape — see the
  round-1 addendum's P3-2); a repeated pass under the limit
  answers identically; lifting the
  limit lets the very next `set_files` converge everything (the
  re-arm is unconditional, so the retry needs no flag); and the
  call log pins that every pass re-arms every wanted directory,
  refused ones included (the idempotent retry). Mutation-verified:
  ignoring the refusal (arming regardless) fails the three limit
  tests; trusting "already in the map" (skipping the re-arm) fails
  the log pin and T-102's re-created-directory test.
- _The extracted `dispatch` (the overflow half)._ The debouncer
  callback's body became a private function the callback forwards
  into, so the mapping is drivable without notify's event thread.
  The overflow arrives INSIDE an `Ok` batch as notify's rescan
  flag (round-1 P1-1, below) and the `Err` batch is the rarer
  stream-read failure — both deliver exactly ONE `Backend` event
  per batch (SYS-010's response is one full re-check; two-signal
  batches pin it), a mixed batch still delivers its ordinary
  events, and a dead consumer drops the delivery instead of
  panicking the event thread. The overflow's full re-check itself
  is the app layer's (`file_watch.rs` maps `Backend` to a full
  `Refresh`; frozen this window, and NOT covered by any test there
  — the pump is an inline loop; recorded follow-up below).

Two platform facts verified in the vendored sources (notify 8.2.2,
`src/inotify.rs:212-214`, `:449-453`, `:385-391`, `:565`; corrected
by the round-1 addendum below): the card's "errno EMFILE" names the
INSTANCES limit, which fails the watcher at CONSTRUCTION
(`inotify_init` allocates the descriptor — `WatcherInitError`'s
no-watch-at-all degrade; adding a watch allocates no descriptor and
cannot fail with EMFILE) — the WATCHES limit is the per-directory
refusal, surfaced as `ENOSPC`, which notify remaps to
`ErrorKind::MaxFilesWatch`. Watch-add refusals are synchronous
`watch()` `Result`s, never stream events for our non-recursive
watches (the recursive re-add path that forwards `MaxFilesWatch`
into the stream is unreachable here). The behavior is
refusal-agnostic either way, so the tests inject a class-only
synthetic refusal and no raw errno (D-111). The watch-limit
refusal is deliberately NOT a `Backend` event — the D-137 P2-4
loop ruling stands; with the fake backend the watcher holds no
sink at all, which is the structural form of that pin.

Follow-up found while tracing the convergence (for the board, not
this task): a wanted directory that was converged and then
DELETED-for-good keeps its map entry across passes — the re-arm
refusal (PathNotFound there) does not evict a kept entry, so
`watched_files` claims a file whose watch cannot exist and
`unwatched_files` under-reports. The same hole opens on the
lost-watch-plus-limit shape (IN_IGNORED ends the watch, the limit
refuses the re-add, the entry stays "watched"), so evicting on
refusal REASON alone cannot fix both halves without evicting
genuinely live watches — the fix needs the watch's liveness, not
just the refusal class, and therefore a `WatchRefused` that
carries more than today's display string. A behavior change this
card does not carry; the limit tests here pin the surviving half —
a converged entry must NOT be evicted on a refused re-arm.

full workspace green

### D-138 — T-118: the `sync_run` command — the D-25 gate as a terminal stop, the one cancel point, and the P3-4 terminal row for every post-phase-0 `Err` — 2026-11-21

Problem: T-118 composes the finished phases (D-130…D-134) into the
§7.10 `sync_run` command over §9.4's whole pipeline. Seven points were
open: what §9.4 phase 1 step 6's "changes nothing" means for the run
row phase 0 already recorded when the D-25 gate fires; where the
cooperative cancel point sits and how minimal the token is (§9.4 phase
2 step 3: "After phase 2 succeeds, the run cannot be canceled"); the
terminal state of a `running` row behind a phase-level `Err` — the
P3-4 follow-up D-133 recorded for this task; where DB-032's
"before a sync" availability checkpoint runs relative to the flag; the
command's answer shape over `Phase4Outcome`; and which §10 mappings the
command itself owns by name (`E_MARKERS_INVALID`/`E_CONTENT_RESERVED`/
`BackupNameError`).

Solution: `commands.rs`'s `sync_run` section — the command
(`Result<SyncRunOutcome, AppError>`), the `sync_run_with` body
(`dialog_pick_folder_with`'s split: the one `logging::sync_run_failed`
edge covers every failure; tests drive the body with their own token
and seams), `CancelToken`, `SyncRunSeams` (phase 2's copy + phase 3's
§9.5 write behind `Arc<dyn Fn>` aliases — the D-089 injector pattern
bundled for one call site), `stop_run`, `pipeline_refusal`,
`summary_of` — plus three facade edges (`sync_run_failed` error,
`sync_run_aborted` info, `sync_run_degraded` warn), one
`collect_commands!` line in `lib.rs`, the regenerated
`src/bindings.ts`, and the `ipc_tests.rs` section.

- _The composition._ Phase 0 (the flag inside, `E_SYNC_RUNNING` for a
  second start) → `availability::recheck_and_emit` → phase 1 → the
  D-25 gate → the cancel check → phases 2/3/4 → the watcher's
  `refresh_after_sync` → the summary. The `Phase0Outcome` (guard
  included) is held for the whole run — every exit is §9.4 phase 4
  step 5's reset by RAII (D-123). The availability seam runs AFTER
  the flag, BEFORE phase 1: the SYS-005 gate freezes the project list
  the pass reads, and its refusal stops the run (a pass that cannot
  see the list cannot be "before a sync") — `recheck_and_emit`'s own
  docs name this as T-118's entry.
- _The D-25 gate is a terminal stop._ "Changes nothing" is §9.4
  phase 1's own header phrase — about the TARGET files (the one
  housekeeping exception is phase 1's own step-7 sweep of the app's
  stale tmp files, §9.4's own rule, not a target-file change). The run row
  phase 0 recorded cannot stay `running` behind a released flag (it
  would lie until the next restart), and the confirm re-call is a
  FULL NEW RUN (phase 0 records its own row), so the asking run ends:
  `abort_run` with the DB-002 now, the empty `error_code` literal (no
  §10 code names a user decision; readers treat "" as "no code"),
  and the class-only "awaiting the empty-build confirmation for N
  project(s)" details. The answer is `NeedsConfirmation` with the
  ids in `sort_order` — ids, not names: the dialog maps them through
  the columns the matrix already renders. Pinned: files byte-equal,
  no backup, no stamp, flag free, row `aborted`, rows `not_started`;
  the confirmed re-call answers `success` over its own row while
  history keeps both.
- _The cancel point and the token._ One consultation, after the gate,
  before phase 2 — §9.4's own point of no return; the token is a
  latched `Arc<AtomicBool>` (`cancel`/`is_cancelled`, Release/Acquire)
  because everything between the check and phase 2 is already running
  and everything after phase 2 is uncancellable, so a channel buys
  nothing. A latched token stops the run the D-131 `E_DISK_FULL`-tail
  way: the row `aborted`, phase 1's verdicts stay (an `unchanged` row
  claims no write; the phase-2 per-project reset belongs to the
  backup abort's own transaction), and the answer is the `aborted`
  SUMMARY, not an `Err` — the user asked for this. The public command
  constructs a token nobody can reach; publishing the running run's
  token for the future `sync_cancel` command (a managed slot in
  `lib.rs`'s setup, outside this card's one-line allowance) is the
  recorded follow-up.
- _The P3-4 ruling (every post-phase-0 `Err` gets a terminal row)._
  `pipeline_refusal` wraps the availability seam and phases 1–4 with a
  best-effort `abort_run` carrying the error's own §10 literal and a
  class-only stage line ("the run stopped at the write phase:
  E_DB_LOCKED"), decided by the ROW's state inside the one transaction
  (`stop_run_if_running`: a row no longer `running` answers untouched)
  — never by the error's code: the shared SQL classifier maps
  `SQLITE_FULL` to `E_DISK_FULL` from ANY phase's transaction, an
  error shape indistinguishable from phase 1's in-phase free-space
  tail, so the first cut's code-skip would have left exactly the
  corpse this ruling exists to prevent (the round-1 P1 fix). No per-project reset rides these aborts: a
  `written`/`failed`/`unchanged` row claims what actually happened
  (D-131's posture, spelled for every stop point). A refused abort
  (the store that just failed failing again) leaves the row
  `running` — the startup `interrupted` recovery's case — logs one
  degraded line, and returns the ORIGINAL error (the first error
  names the cause; the second only compounds it). Pinned through a
  planted wrong-state row refusing phase 3's success transaction
  mid-loop (the parked write seam): the command answers the store
  error, the row is `aborted`/`E_DB_LOCKED`, the already-written file
  stays (§9.5's old-or-new, D-133's residual window), and the
  §10-idempotence tail converges — the retried run reads the file
  `unchanged` and stamps it.
- _The answer shape._ `SyncRunOutcome` (serde-tagged
  `{"outcome": "needsConfirmation"|"completed"}`) — no "cancelled"
  member exists because a cancel cannot land after phase 2. The
  summary is the COMMITTED rows read back (`get` + `list_projects`):
  verdict and statuses as the store's §6.2 literals, MAIN-024's
  counter chips (as `i32` — specta forbids BigInt-style types on the
  wire; `wire_count` is the reasoned-panic conversion), the §9.4
  empty-run details cell, and one entry per project with its §10
  code. The finish's never-fatal reports (D-134) and the watcher's
  refresh refusal never reach the wire or fail the command:
  `sync_run_degraded` warn-carries them (the D-134 follow-up "T-118's
  log lines consume the reports", closed).
- _The mappings by name._ The command carries the phases' codes; it
  maps nothing new. Pinned on the wire: `E_MARKERS_INVALID` (the
  scheme-B skip) and `E_FILE_LOCKED` (the refused write) as
  per-project literals with class-only messages, `E_BACKUP_FAILED`
  as the abort envelope with BKP-005's `project`/`path` params and
  the OS facts, `E_SYNC_RUNNING` as the second-start envelope.
  `E_CONTENT_RESERVED` and `BackupNameError` are unreachable through
  this command by construction — the reserved-line check is the
  library-save boundary (no instruction text enters the pipeline
  except through stored variants, and phase 0 builds them verbatim),
  and the backup-name validation folds into phase 2's
  `NameFailed`→`E_BACKUP_FAILED` envelope (D-132's table, pinned by
  its suite); recorded here as the checklist's "by name" audit.
- _The mock-layer deviation (rule 10)._ D-154's loud-drift layer
  (`src/ipc/mock/commands.ts`, typed by the generated `IpcCommands`)
  fails `pnpm typecheck` until every new command has a mock — the
  card froze `src/**`, but a red typecheck is not a shippable
  alternative, so the minimal stand-in landed: one `syncRun` member
  (available actives `written` with `dirty` cleared and
  `lastSyncedAt` stamped, unavailable ones skipped
  `E_PROJECT_UNAVAILABLE`, one journal entry per project plus the
  summary; D-25 and `E_SYNC_RUNNING` not modelled — no builds, no
  flag state) and the D-108 pin's one-line list extension in
  `src/ipc/mode.spec.ts`. Two files, one member each — the frozen
  Vue UI was not touched.

Tests: `ipc_tests.rs` — 10 through the real IPC path or the body
seam: the D-25 criterion (list + nothing-changed + terminal row),
the confirmed re-call (new run in history, emptied file, backup of
the overwritten bytes), the parked-write second start
(`E_SYNC_RUNNING`, refused start records no row), the cancelled
token (aborted summary, D-131-tail verdicts, no backup/stamp), the
full happy path over the real phases (A rewrite + C creation, one
marker, one backup, 3 journal entries, stamps, free flag), the
failing backup (typed envelope + params + OS code, in-phase aborted
row untouched by the wrapper), the phase-3 store failure + retry
convergence (P3-4), the by-name codes (`E_MARKERS_INVALID` +
`E_FILE_LOCKED`, verdict `failed`), the recovery-mode honesty
(`NoDatabase`, flag down), and the registration pin. Mutation
check: M1 gate disabled → the criterion red; M2 cancel check
disabled → the cancel test red; M3 wrapper disabled → the terminal
row red ("running" vs "aborted"); M4 the gate's stop dropped → the
terminal-row pin red — all green after revert; `cargo test
--workspace` green (33 binaries), clippy `-D warnings` green, the
frontend quartet green.

### D-142 — T-256: schema v2 — the `backup_records` per-pair lookup index (`ix_backup_records_pair_lookup`) — 2026-11-22

Problem: D-132's sync phase 2 issues `last_checked(conn, project_id,
source_path)` once per eligible project per run, and schema v1 had no
index on `backup_records` — every lookup was a full table scan, N scans
per sync run (D-132's recorded follow-up). An index is an owner
decision; the owner approved the column set
`(project_id, source_path, status, created_at)` by moving T-256 into
the dev cycle. Secondary questions: how a v1→v2 upgrade is tested
through the public API (which applies the whole embedded set, so a
"v1 database" must be built, not migrated down); how an
`EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` test stays tied to the production SQL that lives
private in the repository module; and which version pins advance
legitimately with the version bump (updating a pin because the
version moved is fine; weakening one is not).

Solution: `migrations/0002_backup_records_pair_index.sql`, appended to
`MIGRATIONS` (append-only; `0001_init.sql` untouched) —
`CREATE INDEX ix_backup_records_pair_lookup ON backup_records
(project_id, source_path, status, created_at)`; `user_version` 2;
naming per `ix_<table>_<purpose>` (`ix_items_position`, `ix_log_ts`).

- _The shape, as approved._ The equality prefix
  `(project_id, source_path, status)` is the lookup's WHERE clause and
  its "project and file" pair; `created_at` is the ORDER BY's first
  term. The green plan reads
  `SEARCH backup_records USING INDEX ix_backup_records_pair_lookup
(project_id=? AND source_path=? AND status=?)` — the seek replaces
  the scan; the pair's rows walk newest-first from the index, and only
  the `id DESC` tiebreak term still sorts
  (`USE TEMP B-TREE FOR LAST TERM OF ORDER BY`: `id` is not an index
  column — a wider shape would be a new owner escalation, not this
  task's call). `backup_retention::apply`'s window (PARTITION BY
  project_id, source_path; ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC;
  status='ok') reads the same pair/stamp columns — a likely secondary
  beneficiary, noted without a claim (its plan is not pinned here).
- _Mechanics unchanged by design._ rusqlite_migration's per-step
  transaction and the D-038 pre-migration `VACUUM INTO` copy carry the
  step: a v1 database upgraded through the public API writes
  `pre-migration-v1-<UTC>.sqlite3` — the first real upgrade path
  through `run_migrations` (D-038's "the embedded set defines a single
  migration" testing boundary moved; the private synthetic seam keeps
  the multi-step and broken-step paths, which a two-step set still
  cannot provide).
- _The v1 fixture's authenticity (Rule 2)._ `tests/schema_v2.rs`
  builds a v1 database by executing the real `0001_init.sql` and
  setting `PRAGMA user_version = 1` inside one transaction — the exact
  steps rusqlite_migration 2.7's `goto_up` performs (src/lib.rs
  618–653: `execute_batch` of the SQL, then `PRAGMA user_version`
  inside the transaction, commit), verified against the installed
  sources, not assumed: the upgrade starts from a state schema- and
  version-identical to what a shipped v1 app leaves behind.
- _The plan test's mirror._ `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` needs the statement
  text; `backup_records::last_checked` keeps it private. The test
  mirrors the SQL and cross-checks the mirror against the production
  function on the same fixture (both must answer the pair's newest
  `ok` copy identically), so a semantic drift fails the suite — the
  D-132 `db002_stamp` mirror posture. Residual, recorded: a purely
  syntactic rewrite of the production SQL (same semantics, different
  text) would not be caught.
- _Pins advanced with the version._ `schema_v1.rs`: the version
  asserts moved 1→2 and `ix_backup_records_pair_lookup` joined the
  exhaustive explicit-index list (the list stays exact — strengthened,
  not weakened); `storage_migrations.rs` and `storage_open_db.rs`
  pins 1→2; `storage.rs`'s too-new test now bumps to
  `latest_schema_version() + 1` (the `db_tests.rs` `app_schema_version`
  posture — structural, will not rot at v3), the daily-copy schema
  assert reads the same constant; ARCHITECTURE.md's storage paragraph
  and the storage.rs module/`MIGRATIONS`/`migrate`/`set_of` docs (the
  "single migration / no upgrade path" claims) updated in the same
  change.

Tests: `tests/schema_v2.rs`, 4 integration tests, all red first
against the un-migrated schema for the right reasons (version 1≠2; the
plan `SCAN backup_records; USE TEMP B-TREE FOR ORDER BY`; zero copies
written): the v1→v2 upgrade over a v1 database with rows (project,
settings and five records verbatim after — every column of every row,
not a key subset — three `ok` of the pair including a same-stamp pair
for the id tiebreak, one `pruned` seeded NEWER than the newest `ok`,
one other project's — and `last_checked` answers the newest `ok` on
the upgraded database, tiebreak included); the fresh bootstrap reaches
`user_version` 2 with the index's columns pinned by `PRAGMA
index_info` to exactly the approved set, in order (the card is the
oracle, not the SQL); the `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` of the exact
`last_checked` statement (`USING INDEX ix_backup_records_pair_lookup`,
no `SCAN`) with the production cross-check; and the pre-migration copy
(name shape `pre-migration-v1-<19-char UTC>`, `integrity_check` ok,
`user_version` 1, no v2 objects, rows preserved, no `.tmp` debris).
Mutation checks: M1 index dropped → plan/index/upgrade tests red; M2
`created_at`→`size_bytes` in the index → the column pin red (the plan
test stays green — SQLite still seeks the equality prefix through a
misshapen index; the column pin is what discriminates the approved
shape); M3 a destructive `DELETE` added to the migration → the
preservation test red (the copy test correctly stays green: the copy
is the pre-step state). The existing suites are untouched and green as
moved: `backup_records` (`last_checked` correctness, the D-132
handshake), `backup_retention`, `sync_runs`, `schema_v1` constraints,
the storage daily-copy and migration suites, and src-tauri (whose
too-new gate reads `latest_schema_version()` dynamically — no pin
existed to update).

Honest boundaries: the planner's choice is SQLite's — the plan test
pins that the current planner prefers the index over a scan for this
statement (shape-driven; production runs no ANALYZE); the same-stamp
`id` tiebreak still pays a temp b-tree; a hypothetical "v1" database
whose schema drifted from `0001_init.sql` is outside what the fixture
can reproduce.

Follow-ups for the board (the orchestrator cards them): pin the
retention window's query plan the same way if its scan ever matters;
the pre-migration copies' uncapped accumulation (D-038's known open)
becomes observable in production with the first real upgrade wave —
a retention owner may now be worth its card (discharged — D-180: the
T-253 age rule governed these copies before this line was written);
the dangling "D-141"
references (the never-written mock-layer loud-drift entry:
DECISIONS.md 9649/13120, `src/ipc/mock/commands.ts:6`) need their
entry written under a fresh `next_id` number.

Numbering note: task-id-mcp first issued 141 for this entry; 141
collides with those legacy hand-made references (no D-141 entry
exists), so per the counter policy the entry took the next issued
number, 142 — the counter is never corrected, nothing was renumbered.

full walk, but through the pair-ordered index instead of the table,
the `status = 'ok'` filter riding the walk and the partition grouping
coming free from the index order (the entry's "likely secondary
beneficiary, noted without a claim" is now a pinned fact). The pin
therefore does not transplant the `LAST_CHECKED_SQL` plan test's shape
(`SEARCH …` plus banning `SCAN backup_records`): here the walk IS a
scan and `SCAN backup_records` is a prefix of the wanted fragment, so
the discriminating assertion is the whole fragment — on a v1 database
without the index the same statement plans as a bare `SCAN
backup_records` and the pin goes red (M1, run as a throwaway probe
against the real `0001_init.sql` fixture, never committed). The
statement text lives inside `apply`'s body, so the mirror posture
carries over (`PRUNABLE_ROWS_SQL`) with `apply`-specific mechanics:
the mirrored selection must equal the set of rows `apply` marks
`pruned` on the same fixture (keep = 1, no copy files written — every
removal converges on NotFound and the record is marked, the D-091
posture), and the fixture carries three discriminators, each verified
red against a drifted mirror before pinning (throwaway probes,
removed): the terminal row seeded NEWER than every `ok` of its pair
(dropping `status = 'ok'` pushes the newest `ok` into the prune set),
a same-stamp tie on `new_id()` ids (flipping `id DESC` swaps the
survivor), and a second project's within-limit pair seeded at an OLD
stamp (dropping `PARTITION BY` ranks it globally into the prune set —
an old stamp, because the globally newest row would take the one
global keep slot and survive instead). Left unpinned on purpose: the
plan's temp b-trees (the window's `created_at DESC, id DESC`; the
outer `ORDER BY backup_path`) — planner-spelled bookkeeping under the
same phrasing boundary as the entry above, and an index shape that
could remove them is the alternative-shapes card T-274's owner
decision; the outer `ORDER BY backup_path` orders the walk, not the
selection, so no answer-preserving fixture can discriminate it — it
joins the mirror's recorded residual. The same boundary covers the
asserted fragment itself: `SCAN … USING INDEX …` is the bundled
SQLite's spelling, so a `libsqlite3-sys` bump can turn the pin red
with no project regression — that red is a re-read-and-re-pin event,
not a bug. The mirror is byte-identical to the production literal
(same whitespace), so the pair can be diffed mechanically. No
production code changed. Honest staleness recorded:
`backup_retention.rs`'s module doc still says the window "scans that
whole history each run" and defers the index as a future "schema
task" (written before this index existed); src/ was outside this
task's allowed surfaces (tests/** + this addendum), so the sentence
is reported for a docs-surface follow-up card (the orchestrator cards
it — executor subagents do not create board cards), not silently.

### D-143 — T-255: the file log's size half — a custom daily+10 MB writer with same-day parts; the Windows eprintln exposure retired — 2026-11-22

Problem: the owner's 2026-11-21 ruling "ротация 5 файлов × 10 МБ
(≈50 МБ максимум)" was half-enforced (D-129/T-253: the count half via
the crate's `max_log_files`, the per-file 10 MB honestly not), and the
card sanctioned either a custom writer or a post-rotation size check,
leaving four decisions to this task: which of the two options can
actually enforce the cap; whether the §5.5-pinned
`logs/eunomiasync.<date>.log` name scheme admits in-day size-rolled
files at all (Rule 1); what the writer's own prune orders by and
protects; and whether `prune_old_logs`' `eprintln!` can abort a
Windows GUI build (the D-032/D-129 analysis, this task's second half).

Solution, four decisions:

- _Custom writer — the post-rotation check cannot enforce anything._
  Verified in the vendored tracing-appender 0.2.5 sources: `Rotation`
  is time-based only — `RotationKind` is
  Minutely/Hourly/Daily/**Weekly**/Never (`rolling.rs:490-497`, consts
  `:499-509`; the T-253 card brief and D-129 said
  "NEVER/MINUTELY/HOURLY/DAILY only", missing WEEKLY — no material
  difference, recorded here as the correction); the appender decides
  rotation solely from the wall clock inside its private write path
  (`rolling.rs:226-241`; `should_rollover` `rolling.rs:758-770`), the
  file handle is a private `RwLock<File>`, and the builder surface
  (`builder.rs:9-15`, `:298-300`) exposes no force-roll. Renaming the
  open file out from under the appender is no substitute: it keeps
  writing into its open handle and reopens by its own date name on its
  own clock, and rename-while-open semantics vary by Windows version
  and filesystem (std's default share mode _does_ permit the rename —
  `OpenOptionsExt::share_mode` documents
  `FILE_SHARE_READ | FILE_SHARE_WRITE | FILE_SHARE_DELETE` as the
  default, and D-099 had to strip the flag to manufacture a sharing
  violation — but the vacated name's reuse while the handle lives is
  no promise std makes), so the trick is neither supported nor
  portable. A retroactive trim at startup bounds nothing while the
  app runs — a chatty day grows unbounded between midnights,
  exactly what the ruling bounds. So the size half required owning the
  file: `CappedDailyWriter` in `logging.rs`, moved onto
  `tracing-appender`'s `non_blocking` worker thread (the crate's
  remaining role; no new dependency — Rule 9 untouched, the
  `Cargo.toml` comment updated).
- _Name-scheme reading (Rule 1, resolved before implementation): the
  first file of each UTC day carries the exact §5.5 name; same-day
  size-rolled parts insert `.<N>` (N ≥ 2, decimal, no leading zeros)
  before `.log`._ This is an interpretation, not a contradiction: the
  ruling is unsatisfiable without same-day files (a single chatty day
  passes 10 MB mid-day), the task card itself sanctions the custom
  writer that produces them, and the §5.5 structure block lists
  primary shapes only — T-024's `pre-recovery-*` files (D-049) are the
  in-repo precedent of a task adding a name variant recorded in
  DECISIONS.md without a spec conflict. Rejected readings: a uniform
  `.<N>` on every file (would break the literal spec name every day)
  and truncating the day file at 10 MB (destroys lines, and still
  needs writer-level enforcement). The cap now counts same-day parts
  like any other file — a chatty day can spend all five slots on
  itself, which is exactly the ruling's "5 файлов × 10 МБ" model.
- _Rotation and prune semantics._ Two triggers: the UTC day change
  (jiff `Timestamp::now()` → UTC civil date → `YYYY-MM-DD`; D-032's
  untestable-midnight boundary unchanged) and size — rotate when
  `current_len > 0 && current_len + incoming > cap`, so a write
  landing exactly at the cap stays (a part reaches the cap precisely,
  the next write rolls) and a lone line larger than the whole cap
  lands alone in its part (anything else would spin empty parts);
  `MAX_LOG_FILE_BYTES = 10 MiB`, and no file exceeds it but that one
  lone-line case. The writer's own prune runs at construction and
  before every rotation: keep the newest `max_files − 1` (the crate's
  own `max_log_files` semantics, `builder.rs:192-198`), ordering by
  the (date, part) stamps **parsed from the names** — never mtime, the
  D-129 age-from-name rule — and a name outside the canonical grammar
  is never deleted (`parse_log_file_name`: hand-checked dashed shape +
  jiff calendar validation; the hand check exists because jiff's
  `Date` parser also admits the basic `YYYYMMDD` form — a real gap the
  grammar test caught before review). During a rotation the prune
  protects the file being replaced (its handle is still open; Windows
  cannot remove an open file, and the protection keeps the outcome
  identical across platforms — the next prune, handle closed,
  converges) and the target; protection wins over age so the count
  still lands on the cap (pinned by a test). Idempotency
  (make-operations-idempotent): construction opens today's _highest
  existing part_ at its true length and appends — a rerun continues,
  a part left by an interrupted rotation is finished rather than
  restarted, gaps in part numbers are never refilled, and a part
  already at the cap rolls on its first write. The construction prune
  mirrors the keep-`n`-then-create reasoning only when a file is about
  to be created: a day with no file yet prunes to `max_files − 1` so
  the new file lands the total at the cap, while a restart over
  today's existing file prunes to `max_files` — a directory already at
  the cap loses nothing to a mere restart (the round-1 review's P2-2;
  the crate's own construction prune dipped below the cap there, and
  its builder docs admit it — the writer does not).
- _Degradation, and the Windows `eprintln!` half._ A rotation-time
  prune or open failure is reported **once** through the facade
  (`log_rotation_failed`: step code + path + OS error — the SEC-008
  vocabulary), then retried silently on every following write while
  the writer keeps writing into the current file: the cap is exceeded,
  never the launch, and a healed disk heals the log (D-032's
  writer-error policy applied to rotation). Reporting once per
  degradation episode — the gate re-arms on the next successful
  rotation, so a later, different failure gets its own line — rather
  than per line, keeps a persistent failure from storming the pipeline
  it is failing; the report is an _attempt_ (it rides the same lossy
  channel as every line, and a full queue drops it — the honest
  boundary of diagnosing a pipeline through itself). Routing the
  report through the subscriber is
  deadlock-safe because `non_blocking` is lossy by default
  (`try_send`, `non_blocking.rs:228-233` default builder / `:238-243`
  write arm) and the worker drops writer errors silently
  (`worker.rs:81-83`). A
  construction-time prune failure stays silent (no subscriber exists
  yet to report through); a construction open failure remains the
  `LogInitError` → stderr degradation path (the source type is now
  `io::Error`; the display shape and the failing-path test are
  unchanged). The `eprintln!` enumeration: before this task the
  rolling appender's prune/refresh sites (`rolling.rs:704-707`,
  `:718-724`, `:741-746`) were reachable since T-253 enabled
  `max_log_files` — under D-032's Windows-GUI analysis (no stderr →
  `eprintln!` panics → `panic = "abort"` aborts the process) that was
  the exposure D-129 flagged; after it, those sites are unreachable
  (no `RollingFileAppender` in the path), and the crate's one
  remaining `eprintln!` (the worker's final flush at guard-drop
  shutdown, `worker.rs:86-88`) cannot fire in the app — tauri exits
  via `std::process::exit`, which skips the guard's drop (D-032's own
  boundary) — and `File::flush` is an `io` no-op besides. Structurally
  encoded (encode-lessons-in-structure):
  `#![deny(clippy::print_stderr)]` in `lib.rs` and `main.rs` keeps the
  app crate's production
  code `eprintln!`-free; the pre-existing test
  skip-notices (`ipc_tests.rs`, `sync_phase2_tests.rs`,
  `dirty_recalc_tests.rs`, one `commands.rs` test fn) allow the lint
  locally. Compile-level proof available here: the whole suite,
  writer tests included, runs on the `windows-latest` CI leg
  (`ci.yml:65`) — the writer is std-only file mechanics
  (`OpenOptions` append/create, `read_dir`, `remove_file`,
  `metadata`), so the leg proves the portability of every call it
  compiles and runs. What automation cannot prove goes to the manual
  smoke list (no smoke-checklist file exists in the repo; this entry
  and ARCHITECTURE.md's Logging section carry the steps): (1) a
  Windows GUI session logs into `logs/eunomiasync.<date>.log` and
  rolls into `.2.log` parts past 10 MB with at most five files total;
  (2) a read-only `logs/` starts the app in the stderr degradation
  without aborting; (3) a locked log file does not crash the prune.

Tests: the decision logic is pure and table-tested (name building
against the spec literal; the grammar's accept/reject table incl. a
real leap day, impossible dates, the basic `YYYYMMDD` form, `.1.log`
and leading-zero parts; the boundary arithmetic incl. the exact-cap
case; the prune plan incl. the numeric `.10`-vs-`.2` ordering, the
protection tie-break and dedup), the IO seam is behavior-tested (a
real-constants end-to-end pin that writes past 10 MB through the
production seam and asserts the parts — written first and run RED
against the unchanged T-253 code, then green; a small-cap twin over
the same seam; direct-drive restart idempotency — continue the tail
part, roll only past the cap — and restart-over-a-full-day; parts
counting toward the five-file cap; the blocked-rotation degradation:
every line survives in the current file, exactly one warn, no part
file created). T-253's two cap tests pass — the construction prune
keeps their count expectations (seven seeds → five files), now
tightened by the round-1 review to pin the deterministic survivors by
name and to seed foreign names (`notes.txt`, `.log.bak`, a
leading-zero part, a basic-format date) that must survive untouched.
Mutation checks ran red→green: the boundary comparison flipped
(caught by the arithmetic table); newest-first pruning (caught by the
plan table and the parts-count behavior test); the parser admitting
`.1.log` (caught by the grammar table); dropping lines on a degraded
rotation (caught by the blocked-rotation test — the first mutation
attempt mis-modeled the degraded state and was re-modeled before it
counted); disabling the once-gate (caught by the warn-count
assertion).

Honest boundaries: the midnight crossing still rides the real clock
(D-032's boundary, unchanged — the dated name proves the wiring); a
backwards clock step mid-run makes `next_write_target` append into the
older date's file (log-only, self-correcting on the next write — the
date comparison is by stamp, not direction); the production path of
the degradation warn fires on the `non_blocking` worker thread, where
the tests' thread-local `with_default` subscriber does not exist — the
degradation suite drives the writer directly on the test thread, so
only the global-install production path carries the line untested;
and the three Windows smoke items above. Docs
updated in the same change (Rule 11): the `logging.rs` module docs,
ARCHITECTURE.md's Logging and Data-directory sections, the
`Cargo.toml` comment on `tracing-appender`; D-032/D-129 stand as
history — the addendum below points here. Follow-up material: when a
future `tracing-appender` ships size-based rotation, the custom writer
can retire onto it (a conscious swap task, not a drive-by); and the
`print_stderr` gate covers `src-tauri`'s two crate roots — extending
it workspace-wide (`[workspace.lints]`, plus `print_stdout` for the
same hazard class) is a small task of its own, kept out of this one
by the frozen `crates/eunomia-store` manifest.
