### D-144 — T-257: the watcher refresh wired into `project_add_manual` and the `projects_list` column carrier — D-137's follow-ups 2 and 5 closed — 2026-11-22

Problem: D-137 recorded two follow-ups this card closes. (2) the
watch service's set followed startup, availability and sync only — a
project ADDED after startup stayed unwatched until some other anchor
happened to fire; (5) the §5.7 verdicts reached only an
already-listening webview (`state://file-changed` fires from the
`setup` hook before the frontend registers, and Tauri does not
replay events), so a cold-start caller had no read path —
`snapshot()` was added in D-137's round 1 precisely as the future
carrier, with `commands.rs` frozen then. Five readings were open:
which mutations trigger the refresh; what the refresh failure does
to the user's mutation; awaited or fire-and-forget; where the
carrier's fields come from at command time; and what an archived or
unobserved row reads as.

Solution — follow-up 2, the refresh wiring:

- _SYS-007's own list is the arbiter of scope._ "Watches are added
  when a project is added or its scheme or file name changes, and
  removed when a project is archived or becomes unavailable" — of
  those mutation points, exactly ONE command exists today:
  `project_add_manual` (the spec's `project_update`,
  `project_archive`, `project_restore`, `project_relink` are §7.10
  names without commands; `project_archive`/`project_restore` are
  T-109's card — `ipc_tests.rs`'s own comments say so). The
  committed arm ("added") awaits [`file_watch::refresh_after_sync`]
  after the write-access probe — the SAME seam the sync pipeline
  calls (D-138), never a second refresh path; the future commands
  call the same one-liner as they land (the SYS-005 gate's "join as
  they land" precedent, `reject_during_sync`'s docs). The other
  existing mutations run no refresh, each for a stated reason:
  `projects_reorder` moves `sort_order` only (neither the watched
  SET nor any verdict input), `exclusion_remove` touches no project
  row, `settings_set` writes `default.*` which is copy-at-creation
  (PRJ-012/DEF-005 — never retroactive). The DB-022 commit hook is
  deliberately NOT reused as a trigger: the hook runs under the
  connection's mutex and must never block (D-121), while a watch
  pass probes folders.
- _Never-fatal aftermath, the D-138 watch posture._ The project IS
  added whatever the pass answers: `let _never_fatal… =
refresh_after_sync(&app).await`, the refusal swallowed. The real
  refusal case is a watcher backend that refused to start (the
  service task never exists; the bus receiver was dropped with it,
  so the send fails fast — never a hang; recovery mode is
  unreachable in this flow, it already answered `NoDatabase` at
  `managed_db`). Convergence survives the degrade: every full pass
  re-derives the watch set from the project table
  (`set_files`' idempotent full-set convergence), so the next
  anchor — an availability change, a debounced file event, the next
  sync or mutation — re-converges without loss. The warn line the
  degrade deserves lives in `logging.rs`, a frozen zone this window
  (T-255); recorded as the follow-up below (the D-096/D-121
  documented-gap precedent — no invented log path, SEC-008 holds:
  nothing user-content rides any diagnostic).
- _Awaited, not fire-and-forget._ The card names `refresh_after_sync`
  as the seam; the awaited form guarantees the converged set and the
  emitted first-observation diff by the time the answer lands, and it
  cannot silently no-op (`send().await` on a full bus waits;
  `try_send` drops). The cost is one full pass in the response
  latency — the same pass the sync pipeline already pays after every
  run. The wiring test pins the pass's PRESENCE and its coverage of
  the committed row (the falsifiable facts); awaited-vs-spawned
  ordering is this entry's design guarantee, not a test-oracled fact
  (a spawned refresh would usually also land before the test's
  reads — the round-1 review's P3-3 wording fix).

Solution — follow-up 5, the column carrier:

- _`ProjectColumnEntry` gains `external_changed`/`file_deleted`_
  (D-137's naming; MAIN-028's "externally modified"/"target deleted"
  markings — the icon set's last two members become readable by any
  caller of `projects_list`, closing the cold-start gap). The source
  is ONE `FileWatchState::snapshot()` read per command — the read
  D-137's round-1 P1-1 prepared — taken AFTER the blocking
  availability probes (the T-254 dirty ordering rule: probes over
  dead folders can stall seconds, and a snapshot taken before them
  would let the response carry verdicts older than an event the
  webview already applied), read under the cache's existing mutex
  (no new locks), then per-row map lookups (linear, no re-read per
  row).
- _The per-row rules mirror `dirty_verdict`, plus the watch set's own
  second row-decidable half._ An ARCHIVED row and a row whose folder
  fails THIS response's availability probe both read `(false,
false)`, decided from the row and the probe BEFORE the cache —
  SYS-007's watch set is the active, available projects' (the
  service's own pass PRUNES every leaver from its covered set), and
  the rules close the windows between a folder dying or a row being
  archived (no command exists yet) and the next full pass's prune,
  where a stale cache entry would leak a marking onto a column that
  shows unavailable/archived (each window pinned by a test that holds
  the stale entry open and reads through it). An active, available
  row the service has not observed — before the first pass, a
  service that never started — reads the clean baseline `(false,
false)`: absent ≡ clean, the service's own diff rule, one truth
  with the event. A missing managed state (an uninitialized-app bug;
  `setup` manages it before anything that could fail, recovery mode
  included) answers the clean baseline, never a failed read over
  display flags — the `DirtyState` degrade posture.
- _The loud-drift chain held._ The regenerated `bindings.ts` (D-003;
  the export test's rewrite-and-compare cycle) forced the fixture
  generator (`ProjectFixture` IS the wire type), `MockProjectRow`,
  `toColumnEntry` and the mock's add-row to carry the fields before
  `pnpm typecheck` went green. The fixture's final pass models the
  domain rules the way the dirty pass does (deliberately ahead of
  nothing here — the backend now computes these): only active,
  available rows are flagged, `file_deleted` only after a recorded
  sync (SYS-009's gate), the two never both true — deterministic
  PICKS over the seed-pinned synced pattern (pure scans, NO rng draws
  so the dirty pass's rng sequence stays byte-identical): the first
  watchable synced row is the target-deleted case, the first other
  watchable row the externally-modified one, so every world with two
  active available rows (one synced) — set S included — shows exactly
  one marking of each kind. `snapshot()`'s and `refresh_after_sync`'s
  `cfg_attr(not(test), allow(dead_code))` markers are gone — both
  now have production consumers (the latter already did since
  D-138; its doc's "Unused in production until T-118 lands" line was
  stale and is fixed here, Rule 11).

Tests: 5 new IPC tests in `ipc_tests.rs` — the carrier over the real
command path (a synced-edited, a synced-deleted and a matching file
through the real builder oracle, all three §5.7 states on the wire);
the archived stale-entry pin (the cache's entry verified open, the
archive through the store — no command exists, T-109's seam — and
the column read clean through it); the unavailable stale-entry pin
(the round-1 review's P3-1: the folder dies after the recording
pass, no recheck runs, and the SAME response that probes the folder
dead serves the column clean — the probe is the only fresher fact);
the wiring's positive proof (a pre-existing differing `AGENTS.md`:
only a pass that covered the committed row can record
`external_changed: true`, plus exactly one pass after the startup
one, plus the display-only no-write pin); and the refused-add
negative (the duplicate arm runs no pass — the counter is the
deterministic observable). The existing full-field set pin carries
the cold baseline; `add_manual_app` now manages the watch state with
the receiver dropped, so every existing add test pins the
never-fatal degrade implicitly (the seam answers `FileWatchGone`;
the adds succeed). Frontend: the mock key-set pin gains the two
fields, a row→wire round-trip pin plus the generator invariants
(mutual exclusivity, archived/unavailable clean,
deleted-only-after-sync, exactly one marking of each kind in the
pinned worlds and in set S). Mutation checks, all red-then-green:
M1 the seam call stubbed out → both wiring tests red (empty
snapshot, pass count 1); M2 the snapshot read disabled → the carrier
red (clean column over a live modified verdict); M3 the archived
rule dropped → the stale marking leaks onto the archived column; M4
the generator's marking disabled → the frontend pins red; M5 the
unavailable arm dropped → the stale marking leaks onto the
unavailable column.

Honest boundaries: the carrier reads the service's LAST RECORDED
verdict, not a fresh probe — a file edited after the service's
latest pass reads stale until that pass's debounce lands, exactly
like the event a listener would instead receive (the reconciliation
rule: the read corrects, the event updates). The add's response
awaits one full watch pass — a hung mount hangs the response, but
the add flow ALREADY touches the same folder's target file in its
own write-access probe before that (the §6.9 step-5 ordering), so
the exposure is not new; a bounded wait for mutation callers is a
recorded follow-up idea (the pass would keep converging on the
service task whatever the caller does). The add-flow refresh
degrade is silent (no log line exists for it; the frozen
`logging.rs` owns the fix). After a recovery-mode `db_recreate`/
`db_restore_backup` no watch service exists (the D-121-recorded
recovery gap — the recovery commands' task re-arms the services);
the carrier reads the clean baseline there, which is honest for a
session whose watcher never started. The carrier closes the
cold-start gap only for a read that happens after the first pass —
a screen whose first `projectsList` races that pass still reads the
baseline, and (the same reason the carrier exists) nothing replays
the startup event to a late listener: the MAIN-028 UI card must
re-read on listener registration (recorded for that card). D-137's
follow-ups (1) (logging.rs facade lines — frozen zone, untouched
here), (3) (the mock bus's `stateFileChanged` emitter), (4) (the
SYS-010 notice) and (6)/(7) remain open on their own cards.

Addendum (2026-11-23, T-322/D-186): the recovery boundary above holds
only for recovery mode BEFORE the command — a successful
`db_recreate`/`db_restore_backup` now starts the watch service over
the recovered database (the shared session tail), so the carrier reads
recorded verdicts from its first pass on.

### D-145 — T-265: the three content-build mirrors consolidated into eunomia-core (`managed_text` into `target_file`, the chunked pass into `content_build`), every consumer keeping its own pins — 2026-11-22

Problem: D-130's recorded follow-up (joined by D-135's third copy):
the content-build mechanics exist as THREE deliberate mirrors —
`managed_text` (D-064's markerless seam) and the chunked
mini-snapshot pass of 25 (D-121's set-L batching) in
`src-tauri/src/dirty_recalc.rs` (D-121), `src-tauri/src/sync_phase0.rs`
(D-130, born because `dirty_recalc.rs` was T-102's
frozen zone), and `benches/eunomia-load` (D-135, behind pin tests
with a source-scan tripwire). Each copy is independently pinned, but
three spellings of the same bytes are three chances to drift; the
structural fix was carded the moment `dirty_recalc.rs` unfroze.

Two readings recorded BEFORE coding (rule 1):

- _The site is `eunomia-core`, not a src-tauri helper._ The
  mechanics are pure (a string join over core types; a
  `BuildSnapshot` → `BuildSnapshot` scoping; per-project composition
  of `build_body` + `extra_file_lines` + `managed_text` +
  `target_file_name` + `build_hash` + `is_dirty` — every input a
  core seam, no clock, no I/O, no runtime), and D-130's judgment was
  already that the build IS pure core logic. Decisive structural
  fact: the third consumer is `benches/eunomia-load`, which cannot
  depend on the app crate — a src-tauri helper could consolidate
  only two of the three mirrors, recreating the drift one level up.
  A new workspace crate is out (rule 9; the card sanctions core or
  a helper only). No new dependency enters any manifest: core, the
  app, and the bench crate already sit on `eunomia-core`.
- _The mechanical boundary._ What MOVES: `managed_text` →
  `target_file.rs` as a public seam (total over all schemes: B takes
  the body alone — `assembly_b`'s own "the managed block is the body
  alone", which `build_content`'s private `managed_block` could
  never express because it refuses B as a caller bug).
  `build_content` now delegates its A/C join to it, so the join
  exists ONCE inside core itself (the private `managed_block` is
  deleted; its part helper `push_lines_part` survives, private
  before and after, as `managed_text`'s builder). The chunked pass
  → a new `content_build` module:
  `MINI_SNAPSHOT_PROJECTS` (25), `StoredHashes`,
  `AssignmentsByProject`, `group_assignments`, `BuiltProject` (the
  four-field product `PreparedProject` always was: id, managed,
  target_path, build_hash), `build_projects` (the sequential
  whole-snapshot content pass), `compute_dirty_verdicts` (the
  sequential verdict pass), and `chunk_verdicts` (the per-chunk
  half). What STAYS consumer-specific: the DB-reading seams
  (`Db::run` vs the bench's standalone `rusqlite` transaction), the
  parallelism substrate (the app spreads chunks over
  `spawn_blocking`, the bench over `std::thread::scope` — one
  per-chunk entry call each), the `state://dirty` diff cache and
  emit, the AppError mappers, phase 0's run-record composition
  (`PreparedProject` becomes a type alias of `BuiltProject`;
  phases 1–4 and their tests are untouched by shape), and the bench
  crate's fixtures/reads/profile constants. `sync_phase1`'s
  `splice_without_marker` (the ALG-031/B half) and `sync_phase3`'s
  `whole_file` tail are NOT these mirrors (D-131/D-133's own
  spellings, pinned against the real builders) and stay.

The migration map, consumer by consumer:

- `dirty_recalc.rs`: the six mirrored items (the const, the type,
  `group_assignments`, `compute_dirty_verdicts`, `chunk_verdicts`,
  `managed_text`) are deleted; `recalc_and_emit`'s parallel loop
  now calls
  `eunomia_core::content_build::{group_assignments, chunk_verdicts}`;
  the verdict-semantics unit tests (DB-021
  through the composition — never-synced both spellings, the
  no-assignments exception, stored-matching/-differing, the extras
  change, snapshot order, crossing-wires, the per-scheme clean
  pins, the partial last chunk) MOVE to `content_build`'s own suite
  — they verify the shared mechanics, not the service's wiring; the
  service keeps its wiring pins (the diff semantics, the wire name,
  the debounce literal, everything in `dirty_recalc_tests.rs`, the
  set-L budget test whose sequential reference import moves).
- `sync_phase0.rs`: the same six items deleted;
  `build_projects` delegates to core's; `PreparedProject` = the
  alias; the two managed-mirror inline tests are deleted (core's
  suite owns the seam now) while the composition pins stay
  (`sync_phase0_tests.rs`'s verbatim content/hash oracles, the
  settings-coverage matrix, the 26-project chunk boundary — each
  still able to fail if THIS module's wiring diverges); the module
  docs' "deliberate mirror" paragraph is rewritten (rule 11).
- `benches/eunomia-load`: the mirror half of the harness lib is
  deleted (`managed_text`, the const, `group_assignments`, the
  types, `prepare_project`, `scope_chunk`, both chunk fns,
  `compute_verdicts_sequential`, `build_projects_sequential`,
  `BuiltProject`); the benches and pin tests call core directly;
  `compute_verdicts_parallel` stays (the bench-local
  `std::thread::scope` substrate over core's `chunk_verdicts`) and
  keeps its sequential-vs-parallel pin. The D-135 tripwire is
  RELOCATED, not retired: it pinned the production chunk size by
  source-scanning two files that no longer carry the constant; it
  now pins
  `eunomia_core::content_build::MINI_SNAPSHOT_PROJECTS == 25`
  by value — the §12.2 budgets were measured at 25, and a core
  change turns the harness red until the budgets are re-measured
  (mutation-verified below). The managed-text pins in
  `mirror_pins.rs` lose their `build_content`-equality half (core's
  `build_content` now delegates to `managed_text`, so that
  equality became a mirror of the implementation — rule 4) and pin
  the D-21 sentence literals directly instead.

A fourth partial copy exists and is OUT of this task's reach:
`file_watch.rs` (D-137) borrowed the same `group_assignments` +
chunked-mini-snapshot arithmetic for `bodies_of` (bodies of a
wanted subset), and that file is T-259's frozen zone — untouched
here, reported as a follow-up card for the first task allowed to
edit it.

No behavior change, proven twice. Logically: the byte-level oracles
the old pins used (`build_content`'s spec-literal suite, the
independent full-snapshot `build_body` spellings) are code this
task did not touch, and the consumers' pins against them stayed
green through the migration. Empirically: an uncommitted dump test
hashed every built project's managed text over two generated
fixture profiles (the 57-project boundary-crossing set and a
zero-assignment set — 60 projects) before and after the migration;
the sorted digest lists are identical (sha256 `be6dbd0c…`, both
sides), and the probe was deleted after the proof.

Mutation checks, all red-then-green: M-A the shared scoping leak
(unscoped assignments into a chunk's mini-snapshot) failed
`chunked_builds_equal_the_full_snapshot_builds` red — the mini's own
validation refuses the foreign project's row, the same discriminator
D-130/D-135 recorded; M-B the dirty wiring dropping the stored
hashes at the seam failed three service pins (the sync-clears
criterion, the hidden-instruction silence, the `projects_list`
cache carrier); M-C phase 0 recording an empty fingerprint failed
the verbatim content/hash oracle; M-D the core constant moved to 26
failed ONLY the relocated tripwire (the five other bench pins
stayed green — the tripwire is the chunk-size discriminator); M-E
the bench's parallel substrate collecting chunks out of order
failed the order pin.

Testing: `eunomia-core` gained the shared mechanics' own suite —
`target_file`'s two `managed_text` pins against the D-21/ALG-030
literals (never against `build_content`, which now delegates the
join — an equality pin would mirror the implementation) and
`content_build`'s twelve (nine relocated from the dirty service's
suite — the DB-021 verdict semantics, the per-scheme clean pins,
the partial last chunk — plus three new: the full-snapshot
equivalence with an independently spelled oracle, the grouping
map's contract, the missing-key verdict). `dirty_recalc.rs` keeps its nine
diff-semantics/wire-name/debounce unit tests (eleven verdict and
mirror tests moved or retired with the mechanics) and all of
`dirty_recalc_tests.rs` (the L test's sequential reference now
imports core's `compute_dirty_verdicts`); `sync_phase0.rs` keeps
its mapper/target-path tests (the two managed-mirror tests retired
with the mirror — the seam is pinned where it lives) and all of
`sync_phase0_tests.rs` untouched except one doc-comment's constant
reference; `eunomia-load`'s `mirror_pins.rs` carries six pins
(three managed-text equality pins retired as newly tautological,
one D-21 splice pin added in their place; the `BuiltProject`
oracles gained the `target_path` field) plus the profile unit
test. `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets
-- -D warnings` and `cargo test --workspace` all green (exit codes
checked).

Honest boundaries: the criterion budgets were NOT re-measured (the
measured code path is unchanged — the harness now calls the very
per-chunk function the old mirror implemented — and §12.2's
reference-machine rerun stays the §15.5 gate D-135 left open); the
consolidation deliberately does not touch `sync_phase1`'s
`splice_without_marker` or `sync_phase3`'s `whole_file` tail
(D-131/D-133's own spellings, pinned against the real builders) —
if the owner wants those folded into core too, that is its own card
with its own oracles; and `file_watch.rs`'s fourth partial copy
(frozen zone) is the reported follow-up.

Problem: T-259 closes two of D-139's recorded follow-ups, both

(Round-1 P2-2) the pump's event→command mapping — the inline loop
that turns `WatchEvent`s into bus commands, at current-main lines
950-956, drifted from the card's ≈946-955 — had NO test, with extra
weight since D-139 because `WatchEvent::Backend` carries BOTH
lost-events shapes (the overflow rescan batch AND the stream-error
batch), not just the rarer stream error the old comment implied.
(Round-2 P3-1) the module doc at :61-62 still called `Backend` "an
event-stream error, SYS-010's overflow case" — the pre-D-139 premise
D-139's own docs were corrected away from.

Solution: the watcher's `dispatch` precedent (D-139), applied one
layer up — the extraction D-139's own follow-up text prescribed
("extract the event→command mapping into a testable function"). (The
card's named fake-backend seam cannot reach this layer: `WatchBackend`
only arms and disarms watches and never emits events — the debouncer
that delivers lives inside `NotifyBackend` — and `spawn_service`
constructs its own watcher internally, so "no real-FS waits" is
achievable only through the extraction, the follow-up's alternate
route; round-1 review P3-1 asked for this sentence.) The pump's
per-event step — the match plus the `try_send`, verbatim — moved into
`pump_event(event, &trigger)`; the pump thread is now a one-line
forward per event; `spawn_service`'s signature, its `lib.rs`
caller and the thread's lifecycle are untouched, and the mapping's
logic is unrefactored. Four tests in the module's colocated suite
drive `pump_event` directly over a fresh bounded channel — the same
observable the service task consumes; no notify event thread, no app
harness, no filesystem waits:

- `changed_and_removed_events_become_files_changed_batches_of_their_own_path`
  — each file variant maps to a `FilesChanged` batch of exactly its
  own path (the partial re-read's input, SYS-008's noise filter), one
  command per event; the variants are asserted separately so the
  shared or-pattern cannot hide a variant swap behind one combined
  assertion.
- `a_backend_event_becomes_a_fire_and_forget_full_refresh` — the
  lost-events signal maps to `Refresh { done: None }`: the one full

  drops the delivery, never blocks the pump, never displaces the
  commands already queued.
- `a_dead_bus_drops_every_variant_delivery_instead_of_panicking` —
  the closed-bus teardown shape (the service task gone while the pump
  thread lives) through all three variants, the pump-side twin of
  D-139's round-2 P3-2 dead-consumer pin; the documented

### D-147 — T-258: the live run's cancel token published through a managed slot; the startup `interrupted` recovery T-122 never landed, landed here; and D-138's first-reader obligation pinned at a seam — 2026-11-22

Problem: T-258 carries three halves out of D-138's follow-up list.
(1) The `sync_run` command constructs a cancel token nobody can reach
— D-138 recorded "publishing the running run's token for the future
`sync_cancel` command (a managed slot in `lib.rs`'s setup …) is the
recorded follow-up", and the card IS that follow-up (the command
itself is T-120's, not this card's). (2) The card's text says the
startup `interrupted` recovery (card T-122) "exists — synchronize
the spec"; verification said otherwise, and Rule 11 forbids papering
over the drift. (3) D-138's round-1 P2-1 records "the follow-up
below names the first reader's obligation" for the run row's
`error_code = ""` spelling — the obligation needed a binding place.

Solution, half by half.

**Half 1 — the token publication.** `commands.rs` gains
`SyncCancelSlot` (a `Mutex<Option<CancelToken>>` managed by `setup`
in every mode beside `SyncRunning`, for the same reason the flag is:
the future `sync_cancel` must find the state, and in recovery mode
the slot simply stays empty) and `CancelLease`, the clearing half in
the `SyncGuard` RAII shape (D-123) — the ONE mechanism, not a second
cancel path:

| moment                                                                                                | the slot holds                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| no run live (fresh app, between runs, recovery mode)                                                  | `None`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `sync_run_with` entered, after `data_root`, before phase 0's flag take                                | the run's token (`publish`: set-if-empty)                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| the run runs                                                                                          | the run's token; a refused second start publishes nothing and clears nothing (its latch is not current)                                                                                                                                                           |
| the run answered — finish, the D-25 stop, the cancel stop, the P3-4 wrapper's `Err`, a panic's unwind | `None` (the lease's `clear_if_current`; the finish path drops the lease explicitly beside the guard, before the never-fatal aftermath — the D-138 P2-2 shape applied to the slot: a wedged after-run seam must not leave a published token behind a finished run) |
| the process dies mid-run                                                                              | the slot dies with it (in-memory); the corpse row is half 2's case                                                                                                                                                                                                |

Readings chosen: publish BEFORE the flag take (phase 0's snapshot
build takes real time — a cancel arriving over it must find the
latch; a token published but never taken is a harmless latch the
lease clears); set-if-empty so a second start can never evict the
live run's token; `clear_if_current` compares the inner `Arc`
(`ptr_eq`) so no run's exit unpublishes another's; publication
itself looks the state up with the panicking `app.state` (a wiring
bug must be loud) while the lease's `Drop` uses `try_state` (a Drop
must not abort mid-unwind). A stale token cannot exist in a live
process: every exit drops the lease, and a release-build panic
aborts the process (the flag's own `panic = "abort"` caveat). The
cancel POINT is untouched — D-138's law: `token()` hands the future
command a clone of the same latched `Arc`, so "cancel through the
slot" IS the existing check, never a second consultation.

**Half 2 — the interrupted recovery, and the honest T-122 finding.**
The card believed T-122 ("mark interrupted runs at startup") DONE.
Verification (Rule 11, before any design): no commit in
`git log --all` names it; no D-entry exists; `grep -rn interrupted`
finds the status literal, doc comments promising the pass, and tests
commenting on it — but no store writer, no startup call, no tests.
The behavior had NOT landed; the drift is recorded here and the
board card needs the orchestrator's correction (follow-up below).
This card implements it (the "close the gap" reading — the half is
this card's own title):

- `eunomia_store::sync_runs::mark_interrupted_runs` — one UPDATE,
  `running → interrupted` + `finished_at`, scoped to the source
  state (the `reset_projects_not_started` bulk-sweep shape:
  `Ok(0)` over a clean database, idempotent on re-run; NOT the
  per-row writers' zero-row refusal — a clean startup is normal).
  Deliberately NOT written: `error_code`/`details` (a process death
  is nobody's recorded decision — "" stays exclusive to the two
  deliberate user-shaped stops, and `finish_run`'s verdicts write
  NULL, so interrupted matches the finished runs' spelling), the
  counters (phase 4's), and every `sync_run_projects` row (§9.4:
  "the project status already reflects what was written at the time
  of the crash" — the T-F3 shape). `finished_at` IS stamped — the
  moment the row went terminal is what the column names for `aborted`
  rows too, and every terminal row carrying it keeps the summary
  DTO's documented invariant true for the future `sync_last_result`.
- `Db::mark_interrupted_runs` — the sweep over the SYNCHRONOUS seam
  (`ensure_daily_backup`'s shape: `lock_recovering_poison` + one
  short transaction). Synchronous on purpose, and stronger than
  precedent: the sweep is only correct over rows no live run owns,
  and the one moment that holds by definition is startup, before the
  event loop serves a command (the same setup-completes-before-
  invokes assumption every managed state and the ERR-001 copy
  already rest on). A `Db::run`-shaped spawned pass could race this
  process's own first `sync_run` — the flag lives in memory, SQL
  cannot see it — and mark a LIVE run `interrupted`.
- `lib.rs` `setup` runs it right after `Db::open` succeeds, BEFORE
  the commit hook (the marking's row change would otherwise drop a
  dirty trigger for a pass that reads projects, not runs). A refusal
  degrades — logged through the new `sync_runs_interrupt_failed`
  facade edge, the launch continues (D-046/D-054), the next restart
  retries the idempotent sweep; zero corpses log nothing (the
  `AlreadyPresent` posture); N ≥ 1 corpses take one `warn` line
  carrying the count alone (`sync_runs_interrupted`; SEC-008 — run
  ids would be legal but the count is the triage fact). The spec's
  "hashes are recalculated" clause is ALREADY wired — the DB-022
  startup recalculation pass (T-101) — and the §7.7 journal stays
  phase 4's (D-138: the action vocabulary has no member for this;
  recorded, not invented).

**Half 3 — the first reader's obligation, pinned at a seam.**
Verification first (the card asks where the obligation binds): grep
shows NO production reader of the RUN row's `error_code` today —
`summary_of` reads only per-project rows' codes, phase 4's journal
reads only per-project codes (and shape-checks them against §10), so
the pins at `ipc_tests.rs` (`error_code == Some("")`) are the only
readers. The first production reader will be `sync_last_result`
(§7.10, a future card — this card adds no command, no `bindings.ts`
change). What lands so the obligation BINDS in code instead of
prose: `commands::run_error_code_or_none` — the one seam collapsing
BOTH no-code spellings (NULL and "") to "no code", dead-code-allowed
with the true reason (the `CancelToken::cancel` precedent), which
the future reader calls instead of re-deciding; plus the census
(`count_empty_run_error_codes` in the tests) counting the empty
literal across `sync_runs`, pinned per run shape: the D-25 gate stop
and the cancel stop each hold exactly one, a finished run zero
(NULL), an error abort zero (its §10 literal), an interrupted row
zero (half 2's NULL ruling) — a future writer inventing a third
source of "" (or losing one of the two) fails the count.

Tests: store (`tests/sync_runs.rs`) — the sweep takes every corpse
and no terminal row (two corpses + one success + one aborted: count
2, statuses and finish stamps verbatim), and the idempotent second
pass touches neither the row nor any project row (a crash-mid-write
`written` row keeps its fingerprint). `db_tests.rs` — the sweep over
the `Db` seam with crash-shaped rows planted by raw SQL (the oracle
is the schema, not the store's DTOs), read back verbatim, idempotent
on the second call. `ipc_tests.rs` — the lifecycle in one run over
the parked-write shape: empty before; `Some` while parked (flag up,
mid-phase-3); STILL `Some` after a refused second start's
`E_SYNC_RUNNING` (set-if-empty held); a cancel latched through the
slot's token AFTER the check point is the §9.4 no-op (the run
finishes `success`, the project stamped); `None` after the answer —
and THAT clearing is the identity discriminator: only the first
run's own lease can produce it (an overwrite would have left the
second start's token, an unconditional clear would have emptied the
slot at the refusal); census 0 over the finished run. The gate stop
(slot cleared, census 1), the cancel stop (existing test
strengthened: slot cleared, census 1), the error abort (slot
cleared, census 0 — the row carries `E_BACKUP_FAILED`), the
normalizer's three cases, and the `setup` wiring pin (the
config_tests style: open → sweep → commit hook → manage, each marker
exactly once, in order). `logging.rs` — both new edges' lines (warn
with `count=N`, error with the code literal, both class-only).
Mutation check: M1 the then-only publication step disabled (the
pre-`publish_owned` first cut) → the lifecycle test red at the
mid-run read; M2 clear made unconditional → red at "the refused
start left the live run's token in place"; M3 publish made
overwriting → red at the same assertion (the second start's lease
then empties the slot); M4 the store UPDATE's `running` scoping
dropped → both store tests red (terminal rows taken, idempotence
broken); M5 the `finished_at` stamp dropped → the store test red at
the stamp pin; M6 the normalizer's "" arm dropped → the normalizer
test red — all green after revert; `cargo fmt --check`, clippy
`-D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace` all green (exit codes);
`src/bindings.ts` byte-identical (no command or type surface
changed). The composition note, honestly: the end-to-end "cancel
through the published token stops a run at the check point" is
proven as (identity: the slot's token shares the latch with the
token the pipeline consults — ASSERTED through the test-only
`shares_latch` probe while the run is parked) + (D-138's existing
pre-latched-token test: a token cancelled before the run stops it
at the point, before the backups) + (the no-op above for post-point
latches) — three deterministic tests instead of one racy one (no
injectable seam exists between the check and phase 2 to park a run
AT the point; a polling race was rejected as flaky by design, the
D-140 posture).

Frozen zones untouched (`file_watch.rs`, `dirty_recalc.rs`,
`sync_phase0.rs`, `benches/`); `commands.rs` + `lib.rs` owned as
briefed; the store sweep, the `Db` seam method and the two logging
edges are the minimal unavoidable widenings outside that pair,
each justified above. Stale docs fixed in the same change (Rule 11):
`CancelToken`'s "recorded follow-up" sentence, `stop_run`'s
"obligation recorded in D-138's follow-ups" pointer, and the store
module docs' "the one remaining transition" line.

Follow-ups for the board (the orchestrator cards them): the T-122
card's claimed done-state is FALSE — the behavior landed HERE (the
board needs the correction or a close-as-duplicate note); T-120
(`sync_cancel`) consumes the slot (`token().cancel()`; its answer
shape and registration are that card's); T-122's speculative
`sync_last_result` sibling card, when carded, must start from
`run_error_code_or_none` and the census; the D-138 ARCHITECTURE.md
rows follow-up stands. Honest boundaries: a refused-abort corpse
row (D-138's degraded path) stays `running` until the NEXT restart
— mid-session corpse sweeping is out of scope (the spec's recovery
is startup-only, and no in-process marker can distinguish a live
run's row from a corpse's); the `setup` wiring is marker-pinned, not
executed in a test (the house posture — the real `run()` cannot
launch under a unit harness).

- P2-1 (taken): slot ownership and run ownership are decided by
  different races — the pre-take `publish` is set-if-empty, the flag
  is `compare_and_swap` — so a start that pre-published first but
  lost the flag left ITS token published, and its lease's exit then

  The lifecycle table above carries the new row.

### D-148 — T-260: the phantom map entry killed by a liveness attribute — `watched_files` counts only live watches, `unwatched_files` reports the gap — 2026-11-22

Problem: D-139's own follow-up (its "Follow-up found while tracing the
convergence"): a wanted directory that was converged and then deleted
FOR GOOD keeps its map entry across passes — `set_files`' first loop
keeps every still-wanted entry unconditionally, the re-arm refusal
(notify's `PathNotFound` there) does not evict it, so
`TargetWatcher::watched_files` claims a file whose watch cannot exist
and `unwatched_files` under-reports. The same hole opens on the
lost-watch-plus-limit shape (`IN_IGNORED` silently ended the watch,
the watches limit refuses the re-add, the entry stays "watched"). The
app layer inherits the lie: `file_watch.rs`'s full pass records
`unwatched_files()` into `FileWatchState::unwatched_targets` — SYS-
010's observable for the future warning line and notice.

Readings recorded BEFORE coding (rule 1):

- _The map lives in `eunomia-fs/src/watcher.rs`, not the card's named
  `src-tauri/src/file_watch.rs`._ The card's own description — the
  `watched_files` map, `set_files` convergence, `unwatched_files()`,
  the SYS-010 refusal paths — names `TargetWatcher`'s state, which is
  the fs crate's (the D-010 layer split; `file_watch.rs` only consumes
  the two queries in `blocking_half`). The fix therefore edits
  `watcher.rs` (plus docs); `file_watch.rs` needs no code change —
  its call sites keep the same signatures. Recorded as a rule-10
  deviation from the card's file attribution, not from its substance;
  the window's frozen zones (`commands.rs`, `lib.rs`) are untouched.
- _Liveness is per wanted-directory entry, decided by evidence._
  LIVE means: the backend armed the directory's watch at the last
  `set_files` pass (`watch` returned `Ok`), or the entry's previous
  liveness stands because the re-arm's refusal is NOT evidence about
  the watch's life (class `Other` — an I/O hiccup, a permissions
  refusal: an existing kernel watch keeps delivering either way).
  NOT LIVE means: never armed (a fresh refusal — unchanged since
  D-137), or the re-arm was refused with a class that proves the
  watch cannot exist — `Gone` (the directory is gone; the kernel
  ended its watch with the silent `IN_IGNORED` at deletion) or
  `Limit` (the kernel never refuses a genuinely live watch's re-arm
  — it updates the existing mark without allocating, D-137's
  round-2 verification against notify 8.2.2's `add_single_watch` —
  so a limit refusal of a converged entry proves the watch was
  LOST). This is exactly D-139's "the fix needs the watch's
  liveness, not just the refusal class": the class alone cannot
  separate the phantom shapes from genuinely live watches (an
  `Other` refusal of a live watch must not kill it), and liveness
  alone cannot read the refusal's meaning.
- _The queries tell the truth in both directions._ `watched_files`
  answers exactly the wanted files under a LIVE directory; every
  other wanted file lands in `unwatched_files` — never-armed,
  refused-gone and refused-limit alike (the under-report was the
  phantom). The answer stays a path set: no consumer of a
  class-carrying answer exists today (the recorded follow-ups'
  warning line and notice read paths — D-137's ruling); the class
  drives the internal evidence table, and inflating the API for a
  hypothetical consumer would be the speculative shape D-139's
  round 2 refused.
- _Recovery is unchanged and flag-free._ Every pass re-arms every
  wanted directory (D-137 P2-4/P3-6), so a directory that comes
  back arms `Ok` and is live again on the very next `set_files`;
  liveness is recomputed from the pass's own evidence, never a
  sticky bit to clear.
- _`snapshot()` and the column carrier see no change (D-144)._ The
  verdicts are computed by READING the files (`blocking_half`
  classifies every available project regardless of watch state),
  never from `watched_files` — a phantom watch never produced a
  verdict, so it cannot produce a phantom verdict; `external_changed`/
  `file_deleted` semantics are untouched. Only the `unwatched`
  recording becomes truthful.
- _D-139's battery survives in intent, one pinned assertion flips._
  The battery pinned "a converged entry must NOT be evicted on a
  refused re-arm" as the SURVIVING half of the then-known bug ("A
  behavior change this card does not carry" — D-139). This card is
  the carrier: in the battery's second pass the converged
  directory's re-arm is refused with the limit class, which per the
  kernel rule above proves the watch lost — the honest answer moves
  it from `watched_files` to `unwatched_files`. The code keeps the
  entry in every case (verified by reading; as a TESTED pin this
  holds only for the `Other` class — evicting on `Gone`/`Limit`
  would be observationally identical through the queries, since
  liveness already discounts the entry, and no test distinguishes
  it; the retention with behavior is the carried-live `Other`
  entry, pinned by the non-evidential test through
  `is_live_watched_name`'s two halves), and the battery's other
  halves (the mid-set fresh refusal, the lift, the re-arm log) are
  unchanged in substance.
- _The pump pins (D-146) and the D-144 carrier tests are untouched_
  (`pump_event`, `refresh_pass`, `blocking_half` bodies unchanged).

Solution: `WatchRefused` gains the class — `WatchRefusalKind`
(`Gone` | `Limit` | `Other`) with a `kind()` accessor, `new(kind,
reason)`. The production classification is TWO halves: the stat
pre-check in `NotifyBackend::watch` establishes `Gone`
platform-neutrally (`std::fs::metadata`: a missing path, or a path
that is not a directory — one probe per directory per full pass;
notify's backends disagree on how a missing path reaches the
caller, so the error kind alone cannot carry it — see the round-1
addendum's P1), and the kind mapping classifies the backend's own
refusals (`PathNotFound` → `Gone`, `MaxFilesWatch` → `Limit`, the
rest → `Other`; verified in the registry sources, notify 8.2.2
`src/inotify.rs:451-457` — ENOSPC remapped to `MaxFilesWatch`, an
io `NotFound` to `PathNotFound` — and the debouncer's synchronous
passthrough, notify-debouncer-full 0.7.0 `src/lib.rs:600-608`). `TargetWatcher` gains `live:
BTreeSet<PathBuf>` — the liveness half of the converged map, kept
beside the shared `dirs` filter map deliberately: the event thread
filters by NAMES only (a dead watch delivers nothing anyway, and a
carried-live entry must keep delivering), so liveness stays on the
caller's side with no lock at all. `set_files` re-arms as before
and records the evidence: `Ok` → live; refused `Gone`/`Limit` →
not live; refused `Other` → the carried liveness stands; a
directory leaving the wanted set drops both its map entry (the
existing `unwatch`) and its liveness. The converged `files` set is
computed against the map AND liveness, so `watched_files` counts
only live watches and `unwatched_files` — the unchanged
wanted-minus-watched difference — now reports the phantom shapes.

Tests: the battery in `crates/eunomia-fs/tests/watcher.rs` gains
three tests and one honest flip. NEW, red against the pre-fix code
(observed: both failed on `watched_files` still naming the phantom
file):
`a_wanted_directory_deleted_for_good_leaves_watched_files_and_reports_the_gap`
(a REAL backend: converge, `remove_dir_all`,
re-set — watched empties, the seam answers the file, and the
directory's return re-arms) and
`a_limit_refused_re_arm_of_a_converged_directory_leaves_watched_files_and_reports_the_gap`
(the seam's `Limit` kind: the refused re-arm empties `watched_files`
and fills the seam, a repeated pass answers identically, the lift
converges). NEW, green-on-arrival by design and discriminating via
mutation M2:
`a_non_evidential_refused_re_arm_keeps_the_converged_watch_counted` (an
`Other`-kind refusal of a converged re-arm keeps
the watch counted — the genuinely-live-watch half, the reason the
class exists). FLIPPED: the D-139 battery's second pass
(`a_watch_limit_hit_mid_set_leaves_the_later_directories_unwatched`)
— its "the already-converged directory survives its refused re-arm"
assertion pinned the phantom as the surviving half of the then-known
bug; this card carries the behavior change D-139 deferred, so the
pass now asserts the honest answer (the whole set unwatched) plus a
third pass pinning idempotence. NEW unit test in `watcher.rs`'s
colocated suite: `notify_error_kinds_map_onto_the_refusal_evidence_classes`
(PathNotFound→Gone, MaxFilesWatch→Limit, generic and io→
Other, through notify's public `Error::new`). The fake gained the
refusal class (`LimitBackend::refusing_from_with(kind, from)`,
`refusing_from` = the `Limit` kind, so the existing battery's
modeling is unchanged). Checks green by exit code: `cargo fmt
--check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`,
`cargo test --workspace` (the app crate's 518, including every
watch-related ipc test, untouched and green — `pump_event`,
`refresh_pass` and `blocking_half` bodies did not change).

Mutation-verified, each red with the cargo exit code observed, then
reverted to green: M1 the refusal stops clearing liveness → the
three phantom tests red (the non-evidential one green — the
discriminator); M2 the evidence table collapsed to "any refusal
kills liveness" → ONLY the non-evidential test red (the
genuinely-live-watch half has its own guard); M3 the files
computation reading bare map membership instead of liveness → the
three phantom tests red, the non-evidential one green.

Honest boundaries: the fix is map-level; the app layer's phantom
exposure was already partial — `blocking_half` probes availability
first, so a project whose ROOT is gone leaves the wanted set before
`set_files` and was honestly evicted even before this fix; the
shapes the app could actually hold (the root alive, the watch dead:
lost-watch-plus-limit) are now honest through the same recording
(`note_unwatched` reads `unwatched_files()` after `set_files`).
No ipc-level test drives the phantom: the fake backend cannot
reach the app layer (`spawn_service` constructs its own watcher
internally — D-146's P3-1 ruling), and a real limit cannot be
produced on demand (D-139's premise); the watcher-level battery is
therefore the card's end-to-end proof. The battery flip is a
behavior change to a previously pinned answer, recorded above as
this card's sanctioned substance. `unwatched_files` still answers
a plain path set — a class-carrying answer has no consumer today
(D-137's facade ruling); when the SYS-010 notice card wants the
reason text, the `kind` is already on the refusal. The known
timing-sensitivity of the fs suite's real-event tests (60 s
deadlines under load) predates this change; one such test missed
its deadline once during a loaded first-compile run here and passed
on every subsequent run, in isolation and in the full workspace
suite. The evidence table is deliberately BIASED against lying
about a live watch, and the bias has residuals: an `Other` refusal
of a LOST watch keeps it counted (a phantom entry can still hide
behind a non-evidential refusal — say a permissions failure after a
delete-recreate), and a `Gone` on a transient stat `NotFound` (a
momentarily unresolvable mount) kills liveness the kernel mark may
still hold (a brief phantom gap); both self-heal on the next pass's
re-arm and were chosen over silently discounting a still-delivering
watch — `Other` is not a liveness oracle.

### D-149 — T-264: the sync-run error mapper consolidated to one `db.rs` spelling — seven copies deleted, the deliberate non-copies ruled real — 2026-11-22

Problem: D-132's follow-up card. The `SyncRunsError → AppError`
wire mapping had accumulated SEVEN production copies, not the card's
four (the card was written at D-132, before phases 3/4 and T-258
existed): `sync_runs_to_app_error` in each of `sync_phase0.rs`
(325, via its private `sync_fallback`), `sync_phase1.rs` (827),
`sync_phase2.rs` (913), `sync_phase3.rs` (502), `runs_app_error` in
`sync_phase4.rs` (654), `runs_to_app_error` in `commands.rs` (1506),
and an inline match in `db.rs`'s `mark_interrupted_runs` (474–492,
born in D-147's R1-P3-3 fix). Every copy carried the "each module
owns its mapper" doctrine, which was only ever a frozen-zone
workaround (`commands.rs` was frozen when the phases landed,
D-130/D-132). Three readings were open before coding: where the one
mapper lives; what its input type is (the union must be explicit);
and whether any two copies DELIBERATELY differ (D-138's P3-4 warning
— the mapping is entangled with which terminal state each error
class produces).

Solution: one `pub(crate) fn sync_runs_to_app_error(SyncRunsError)
-> AppError` in `db.rs`, placed beside `sqlite_error_to_app_error`
— the shared base classifier it delegates to, which every consumer
already imports from `crate::db`, and whose module docs already
claim the "shared base classifier" role. No new module (a two-entry
store-mapper module would be structure for structure's sake).

- _Deliberate differences: none among the seven._ All seven spelled
  the identical two arms: `Sql` → the shared classifier; `Member` →
  `DbLocked` + `SyncRunsCorrupt` + the class-only "a stored {column}
  cell is outside its vocabulary" (SEC-008). The only drift was
  naming (three spellings) and phase 0's `sync_fallback`
  indirection. A truly-identical merge was therefore possible; no
  parameterization, no variants. The input type is exactly
  `eunomia_store::sync_runs::SyncRunsError` — the type every copy
  already took; the union widened nothing.
- _Deliberate non-copies, ruled real and kept distinct._ (1)
  `backup_records_to_app_error` (was `sync_phase2.rs` 896): a
  different input enum (`BackupRecordsError`) and a different kind
  label — `BackupRecordsCorrupt` names WHICH table's cell is
  corrupt, a real triage distinction. D-132's follow-up named it in
  the consolidation parenthetical, so it moved to `db.rs` as the
  sibling — co-located, same two-arm shape, distinct label and
  enum, NOT folded into one parameterized function. (2) The six
  test-side assertion helpers (`sync_runs_app_error` in
  `sync_phase0_tests.rs`, `runs_app_error` in the phase 1–4 test
  files, `sync_runs_read_error` in `ipc_tests.rs`): assertion
  plumbing, not wire mappers — their fallback is `SyncRunsRead` +
  the error's `Display` (the richest panic message; the wire
  mapper's class-only rule exists for user-facing diagnostics), and
  their `Member` arm is unreachable (the suites read rows they just
  wrote through the sanctioned writers). Left as-is.
- _The P3-4 and "" boundaries are untouched by construction._ The
  mapper answers only the `Err` envelope; which terminal state a
  failed run's row reaches is decided by `stop_run_if_running` from
  the ROW's state (D-138's law), and the run row's `error_code`
  literals ride `abort_run`'s arguments, not this mapping — so no
  caller's terminal-row semantics can change and no new "" spelling
  can appear (D-147's exclusivity census stays valid; its counts are
  re-proven green by the untouched `ipc_tests` pins).
- _The migration map._ 17 production sync-run call sites re-pointed
  (phase 0: 1, phase 1: 3, phase 2: 2, phase 3: 3, phase 4: 3 —
  renamed from `runs_app_error`, commands: 5 — renamed from
  `runs_to_app_error`) plus the `db.rs` inline collapse (18 sync-run
  mapping sites in all) and phase 2's 3 backup-record sites. Phases
  0–3 kept the name, so their sites changed only by import. The
  deleted per-copy docs ("spelled again because…") went with the
  functions; `sync_phase0.rs`'s `# Errors` link and `db.rs`'s
  `mark_interrupted_runs` `# Errors` section now name the one
  mapper (Rule 11). `file_watch.rs` (T-260's frozen zone) never
  referenced any copy — untouched.

Tests: the union pin lives at the one mapper's home,
`db_tests::sync_runs_failures_map_to_the_wire_through_the_one_mapper`
— phase 0's old inline pin (deleted with its copy) moved there and
grew into the consolidation table: three representative §10 classes
through `Sql` (busy/full/constraint — one per or-group; the
classifier's own nine-member table above it stays the classifier's
oracle), the non-`SqliteFailure` fallback arm (`InvalidQuery` →
`DbLocked`, the old pin's case), the `Member` envelope asserted in
full on the SERIALIZED wire (code, message key, `SyncRunsCorrupt`,
the exact class-only message) with a hostile `found` value
(`paused<script>`) proven absent from the whole JSON, and the
sibling's distinct `BackupRecordsCorrupt` label. The per-caller
oracle is unchanged: every `sync_phase*_tests.rs` and `ipc_tests.rs`
pin that reads these envelopes through the real phases stayed green
without one edit. Mutation check: M1 the `Member` kind label
flipped → the pin red; M2 the `Sql` arm mutated to bypass the
classifier → red at the delegation assertion (db_tests.rs:616);
both green after revert. `cargo fmt --check`, clippy
`--workspace --all-targets -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace`
(34 suites) — all green by exit code.

Honest boundaries: the six test-side helpers keep their own
spelling (the ruling above); TWO of them (the phase-0 and phase-1
test files) carried doc comments claiming "class-only here too"
while a reachable `Member` arm would embed the `Display` text — the
round-1 review caught the lying wording and it is reworded in this
change (assertion-only, deliberately `Display`-rich); whether the
six helpers should adopt the shared mapper's `Sql` arm outright is
the follow-up below. The OTHER store-table
mappers (`projects_store_to_app_error`, `activity_log_to_app_error`,
the settings pair in `commands.rs`, the library mapping in
`dirty_recalc.rs`) are single-copy, not duplication, and stay where
they are — this card consolidates the sync-run family only.
ARCHITECTURE.md has no mapper rows to update (the D-138 rows
follow-up stands).

Follow-ups for the board (the orchestrator cards them): the
test-side assertion helpers (six sites) could adopt the shared
mapper's `Sql` arm with a documented panic-rich fallback instead of
their local spellings; revisit the wider store-mapper family only if
any of its members ever gains a second copy.

NUL addendum (T-286, 2026-11-22): item 7 is closed by the owner's
ruling (board card «РЕШЕНИЕ: NUL в описании», closed 2026-11-22) —
sanitization, not rejection. A `NUL` (`U+0000`) in the project
DESCRIPTION is silently stripped at the save boundary; the save never
answers `E_VALIDATION` for it. The contrast with the names (D-126)
is deliberate and untouched: a name is file-name and file-content
material (`base_name` derives file names, the heading title is
written verbatim into the target file), so there `NUL` is rejected
outright; a description is inert prose for the stored row, and the
invisible byte is not user intent. The readings this task picked,
recorded before the code:

- _The strip lives in the validator layer_, inside
  `validate_description`
  (crates/eunomia-core/src/project_validators.rs) — not in a command.
  The function now returns the SANITIZED string, the value to persist
  (`validate_name`'s trim precedent: a validator's return is what the
  store keeps), so every future caller — `project_update` (T-279,
  whose card already carries the note), the PRJ-008 modal save, any
  store-level writer — inherits the strip by calling the validator it
  already has to call. `project_add_manual`'s save path routes its
  description through the validator too (the constant `""` today: no
  user description enters at add time — the add flow collects none,
  §7.1), so every COMMAND save boundary passes the validator by
  construction. The store does NOT enforce the strip — D-126's
  posture verbatim: the gate is the validator, not the CHECKs, so a
  store-level writer that bypasses the commands (the `data_sets`
  fixture generator today, with NUL-free literals; the future
  `update` callers) must route the description through
  `validate_description` itself. Round-1 review's P2: the first
  draft claimed "every stored description passed the validator" —
  true only of the command paths, and now said so.
- _Length measures the stored truth_: strip first, then count. The
  ≤1000 limit governs what lands in the column, so 1001 characters
  including one `NUL` save as 1000 (legal), and a 1002-character
  input with one `NUL` is rejected as 1001 — `DescriptionTooLong`'s
  length field reports the post-strip count, so the message talks
  about the description that would be stored, not the one typed.
- _Empty after the strip is legal_ — `"\0\0"` saves as `''`, the same
  legal empty description §6.9's row (no minimum) and §6.2's column
  default already define. The label rules (D-042/D-075) govern
  labels; descriptions keep newlines and every other character.
- _The strip is silent_: no journal entry, no warning, no log line —
  the added row's `project.added` entry is unchanged (it never
  carried the description). The name's rejection stays loud
  (`NameNul`, `E_VALIDATION`): the two policies coexist by ruling.
- _Spec §6.9 grows one sentence_ under the name-`NUL` line (the
  T-250 item-6 pattern): the description is the exception — `NUL` is
  stripped before the length is checked, the visible text kept.
  Without it the row would under-describe the stored truth: a
  spec-alone implementer would store the `NUL` and diverge (the very
  `length()` arithmetic break D-126 recorded).

### D-153 — T-076: the `scan_start`/`scan_cancel` commands and the throttled `scan://progress` event — 2026-11-22

Problem: PRJ-002's scan window needs its backend: two §7.10
commands (`scan_start`, `scan_cancel`) and the `scan://progress`
event (SYS-003/ALG-053: no more than 10 emissions per second,
carrying folders-checked, found, current path), over the landed
walker (`eunomia-fs` `scan.rs`, D-086-era), the classifier
(`scan_classify.rs`, T-075) and the settings store
(`scan.max_depth`/`scan.exclude_names`, D-04/D-05). ERR-002: an
interrupted scan saves nothing. T-077 (`scan_commit`) stays out.

Readings chosen (Rule 1, recorded before implementation):

- **The answer shape.** `scan_start` runs the whole walk (on the
  blocking pool, SYS-001 — the `sync_run` precedent) and answers
  the found/candidate set when it ends: NFR-015's "runs in the
  background, the window stays responsive" is about the UI thread
  (an async command + `spawn_blocking` + progress events), not
  about a detached task — and §7.10's `scan_commit` being a
  SEPARATE command means the answer must carry the result for the
  UI to select from, while ERR-002 means nothing server-side may
  outlive a cancelled call. The outcome is a tagged enum the
  `SyncRunOutcome` way: `Completed { checked, found, repositories,
skipped }` and `Cancelled` — the Cancelled arm carries NO
  payload, structurally: an interrupted scan has no result to show
  and nothing to keep (the walker's docs leave "trust or drop
  events after a Cancelled" to this layer; the answer drops them).
- **The progress payload** is the card's three facts:
  `{ checked, found, current_path }`. `checked` counts every walk
  event (each is one folder the walk made a decision about —
  found, plain, or skipped), `found` counts repository events, and
  `current_path` is the newest event's path (lossy-rendered only
  for the non-UTF-8 skips the walker itself reports — the
  consumer's rendering, per `scan.rs`'s docs).
- **The throttle** is event-driven coalescing with ≥100 ms
  spacing (`PROGRESS_MIN_INTERVAL = 100 ms`, the arithmetic of
  "≤10 per second"): every event updates the coalesced state; an
  emission fires only when no emission happened in the last
  100 ms. There is deliberately NO timer-based and NO
  end-of-walk trailing flush: a forced final emission can land
  < 100 ms after the previous one and break the very bound the
  card pins, and the terminal state lands in the command's ANSWER,
  which supersedes progress the moment the walk ends. While events
  flow, the newest coalesced state reaches the UI within ≤ ~100 ms.
- **The cancel token lifecycle** mirrors D-147's slot shape in a
  dedicated `scan::ScanCancelSlot` (managed in every mode, cleared
  on every exit by a RAII lease, `clear_if_current` by `Arc`
  identity) but collapses D-147's two-step publish into ONE: the
  slot IS the guard — `try_publish` (set-if-empty) decides the
  single live scan, and there is no separate flag whose race the
  second step would reconcile (the walk starts immediately after
  the publication; a cancel latched during the SEC-003/settings
  reads is honored on the walk's first entry check, the same
  missed-cancel window D-147's pre-take publish closes). The token
  is `eunomia_fs::scan::CancelToken` — the walker's own primitive,
  exactly what that crate's docs assigned to "T-076's plumbing";
  the sync token stays a separate latch (no coupling).
- **A second `scan_start` while one is live** answers the
  `E_SYNC_RUNNING` envelope (`sync_running_refusal`): §10's only
  "already running — command rejected — wait until it finishes"
  row, and the closed twenty-code registry (the `errors_tests`
  bindings pin forbids a twenty-first `E_SCAN_RUNNING` literal).
  `scan_cancel` with nothing live is an idempotent `Ok(())` —
  NFR-015's "closing the scan window means cancel" races the
  walk's natural end and must not error in the loser branch.
- **The scan root** goes through `session_paths::validate_ui_path`
  (SEC-003: session-picked or a registered project), whose
  canonical answer is the walk root — the `scan_classify` caller
  obligation (the registry keys and the walked paths must spell
  the identity the same way). Settings (`scan.max_depth` →
  `NonZeroUsize`, `scan.exclude_names`) and the three registry key
  sets (active, archived, exclusions) load in ONE `Db::run` read
  transaction before the walk — the per-scan snapshot rule that
  keeps classification deterministic over the scan's lifetime.
- **Events follow the T-246 capability truth**: `scan://progress`
  is a manual `tauri_specta::Event` impl (the derive macro cannot
  produce the `://` wire name, D-112), emitted from Rust only, and
  the webview subscribes through the existing
  `core:event:allow-listen`/`-unlisten` grant — no capability
  change.
- **Errors**: cancellation is NOT an error (the `Cancelled`
  outcome); failures map to the honest existing codes — the
  SEC-003 `E_VALIDATION` refusal (which is also what a root that
  cannot be RESOLVED meets at that gate: `validate_ui_path` maps
  every unresolvable spelling to the allowlist sentence, T-073's
  recorded behavior), `settings_cell_to_app_error`/
  `projects_store_to_app_error`/`storage_fallback` for store
  reads, the D-037 no-database fallback, and
  `join_failure_to_app_error` — with ONE log edge per failure
  (`logging::scan_start_failed`, D-096) plus the class-only info
  line `logging::scan_cancelled` (the ERR-002 record) and
  `logging::scan_progress_emit_failed` for a refused emission
  (display-only, never fatal to the walk — the answer carries the
  truth). A root that vanishes AFTER the gate is not a command
  failure at all: the walker reports it as an `Access` skip and
  the scan still `Completed` (PRJ-007's rule — the refusal never
  aborts a walk; corrected in the round-1 review).

Solution: `src-tauri/src/scan.rs` (the new module, registered at the
`lib.rs` anchor beside `file_watch`) — the wire DTOs
(`ScanRunOutcome` (tagged `outcome`/camelCase, the `SyncRunOutcome`
shape), `ScannedRepository`, `ScanClassWire`, `ScanSkip`/

pinning `scan://progress`), `ProgressTracker` (the pure

one-mutex accumulator), `ScanCancelSlot` + `ScanLease` (the

(idempotent, missing-state fallback). `lib.rs` registers both

### D-152 — T-267: the watcher's swapped `extra_file_lines` arguments fixed red-first, and the fourth content-build copy joined onto the shared pass — 2026-11-22

Problem: two halves on one card. (1) D-145's round-1 P1, pre-existing

with `extra_file_lines`'s two `ExtraFile` arguments swapped
(local-then-project instead of the contract's project-then-local,
§7.5's tie order) — a correctly synced scheme-A project with extras
at differing positions read `ExternalChanged` forever, and nothing

ipc fixture seeds the options off. (2) The same file carried the

- Every other caller audited against the signature
  (`base_name, extra_project, extra_local`): production —

Rule-1 reading recorded before the migration (the seam question):
the shared pass genuinely lacked a BODIES seam. Everything public in

or verdicts, but the watcher's ALG-033 verdict consumes the RAW §9.2

String)>` — the sequential whole-snapshot BODIES pass, the exact

### D-154 — T-270: the mock layer's loud-drift rule written as the entry the dangling "D-141" citations promised, the three citations re-pointed — 2026-11-22

Problem: three live citations pointed at "D-141" — a number the
counter never issued and no entry ever carried (D-142's round-1 P2-1,
carded as the T-256 follow-up): D-115's scope note ("the D-141
loud-drift rule"), D-138's mock-layer-deviation bullet ("D-141's
loud-drift layer"), and the mock module header (`src/ipc/mock/commands.ts` 6,
"see DECISIONS.md D-141"). A reader following any of
the three landed on nothing: the design the citations promised
existed only as prose inside D-108 and the code comments. The same
gap class T-287 closed by restoring D-071/D-072; closed here by
writing the missing record under a fresh number.

Solution (T-270): the loud-drift rule, recorded as its citation sites
use it — the Rust command surface and the frontend mock layer cannot
drift apart silently, by composed pins on both sides:

- _The Rust half._ `export_bindings_are_up_to_date`
  (src-tauri/src/lib.rs 705–724, D-034) re-exports the specta
  bindings inside `cargo test` and compares the fresh output
  (EOL-normalized) with the committed `src/bindings.ts` embedded at
  compile time: a changed contract without regeneration is red on the
  developer's first run (the same run regenerates the file), and CI —
  which compiles the committed file before any export — stays red
  until the regenerated bindings are committed. The per-command
  registration pins in `ipc_tests.rs` (each asserts its own
  `commands::*` line present exactly once, the D-034 wiring-pin
  rationale) guard the registry itself: a registration dropped and
  the regeneration committed would leave the export check green
  while the command quietly vanished from the wire.
- _The frontend half._ `src/ipc/mock/commands.ts` implements every
  generated command as one object annotated with the derived
  `IpcCommands` type (`typeof commands`, src/ipc/contract.ts 14): a
  regenerated `bindings.ts` carrying a new command fails
  `pnpm run typecheck` until a mock member with the exact signature
  exists — the citation sites' own wording ("every bindings command
  needs a mock or `pnpm run typecheck` fails", D-115's scope note).
  A REMOVED command fires the same boundary from the other side (the
  annotation flags the now-extra member), so the mock can neither lag
  nor outrun the real surface.
- _Why "loud"._ The pins compose into one chain: a contract change →
  the Rust pin red until regeneration → the regenerated `bindings.ts`
  → the frontend typecheck red until the mock member lands (the
  first exercise: T-078's exclusions commands demanded their mocks at
  the T-141 rebase, D-108). Skipping a step anywhere turns a test
  red — drift is announced, never absorbed. This is the rule the
  mock header alludes to as "the same loud-drift rule the bindings
  tests pin on the Rust side" — plural, because the export check and
  the registration pins together own the Rust half.
- _The reader-facing complements._ `src/ipc/mode.spec.ts`'s
  shipped-set test lists every mock member by name: a command the
  type annotation forced into the mock also fails this explicit list
  until it is pinned there (the one-line list extension D-138's
  bullet records). D-108 carries the prose version of the rule; this
  entry is the citable home both kinds of citation can point at.

Numbering note: the three citations predate this entry and were
hand-made — git attributes the commands.ts one to the mock layer's
own creation commit (`87ed97b`, T-141) and the DECISIONS.md ones to
T-080 (`2032910`, D-115's scope note) and T-118 (`74cf781`, D-138's
bullet); no counter issuance ever stood behind the number. The
collision surfaced when task-id-mcp issued 141 for D-142 (T-256):
that entry took the next issued number per the counter policy, 141
stayed burned, and the follow-up card asked for this entry under a
fresh number. task-id-mcp issued 154 at the moment of writing; the
three citations are re-pointed to this entry, nothing was renumbered,
and D-142's numbering note keeps quoting the old number as history.

Honest boundaries: this entry records the rule and its pins, it pins
nothing new in code; the mock's behavioral LIMITS (D-108's deliberate
approximations, the module header's list) are a different subject —
the loud-drift rule is about the command SURFACE (every command
mocked, exact signature), not about each mock's fidelity, and the
citation contexts (the D-115 scope note, the D-138 freeze deviation)
were exactly that surface.

Checks (docs pass; the only non-md change is one comment line in
`src/ipc/mock/commands.ts`): tests waived under the md-only ruling
as the card extends it to the one comment line; `pnpm lint`,
`pnpm run typecheck` and `pnpm run format:check` green by exit code;
the acceptance grep over tracked content (`git grep -n "D-141" --
'*.md' '*.ts'`) returns only historical quotations — D-142's
follow-ups paragraph, its numbering note, its orchestrator addendum,
and this note's own history.

`.opencode/reviews/t270-round1.md`, deepseek-v4.1-flash — verdict

been attributed here to D-116's scope note, but the scope note lives

### D-156 — T-280: the bounded wait for mutation-initiated watch refreshes — the add's watch refresh can no longer hang the interactive answer on a stuck mount — 2026-11-22

Problem: D-144's round-1 P3-4 (this card). `project_add_manual`'s
committed arm awaits ONE FULL pass through `refresh_after_sync`;
a pass stuck on a dead network mount (a stat that never returns)
hangs the interactive answer with it. D-144's honest-boundaries
sentence called the exposure not-new — the flow's own write-access
probe touches the same folder first — but the probe touches ONE
file while the pass probes EVERY available project's folder:
strictly wider exposure than any other step of that flow, and the
one place a UX answer waits on hardware the command never chose.
(The flow's older unbounded awaits — the path canonicalize, the
git-root walk, the write-access probe — stay D-144's recorded
boundary; this card bounds the refresh pass the card names.)

Readings recorded BEFORE coding (rule 1):

- _The budget: a named 10-second constant beside the seam, not a
  config key._ `MUTATION_REFRESH_BUDGET = Duration::from_secs(10)`
  in `file_watch.rs` (§5.8/D-129's constants-not-config ruling for
  this class). The value sits an order of magnitude above every
  healthy pass's worst case — a full pass is local-fs work (one DB
  transaction, per project a stat, a symlink resolution, one file
  read and an in-memory build, per wanted directory one stat and a
  watch syscall), milliseconds per project and sub-second for
  hundreds — so a loaded machine cannot trip a false degrade,
  while 10 s is still inside the interactive-patience band where
  the user reads the answer rather than retries. The budget bounds
  ONLY the refresh region: the write-access probe before it (which
  can itself stall seconds on a dying disk) is not counted.
- _The degrade: the walk continues in the background, never
  cancelled._ On expiry the caller returns and the Refresh command
  stays exactly where it was: if the bus accepted it, the service
  task runs the pass whenever it becomes free and its completion
  ack fires into a dropped receiver (the existing `let _ =
done.try_send` — the at-least-once discipline needs no ack
  consumer); if the bus was FULL, the send future was dropped and
  the command never enqueued — that refresh is honestly abandoned,
  and convergence rides the anchor set (every full pass re-derives
  the watch set from the project table, D-144's idempotent
  convergence; the next availability change, debounced event, sync
  or mutation re-derives it without loss). Cancelling the walk
  (a cancel seam the sync pipeline's runs have, D-147) is rejected:
  the watch pass has no cancel seam, and killing it would forfeit
  convergence the service can still deliver — for an ADD the
  verdict inputs the user just created matter, the D-144 shape.
- _The other callers keep the unbounded wait._ `refresh_after_sync`
  is unchanged for the sync pipeline (D-138's never-fatal
  aftermath) and the seam's own tests: the pipeline's phases 1 and
  3 already read and write the SAME folders, so a mount hung enough
  to hang the aftermath pass would have hung the phases long
  before it — bounding only the aftermath protects nothing there
  and would add a timeout class to `sync_run_degraded`'s
  vocabulary. The mutation seam is a TWIN sharing the same
  command/ack core (`Command::Refresh` with a done sender — one
  refresh path, two wait policies), not a second refresh path.
- _The timer is the already-present tokio `time` feature._
  `tokio::time::timeout` (verified in the installed tokio 1.54.1
  sources, `src/time/timeout.rs:86`) — tokio 1 with only `time` is
  already a direct dependency of the app crate (D-054's retention
  tick), so no new crate or feature crosses rule 9. The bounded
  region wraps the send AND the recv: a full bus (64 queued
  commands behind a hung pass) backpressures `send().await`, and
  bounding only the ack would leave the unbounded path this card
  exists to kill. Cancellation safety holds — mpsc send/recv are
  cancel-safe; a send dropped mid-await either enqueued the value
  or did not, and both states are correct under the anchor
  discipline above.
- _The test knob is the managed state's budget field._
  `FileWatchState::with_budget(Duration)` (production `new()`
  delegates with the constant — the DEBOUNCE-parameter precedent:
  a parameter exists only so tests can run short windows) carried
  on the managed state because the command under test takes no
  parameters; the injection point must be reachable from the app.
- _The degrade's diagnostics stay silent in this card._ No log
  line is added (SEC-008 trivially holds): the add-flow refresh
  warn is T-278's card, not absorbed here. The expiry answers the
  caller with the `send_error()` family's class-only shape —
  `DbLocked` + `os_kind: "FileWatchTimeout"` (mirroring
  `FileWatchGone`'s D-037 shape) — a THIRD class beside the
  refused seam and the pass failure; whether T-278's line covers
  all three classes is that card's decision (recorded as a
  follow-up note below).

Solution — the seam, in `file_watch.rs` beside its twin:

- `MUTATION_REFRESH_BUDGET` (the const above) and
  `FileWatchState::with_budget` (the knob; `new()` delegates with
  the const — the constructor is NOT test-only code, so no cfg
  marker). `refresh_after_sync`'s body is factored into two
  private helpers both seams share — `send_refresh_command` (the
  `Refresh` with its ack onto the bus) and `await_ack` (the
  receive) — so the twin differs from its sibling in exactly ONE
  thing: `tokio::time::timeout(budget, send-then-ack)`, with the
  expiry answering `mutation_refresh_timeout()` (the class-only
  error). `project_add_manual`'s committed arm calls the twin; the
  sync pipeline's aftermath (`sync_run_with`) and the seam tests
  keep `refresh_after_sync` verbatim. Docs updated in the same
  change (Rule 11): the module docs' mutation bullet, the twin's
  and `Command::Refresh`'s docs, the add command's step-6 doc and
  inline comment (which still called `logging.rs` a frozen zone —
  stale since D-155), the service-loop and `logging.rs`
  pass-failure docs (the "add flow's line" now names T-278's card
  and both awaited seams), `ARCHITECTURE.md`'s watcher paragraph,
  and the regenerated `src/bindings.ts` (the command-doc drift the
  export test's loud-drift chain forces, D-003/D-144 — the test
  was red until the regenerated file was staged, by design).

Tests: 2 unit pins in `file_watch.rs` (the budget IS the recorded
ten seconds; `new()` defaults to the constant and `with_budget`
overrides it) + 4 ipc tests in `ipc_tests.rs`:

- the seam's degrade: a parked receiver (the bus accepts commands,

- the bound's edge: the same parked world with the bus PRE-FILLED

- the no-false-degrade half: the real service over the production

- the headline scenario end to end: the real `project_add_manual`
