### D-157 — T-138: the assignment-toggle save benchmark — §12.2's third budget row measured through the store's own `reassign`, the alternation keeping every iteration a real write — 2026-11-22

Problem: T-138 turns §15.1's Load row toward §12.2's third budget
row — "Saving an assignment toggle (p95, set L): no more than 50 ms"
(spec §12.2's table). Open points: what the store write behind a
toggle even is (the `assignment_set` IPC command, T-097, is not
landed — a grep of `src-tauri/src/commands.rs` finds no assignment
surface); what one iteration honestly measures given `reassign`'s
verified no-write no-op on the held variant; which pair to toggle on
set L; whether this bench needs a mirror/tripwire like the read-side
benches; and how the row's p95 framing maps onto criterion's
mean/median report.

Solution: `benches/eunomia-load` gains its third bench target,
`assignment_toggle`, on the D-135/D-145 discipline: no new
dependencies (criterion `=0.8.2` minimal already pinned), the
harness measures the store's own code — no mirror to keep honest.

- _The write measured._ The store half of §7.10's `assignment_set`
  is `library::reassign` (`crates/eunomia-store/src/library.rs`):
  read the current row by the composite key, DB-012's
  active-sibling verification, the `UPDATE project_instructions`
  variant flip with the `updated_at` restamp (one autocommit
  transaction over the fixture's WAL/`synchronous=FULL` connection —
  NFR-007's fsync is inside the measured cost), the stored row read
  back. No STOP: the store HAS the toggle-shaped write (a real
  UPDATE, not delete+insert); no store API was added or changed. The
  command's `action_log` entry and event emit are the IPC layer's
  (T-097) and are cut here — the same seam D-135 cut for the two
  read rows; the store function itself writes no journal row, so
  nothing else is being skipped.
- _One iteration = ONE real save._ `reassign` naming the held
  variant is a verified no-write no-op (pinned in the store's own
  suite), so a fixed A→B target would measure the no-op from the
  second iteration on. The harness `AssignmentToggle` alternates
  A→B→A… — every measured iteration performs the real write path.
  Two `LoadError` variants joined the harness boundary: `Library`
  carrying the store's error, and `TogglePremise` carrying a
  `PremiseHalf` discriminator (missing shape / no assignment /
  variant mismatch) plus the held and promised ids — the refusal
  names its cause without free text (rule 8).
- _The pair._ The generator's own first: project ordinal 0, `k=0` →
  instruction ordinal 0, initial variant ordinal 0 (D-109's closed
  form at the origin — scale-independent, so the pins run on a
  4-project fixture while the bench itself runs `data_sets::L`). The
  flip target is the instruction's second variant, an active sibling
  by construction. `AssignmentToggle::new` verifies the premise in
  setup only — never inside a measured iteration.
- _No mirror, no tripwire._ Unlike the two read-side benches (born
  mirroring production compositions), this iteration IS the store's
  own call — the D-145 direct-to-core posture applied to a store
  write, so there is no mirrored constant or spelling to pin by
  source-scan. What needs guarding is the bench's own premise, and
  `tests/assignment_toggle_pins.rs` does: the premise (the first
  pair holds the generator's variant ordinal 0; the sibling
  differs), the typed refusal after an external move names both ids,
  the alternation verified through `get_assignment` on the database
  (never the toggle's return alone), and the no-op diagnostic
  targeting the truly held variant (byte-identical row, no restamp —
  a desynced target would be a real flip and differ in `variant_id`
  and `updated_at`). All mutation-verified red: the four
  original pins by this task's three mutations plus round-1's
  independent six-mutation table, the two round-2 refusal pins by
  round-2's two targeted mutations (each failing only its intended
  arm's pin).
- _Measurements (bench profile, this 8-core box, 14 GiB free,
  fixture DB under tmpfs — D-135's condition; numbers re-run on the
  delivered revision after the round-1 fixes)._ The bench sets its
  own sample size (100) and measurement time (20 s per benchmark);
  those programmatic settings override criterion's CLI flags, so the
  "bounded" check run was the full measurement.
  `assignment_toggle/save_set_L`: **64.290 µs** [63.691, 64.937],
  100 samples (318,150 collected iterations); the per-iteration
  distribution read off the recorded sample data: p50 63.1 µs,
  **p95 68.8 µs**, max 84.5 µs — the worst observed iteration sits
  ~590× below the 50 ms budget, so the row is inside it on this
  machine at p95 too.
  `assignment_toggle/noop_same_variant_set_L`: **9.623 µs**
  [9.429, 9.828], p95 11.5 µs. The no-op path is the current-row
  read plus the early return — the store checks DB-012 only _after_
  that return — so the diagnostic is ~15 % of the save, and the
  residual ~55 µs is DB-012's verify read + UPDATE + commit +
  read-back (round-1 review's P3-2 relabelling). Honest boundaries:
  criterion's console report is mean/median/CI, the p95/max above
  come from the recorded sample data of this run, not the report —
  and neither is the reference machine: the §15.5 rerun (D-135's
  open gate, now covering three rows) stays the confirmation; the
  tmpfs fixture makes the per-commit fsync cheap, so an SSD-backed
  data directory shows a higher per-save floor; and the number is
  the STORE half — the full save path (command transaction +
  `action_log` insert + emit, T-097) lands above it by the journal
  write's cost.

Testing: the six assignment-toggle pins (four born with the bench,
the two refusal-arm pins added by the round-1 review's P3-3) join
the six mirror pins and the profile unit test in `cargo test
--workspace` (1709 passed workspace-wide, zero failures); the bench
itself ran green with the numbers above. ARCHITECTURE.md's workspace
tree and the crate description now name the third bench (rule 11).

Follow-ups: when T-097 lands `assignment_set`, its composition
(store write + journal entry in one transaction) should be measured
against this row or the bench extended to compose it; the §15.5
reference-machine rerun now covers all three §12.2 budget rows this
crate measures.

### D-158 — T-104: the watcher-test card closed as a gap analysis — four unpinned §5.7 transitions given their tests (the real-pipeline T-F13 half, SYS-009's recreation clearing, SYS-007's archive removal, SYS-008's both-flags world) — 2026-11-22

Problem: T-104 is an original-plan-era card ("write the watcher
tests: T-F13 and the state transitions") that assumed the watcher
would land without them; in the actual history T-102 (D-137) landed
the watcher WITH its battery, and T-103/T-259/T-260/T-262
(D-139/D-146/D-148/D-155) extended it. The card's first job was the
gap analysis: map every §5.7 requirement onto the landed tests and
close only what is genuinely unpinned. The mapping (requirement →
existing pin): the T-F13 flag/display half + the SIMULATED
next-sync clearing →
`an_external_edit_marks_the_project_externally_modified_without_writing_anything`;
deletion vs never-synced →
`deleting_a_synced_target_file_reports_target_deleted…`; the
verdict battery (A/B/C, body/marker/outside edits, broken markers,
non-UTF-8, CRLF, pre-existing files) → the 15-test unit battery in
`file_watch.rs`; the debounce/wire literals → the two literal pins;
startup computation →
`projects_list_carries_the_watch_service_verdicts_from_its_snapshot`;
unavailable→unwatch→rewatch →
`an_unavailable_project_is_unwatched_until_its_folder_returns`;
SYS-010 in full → the D-139/D-148/D-155 batteries; the
overwrite+backup write itself → the sync battery
(`sync_run_with_confirm_empty…`, phase-3's creation case). FOUR
transitions had no pin anywhere:

1. T-F13's second sentence through the REAL pipeline — the clearing
   was proven only on a simulated sync, and no `sync_run` test ever
   ran with the watch service live (the `sync_app` doc's "the one
   test that wants a converging refresh spawns the real service
   itself" was aspirational since T-118: no test in that section
   ever called `spawn_service`).
2. SYS-009's second half — the deleted→recreated-by-next-sync→hint-
   clears transition (the batteries stop at the flag being SET).
3. SYS-007's third removal rule — archived→watch-removed (only the
   record-level prune and the carrier row rule were pinned; the
   watch-set removal and its silence never were).
4. SYS-008's last sentence (DB-021) — the both-flags world ("dirty,
   externally modified, or both"): no test ever showed both flags on
   one row.

Solution: four tests + six helpers in `ipc_tests.rs` (watch section;
the `sync_watch_app` harness is the shared body `sync_app` now
delegates to), no production change — every seam the tests need
already existed:

- _`sync_watch_app` / `synced_world_between_syncs`_ — the sync
  battery's app widened with `projects_list` and the watch command
  bus returned UNSPAWNED: the service must go live before any
  `sync_run`, because the run awaits `refresh_after_sync`'s ack and
  that await has NO budget (a held-but-unconsumed receiver is the
  D-137 session-history hang; `sync_app` avoids it only by dropping
  the receiver). The fixture builds T-F13's "between syncs" world
  with a REAL first run — file, hash, stamps — under the live
  watcher, settles past the debounce, and returns the whole file the
  run left; the callers compare the MANAGED BLOCK only
  (`split_written_target`), because cross-run byte equality is
  deliberately NOT the oracle: every run writes its own ALG-032
  marker timestamp (SYNC_MARKER's "the timestamp never decides").

### D-159 — T-139: the sync-pipeline and scan benchmarks — §12.2's two missing budget rows measured through the real seams (the composed §9.4 core over 100 ten-KB projects; the walk engine over a 101 100-folder tree) — 2026-11-22

Problem: T-139 turns §15.1's Load row toward the two §12.2 budget
rows no bench measures yet — "Sync of 100 projects, files up to
10 KB, SSD: no more than 10 s" and "Scan of 100,000 folders on an
SSD: no more than 30 s; UI input response no more than 100 ms".
Rule 1, the mapping recorded before coding: of §12.2's eight rows,
three are already owned by this crate — the build row (D-135
`project_build`), the dirty row (D-135 `dirty_recalc`), the toggle
row (D-157 `assignment_toggle`) — and are NOT duplicated; four are
not criterion-benchable at all (startup-to-window, matrix scrolling,
RSS, and the scan row's "UI input response" half: UI/e2e-script
territory, §15.1's other half); the two NEW rows are the sync
pipeline's and the scan walk's. The open points: what the sync row
can even measure without the app shell (the §9.4 phase machinery
lives in src-tauri, and the bench crate cannot depend on the app
crate — D-145's recorded fact); what keeps a sync iteration off the
no-op path (a second sync with no changes is all-`unchanged`, D-24);
what the scan row's honest fixture is (no generator produces a
100 000-folder tree — D-109's `TempRepos` maxes out at the project
count); and which scan settings the walk runs under.

Solution: two new bench targets in `benches/eunomia-load`
(`sync_pipeline`, `scan_walk`), no new dependencies (criterion
`=0.8.2` minimal already pinned), the harness measuring real code
only — every per-step mechanic is the production seam function the
src-tauri phases call.

- _The sync row's measurable core._ The src-tauri phases orchestrate
  store transactions and app state AROUND per-step work that lives in
  `eunomia-fs`/`eunomia-core`; the bench composes that per-step work
  in §9.4's own phase order: phase 0's pure half (one ALG-001
  snapshot read transaction + `content_build::build_projects`), then
  per project in `sort_order` the seven preflight steps
  (`check_project_available`, `resolve_target_path`, the regular-file
  gate, `check_write_access`, the existing file's read, the scheme
  branch, `remove_stale_tmp_files`), the free-space tail
  (`check_backup_space` over `free_bytes(data_dir)`), phase 2's
  `backup_target_file` per ready project with an existing file, and
  phase 3's `write_target_file` (§9.5's whole pipeline: staging file,
  fsync, rename, directory fsync, re-read, digest verify, with
  production's own free-space closure over the target's folder). The
  scheme branch is honest per scheme: A/C compare through
  `contents_match` against the markerless whole-file basis; B splices
  the NEW managed text into the file just read through the REAL
  `assembly_b::splice` — the written bytes and the comparison basis
  in one builder (the file is unchanged when the resplice reproduces
  its bytes: a decision identical to phase 1's markerless ALG-033
  rule on this fixture, whose marker line is a constant, and
  STRICTER in general — a differently-stamped marker would take the
  write path, so the formulation cannot understate the row), so no
  `splice_without_marker` mirror is needed
  (src-tauri's phase 1 has one; this composition does not). TWO
  ALG-030 spellings the pass DOES mirror over an already-built
  managed text — the whole-file tail (production `sync_phase3`'s own
  `whole_file`, pinned against the real `build_content` builder's
  output, the D-130 pattern) and the markerless comparison basis
  (pinned behaviourally by the all-unchanged second pass). Cut and
  documented (the crate docs'
  seam list): the run bookkeeping — `sync_runs`/`sync_run_projects`
  rows, the `sync_running` flag, phase 3's per-project `last_synced`
  commit (a store UPDATE at D-157's measured ~65 µs; hundredths of a
  percent of the row's 10 s), the `backup_records` rows and the
  BKP-010 dedup lookup (the alternation makes every copy a fresh
  digest, so `Created` is the outcome either way), §9.4 phase 1
  step 6's D-25 confirmation list (the fixture's builds are never
  empty — the branch is unreachable and costless), and phase 4 whole
  (retention, journal, verdicts) — with the per-iteration backup
  sweep standing in for retention so copies do not accumulate.
- _The alternation (iteration reading)._ One measured iteration is
  one full pipeline pass; the no-op path exists and would poison it,
  so the harness flips ONE assignment per project between iterations
  — project `p`'s `k = 0` pair by D-109's closed form (instruction
  `(37·p) mod I`, variant `p mod V` → sibling), the D-157 trick
  scaled to every project — inside criterion's `iter_batched` SETUP
  (excluded from timing), together with the backups sweep. The
  premise is verified per project at fixture construction through
  the store's own read (typed `TogglePremise` refusals) and pinned
  recomputed-by-hand. The `fs_phases_100_projects` diagnostic runs
  the same pass over setup-built content, splitting the row's cost
  between the store/build half and the fs half (the D-121/D-135
  breakdown pattern).
- _The fixture._ `SYNC_100_PROJECTS_10KB`: 100 projects at set L's
  density (200 assignments each over L's library shape) — the
  generator's §12.2 sizing builds each managed text at ≈10 KB (the
  row's "files up to 10 KB"; the pin's band is 8–12 KB, the exact
  sizes deterministic). Scheme-B targets start as hand-planted
  marker-pair seed files (SYS-009: a missing B target is a skip, not
  a creation — pinned), so the B branch splices into a real marked
  file; one unmeasured priming pass then writes every target. The
  ALG-032 marker line is a fixture constant (the comparison drops
  it); each pass's `BackupTime` advances one second (fresh
  `create_new` copy names — a collision would be a `CopyFailed`).
- _The scan row._ `scan_repositories` itself — the ALG-050..054
  walker with its per-entry cancel checks, its `.git` probe, its
  exclude-name skips, `min(4, cores)` threads — over a generated
  tree (`ScanTree`): a pyramid of 100 groups × 10 subgroups × 10
  leaves × 9 children = 101 100 folders below the root (≥ the row's
  100 000 floor), the 1 000 subgroups planted as repositories (a
  `.git` directory each — the probe's form), depth 4 within the
  §6.5 default `max_depth` of 6, walked under the §6.5 default
  settings — wired from the SETTINGS REPOSITORY's own
  `SettingKey::default_value()` (the spec table's seven-name
  exclusion list with `.git` on it, pinned against the spec
  literals: exclusion stops descent, not detection, so the 1 000
  `.git` folders surface as excluded skips while their parents are
  found — 102 101 events, every directory exactly one). The walk is
  read-only: every iteration does identical full work — no no-op
  path, no alternation needed (the honest difference from the sync
  pass, stated in the bench docs). The callback only counts
  (checked/found); the surroundings cut are the command layer's —
  the `scan://progress` throttle (its per-event mutex and clock
  check), the cancel slot, the SEC-003 root gate, and the ALG-053
  classification of found repositories
  (`scan_classify::classify_entry`, T-075's module with its own
  tests) — D-153's layer, measured there by its own tests.
- _Measurements (bench profile, this 8-core box, ~20 GiB available,
  fixture DB and tree under tmpfs — D-135's standing condition; the
  programmatic settings — sample size 10, 1 s warm-up, 20 s
  measurement per benchmark — override criterion's CLI flags, so
  the check run WAS the full measurement, the D-157 posture; the
  numbers below are the FINAL-TREE run, after every round-1 fix)._
  `sync_pipeline/full_pass_100_projects`: **149.95 ms** [141.29,
  158.63], 10 samples, 165 collected iterations — inside the
  ≤ 10 s budget by ~67×. `sync_pipeline/fs_phases_100_projects`:
  **25.634 ms** [24.191, 26.428] — the fs half (preflight + backups
  - atomic writes) is ~17 % of the pass; the store/build half
    (snapshot read + `build_projects` over 100 projects/20 000
    assignments) owns ~124 ms, the same attribution D-121/D-135 made
    for the read-side rows. `scan_walk/walk_100k_folders`:
    **336.81 ms** [330.72, 344.33], 10 samples, 110 collected
    iterations — inside the ≤ 30 s budget by ~89×. Run-to-run spread
    on this non-isolated box across the task's three full runs:
    the full pass 150–162 ms, the fs half 22.5–25.6 ms, the walk
    337–412 ms — every budget verdict unchanged throughout (the
    spread, not a code change, is why the walk once read 412 ms;
    criterion's own change detection calls the final-vs-first walk
    delta "improved" and the full-pass delta "no change"). The row's
    "SSD" premise versus the tmpfs fixture is the standing honest
    condition: fsync-backed costs on a real SSD run higher, and the
    §15.5 reference-machine rerun (D-135's open gate) now covers all
    five rows this crate measures. No optimization was needed or
    performed.

Testing: nine new pins join the crate's suite in `cargo test
--workspace` (1724 passed workspace-wide, zero failures). The six
sync pins (`tests/sync_pipeline_pins.rs`): the premise recomputed
by hand through the store's read; the row profile's ≈10 KB sizes;
the alternation flip-and-restore (build hashes, every project);
D-24's acceptance through the composed pass (a no-flip second pass
is all-unchanged, zero copies — the no-op path the alternation
exists to exclude); the flipped pass's shape (all ready, all backed
up, all written, and the written bytes equal the REAL builders'
output — `build_content` over an independently built body for A/C,
the seed literal's preserved outside plus the built managed text
for B); and SYS-009 (a missing B target skipped, not created). The
three scan pins (`tests/scan_walk_pins.rs`): the builder's
arithmetic against an independent `std::fs` directory census; the
real scan of a small tree (completion, every planted repository,
the exact event count); and the row tree's floor/shape/default
literals. All mutation-verified red-then-green: the closed form
drifted (→ premise refused, pin red), the alternation no-op'd (→
red), the whole-file tail's blank line dropped (→ the
`build_content` oracle red), the missing-B arm fabricating a seed
(→ red), the tree's `.git` not planted (→ census and found-count
red), the folder arithmetic off by one (→ all three scan pins red).
Frozen zones untouched (`src-tauri/src/commands.rs`, `logging.rs`,
`file_watch.rs`, `crates/eunomia-fs/tests/watcher.rs`); no
production code changed at all — the whole diff lives in the bench
crate, DECISIONS.md and ARCHITECTURE.md.

Follow-ups: the §15.5 reference-machine rerun now covers five rows;
the sync row's store half would move if the `assignment_set`/run
bookkeeping composition ever lands in a benchable layer (T-097's
card already carries the neighbouring note from D-157); the scan
row's "UI input response ≤ 100 ms" half stays with the e2e scripts
(§15.1's other half, untouched by any task so far).

### D-160 — CI 45120662560: two platform-assumption test bugs — the refusal plan and the progress prefix now spell paths the way production resolves them — 2026-11-22

Problem: CI run 45120662560 (push 837dc8f..a2ba5d8): test-matrix
green on ubuntu-latest, red on macos-15, macos-15-intel and
windows-latest — exactly two tests on all three legs (both green
locally on ubuntu):

1. `file_watch::tests::a_limit_refused_target_flows_through_the_real_pass_to_the_gate_and_notice` (T-262/D-155's composite proof)
   panicked at the pre-fix file_watch.rs:1907 — `left: {}` against
   `right: {"limited": Limit}`: the SYS-010 seam's unwatched map came
   back EMPTY, the synthetic limit refusal never fired.
2. `scan_tests::a_completed_scan_answers_the_four_classes_and_writes_nothing` (T-076) panicked at the pre-fix scan_tests.rs:593 —
   `payload.current_path.starts_with(root.to_string_lossy().as_ref())`
   failed.

Diagnosis — both are TEST platform-assumption bugs; production was
verified correct, no production defect:

1. The composite proof builds `TargetWatcher::with_backend(RefusingBackend)`
   (the pre-fix :1896-1899), so the REAL notify
   backend never runs and D-148's refusal classification (the stat
   pre-check, notify's kind mapping — notify's windows.rs:557-564,
   inotify.rs:451-457) is NOT in play: the fake refuses iff its plan
   set CONTAINS the directory `set_files` hands it (file_watch.rs
   `RefusingBackend::watch`, :1830-1843). The plan was seeded with
   the RAW tempdir path (`limited_root.clone()`), but the real pass
   names watch dirs through the §9.4 resolution's canonical
   spelling: `blocking_half` → `target_of` (file_watch.rs:920-926) →
   `resolve_target_path` canonicalizes the root first (paths.rs:1235
   through `canonicalize_raw` = `dunce::canonicalize`, :1359-1371;
   that function's own doc :1229-1231 names the macOS
   `/var` = `/private/var` temp-fixture case), the absent target is
   the lexical join under the canonical root (paths.rs:1330-1333),
   and `wanted_dirs` hands `backend.watch` the canonical root
   (watcher.rs:853-864, the call at :610). On macOS the tempdir
   lives behind the `/var` symlink (`dunce::canonicalize` IS std
   `fs::canonicalize` on unix — dunce-1.0.5/src/lib.rs:65-76 —
   realpath resolves to `/private/var/…`); on Windows the resolved
   final form (std canonicalize is GetFinalPathNameByHandleW; dunce
   lib.rs:79-86 strips the `\\?\` prefix where safe) need not equal
   the env spelling of the tempdir — the exact divergence was not
   observed verbatim, only that the raw-vs-canonical comparisons
   failed on that leg too (see Honest boundaries). `plan.contains(dir)` is
   then false → no refusal → the empty map. On ubuntu `/tmp` is a
   real directory: canonical == raw, the strings match — exactly
   why the ubuntu leg and local runs were green.
2. The scan walks the CANONICAL root by contract (scan.rs:39-45:
   the SEC-003 check "returns the CANONICAL form, which becomes the
   walk root"), and the test already feeds the canonical form to
   the picker (the pre-fix :474, now scan_tests.rs:482, the
   a19fe45 discipline) with
   every other assertion built on canonical fixtures (`repo_under`
   and `git_file_under` return canonical, :177-190 — which is why
   the by_path and skip assertions PASSED on the failing legs).
   Only the progress assertion compared against the RAW `root`
   spelling — a plain string prefix check cannot match
   `/private/var/…` against `/var/…` (or Windows' resolved form
   against the short-named spelling).

Solution — a19fe45's class, Project Rules 3 (expectations built
with the project's own `eunomia_fs::paths::canonicalize`, never the
raw tempdir spelling):

1. file_watch.rs: the plan is seeded with
   `canonicalize(&limited_root)` — the fake refuses the dir under
   the spelling the pass actually names. This is fixture CONFIG,
   not the oracle: the oracle assertions (the id-keyed map with its
   class, one episode for a standing refusal, the notice
   read-back, the healed pass clearing everything) are untouched.
2. scan_tests.rs: `walk_root = canonicalize(&root)` once, used both
   for the pick and as the progress prefix expectation, which also
   gains a failure message naming both spellings (the red run
   printed only the bare assertion text).

Falsifiability (Rule 4; mutations observed red, then reverted):
discarding the refusal-CLASS RECORDING in `set_files`' Err arm
makes the composite proof fail at its map assertion
(`{"limited": Other}` against `{"limited": Limit}` — the class
flow is pinned); poisoning `ProgressTracker::on_event`'s `current_path` with a prefix outside
the root makes the scan test fail naming both paths. (A first
scan-mutation attempt through `Path::join` was ineffective — `join`
with an absolute path REPLACES the base; redone as string
concatenation.)

Honest boundaries: macOS/Windows cannot be executed here. The
mechanism is proven from sources (dunce lib.rs cited; std
canonicalize semantics; the project's own docs at paths.rs:1229-1231
and scan.rs:39-45) and, for the scan test, by the controlled
comparison inside it (the canonically-built by_path/skip assertions
passed on the failing legs while the raw-built prefix failed); the
file_watch proof rests on the traced pass chain plus the identical
empty-map red on all three legs. The exact Windows spelling
divergence was not observed verbatim (the old assertion printed no
values; the run log carries no temp path): what is proven is that
both raw-vs-canonical comparisons failed on every non-ubuntu leg
while the canonical-built assertions passed — the divergence family
(resolved form vs env spelling) follows from std/dunce semantics
and a19fe45's recorded Windows class, and the fix is identity-based
(every expectation built through the project's own canonicalize),
so it does not depend on the exact mechanism. The three platform
legs' green is CI's to confirm on the merge push. No gating was
introduced (no `#[cfg]`, no `#[ignore]`)
and no assertion weakened: on ubuntu both assertions are exactly as
strong as before (canonical == raw there); on the failing legs they
change from always-red to checking the real contract. Swept for
siblings: scan_tests.rs holds no other raw-root comparison (every
other pick/assertion already goes through the canonical helpers);
file_watch.rs has the one `with_backend` fake.

Checks: `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2 cargo fmt --check`,
`CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2 cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets
-- -D warnings`, and `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2 cargo test --workspace` —

### D-161 — T-288: the store-mapper family's second-copy rule — any member's duplicate triggers a family revisit, a member is consolidated only on its own second copy, the trigger a review finding one — 2026-11-23

Problem: D-149's second follow-up card (that entry's orchestrator
addendum tracked two cards; this is the store-mapper-family one,
follow-up T-264). T-264 consolidated the sync-run error mapper
family only; the honest-boundaries ruling deliberately left the
other store-table mappers where they live. D-149 recorded the
deferral and the trigger only as prose inside its own entry —
nothing operative: no rule statement a review is bound to and no
mechanism — so the deferral lives or dies with a reader's attention
to one paragraph, and a future task or review could still read
D-149 as "the family awaits consolidation" and finish the job over
members no duplication justifies — premature consolidation is
speculation (structure for structure's sake, the same doctrine
that kept D-149 from creating a two-entry mapper module).

Census (verified before writing, Rule 2; grep census over this
worktree at this commit; every other occurrence of these names is
an import, a call site or a doc cross-reference, and no test-side
re-definition of any of them exists): each member has exactly ONE
production definition today — `projects_store_to_app_error`
(src-tauri/src/commands.rs:2512), `activity_log_to_app_error`
(commands.rs:1644), the settings pair `settings_write_to_app_error`
(commands.rs:1995) and `settings_cell_to_app_error`
(commands.rs:2023) — two distinct mappers, not two copies of one —
and the library mapping inside `build_snapshot_to_app_error`
(src-tauri/src/dirty_recalc.rs:556, the `BuildSnapshotError::Library`
arm; its doc at :546-551 states the library read has no
command-layer mapper yet). Test-side seeding helpers that map
`LibraryError` (eight sites: `library_seed_error` in
`dirty_recalc_tests.rs:170` and the five `sync_phase*_tests.rs`,
`sync_library_seed_error` and `library_watch_seed_error` in
`ipc_tests.rs`) are plumbing by D-149's test-side ruling, not
copies of the library member — the rule below does not fire on
them.

Solution (recorded as a rule future tasks and reviews apply):

- The family's membership is the census list: the command-reachable
  wire mapper per store table — projects, activity-log, settings
  write, settings read, library (via the snapshot read's arm) —
  today. A private module-local mapper serving one internal seam
  (e.g. retention's `storage_to_app_error`, retention.rs:535) is
  NOT a member, however similar its `StorageError → AppError` shape
  looks.
- A member of the store-mapper family is consolidated only when a
  second copy of THAT member appears; a still-single-copy member
  stays where it is, however many of its siblings consolidate.
- Premature consolidation is speculation: no proactive
  finish-the-family pass, no shared mapper module created ahead of
  a duplicate.
- The trigger is a REVIEW finding a duplicate (or equivalent
  duplicate evidence verified in another task's fact-gathering);
  the consolidation then follows T-264's own shape — one spelling,
  the migration map, the union pin at the survivor.

Reading note (Rule 1): the card's title ("revision only when a
second copy appears at ANY member") and its rule line ("a member is
consolidated only when IT gains a second copy") admit a collapsed
single-trigger reading; the composed reading recorded here is
two-clause: ANY member's duplication triggers a REVISIT of the
family (a look), while a member is CONSOLIDATED only on its OWN
second copy — a revisit never moves a member still single-copy.

Checks: md-only change — DECISIONS.md is the only file in the diff;
nothing compile-bearing changed, so no cargo run (the md-only
exception, which in this batch coincides with the batch regime:
suites are not run). `pnpm exec prettier --check DECISIONS.md` and
`pnpm run format:check` exit 0; the pre-commit hook gates the
commit. The census above is point-in-time: the cited lines move as
the files evolve — the RULE is the durable content, not the line
numbers.

Honest boundaries: this entry encodes a policy, not a mechanism —
no CI job or hook detects a second mapper copy; enforcement lives
in this file and in reviewers' briefs carrying D-149's doctrine,
i.e. it is human. The single-copy census is asserted from grep,
not pinned by a test, and is correct only as of this commit.

### D-162 — T-289: the six test-side sync-run assertion helpers consolidated onto the one `db.rs` mapper, the `Member` arm a documented panic — 2026-11-23

Problem: D-149's follow-up card. The six test-side assertion
helpers (D-149's exact list: `sync_runs_app_error` in
`sync_phase0_tests.rs` 123, `runs_app_error` in each of
`sync_phase1_tests.rs` 96, `sync_phase2_tests.rs` 128,

their own `Sql`-arm spelling (`Sql` → `sqlite_error_to_app_error`)
plus the `SyncRunsRead`+`Display` fallback — six copies of the
assertion-side mapping, each able to drift away from the one
production mapper. Three readings were open before coding: which
mapper is "the common mapper"; where the shared test helper lives
(the card names no home); and what the new `Member` shape means
for behavior preservation.

Solution: one
`#[cfg(test)] pub(crate) fn sync_runs_app_error_for_tests(SyncRunsError) -> AppError`
in `db.rs`, directly after the mapper family (`sync_runs_to_app_error`
then its `backup_records_to_app_error` sibling — D-149's co-located
pair stays contiguous, the twin is the next item) — the home is
the family's convention, not a fresh location choice: `db.rs`
already hosts a `cfg(test)` seam beside production code (the
`Db::set_busy_timeout_for_tests` shape, named as the seam shape in
`commands.rs`'s own cfg(test) doc at 797), and the helper belongs
beside the mapper it delegates to. No new module (one function —
structure for structure's sake is what D-149 refused for the
production side too).

- _"The common mapper" is the production one._ The helper's `Sql`
  arm delegates directly to `db::sync_runs_to_app_error` (the
  T-264/D-149 one-mapper), NOT a re-spelled
  `sqlite_error_to_app_error` call: the repo keeps exactly one
  `Sql`-arm spelling (db.rs 1140), and if production's arm ever
  changes, the suites follow it — the card's "переход на общий
  маппер" reading. The classifier call the six helpers spelled is
  now reachable only through the mapper.
- _The `Member` arm is the documented panic-rich fallback._ The
  helper's match names both variants (the six `other =>` catch-alls
  are gone — a new store variant is now a compile error at the
  helper, the pat-exhaustive law) and panics on `Member` with a
  message naming what happened (the arm, why the suites cannot
  produce it) plus the error's `Display` — the D-149 assertion-side
  vocabulary ("the richest panic message"), deliberately
  value-embedding and never on the wire; the wire's class-only rule
  stays in the mapper (SEC-008), and the helper's `# Panics` doc
  section carries the contract. Behavior preservation: the arm is
  unreachable in every suite (D-149's ruling — rows are read back
  only through the sanctioned writers), so on every input the
  suites can produce, the helper returns exactly what the old
  helpers returned; the deleted silent `SyncRunsRead` fallback
  envelope was never observed by any test.
- _The migration map._ Six definitions deleted, 17 call sites
  re-pointed to the one helper (phase 0: 2 — 97, 111; phase 1: 2 —
  122, 136; phase 2: 4 — 154, 168, 575, 726; phase 3: 2 — 139,
  153; phase 4: 5 — 140, 151, 396, 478, 1438; ipc: 2 — 9349,
  9363). The phase suites import it by name (a plain `use` line —
  those files' one-import-per-line style); `ipc_tests.rs` uses the
  fully qualified path (that file's style for `crate::db` items).
  The
  per-suite doc comments went with the definitions; D-149's P3-1
  "class-only here too" rewording is superseded by the shared doc.
- _Out of scope, ruled so._ The `LibraryError` sibling family
  (`sync_library_seed_error` in `ipc_tests.rs` 9306 and the
  per-phase library-seed helpers) is a different input enum and a
  different candidate (routed below as a follow-up for the board);

  stands. No production code changed: `sync_runs_to_app_error`,
  `sqlite_error_to_app_error` and the store enum are byte-identical
  to the parent commit.

Tests: the two helper pins live in `db_tests.rs` beside the
mapper's union pin (the round-1 P2-1 fix — the suites' own
`map_err` sites `.expect` success and never observe an envelope,
so they were never a falsifiable oracle for the helper):
`the_assertion_side_helper_routes_sql_through_the_one_mapper`
drives one representative §10 class (`SQLITE_FULL`) through the

against the mapper itself, which would mirror the implementation —
and `the_assertion_side_helper_panics_on_the_unreachable_member_envelope`
pins the `# Panics` contract with `#[should_panic]` on the
documented panic text. The six suites' own pins stay the oracle
for the reads they assert;
`sync_runs_failures_map_to_the_wire_through_the_one_mapper` keeps
proving the mapper's arms.

Honest boundaries: the batch regime (owner instruction
2026-11-23) defers suite runs to the orchestrator's central run —

Addendum (2026-11-24, T-336): the "mirrored by `action_logged`"
anchor above (and ARCHITECTURE.md's "The journal is mirrored into the
file log" sentence) read as "every written entry is duplicated into
the file log", which the facade never promised: `logging::action_logged` owns a
selection policy, and only its picks mirror — an `error` or `warn` row
whatever its visibility (an `info` row whose result is an error
included), a diagnostic `info`, and nothing else; the
`info` + `user` + non-error shape is the Activity window's own data
and stays in the database journal alone.

facade's own doc opening, and this addendum is the D-record's half
(the dated-record posture: the entry's text above stays as written).

### D-167 — T-297: the NFR numbering sweep — NFR-018 defined where its two references point (new §12.6 Error Presentation), the NFR-014/NFR-016 gaps annotated under §12's heading, the census's remaining danglers NFR-011/012/021 reported, not fixed — 2026-11-23

  referenced-but-undefined IDs: NFR-011 (SEC-012), NFR-012 (SEC-004),
  NFR-021 (§10's general rules and UI-010) — and a second absent
  number: NFR-016. History checked, not assumed: all four danglers
  first appear as citations in spec v1.0 (`ae89176`) and were never
  defined anywhere later (nothing was dropped — dangling from day
  one); `git log -S` over the whole repository history finds no trace
  of NFR-014 or NFR-016 ever carrying a requirement — before this

  (`deb2d98`) and NFR-016 had none; this commit's note adds both
  numbers to `docs/spec.md`, so the note and this entry are now their
  only mentions. The range spellings (NFR-001…003 and friends) count
  as definitions of every number they span; NFR-002/003/005 are not

- _NFR-018 — defined, not re-pointed._ Both references mean the

  requirement) artificially. The wording claims only what is
  provable: no requirement was ever written under either number in

  either, the gaps are recorded, nothing renumbered. The card's

  014 and says "report any others"; defining three more requirements

### D-169 — T-277: the manual smoke checklist created (docs/manual-smoke.md) — D-143's three Windows GUI log items made first-person-executable; the in-repo home for what CI cannot prove — 2026-11-23

Problem: D-143's honest boundaries closed T-255 with three smoke items
that automation cannot prove, carried only in its prose and
ARCHITECTURE.md's Logging section — "no smoke-checklist file exists in
the repo; this entry and ARCHITECTURE.md's Logging section carry the
steps". Spec §15.5 conditions the release on manual checklists whose
in-repo home did not exist either. The card asked for the file: a
first-person-executable Windows GUI checklist with the three items as
its first entries.

Solution:

- _New file `docs/manual-smoke.md`._ Name chosen from the vocabulary
  the sources already use (D-143 "manual smoke list",
  ARCHITECTURE.md "the manual smoke run") — "smoke" and not "checklist"
  in the file name because the release checklist of spec §15.5 is a
  different, larger artifact the spec owns; this file is the home for
  individual manual proofs. The header states the relation explicitly:
  a release run walks both, the S1–S7/S9/S10 scenario runs stay
  defined in the spec and are not reproduced here (out of scope per
  the card). Room for future items is structural — every item carries
  its source and the same Prepare/Do/Pass-when shape.
- _Scope: exactly the three D-143 items, nothing invented._ Each pass
  criterion restates a verified source (Rule 2): 10 MiB = 10,485,760
  bytes and five files (`MAX_LOG_FILE_BYTES`/`MAX_LOG_FILES`,
  `src-tauri/src/logging.rs:215`/:206); the name scheme (the day's
  first file keeps the exact §5.5 name, same-day parts `.2.log`/`.3.log`
  decimal from 2, no leading zeros; UTC stamps); the startup
  degradation (one `error` event, "file log unavailable; logging to
  stderr", `logging.rs:794`); the mid-run blocked rotation (one warn
  per episode, "the file log could not rotate; writing continues into
  the current file" with `step=open|prune`, `logging.rs:2042-2050`;
  lines keep landing in the current file; a healed disk heals the
  log); the locked-file prune resilience (the `step=prune` warn, the
  rotation still happens, convergence after the hold is released);
  `log_level` values and the default-config creation
  (`src-tauri/src/config.rs`, `load_or_create`). D-143's
  construction-prune-failure-is-silent boundary is encoded as
  guidance — item 3 locks the file mid-run, because only the mid-run
  prune can show its verdict.
- _Item 2 deliberately split into 2a/2b._ D-143's item (2) is the
  startup half ("a read-only `logs/` starts the app in the stderr
  degradation without aborting"); the card's parenthetical ("строки
  идут в старый файл, warn через фасад") is the mid-run rotation half.
  Neither source states both, so both variants are written down with
  their own sources rather than blending one into the other.
- _Windows mechanics made executable._ The read-only case is driven by
  an icacls deny ACE (`/deny "user:(WD,AD)"`), not the DOS read-only
  attribute — the attribute does not stop file creation, an ACL deny
  does; the locked file with an `[IO.File]::Open` handle opened with
  share mode `None` (an exclusive hold: deletions fail while it
  lives); the stderr degradation is made observable by launching from
  a console with `2>` redirection (a GUI-subsystem executable
  inherits redirected handles), with the honest note that without it
  the missing log file is the only observable half.

Checks: md-only diff (`docs/manual-smoke.md`, this file); prettier
green; batch regime (owner instruction 2026-11-23) — tests not run,
the orchestrator runs the suite centrally after the flash batch; one
review round.

Honest boundaries: written without a Windows machine — the platform
mechanics above (icacls deny syntax, share-mode-None locking,
stderr-handle inheritance) are standard-platform behavior cited from
the sources' own analysis (D-099's manufactured sharing violations,
D-032's Windows-GUI/stderr work), not verified on the target; the
first real pass on the owner's machine is the proof. The spec §15.5
cross-reference (pointing "the release checklist" at this file) would
be a `docs/spec.md` edit — owned by the parallel T-299 in this batch —
so it is reported as a follow-up card, not done here.

### D-170 — T-303: the D-167 danglers defined — NFR-011 in §12.1 (no-elevation), NFR-012 in §7.9 (updater-only network use), NFR-021 in new §12.7 Safety (destructive-action confirmations); re-pointing declined for all three — 2026-11-23

Problem: D-167's census left three referenced-but-undefined NFR IDs as
follow-up cards (its "NFR-011/012/021 reported, not fixed" bullet).
All three dangle since spec v1.0 (`ae89176`): `git log -S` over the
whole history finds each number's first appearance as a bare citation
in v1.0 and no definition anywhere before this commit — nothing was
dropped, dangling from day one (the same state D-167 proved for
NFR-018).

Solution (D-167's play repeated; one census and one reading per
number):

- _Census first (Rule 2)._ NFR-011: the spec cite at SEC-012 (§13);
  the content spread with T-009 (`c7ad647`) into
  `src-tauri/windows/app.manifest` (header and trustInfo comments),
  `src-tauri/build.rs`, `src-tauri/src/config_tests.rs` (the module
  doc, one inline comment and four assertion messages) and
  ARCHITECTURE.md's Windows platform
  note; DECISIONS.md's T-009-era entries mention it too. NFR-012: one
  cite, SEC-004's "(NFR-012, NFR-013)" (§13). NFR-021: two cites, §10's
  general rules and UI-010 (on the bulk-actions list item). No other
  requirement cites any of the three.
- _NFR-011 — defined in §12.1 Platforms, beside NFR-023_ (the other
  manifest-sourced requirement). The content is the no-elevation
  contract: user rights, no elevation request, on any platform; the
  Windows mechanism is the manifest's pinned
  `requestedExecutionLevel level="asInvoker" uiAccess="false"` — the
  exact element `windows_manifest_never_requests_elevation` pins
  (`config_tests.rs:1523`), including the banned spellings
  (`requireAdministrator`, `highestAvailable`, `uiAccess="true"`,
  `autoElevate`). Re-pointing declined: SEC-012 — the citing
  site — is the only statement of the content in the spec, so the only
  re-point target would be a self-citation (D-167's NFR-018 lesson).
  The new definition cites SEC-012; SEC-012's pre-existing NFR-011
  cite closes the pair two-way. ARCHITECTURE.md and the manifest,
  build.rs and test comments needed no change — their cites resolve to
  §12.1 now.
- _NFR-012 — defined in §7.9, immediately before its sibling NFR-013_
  (the file's precedent of NFRs defined where their subject lives:
  NFR-013 there, NFR-015 in §7.1's row, NFR-017/022 in §7.4's row).
  The content: the app's only network use is checking for updates and
  downloading the signed artifact (UPD-003); no telemetry, analytics,
  crash reporting or any other outbound connection — grounded in the
  spec's own v1 out-of-scope line (§1) and §3.2's D-28 row ("Telemetry
  (43) … Not doing these"). Re-pointing to NFR-013 declined: NFR-013
  (v1.0's wording) stated "the app's only network request is the update
  check" —
  narrower than SEC-004's "checking for and downloading updates" (the
  artifact download is a separate request under UPD-003) and silent on
  the no-other-use rule; pinning the use restriction to it would
  repeat D-167's declined-NFR-006 defect. SEC-004's two cites now
  decompose cleanly: NFR-012 = the use restriction, NFR-013 = request
  content and module isolation. The new definition cites NFR-013 and
  SEC-004; SEC-004's cite stays as written.
- _NFR-021 — defined in new §12.7 Safety_ (one bullet, the §12.6
  shape): a destructive UI action never executes without an explicit
  confirmation explaining what will happen; UI-010 enumerates the
  actions that require this confirmation, with their dialogs and the
  P1 extensions. Re-pointing declined: at UI-010's inner cite the only
  statement of the content is UI-010 itself — a self-citation;
  re-pointing §10's cite to UI-010 would still leave UI-010's own cite
  dangling. Defining one requirement resolves both sites, two-way
  (UI-010 and §10 already cite NFR-021).

The §12 numbering note (NFR-014/016) stays untouched: after this

002/003/005 per D-167's settled reading), so the note's claim remains

### D-171 — T-304: the eight test-side `LibraryError` seed helpers consolidated onto one `dirty_recalc.rs` seam routed through the production `Library` arm, the non-`Sql` arms two documented panics — 2026-11-23

Problem: D-162's follow-up card. The card's census
(`sync_library_seed_error` in `ipc_tests.rs` 9306 plus five per-phase
`library_seed_error` helpers) did not match reality: find-by-content
sweeps (the `"LibrarySeed"` literal and the `LibraryError) ->`
signatures, Rule 2) found EIGHT copies, the census D-161 had already
inventoried — the card's six plus `library_seed_error` in
`dirty_recalc_tests.rs` 170 (the sixth sibling the card itself
anticipated) and `library_watch_seed_error` in `ipc_tests.rs` 6442
(the eighth, which neither the card nor D-162's follow-up list
named; both included here as members of the class). All eight carried
the same two-arm mapping — identical once each file's import
spelling resolves (three textual forms: the phase 1–4 local-import
form, phase 0's mixed form, the fully qualified ipc/dirty form; only
the `Sql` arm line is byte-identical in all eight):
`Sql` → `sqlite_error_to_app_error`, an `other =>` catch-all →
`DbLocked` + `os_kind: "LibrarySeed"` + the error's `Display` —
eight copies able to drift from the production spelling. 29 call
sites (phase 0: 5; phases 1–4: 3 each; `dirty_recalc_tests`: 6;
`ipc_tests`: 6). Three readings were open before coding: the seam's
home (unlike the sync-run family, NO whole-enum production
`LibraryError → AppError` mapper exists — the only production
mapping is the nested `BuildSnapshotError::Library` arm of
`build_snapshot_to_app_error`, dirty_recalc.rs 556–603); what the
enum's other fifteen arms become (the card's "documented panic" is
written for a two-variant enum); and whether the dirty and watch
siblings belong to the family at all.

Solution: one seam function under `#[cfg(test)] pub(crate)` —
`library_seed_error_for_tests(LibraryError) -> AppError` — in
`dirty_recalc.rs`, directly after `dirty_fallback` — beside
[`build_snapshot_to_app_error`], whose `Library` arm IS the
production `LibraryError` mapping. No new module; the dirty sibling
and the watch sibling are in (the same mapping, same input enum,
same class of hand-rolled copies).

- _The home is the family convention, applied where the family
  lives._ D-162's law is "the helper belongs beside the mapper it
  delegates to"; the mapper this family delegates to for `Sql` is
  the shared base classifier, but the enum's production mapping
  lives in `dirty_recalc.rs`, so the seam is co-located with it.
  `db.rs` (T-289's home) was rejected: it hosts the sync-run family
  and the classifier, but no `LibraryError` production code —
  placing the seam there would co-locate it with the wrong family.
  The seam sits after `dirty_fallback` so the mapper and its private
  helper stay contiguous (D-162's R1-P3-3 ruling), and directly
  before the module's own `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`.
- _The `Sql` arm routes through the production mapping — D-162's
  one-spelling law, applied where the family lives._ The card's
  "delegating to the PRODUCTION mapper" resolves here to
  `build_snapshot_to_app_error(BuildSnapshotError::Library(error))`:
  the production `Library` arm (dirty_recalc.rs 560–562) IS the
  enum's production mapping, its `Sql` treatment today the shared
  base classifier, and routing the seam's `Sql` arm through it keeps
  the classifier call reachable only through the mapper (the D-162
  Solution's exact wording) — if production's `Sql` treatment ever
  changes, the suites follow it without a re-spell. Wrapping in
  `BuildSnapshotError::Library` is the only route (the mapper takes
  the snapshot enum, not a `LibraryError`), is behavior-identical
  today (the wrapped call unpacks to the same classifier call the
  eight copies spelled), and never sees the other arms — those panic
  in the seam before any delegation, so the class-only wire fallbacks
  of the production `Member`/write-path arms (the D-149 wire-vs-
  assertion split) are unreachable from the seam by construction.
- _The non-`Sql` arms are two documented panics, not one catch-all._
  The exhaustive match names all seventeen variants (a new store
  variant is a compile error at the seam — the pat-exhaustive law;
  `LibraryError` is not `#[non_exhaustive]`). The fifteen write-path
  outcomes and the `Member` envelope panic with distinct reasons —
  `Member`: the seeds write only through the sanctioned library
  writers (D-149's ruling); write-path outcomes: the seeds construct
  valid-by-construction inputs (ids read back from the rows they
  just wrote; titles unique within the test's database — the
  process-unique counter titles of the phase 1–4/ipc-sync fixtures,
  distinct fixture titles verified per call site for the rest,
  `seed_extra_variant`'s `is_main: false` only ever after
  `seed_instruction` created the main, and the delete/move/reassign
  writers that produce `LastVariant`/`ReplacementRequired`/
  `ReplacementInvalid`/`NoActiveMain`/`PositionOutOfRange`/
  `VariantNotActive` never appear at these `map_err` sites). Both
  panics name the arm and embed the error's `Display`; the `# Panics`
  doc section carries the contract, and the wire's class-only rule
  stays in the production mapping (SEC-008).
- _Behavior preservation, argued per call site._ The five library
  functions the seeds map are `create_item`, `create_variant`,
  `assign`, `hide_item`, `update_variant`; on every error they can
  produce that the suites cannot (everything but `Sql`), the old
  helpers' silent `DbLocked`+`LibrarySeed`+`Display` envelope was
  never observed by any test, so on every input the suites can
  produce the seam returns exactly what the old helpers returned.
  Reachability evidence: the 29 call sites' arguments are ids
  returned by earlier seeds in the same test's fresh per-test
  database (`dirty_app()`/the mock-app fixtures), and the title
  uniqueness was verified caller by caller (phase 0: one
  `seed_instruction` per test, distinct titles; dirty: the
  hidden-instruction test seeds "Assigned"/"Buried" once each, and
  749's burst writes "First"/"Second"/"Third" once each; ipc watch:
  "alpha"/"bravo"/"charlie" and the per-test-distinct pairs).
- _The migration map._ Eight definitions deleted, 29 call sites
  re-pointed (phase 0: 5 — 209, 219, 244, 266, 285; phase 1: 3 —
  205, 215, 224; phase 2: 3 — 279, 289, 298; phase 3: 3 — 235, 245,
  254; phase 4: 3 — 240, 250, 259; `dirty_recalc_tests`: 6 — 228,
  238, 257, 268, 286, 749; `ipc_tests`: 6 — 6416, 6426, 6435, 9279,
  9289, 9298; pre-edit line numbers). Import styles kept per file:
  the phase suites import the seam by name (phase 0 joins its
  existing group import); `dirty_recalc_tests.rs` extends its
  existing `crate::dirty_recalc` group import; `ipc_tests.rs` fully
  qualified (its style for crate items, T-289's precedent). The
  helpers' doc comments went with the definitions. Orphaned imports
  cleaned where the helper was a name's only user: phase 0 dropped
  `AppError`, phase 1 dropped `AppError`+`ErrorDetails`, phase 3
  dropped `ErrorDetails`, phase 4 dropped `ErrorCode`+`ErrorDetails`
  (each verified by a per-file grep census before the deletion).
  No production code changed: `build_snapshot_to_app_error`,
  `dirty_fallback`, and the store enum are byte-identical to the
  parent commit; the seam exists only in `cfg(test)` builds.

Tests: three pins in `dirty_recalc_tests.rs`'s new "the library
seed seam (T-304)" section, T-289's shape adapted to this enum.
`the_library_seed_helper_routes_sql_through_the_classifier` drives
one representative §10 class (`SQLITE_FULL`) through the seam with
the wire literals as the oracle (`E_DISK_FULL`, `errors.disk_full`,
`DiskFull` — the §10 table, not a comparison against the mapper,
which would mirror the implementation). The two `#[should_panic]`
pins hold the guards to their documented texts — "hit the `Member`
envelope" and "hit a write-path outcome" (`NotFound` the
representative arm). Mutation reasoning: returning any other
envelope for the routing pin's class turns it red; re-mapping either
panic arm into a returned envelope, or rewording the panic texts,
turns the respective pin red.

Honest boundaries: the batch regime (owner instruction 2026-11-23)
defers suite runs to the orchestrator's central run — the
consolidated helpers' green run is not proven in this task, and the
pins' mutation check is argued above, not executed;
`cargo fmt --check` and `cargo check --tests -p eunomia-sync`
(type check, no test run) are green by exit code, zero warnings.
The panic messages' `Display` would embed a hostile stored value if
an arm ever fired; that is test-side assertion wording only, never a
diagnostic surface, and the function does not exist outside
`cfg(test)` builds (a production caller is impossible by
construction).

Round-1 review addendum (D-171, same task; report
`.opencode/reviews/t304-round1.md`, deepseek-v4.1-flash — APPROVE,
no P0/P1; 1×P2, 3×P3, all in this entry's prose): the round
re-derived the behavior preservation per call site (the ids/titles
each caller passes, the store functions' error variants, the per-test
database isolation), hashed the eight deleted bodies against

Findings fixed here —

- P3-2 (taken): the "Assigned"/"Buried" two-call evidence was

- P3-3 (taken, the reviewer's alternative adopted): "cannot delegate
  to [`build_snapshot_to_app_error`]" overstated the constraint —
  `BuildSnapshotError` is public, and the `Sql` arm can route through

  The seam's `Sql` arm now does exactly that (behavior-identical

  so the routing pin's §10 oracle still passes; the `Member`/write-
  path arms still panic before any delegation), the Solution bullet

### D-173 — T-310: the one-time "destructive" definition in §12.7's NFR-021 — the recovery pair `db_recreate`/`db_restore_backup` classified by the definition, not by the UI-010 enumeration — 2026-11-23

Problem: D-170's round-1 P2-2 resolved the recovery pair's
"destructive" status only by dropping the enumeration's completeness
claim: the pair (ARCHITECTURE.md 595 calls it "the destructive pair")
stays outside UI-010's list by design, and the class term "destructive
UI actions" (§10's general rules, §12.7's NFR-021) carried no
definition — the card (a T-303 follow-up) asked for exactly this small
spec sweep.

Solution:

- _Census first (Rule 2)._ The word "destructive" appears in the spec
  exactly twice — §10's general rules ("…and destructive UI actions
  (NFR-021)") and NFR-021 itself ("A destructive UI action never
  executes…") — both normative uses of the class, no definition
  anywhere. §7.10's command notes: `db_restore_backup` keeps the
  damaged database as `db-backups/pre-recovery-<UTC>.sqlite3`,
  replaces it with the chosen copy and reopens it; `db_recreate` does
  the same but starts with an empty database; the trio
  `db_backups_list`/`db_restore_backup`/`db_recreate` "backs the
  recovery screen for `E_DB_CORRUPT` (section 10)" — the only screen
  that lists `db-backups/` copies, and recovery mode is entered only
  from `E_DB_CORRUPT` (§10's row); the project Backups tab (BKP-004)
  lists `backups/` file copies, not DB copies. So in a healthy app no
  screen offers the pre-recovery copy back. The frontend recovery
  screen does not exist yet (ARCHITECTURE.md's honest boundary: "the
  frontend screen itself is the recovery-UI task's"), so the pair's
  confirmations are spec-side requirements today.
- _The definition lives in NFR-021's bullet_ (the home D-170 created;
  §12.7 keeps its one-bullet shape): «"Destructive" means one thing in
  this spec: the action's outcome destroys stored data such that, in
  the app's normal operation, no way back to the lost state exists — a
  way back is an in-app restore command, a kept copy the app offers to
  restore, or the replaced value still being selectable in the UI.»
  The criterion is recoverability through the app's own interface in
  normal operation, not severity: overwriting onto a restorable state
  (a sync write goes over a BKP-001 copy; BKP-007 backs up the current
  file before a restore) is not destructive; destroying without an
  in-app way back is.
- _The pair's resolution is now by definition, not by enumeration._
  NFR-021's bullet names the pair destructive — each command replaces
  the database wholesale (an empty database, or the chosen copy),
  while the `pre-recovery-<UTC>` copy is a file on disk that no normal
  screen offers back (recovery mode itself is reached only from
  `E_DB_CORRUPT`, section 10) — and states the consequence:
  both are confirmed on the recovery screen (section 10) before they
  run, outside UI-010's list. That confirmation sentence is the
  requirement the future recovery-UI task implements; the Rust-side
  guards (the triple `E_VALIDATION` gate, ARCHITECTURE.md 595) are
  untouched and are not confirmations.
- _Class census under the definition_ (each member verified against
  its own requirement). Destructive: deleting per-project custom text
  (MAIN-007, UI-010 — no history for it: 9.8's snapshots cover
  instructions and variants, and the custom text bypasses the variant
  model), deleting an excluded path (6.4, UI-010 — a manual entry has
  no way back; a scan-found one is re-created by a rescan, PRJ-017),
  deleting a heading (6.4, UI-010 — the heading itself has no restore
  command; its instructions stay), a heading rename or move (6.2's
  close: "Section headings have no revisions", recorded only in
  `action_log`; the old name is not selectable anywhere, and
  LIB-030/031's one dialog confirms nothing — NFR-021 as amended now
  requires a confirmation the library requirements do not yet
  provide; adding it is requirement authoring and is reported as a
  follow-up card, not written here), the P1 purge of hidden
  instructions (D-11 — "with confirmation"), and the pair. Not
  destructive: edits of instructions and variants (the previous state
  stays in the version history, 9.8 — ALG-070 snapshots changes
  deduped by hash, ALG-072 never deletes the latest; S8 restores a
  version), assignment changes (the definition's third way-back arm —
  the variant stays in the library and selectable; verified against
  MAIN-001…005's confirmation-free toggle, LIB-017…022's
  removal-without-deletion, and the 6.2 CHECK that makes a toggle-off
  a row delete, with no assignment arm in the `revisions` CHECK),

### D-174 — T-313: spec's release-checklist mentions cross-referenced to docs/manual-smoke.md — the file named as the release checklist's in-repo companion, never as the checklist itself — 2026-11-23

Problem: T-277's report asked for a cross-reference "in spec §15.5 —
«the release checklist» → docs/manual-smoke.md" (D-169), but the
verified premise differs (Rule 2): the literal phrase never occurs in
§15.5 — it occurs in §15.1's prose (`docs/spec.md:927`), the §16 M8
plan cell (`:999`) and the Risks table (`:1011`, already pointing at
"(15.1)"); §15.5's manual condition is `:982`. And pointing the phrase
at the file literally would contradict the repo's own records: D-169
and the file header (`docs/manual-smoke.md:17-21`) state the file is
NOT the spec's release checklist and does not reproduce the
S1–S7/S9/S10 scenario runs — "the release checklist of spec §15.5 is a
different, larger artifact the spec owns". Following the card verbatim
would make the spec lie (Rule 11).

Solution:

- §15.1 (`:927`) and §15.5 (`:982`) now name the file as the release
  checklist's companion: "…stays in the release checklist, together
  with the manual smoke checks tracked in `docs/manual-smoke.md`"
  (§15.1) and "…is done on each OS, and the manual smoke checks tracked
  in `docs/manual-smoke.md` pass" (§15.5). The wording implements the
  file header's own "A release run walks both" — without it the spec's
  release conditions and the committed file disagreed (the Rule-11-sync
  gap the card targeted). "tracked in" asserts nothing about the file's
  inventory, so both sentences stay true before and after the parallel
  T-315 populates the scenario runs into the file; the file is never
  called "the release checklist".
- Left alone deliberately: §16 M8's cell (`:999`) is a padded
  plan-table deliverable, and the Risks mitigation (`:1011`) resolves
  through §15.1, which now names the file.

Follow-up for the board: the file header's verbatim quote of the §15.5
bullet (`docs/manual-smoke.md:18-20`, "…is done on each OS") is now a
truncation of the amended bullet — fold the quote update into T-315's
pass over the file (review P3-1; the file is this task's frozen zone,
Rule 10).

### D-175 — T-315: the manual smoke checklist carries the scenario runs S1–S7, S9, S10 — the spec §15.5 release list gets its in-repo executable form; every entry written against the spec's surfaces with the not-yet-landed UI marked pending — 2026-11-23

Problem: T-277's follow-up report (the origin of this card): D-169
closed the checklist with exactly the three Windows log items and an
explicit scoping decision — "the S1–S7/S9/S10 scenario runs stay
defined in the spec and are not reproduced here (out of scope per the
card)". The report flagged the gap: spec §15.5 conditions the release
on the manual checklist for scenarios S1–S7, S9, S10 being done on
each OS (§15.1 keeps the runs manual because e2e drives a mocked IPC,
not the real shell), and those runs had no in-repo executable form —
the release run would walk a checklist that did not say what to do.
The card asked for the scenario runs in the same file (or a separate
release-checklist doc; the same file chosen — one home for manual
checks, per D-169's naming rationale).

Solution:

- _New section "Scenario runs S1–S7, S9, S10" appended to
  `docs/manual-smoke.md`; the header rewritten to describe both
  parts._ The old header paragraph ("those scenario runs are defined
  in the spec and are not reproduced here") is superseded — the file
  now carries both the D-143 Windows items and the scenario runs, and
  states the relation: a release run walks both. S8 and S11 are named
  as deliberately absent, not forgotten (P1, post-1.0 per §15.1's e2e
  row and §16's next stage — the header promises nothing about them).
- _Structure: one entry per scenario, the D-169 Prepare/Do/Pass-when
  shape._ Each entry carries a Source line (the spec §8 scenario plus
  the requirement sections it exercises: §7.1 for S1/S2, §7.3/§7.4 for
  S3–S6, §9.4 + §7.5 for S7, §6.6 + MAIN-024…028 for S9, §7.6 + §9.4
  phase 2 + T-F1 for S10) and pass criteria tied to requirement IDs,
  `E_*` codes and concrete paths — no criterion without a spec source
  (Rule 2). The section preamble adds a Pending-surfaces paragraph and
  a per-OS common preparation (data-dir paths for all three OSes,
  throwaway-repo hygiene, §6.5 defaults).
- _Pending surfaces marked, not pretended (Rule 11)._ The main-window
  UI has not landed: `src/App.vue` is the shell (title, version,
  project count — verified at this commit), and the library/assignment
  commands are not registered (`src-tauri/src/lib.rs`'s
  collect_commands carries 18 commands; the scenario-relevant
  `project_add_manual`, `scan_start`/`scan_cancel`, `sync_run`,
  `settings_get`/`settings_set` are among them). So every entry
  carries a Pending line naming its surfaces and the owning §16
  milestone (the milestone table's own mapping: S1/S2 → M1, S3/S5 →
  M2, S4–S6 → M3, S9 → M4, S7/S10 → M5), and the preamble states
  plainly that no entry below is executable until its surfaces land.
  The entries are still written to be executable then — against the
  spec's named controls, not today's code.
- _Platform mechanics are means, not claims._ Where an entry needs a
  real-OS state the spec only names (a denied folder for S2's "no
  access" skip, a blocked backup subfolder for S10), the mechanics are
  the same class D-169 used: icacls deny ACEs and chmod on Unix, a
  `.git`-file stand-in for ALG-052's submodule/worktree reason, a
  folder rename for D-09's unavailable state. The added discipline
  beyond the card's ask: S10's prepare syncs TWICE so BKP-010's dedup
  cannot blur the run (phase 2's dedup decision creates no copy and
  the abort sweep deletes only copies the run created —
  `sync_phase2.rs`'s module docs — so a pass criterion of "the
  subfolder is empty" would be false; the honest criterion is "holds
  exactly what it held before the run").
- _§15.5's list is the authoritative scope._ The card said S1–S7/S9/
  S10 "per spec §15.1"; the file's own header cites §15.5 as the
  release condition, and §15.1's sentence (the manual run stays in the
  release checklist because e2e is mocked) moved into the header as
  the why.
- _Scope addition folded in (the orchestrator, mid-task, from T-313's
  merged review; the ruling is D-174's board follow-up)._ T-313
  (fc5aad6) amended the §15.5 bullet while this task ran — it now
  reads "…is done on each OS, and the manual smoke checks tracked in
  `docs/manual-smoke.md` pass" — which made the header's verbatim
  quote (D-169's old wording) a truncation. The header quote is
  re-based on the merged bullet, the same quote fixed in this
  section's own preamble, and the header's two standing claims kept
  (the file is not the release checklist itself; a release run walks
  both). One consequence taken deliberately: the new section title is
  plain "Scenario runs S1–S7, S9, S10" — D-174's "the file is never
  called the release checklist" rules out titling the section "the
  §15.5 release checklist"; the preamble's "the scenario runs the
  spec owns" carries the relation instead.

### D-176 — T-318: LIB-025's last-variant guard annotated as UI-unreachable, the refusal scoped to the surfaces behind the disabled button (`variant_delete` 7.10, the store layer) — 2026-11-23

Problem: T-315's round-1 P3-1 (this card's source, folded into the
smoke file then): spec §7.3's LIB-023/024/025 row asks for a Delete
disable "for the last variant" (LIB-025) next to the main-variant
disable (LIB-024), but no UI path reaches the last-variant disable —
LIB-024 fires first. The card offered defer-to-M2 or annotate; the
owner took it into the 2026-11-23 flash batch (act, don't defer).

Reading (Rule 2, verified before writing): three facts compose the
unreachability. (1) DB-010 (`docs/spec.md:352`): every active
instruction has at least one active variant and exactly one active
main variant — pinned at the schema level by the `ux_variant_main`
partial unique index (`docs/spec.md:280-281`). (2) D-125's owner
ruling (§3.2's D-12 row, `docs/spec.md:86`): the main variant cannot
be deleted at all — the Delete button disabled with "Make another
variant main first" (LIB-024), so no UI flow removes the main
variant. (3) Therefore the active variant set always contains the
main variant; the last remaining variant is necessarily the main one,
and its Delete is disabled by LIB-024 with the LIB-024 hint — the
LIB-025 disable (the same button's other condition) has no state to
fire in. The UI surfaces were swept for a counterexample: the
editor's variant list (§7.3's LIB-017…022 row — the only
variant-delete affordance), matrix cells (§7.4 MAIN-001…005 —
assign/unassign only), bulk operations (assignments, not variant
deletes), Hide/Restore (instruction-level), per-project custom text
(bypasses the variant model, §7.3's MAIN-007 row) — none deletes a
last non-main variant. But the row is not UI-only, and not deletable
either: the IPC contract exposes `variant_delete`
(`docs/spec.md:578`, §7.10), a public surface whose callers are not
bound by a webview disable, and the landed store layer enforces
LIB-025 there absolutely — `delete_variant` refuses `LastVariant`
before any replacement logic, "whatever the replacement names"
(`crates/eunomia-store/src/library.rs:1792-1799`; the falsifying test
`the_last_active_variant_cannot_be_deleted_whatever_the_replacement`,
`crates/eunomia-store/tests/library.rs:1014-1030`). So the card's
fork resolved to its second branch: a reachable path exists behind
the UI, and the row is scoped to it rather than marked dead.

Solution: the LIB-023/024/025 row (`docs/spec.md:475`) keeps its
requirement text intact and gains two sentences in the spec's own
idiom (requirement/section references in parens; no invented
jargon): the LIB-025 disable never fires through the UI (LIB-024 +
DB-010 make the last remaining variant always the main one), and
LIB-025 stays in force as the defensive refusal on the surfaces
behind that disabled button — `variant_delete` (7.10) and the store
layer reject deleting an instruction's last active variant even when
a replacement is named. Untouched on purpose: §3.2's D-12 row is a
dated customer-answer record (dated records are not rewritten — the
D-120 addendum posture, the T-305 precedent); §6.4's variant delete
row (`docs/spec.md:367`) states data-model behavior, makes no UI
claim, and is correct as written; the LIB-017…022 disable
enumeration (`docs/spec.md:474`) reads consistently once :475
carries the reading — the button is disabled for the last variant,
which is always the main one; `docs/manual-smoke.md`'s S4 pass note
(:440-443) already states this exact reading and is this card's
source, so it needed no edit. One-row diff; no prettier re-pad (the
cell stays shorter than the column's widest cell).

Honest boundaries: batch regime (owner instruction 2026-11-23) — no
tests run; the store-layer behavior was verified by reading the
landed code at this commit, not by executing its suite. The
`variant_delete` command itself is not yet registered (§7.10's
library commands are unlanded — D-175's record); the annotation is
normative for the contract, as the spec's other command notes are.

edits spec.md after this merge (rebase resolves).
