### D-178 — the task-id MCP returns an object, not a number — sessions must read `.result` — 2026-11-23

Problem: during the 2026-11-23 flash batch (T-288…T-321) the
orchestrator's first numbering pass called `next_id` and string-
interpolated the raw return value into 13 card titles, producing
`T-[object Object]` on the board (the numbers themselves were
consumed correctly and deterministically; no collision resulted).
Executor subagents calling the same tool for `d`-numbers would hit
the identical trap and could write `D-[object Object]` into this
ledger.

Solution: the tool returns `{"result": N}` — every caller (main
session and executors) reads `.result` at the moment of writing, as
every brief in the batch already instructed after the incident. This
entry makes the contract durable for future sessions instead of
relying on brief folklore. Recovery from a broken interpolation:
`peek` the counter to reconstruct the consumed range (the issued
numbers are consecutive), verify no board/repo collision, then re-
title — no counter correction (`set_counter` stays forbidden).

Checks: the 13 affected cards were re-titled T-288…T-300 in the
same session; all later numbering (T-301…T-321, D-161…D-178) went
through `.result` with zero recurrences.

### D-179 — T-077: the `scan_commit` command — the discovered-set SEC-003 rule, the one-transaction batch with typed non-add outcomes, and the manual-add rules shared by construction — 2026-11-23

Problem: PRJ-002's "Add selected" needs its backend (§7.10 Projects
module `scan_commit`, §8 S2, LOG-001…004): the checked "New"
repositories of a scan answer become projects in ONE transaction with
the manual add's rules (defaults, color, label) and without
duplicates. Six points were open: (1) how a path the UI sends back
from a scan ANSWER passes SEC-003 — it is neither a registered
project nor a folder picked in the dialog, and D-100 reserved exactly
this rule for this task ("folders the app itself discovered inside an
allowlisted root must not silently widen SEC-003"); (2) what "an
error on one project rolls back everything" makes of a duplicate, a
vanished folder and an excluded path; (3) how "the same rules as
manual add" is kept true past this task; (4) the journal shape for a
batch; (5) D-29's color across rows created in one transaction;
(6) the wire answer of a batch with several per-repository outcomes.

Readings chosen (Rule 1, recorded before implementation):

- **SEC-003: the discovered-set rule.** `scan_start` publishes the
  `path_key` (DB-030) of EVERY repository a COMPLETED walk reported —
  all four ALG-053 classes — into a session-scoped managed
  `ScanFindings` set that replaces the previous completed scan's set;
  a cancelled or failed scan publishes nothing and clears nothing
  (ERR-002). `scan_commit(paths)` admits a sent path iff the key of
  its OWN text and the key of its CANONICAL form are both in that set
  (the second check refuses a folder swapped in under a reported
  name); anything else is the `E_VALIDATION` rejection of the `path`
  field, raised BEFORE any disk probe. So the commit can register
  exactly what Rust itself found under a root the SEC-003 gate
  admitted — D-100's "the app itself discovered", nothing wider. The
  rejected alternative was the stateless containment rule ("any
  canonical repository root under a session pick or a registered
  project"): it needs no state, but it also admits repositories the
  walk skipped by ALG-051/ALG-050 (excluded names, depth) and any
  folder a webview cares to name inside the picked tree — a wider
  trust boundary than the feature needs. The retained set is in-memory
  session bookkeeping of the `SessionPaths` class, not persistence:
  T-076's "the scan writes nothing anywhere" keeps holding for the
  database and the filesystem. Residual, recorded honestly: the set
  lives one process; a commit is only ever sent from the result view
  the same process answered.
- **One transaction; what is an error and what is a typed outcome.**
  Any `Err` refuses the WHOLE selection and writes nothing: the
  pre-transaction gates write nothing by construction, and a failure
  inside the transaction rolls back every earlier row of the batch
  with its journal entries (the `Db::run` executor, D-037). Errors
  are: a path no completed scan reported, a folder that vanished or
  cannot be read (`E_PROJECT_UNAVAILABLE`), a folder that is no
  longer a repository root (`E_NOT_A_REPO`), an unstorable derived
  field (§6.9 `E_VALIDATION` naming the field), and every store or
  journal failure. NOT errors — typed outcomes that leave the rest of
  the selection adding: `already_added` (an active row holds the key),
  `archived` (an archived row holds it — DB-015's restore offer, the
  id rides the entry) and `excluded` (a `project_exclusions` row
  holds the key and no project does), so a re-sent or stale selection
  CONVERGES instead of failing (D-103's "typed answers, not error
  codes"; the make-operations-idempotent rule). A vanished folder is
  deliberately NOT §10's "Project skipped; the others continue" — that
  is the sync's per-project rule; the card's criterion names the
  rollback, and a result view holding a vanished row is stale as a
  whole ("Scan again" is the user's action).
- **The answer.** `ScanCommitResult { entries: Vec<ScanCommitEntry> }`
  — one entry per DISTINCT repository of the selection, in the order
  sent (which is also the `sort_order` append order). An entry is the
  `ProjectAddResult` discriminant shape `{ path, outcome, project?, existing? }`
  with `outcome` one of `"added"`, `"already_added"`, `"archived"`,
  `"excluded"`. Two spellings of one repository in one selection are
  one entry (first occurrence wins). An empty selection is the typed
  no-op `entries: []` — nothing written, nothing journaled.
- **"The same rules as manual add", by construction.** The per-project
  step has ONE implementation in `commands.rs` and both add flows call
  it: `ProjectFields::derive` (S1's "Fields" step: the folder name,
  DB-042's label, the empty description, the key and the stored path
  text), `WriteDefaults::load` (the PRJ-012 copy of the four
  `default.*` keys, read inside the operation's transaction),
  `ColorOccupancy` (D-29 over the ACTIVE projects' colors, updated as
  rows are created) and `register_project` (color → `create` → the
  `project.added` entry inside the same transaction; the unreachable
  duplicate race converges to the existing row). `project_add_manual`
  is migrated onto the same functions in this change — a second copy
  of the rules would be the drift the card forbids. The scan commit
  writes `added_via = "scan"` (§6.2).
- **The journal.** ONE `project.added` entry per created row —
  info/user/ok, entity and `project_id` naming the new row — inside
  the transaction (D-051). Not one bulk entry: LOG-001…004's bulk
  exception is the assignments' own parenthetical, and an added
  project is an entity with its own id that the Activity window's
  project filter attributes (the D-115 reorder case was ONE fact about
  many rows; N adds are N facts). Typed non-add outcomes journal
  nothing.
- **D-29 across a batch.** The color is decided per created row
  against the active set as it stands inside the transaction — the
  batch's earlier rows count — so PRJ-010's "for 12 projects in a row,
  colors do not repeat" holds inside ONE commit. `ColorOccupancy`
  hands `pick_color` the counts relative to the least-used member
  (the only thing the rule reads, so the pick is identical), which
  keeps the batch linear in its rows instead of re-listing the table
  per row.
- **After the commit.** §6.9's write-access probe runs per added row
  on the blocking pool, never inside the transaction (the D-096
  probe-order rule), and its verdict rides the entry's
  `write_access_warning` exactly as in the manual add; ONE watch
  refresh through `refresh_after_mutation` (never fatal, D-144); the
  DB-022 recalculation rides the commit hook.
- **Gate order.** SYS-005 (`scan_commit` changes projects: the
  `E_SYNC_RUNNING` refusal during a sync, the `project_add_manual`
  gate) → the database (the honest no-database answer before any
  probe) → the SEC-003 discovered set, by the sent text's key — the
  same pass collapses the in-request duplicates, so no disk probe
  runs twice for one repository → canonicalization (a vanished folder
  is `E_PROJECT_UNAVAILABLE` with the OS facts; a non-UTF-8 form is
  the D-086 encoding rejection) → the canonical-form membership and
  the second collapse, by the resolved identity → the `.git` root
  check (`find_git_root` must answer the folder itself) → the §6.9
  fields (a rejection also carries the repository's `path` param, so
  the UI can mark the row) → the transaction.
- **Logging.** One failure edge, `logging::scan_commit_failed` (the
  D-096 law); the typed outcomes and the empty selection log nothing.

Solution (per file):

- `src-tauri/src/commands.rs` — the new-project rules became four
  shared items: `ProjectFields::derive` (S1's "Fields" step plus the
  DB-030 key and the stored path text), `WriteDefaults::load` (the
  PRJ-012 copy, read inside the transaction),
  `ColorOccupancy` (`from_colors`/`load`/`pick`/`record`: D-29's
  counts over the active set, handing `pick_color` the counts
  relative to the least-used member so a batch is linear),
  `register_project` (color → `create` → the `project.added` entry
  and its D-051 mirror call; the unreachable duplicate race answers
  `Registered::Existing`). `project_add_manual` was migrated onto
  them in the SAME change — its transaction closure is now the DB-015
  check plus the two shared calls — so no second copy of the rules
  exists; its wire contract and gate order are unchanged (the ten
  T-074 IPC tests and four unit pins pass untouched).
  `AddedProject::from_store`, `ExistingProject::of` (new
  constructor), `probe_target_name`, `write_access_warning`,
  `repo_lookup_failed` and `reject_during_sync` became `pub(crate)`
  for the scan module.
- `src-tauri/src/scan.rs` — `ScanFindings` (the session's discovered
  set: `publish` replaces, `contains` answers a key, `admits` composes
  it with DB-030's key, poison recovered like the session allowlist);
  `publish_findings` in the completed
  arm of `scan_start_with` (the honest `ScanFindingsMissing`
  fallback when the state is absent); the wire DTOs
  `ScanCommitResult` (one field, `entries`) and `ScanCommitEntry`
  (`path`, `outcome`, `project?`, `existing?`); `scan_commit` →
  `scan_commit_impl` (the gate order above) with its helpers
  (`CommitSlot`, the three entry builders, `is_own_root`,
  `rejected_unreported_path`, `field_rejection_of`,
  `managed_findings`). The per-row write-access warnings are
  POSITIONAL — one slot per created row, a writable row's `None`
  included — since the round-1 review (below). Module docs gained the
  rule's section and lost the "nothing is persisted anywhere in this
  module" sentence, which the writer made false.
- `src-tauri/src/lib.rs` — `scan::scan_commit` registered between
  its two siblings; `scan::ScanFindings::new()` managed beside the
  cancel slot, in every mode.
- `src-tauri/src/logging.rs` — the one failure edge
  `logging::scan_commit_failed` (`eunomia::scan`, error level, the
  `project_add_failed` shape) and its facade test.
- `src/bindings.ts` regenerated through the pin test: `scanCommit`
  (`paths: string[]`), `ScanCommitResult_Serialize`/
  `ScanCommitEntry_Serialize`, and the re-mirrored doc comments of
  the manual add's DTOs.
- The mock chain (forced by the D-154 loud-drift rule — a
  regenerated `bindings.ts` fails `pnpm run typecheck` until a mock
  member with the exact signature exists; D-115 and D-153 record the
  same forced scope): `src/ipc/mock/state.ts` gains `scanFindings`,
  `mock/commands.ts` the `scanCommit` member and the shared
  `appendProjectRow` step (`projectAddManual` migrated onto it, the
  Rust refactor's mirror), `scanStart` publishing on completion;
  `contract.ts` re-exports the two wire types; `mode.spec.ts`'s
  shipped-set pin lists `scanCommit`; `commands.spec.ts` gains the
  mock's suite. The mock models the discovered-set rule and the
  typed outcomes; its header records that the filesystem gates are
  not modelled (D-108's limits posture).
- Docs (Rule 11): `ARCHITECTURE.md` (the module row and the command
  paragraph no longer say the commit has not landed),
  `docs/manual-smoke.md` (the registered-command lists; the S2
  "Add selected" pass condition names the manual-add rules and the
  "found by scan" origin the UI will have to show).

Tests (28 Rust + 5 TS, all through public APIs; oracles are the
spec's own literals, the store read back, and core's own
`pick_color`):

- The card's acceptance pair, in `scan_tests.rs`. The duplicates
  test scans, commits three repositories, rescans (all `known`),
  RE-SENDS the same selection — three `already_added` entries naming
  the rows the first commit created, the census unchanged at
  `(3, 0, 3)` — and finally sends the empty selection (no entries,
  census unchanged). The rollback is proven in two staged shapes: a
  trigger refuses the THIRD row's INSERT after two rows and two
  entries were written inside the transaction — the census is
  `(0, 0, 0)` afterwards, and the control shows the first two commit
  cleanly without the third; and the SECOND row's journal insert is
  refused — the row and the first entry are both gone. A third error
  needs no staging (Unix): D-079's control-named repository among the
  selection answers `E_VALIDATION` naming `label` and carrying
  `path`, nothing is written, and the two sound repositories then
  commit.
- The rules: every field of the manual add read back through the
  store (the canonical path, the folder name, literal DB-042 labels,
  a palette member, `added_via = scan`, `sort_order` 2–4 behind a
  seeded row, the PRJ-012 copy from CHANGED `default.*`, the stored
  rows agreeing, three `project.added` entries in sent order naming
  their rows); PRJ-010's literal inside ONE commit (twelve rows,
  twelve colors; the thirteenth repeats); and Rule 6's large input —
  600 repositories through one commit: one row, entry and journal
  line each, the DB-005 order equal to the sent order, 600 distinct
  ids, exactly 50 rows per palette color (no timing assertion) — the
  selection sent with N ≫ R, every path five times cycled (3000 sent
  paths for 600 reported), costing nothing observable.
- The second collapse: two REPORTED names that resolve to one folder
  (Unix: `beta` replaced by a symlink onto `alpha` after the scan)
  answer one entry and one row — without the resolved-identity
  collapse the same selection answers `added` then `already_added`
  for one repository.
- The typed outcomes: archived answers `archived` with the row's id,
  excluded answers `excluded`, known answers `already_added`, and
  the fresh repository in the same selection is added (census
  `(3, 1, 1)`); one repository sent twice — once under its
  trailing-separator spelling — is one entry keeping its first
  position, while a dot segment is the SEC-003 rejection.
- The gates: a REAL repository created after the scan under the
  picked root is refused (`E_VALIDATION` naming the path and the
  policy) together with the sound path in its selection; a path that
  exists nowhere is refused the same way with NO OS fact — the text
  gate precedes every probe; a blank entry; a cancelled scan
  publishes nothing and clears nothing; a folder that vanished since
  the scan answers `E_PROJECT_UNAVAILABLE` with the path and the OS
  code; a folder whose own `.git` is gone answers `E_NOT_A_REPO`
  even when an ancestor is still a repository; (Unix) a reported
  name swapped for a symlink out of the root meets the SEC-003
  rejection naming the folder it resolves to; during a sync the
  spec-literal `E_SYNC_RUNNING` envelope, input-independent, and the
  same selection lands after it; without a database `NoDatabase`;
  without the findings state `ScanFindingsMissing` for the scan AND
  the commit, while a cancelled scan needs no state.
- After the commit: four rows whose read-only targets sit SECOND and
  LAST, each behind a writable one, and the warning vector asserted
  whole (`[None, Some, None, Some]`) — a warning sliding onto a
  neighbouring row shows, which a first-row-only shape cannot (the
  round-1 review found exactly that slide); and the
  `add_manual_watch_app` proofs mirrored for the batch over the REAL
  watch service — exactly one full pass for the created rows, none
  for the typed outcomes and the empty selection.
- Unit: the discovered set admits exactly the published keys, by
  DB-030's rule, and each publication replaces the set (plus the
  Unix unkeyable-probe arm) in `scan.rs`; the value of
  `ProjectFields::derive` and its label edge, the reduced-multiset
  pick equal to core's own `pick_color` over the UNREDUCED multiset
  (400 deterministic occupancy vectors × 7 ids — the independent
  oracle), and twelve rows taking twelve colors, in `commands.rs`;
  the failure line carrying its code and payload in `logging.rs`. The
  registration pin grew `scan::scan_commit` and
  `scan::ScanFindings::new()`.
- TS (`describe('scanCommit')` in `commands.spec.ts`): the discovery
  added through the shared step with `added_via = 'scan'` and one
  journal entry; an unreported path rejected with nothing added
  (and nothing reported before any completed scan); the typed
  outcomes plus a converging re-send; duplicate spellings collapsed
  and the empty selection; a cancelled scan publishing nothing.

Mutation checks (19, scripted apply-run-restore on the committed
tree, ONE mutation per run; each run executes the 46 tests of the
scan and shared-rules suites and prints how many it ran, so a result
parser that misses failures cannot pass for a kill). 17 die, each by
the tests meant to catch it:

- a failed row swallowed as a typed outcome → both rollback tests;
- a created row's color never recorded, and the pick over an empty
  multiset → the two color tests and the large selection (the latter
  mutation also the equivalence unit test);
- the SEC-003 text gate dropped → the unreported-path test (a path
  that exists nowhere is answered as unavailable once a probe runs)
  and the dot-segment arm;
- the canonical-form gate dropped → the swapped-folder test;
- a cancelled scan publishing an empty set → the cancelled-scan test
  and the missing-state test;
- the exclusion check dropped → the typed-outcomes test;
  `added_via = manual` → four tests;
- the own-root gate dropped → the lost-`.git` test; the SYS-005 gate
  dropped → the during-sync test;
- the resolved-identity collapse dropped → the two-names-one-folder
  test;
- a field rejection without `path` → the label test; a duplicate
  answered as an error → the re-send, the typed-outcome test and the
  no-row watch proof;
- the write-access probe skipped → the warning test; the watch
  refresh dropped → the one-pass proof;
- the created row's journal entry skipped → ten tests; a completed
  scan publishing nothing → twenty.

Two survive BY NATURE, recorded rather than hidden: the text-key
collapse dropped alone changes only COST (the second collapse still
converges every outcome; no probe-count seam exists to observe it —
the bound holds by construction, every admitted key being in the
findings), and the color recorded before the journal insert changes
nothing observable (any earlier failure aborts the transaction) —
which is exactly why that record is structural.

Two harness lessons from this matrix, recorded because each bit once.
The first run under-reported: its result parser missed failures with
single-digit ordinals (`( 1/43)`), which made two unit tests look
surviving under a mutation that directly killed them. And a mutation
must disable an `if cond { push }` with `true ||` — `false ||` is a
NO-OP (`false || x` still evaluates `x`), which silently turned a
"collapse dropped" mutation into the identity and made one run
report a one-test kill where thirty should have failed; a restart

### D-180 — T-271: D-142's "pre-migration copies' uncapped accumulation" follow-up closed by owner ruling as already discharged — D-129/T-253's age rule governed `pre-migration-*` before the line was written (D-038's own addendum said so); D-046's "retention stays uncapped" parenthetical annotated beside it — 2026-11-23

Problem: the card (source: D-142's follow-ups paragraph and D-038;
observation T-256) read: pre-migration copies accumulate without
limit, the first real v1→v2 upgrade wave will make it observable in
production, the cause is unbounded growth of `db-backups/` — the
options were a retention owner "by analogy with D-129 for protective
copies (an age window, the newest protected)" or consciously leaving
it; the owner's decision. The owner ruled on 2026-11-23: close the
card as already resolved — the premise is stale.

Solution: closed, no code change. The card's "by analogy with D-129"
framing was itself the misconception: D-129 is not an analogue of a
missing retention, it IS the retention of these copies — the
`pre-migration-*` scheme (D-038) is one of the two protective kinds
that decision put under the age rule, together with `pre-recovery-*`
(D-049). Verified in this tree before writing (Rule 2):

- _What covers the copies._ `cleanup_db_backups` dispatches on
  `PRE_MIGRATION_PREFIX` = `"pre-migration-v"` (`retention.rs:191`,
  the dispatch at :384-385) into `ProtectiveCopyKind::PreMigration`;
  the window is `PROTECTIVE_COPY_WINDOW`, 7 days (`retention.rs:206`);
  a copy is deleted iff its name stamp is strictly older than
  `now − 7d` (`retention.rs:407`) and it is not the newest of its
  kind — max stamp, the variant breaking ties (`retention.rs:415-421`,
  the skip at :426). The pass is best-effort: an unreadable directory
  or an unremovable file logs a `warn` through the facade and the
  pass moves on (`retention.rs:357-363`, :449-451).
- _Trigger (corrected during this task)._ The pass has a single
  trigger — the end of every successful `Db::open` after the
  migration run (`db.rs:367`); the LOG-006 daily tick deliberately
  does NOT run it (D-129, `DECISIONS.md:11147`, `:11166-11171`). The
  daily loop (`cleanup_loop`, `retention.rs:119-148`) calls only
  `run_once`, which prunes the journal and the sync runs
  (`retention.rs:131`, :172) — `db.rs:367` is the pass's only
  production call site. One trigger suffices for the card's premise:
  a pre-migration copy is created only inside the migration run
  (`vacuum_into_backup`, `storage.rs:739`, called from `migrate` at
  :619, which `run_migrations` calls at :554), and `Db::open` calls
  that run at `db.rs:352`, immediately before the pass — so every
  copy a successful open writes is followed by a pass in that same
  open. The rest wait for the next successful open, on D-129's
  recorded boundaries: a copy whose migration run then fails (the
  copy is written before each step, `storage.rs:617-621`, and the
  failed step propagates out of the open, `db.rs:352-358` — the
  pass at :367 is never reached; `DECISIONS.md:11173-11177`) or a
  copy crossing the 7-day line mid-run ("retired at the next open,
  not at the crossing moment", `DECISIONS.md:11172-11173`).
- _The follow-up line was stale when written._ The primary proof is
  D-038's own dated addendum (2026-11-21, T-253/D-129,
  `DECISIONS.md:1500-1506`): "the app-layer retention this entry
  deferred has landed — `retention.rs` retires pre-migration copies
  older than 7 days at every successful `Db::open`, newest of the
  kind protected". D-142's line cites "D-038's known open"
  (`DECISIONS.md:13665-13667`) — the open at `:1457-1461`
  ("Retention: pre-migration copies accumulate without a cap") had
  been closed by that addendum first. Secondary corroboration, the
  commit order: `90dd3ec` (2026-11-21T12:29:52-08:00, T-253)
  introduces both `PROTECTIVE_COPY_WINDOW` and the `### D-129`
  heading; `c408cbc` (2026-11-22T02:50:30-08:00, T-256) introduces
  `### D-142` — roughly fourteen hours apart. The line was written
  without checking `retention.rs` or D-038's addendum.
- _Pinned._ `a_successful_open_runs_the_protective_copy_retention_pass`
  (`db_tests.rs:2813`) seeds a 12-day-old `pre-migration-v1-*` and a
  10-day-old `pre-migration-v3-*` copy (`:2826-2837`), opens, and
  pins the verdict (`:2844-2855`): the aged non-newest copy goes, the
  newest of the kind survives past the window (versions do not split
  the kind), the daily scheme is untouched.
- _Residual — by design, accepted with the ruling._ Exactly the
  newest `pre-migration-*` copy of the kind is never deleted
  (`retention.rs:426`) — among the names the creating scheme writes.
  It survives indefinitely, so the permanent footprint of
  scheme-written copies is bounded at one database-sized file per
  install (a `VACUUM INTO` copy of the database), plus — for at most
  7 days — any younger copies. A name the pass cannot date
  (hand-renamed, foreign) is left alone as well, by D-129's
  conservative half (`retention.rs:274-281`). This is D-129's
  protected-newest rule (the card's "новейшая защищена"), and it
  operationalizes D-038's "never delete the copy UPD-004 points at":
  the pointer is always the newest pre-migration copy
  (`DECISIONS.md:1503-1505`). The ERR-001 daily-copy count rule
  (D-046) still never touches these copies: `prune_daily_backups`
  counts and deletes `daily-*` names only (`storage.rs:1038-1059`,
  its `is_daily_copy_name` filter at :1044), so the assertion
  message "the retention never deletes pre-migration copies"
  (`db_tests.rs:2091`,
  inside `the_eighth_daily_copy_through_the_db_seam_keeps_the_last_seven`,
  :2055) is a claim about the count pass, not about the T-253 pass.
- _Ledger footprint._ D-046's "pre-migration retention stays uncapped
  per D-038" parenthetical (`DECISIONS.md:2257-2259`) is no longer
  true either, but for a different reason than D-142's line: it was
  true when D-046 was written (2026-11-18) and was superseded when
  D-129 landed (2026-11-21), whereas D-142's line was false from the
  day it was written. A dated addendum beside it points here (the
  D-173/T-320 posture — no separate D-number for it). D-142's line is
  left as written (a historical record stays as written); this entry
  is its discharge record.
- _Stale claims remaining in code, out of this card's md-only scope —
  tracked as a board follow-up._ `storage.rs:896-897` ("the
  pre-migration copies are outside it and accumulate uncapped") and
  the `db_tests.rs:2091` assertion message above. Neither is edited
  here: both are `.rs` files, and touching them would turn this into
  a code task.

Checks: md-only diff (`DECISIONS.md` — this entry and the D-046
addendum); no code, no test suites run — the md-only regime this

2026-11-22; this file records no such date, so none is asserted

The task brief's first statement of the trigger — "`Db::open` plus a

### D-181 — CI 45235995817: the macOS watch batteries' startup race — FSEvents can deliver the pre-spawn fixture writes after the stream starts; the batteries now converge the startup before the act — 2026-11-23

Problem: CI run 45235995817 (push 16a1c51..fd00673, fd00673 =
origin/main): ubuntu-latest, ubuntu-24.04 and windows-latest green
(and the local ubuntu `cargo test --workspace` had been green before
the push), red on both macOS legs — with DIFFERENT test subsets per
leg, the first fact that points at a race rather than a deterministic
platform behavior:

1. `test-matrix (macos-15)` — 2 failed:
   `ipc_tests::an_external_edit_marks_the_project_externally_modified_without_writing_anything`
   panicked at ipc_tests.rs:6542:14 — `the external edit must be
reported: Empty` (the `Debug` of `TryRecvError::Empty`: the wire
   held no event after the pass the test waited for), and
   `ipc_tests::an_archived_row_never_carries_watch_flags_even_from_a_stale_cache_entry`
   at :6889:5 — `assertion 'left == right' failed: no further pass
ran — the stale cache entry is the premise`, `left: 2, right: 1`.
2. `test-matrix (macos-15-intel)` — 1 failed:
   `ipc_tests::an_unavailable_row_never_carries_watch_flags_even_from_a_stale_cache_entry`
   at :7015:5 — the same `left: 2, right: 1` shape.

Hypotheses ruled out first (the spawn brief's list):

- T-304/D-171's seam (`library_seed_error_for_tests`, the batch's
  helper consolidation) — REFUTED by the log shape: its non-`Sql`
  arms panic with documented wording naming the arm and embedding the
  error's `Display`, and neither failure text matches; the failing
  lines (:6542, :6889, :7015) sit AFTER `spawn_service`, while the
  seam runs during seeding, which succeeded (the seeds'
  `.expect("seeding the assignment through the repository must
work")` never fired). T-289's `sync_runs_app_error_for_tests`
  Member-panic: same refutation. The cookie 0.18.3 bump
  (Cargo.lock's only change in the range): the watch batteries never
  touch cookies. Decisive negative fact: the three failing tests'
  bodies, the watch helpers (`wait_for_watch_passes`,
  `listen_file_changed`, `WATCH_DEBOUNCE`) and `file_watch.rs` itself
  are byte-identical across 16a1c51..fd00673 (`git diff` on the range
  touches `dirty_recalc.rs` (+70, a `#[cfg(test)]` fn),
  `dirty_recalc_tests.rs` and `ipc_tests.rs`' seeding helpers and
  comments only) — the batch changed timing, not watch behavior.

Diagnosis — a TEST platform-assumption bug (D-160's class), no
production defect: the batteries write their fixtures BEFORE
`spawn_service` and assume those writes are invisible to the watcher
forever. On Linux that is a structural guarantee (inotify queues an
event only after the watch attaches). On macOS it is only a
probability: the FSEvents stream is bounded by
`kFSEventStreamEventIdSinceNow` (notify 8.2.2 `src/fsevent.rs:289`) —
the greatest event id the DAEMON has assigned at creation, not the
wall clock of the write — and the daemon assigns an id when it
processes the change, so a write that completed just before the
stream's birth can carry a later id and be delivered after it
(`latency: 0.0` + `NoDefer`, `src/fsevent.rs:290-291`, make the
delivery prompt, never earlier). The delivered event's path is the
file itself (`FileEvents` flag), so it passes the watcher's name
filter (`is_watched_name`, watcher.rs:792-799), routes through
`by_path`, and lands as ONE extra debounced partial pass — silent
(the re-read reproduces the same verdict) but counted. That single
extra pass explains all three failures exactly: in the stale-cache
tests it lands between `wait_for_watch_passes(1)` and the exact
`pass_count() == 1` assert (→ `left: 2`); in the external-edit test
it lands before the edit, so `wait_for_watch_passes(2)` returns on
the NOISE pass — which read the still-clean file and emitted nothing
— and the following `try_recv` finds an empty channel (→ `Empty`).
Which test it breaks is a per-leg coin flip on delivery latency —
matching the observed disjoint subsets. The pre-batch run 45134955298
was green on the same coin.

Solution — the batteries now converge the startup before the act
(ipc_tests.rs):

1. `converge_startup_watch(app, target) -> u64`: a CAUSAL settle, not
   a sleep — rewrites the target with its own just-read bytes and
   waits for the partial pass that rewrite itself provokes. The
   settle write is issued strictly after the stream's birth and a
   stream delivers in event-id order, so when the settle pass runs,
   every earlier fixture event has been delivered (before the
   settle's own event or coalesced into its debounced batch). The
   settle changes no verdict (same bytes — the diff contract stays
   silent) and is the TEST's fixture hand, not the service's (OUT-014
   stays pinned). The return value — the settled pass count — becomes
   the baseline the act-window assertions measure against
   (`pass_count() == settled` instead of `== 1`; `settled + n`
   instead of absolute slots).
2. `next_flagged_changes(events)`: the conditional report wait this
   file has called its canonical post-pass pattern since run
   45009611489 (the macos-15-intel legs), extracted to one spelling —
   the two inline copies refactored onto it. Collects the first
   change-carrying batch with a 5 s deadline; an empty return fails
   the caller's `assert_eq!` (never swallows).
3. Applied to the three red tests plus the two same-shape latent
   siblings the sweep found (`deleting_a_synced_target_file…`,
   `a_scheme_b_project_reports_edits_and_deletion…` — absolute
   `wait_for(2/3)` slots + `try_recv().expect`); the
   between-syncs/`refresh_after_sync` battery's one remaining
   `try_recv().expect` (:8716 pre-fix) moved onto the conditional
   wait (the 45009611489 race applies to it directly).

No production line touched, no `#[cfg]`/`#[ignore]` gating
(the 23ab989/45064887502 symlink-test gate stays the exception for a
test whose SUBJECT is the delivery itself), no assertion weakened:
the exact-count asserts still pin "no further pass ran" — now against
the settled baseline instead of a platform-wrong absolute.

Falsifiability (Rule 4; mutations observed red, then reverted):
poisoning the settle to append extra bytes makes the settle pass flip
the verdict and the very next silence assert fail ("a matching file
emits nothing") — the settle provably runs and its re-read reaches
the wire; triggering an extra `Refresh` inside the archived test's
act window fails its baseline assert with `left: 3, right: 2` — the
exact CI failure shape, still caught; making `next_flagged_changes`
return early fails the external-edit assert with `left: []` — the
conditional wait cannot pass vacuously.

Honest boundaries: macOS cannot be executed here. The mechanism is
proven from the sources (notify 8.2.2 fsevent.rs:289-291 cited
above; the name filter and routing read in-tree), from the log shape
(disjoint per-leg subsets; `Empty` exactly where a noise-consumed
slot puts it; `left: 2` exactly where an extra silent pass puts it),
and from the battery's own history (45009611489 and 45064887502 —
the same FSEvents nondeterminism family, already documented in this
file's comments). If the diagnosis is right, both macOS legs go
green and stay green; if it is wrong the same panics recur and the
settle's doc names the suspect (a fixture event delivered out of
order, later than the settle pass — bounded by the stream's in-order
delivery, the residual risk this entry accepts).

Swept for siblings (the watch battery, `wait_for_watch_passes`
callers): `projects_list_carries_the_watch_service_verdicts…` and
`a_healthy_watch_set…` assert columns after the startup full pass
(noise-proof — the verdict comes from the pass, not the wire);
`an_unavailable_project_is_unwatched…` asserts silence with settle
sleeps and ends in the conditional wait; the long-debounce
fire-and-forget test holds every fixture event past the test's
lifetime by construction; the add-manual/mutation-refresh family
spawns over an empty watch set (pre-add noise routes to nothing) and
subsumes file events behind queued `Refresh`es (file_watch.rs's
coalescing); `synced_world_between_syncs` drains 300 ms at the
source before any caller's baseline; the symlink test is already
macOS-gated (D-181 changes nothing there).

Checks: `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2 cargo fmt --check`,
`CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2 cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets
-- -D warnings`, `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2 cargo test --workspace` (37
suites; the src-tauri lib suite: 562 passed, 0 failed) and
`pnpm run format:check` — all green on ubuntu. The two macOS legs
are CI's to confirm on the merge push.

Iteration-2 addendum (CI 45245718226, same dedicated subagent,
2026-11-23): the merge push turned the macos-15 (arm) leg green —
and every other leg and job — but macos-15-intel failed the SAME
`an_unavailable_row…` test at the post-fix ipc_tests.rs:7114 with
`left: 3, right: 2`: the residual this entry's boundaries named, in
its likeliest concrete shape. v1's `wait_for_watch_passes(before +
1)` proves only that A pass ran after the rewrite — not that it was
the rewrite's OWN: a pending fixture delivery can satisfy the wait
first, and the probe's own pass (or a further leftover) then lands
after the baseline was read, inside the act window. Plain in-order
stream delivery suffices — no out-of-order daemon behavior
required; the arm leg simply never drew that interleave, the slower
virtualized intel runner did.

Hardening: `converge_startup_watch` is now a DRAINING convergence
loop. Each round rewrites the target with its own just-read bytes
(verdict-neutral as before), waits for the next pass, and then holds
a 300 ms quiescence window (the file's canonical settle span, 7 ×
the 40 ms test debounce); ANY further pass inside the window is a
straggler — absorbed, and the round restarts with a fresh probe.
The baseline is returned only after a window in which NO pass ran at
all: quiescent, not merely moved. Rounds are bounded (5); exceeding
the bound panics naming the last observed count — a watcher that
never goes quiet is a pathology to hear about, not to wait away.
Every call site shares the hardened helper: the exact-count
premises (the archived/unavailable stale-cache tests — the ones that
actually need quiescence) get it directly; the event-asserting
batteries (external edit, deletion, scheme B, the conformance site)
were already tolerant — a straggler can shift which pass a
`wait_for` observes, but `next_flagged_changes`' 5 s conditional
window still collects the event — so no per-site change beyond the
shared helper and the comments it made plural.

Falsifiability, iteration 2 (all mutations observed, then reverted):
a deterministic straggler injected right after v1's baseline read
(`FilesChanged` for the target through the state's own trigger —
the same interleave the intel leg drew) reproduces the production
failure on ubuntu exactly — `left: 3, right: 2` on the same assert;
the SAME straggler injected inside the hardened drain's first round
is absorbed (round 2 re-arms, the test passes with a quiescent
baseline); injecting it every round exhausts the bound and panics
with the named count (11 passes at round 5). The differential
(v1+straggler red vs drain+straggler green) is the fix's local
proof.

Tightened boundary: after the drain, the failure requires a
delivery that out-lates the LAST 300 ms quiet window and lands
inside the act window, while every physical write it could carry is
at least the drain's full span old (≥ 300 ms–1.5 s behind a daemon
that otherwise delivered five quiet rounds' worth promptly). The
observed intel stragglers landed within sub-second windows of their
writes — the population the drain can still miss is, on the
evidence, empty — and the bound keeps that claim falsifiable
instead of infinitely patient. Checks re-run green on ubuntu:
fmt, clippy `--workspace --all-targets -D warnings`, `cargo test
--workspace` (37 suites), `format:check`. The macOS legs are CI's
to confirm on the second merge push.

### D-182 — T-323: four dev-dependency advisories closed — happy-dom by direct upgrade, glob/minimatch by parent-scoped pnpm overrides living in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` (the pinned pnpm 12 ignores package.json's `pnpm` field) — 2026-11-23

Problem: `pnpm audit` (full) was red with four advisories, every one on a
dev-only path — reproduced bit-for-bit at the start of T-323 (exit 1:
2 high, 2 moderate), matching the 2026-11-23 project review (P2-2):

| Package   | Installed | Advisory (severity)            | Patched  | Paths from the root                                                                                   |
| --------- | --------- | ------------------------------ | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| happy-dom | 20.14.6   | GHSA-834v-8h66-3h79 (High)     | >=21.0.4 | `happy-dom`; `vitest > happy-dom`                                                                     |
| happy-dom | 20.14.6   | GHSA-c8p4-j97h-3vg8 (High)     | >=21.0.0 | the same two paths                                                                                    |
| glob      | 13.0.7    | GHSA-3g3m-2fjr-6pw4 (Moderate) | >=14.0.2 | `@vue/test-utils > js-beautify > glob`                                                                |
| minimatch | 10.2.6    | GHSA-g3hv-75wg-m249 (Moderate) | >=11.0.1 | `@vue/test-utils > js-beautify > editorconfig > minimatch`; the same chain through `glob > minimatch` |

Each path starts at a devDependency (`happy-dom`, `vitest`,
`@vue/test-utils`), so the runtime `dependencies` (`@tauri-apps/api`,
`pinia`, `vue`, `vue-i18n`) were never on a vulnerable path, and
`pnpm audit --prod` is clean after the change. SEC-010 names the CI
audit, and a red full audit would have blocked the gate planned as T-228.

Solution — the mechanism follows what the consumers declare, read from the
installed manifests and the registry rather than assumed:

1. `happy-dom`: direct upgrade, package.json devDependency `^20` →
   `^21.0.4`. vitest 4.1.12 declares `happy-dom` as an optional peer with
   range `*` (`node_modules/vitest/package.json`:
   `peerDependencies.happy-dom`, `peerDependenciesMeta.happy-dom.optional`),
   so one direct upgrade covers both audit paths — the lockfile's vitest
   entry now reads `(happy-dom@21.0.4)`. The floor is the patched version
   of the stricter advisory (vulnerable `>=17.0.0 <=21.0.3`); a bare `^21`
   would still admit 21.0.0–21.0.3. Resolved to 21.0.4, also the
   registry's latest (`engines.node >=20`; the project runs Node 22).
2. `glob`: override `js-beautify>glob: ^14.0.2`. No parent upgrade
   exists — js-beautify 2.0.3 is the latest release (`pnpm view
js-beautify version`) and declares `glob: ^13.0.6`; @vue/test-utils
   2.6.0 (also latest) declares `js-beautify: ^2.0.0`; and glob has no
   patched 13.x (vulnerable `>=9.0.0 <=14.0.1`). Resolved to 14.0.6.
3. `minimatch`: override `editorconfig>minimatch: ^11.0.1`. editorconfig
   3.0.2 is the newest release js-beautify's `editorconfig: ^3.0.2` admits
   and declares `minimatch: ~10.2.4`. editorconfig 4.0.1 already depends
   on `minimatch: ~11.0.5` — the major the override selects — but sits
   outside that range. Resolved to 11.0.9, the instance the tree already
   carried for `@typescript-eslint/typescript-estree`, now shared by all
   three consumers.

Both overrides are scoped to the parent on purpose. A bare `minimatch`
override would also rewrite eslint's own edges — `@eslint/config-array`
0.21.2 and `@eslint/eslintrc` 3.3.7 both declare `minimatch: ^3.1.5` —
which the advisory does not reach (vulnerable `>=7.0.0 <11.0.1`); the
resolved `minimatch@3.1.5` is unchanged. No `glob>minimatch` entry is
needed: glob 14 declares the 11.x line itself (`^11.0.5` in the installed
14.0.6; `^11.0.0` in the registry manifests of 14.0.0–14.0.2), and
resolution takes the highest match.

Addendum (2026-11-24, T-340): the eslint half of the scoping
rationale above no longer holds of the tree — eslint 10.15.0 dropped
`@eslint/eslintrc` and its `@eslint/config-array` 0.23.6 now takes
`minimatch: ^11`, so no `minimatch@3.1.5` instance remains and the
"eslint's own edges" reason for scoping the override has nothing left
to protect (verified with `pnpm why minimatch` and
`pnpm why @eslint/eslintrc`). The overrides themselves stay: their
consumers are the `@vue/test-utils > js-beautify > glob` and
`… > js-beautify > editorconfig > minimatch` chains, which did not
move. `pnpm-workspace.yaml`'s comment is updated to say so, and the
entry's text above stays as written (the dated-record posture).

Rule 1 — the brief's mechanism assumption, resolved before coding. The
spawn brief named `pnpm.overrides` in package.json as "the likely
mechanism". That is the pre-12 location: the project pins
`packageManager: pnpm@12.6.0` (D-018), which no longer reads the field.
Verified on a scratch copy of `package.json` + `pnpm-lock.yaml` with
`pnpm install --lockfile-only`:

```
[WARN] The "pnpm" field in package.json is no longer read by pnpm. The
following keys were ignored: "pnpm.overrides". See https://pnpm.io/settings
for the new home of each setting.
```

with a 0-line lockfile delta — glob 13.0.7 and minimatch 10.2.6 unchanged,
the audit still red. The pnpm 12 documentation agrees (pnpm.io/configuring:
"pnpm does not read settings from the `pnpm` field of `package.json`";
`overrides` is documented under "Settings (pnpm-workspace.yaml)", with the
selector rule "`qar@1>zoo` will only override the `zoo` dependency of
`qar@1`"). The same probe with the overrides in a new root
`pnpm-workspace.yaml` produced exactly the delta below. pnpm 12.6.0 ships
as a native binary with no readable JS, so the install probe — not a
source read — is the citation. The new file carries settings only, with no
`packages` key. In pnpm's own model that is still a workspace — the file
"defines the root of the workspace", and "if the `packages` field is
omitted, only the root package is included in the workspace"
(pnpm.io/settings#packages) — so what is absent is multi-package
semantics, not workspace mode. D-018's "pnpm settings would go into
`pnpm-workspace.yaml` if ever needed" is the clause this entry exercises;
the other half of its guard — no workspace packages, Turborepo or tsdown,
nothing here adopts monorepo tooling — keeps its meaning (wording
corrected after the round-1 review, P3-1).

Lockfile delta (`pnpm install`; package.json +1/−1, pnpm-lock.yaml
+22/−26, nothing else moved): the `overrides:` block is recorded in the
lockfile, so CI's `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` enforces it; the
importer's `happy-dom` specifier and vitest's peer suffix and
`optionalDependencies.happy-dom`; `glob@13.0.7` → `glob@14.0.6`;
`path-scurry@2.0.2` → `path-scurry@3.0.0` (glob 14's own `^3.0.0` — the
one package the card does not name whose version moved);
`minimatch@10.2.6` leaves the tree (its `brace-expansion@5.0.13` stays,
11.0.9 uses it too); `happy-dom@20.14.6` → `happy-dom@21.0.4`;
js-beautify's and editorconfig's edges. "Regeneration" here is the
re-resolution of the changed edges from the existing lockfile, not a
from-scratch re-resolve — that would bump every package and exceed the
card. Operational note: an incremental `pnpm install` leaves the
superseded directories in `node_modules/.pnpm` until a fresh install
(unreferenced by `node_modules/.pnpm/lock.yaml`; `pnpm why` already
resolves only the new versions) — not a sign that the override missed.

Compatibility evidence — the risk an override carries is "a major the
consumer never declared", so both were exercised, not assumed:

- Exposure. In this graph `glob` and `editorconfig` are loaded only by
  js-beautify's CLI: its two CLI files are the only ones in the package
  requiring either (`js/lib/cli.js`, which all three bins load, and its
  source twin `js/src/cli.js`, which nothing loads). The calls:
  `glob.hasMagic` (lib/cli.js:72 and :636), `glob.globSync(pattern, {
absolute: true, ignore: [...] })` (:641-644), `editorconfig.parseSync`
  (:231) → `new Minimatch(...)` (editorconfig lib/index.js:179) and
  `escape` (:246). @vue/test-utils 2.6.0 inlines js-beautify's library
  sources into all four of its dist builds (23 inlined module markers
  each, no external `js-beautify` import), so nothing the project itself
  runs loads these packages at all.
- Differential smoke, before and after, against the real installed
  packages (a one-off script, not committed): `glob.hasMagic`,
  `glob.globSync` with js-beautify's verbatim arguments,
  `editorconfig.parseSync` for both sections of a fixture `.editorconfig`,
  and the real CLI on a glob input, a glob plus `--editorconfig` for js and
  for css, a plain path and stdin. The two JSON outputs differ in exactly
  three fields, the versions (glob 13.0.7 → 14.0.6; glob>minimatch and
  editorconfig>minimatch 10.2.6 → 11.0.9). Every `hasMagic` verdict, file
  list, parsed section, CLI status and stdout line and output-file hash is
  identical — including `node_modules` staying ignored by the glob.
- happy-dom is the vitest environment (`test.environment` in
  vite.config.ts): `pnpm run test` passed 11 files / 287 tests before and
  after. A throwaway spec asserting `navigator.userAgent` contains
  `HappyDOM/21.0.4` passed, and its `HappyDOM/20.14.6` control failed —
  the environment is the new version at runtime, not only in the lockfile.

Tests: no new spec. The diff changes no project code, so there is no
behavior of ours to pin; the falsifiable oracles are the audit's exit
status and the existing 287 specs under the new environment. A spec
asserting resolved versions would mirror the lockfile (a pseudo-test,
Rule 11), and the CLI smoke targets a path the project never runs — it
stays a recorded one-off rather than a permanent test.

Rule 9: the card is the owner sanction. No runtime dependency is added
(the `dependencies` block is byte-identical, `pnpm audit --prod` clean);
the dev graph gains no package name, only `path-scurry` 3.0.0 in place of
2.0.2. Rust is untouched — `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock` and `deny.toml` are
unchanged, so cargo-deny's ignore list is unchanged by construction; the
cargo suites were not run for this diff (CI's).

Checks, all exit 0 on a from-scratch tree (`rm -rf node_modules` first):
`pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` (554 ms; CI's install mode);
`pnpm audit` — "No known vulnerabilities found"; `pnpm audit --prod`;
`pnpm run test` (11 files, 287 tests); `pnpm run lint`;
`pnpm run typecheck`; `pnpm run format:check` (the new YAML is
prettier-checked).

Follow-ups for the board, outside this card: pnpm prints
`[WARN] deprecated eslint@9.39.5. 10.15.0 is not deprecated, outside the
range you declared.` on every install — the eslint 9 → 10 major deserves
its own card; spec SEC-010 (docs/spec.md:897) names `npm audit` while the
toolchain has been pnpm since D-018 — T-228's gate is the moment to align
the wording; both overrides become removable once js-beautify and
editorconfig declare the patched majors.

### D-183 — T-126: the sync-pipeline integration suite on temporary Git repositories in all schemes — the card's "no file observer" clause is spec v1.0 text and is pinned as v1.2's display-only rule, the suite registers under `sync_phase4_tests.rs` while `lib.rs` is a frozen zone, and every oracle is a spec literal — 2026-11-23

Problem: T-126 (spec §15.1's Integration row — "the sync pipeline on
temporary Git repositories in all schemes"; §15.4's mapping of DoD 7,
13–15 and 17; OUT-005, 011, 012, 014, 015) asks for integration tests
of the pipeline: creation and overwrite, order, the marker, external
edits overwritten, library operations that change no file, and "no
file observer in the code". Three questions were open before a line
was written.

- _"No file observer" against the spec._ The card's phrase is spec
  v1.0's OUT-014 verbatim: `git show ae89176:docs/spec.md` line 481
  reads "External edits to target files are not tracked: no file
  watcher, no comparing, no merging — There is no watcher code and no
  conflict dialogs". Commit `16a0597` (v1.1, 2026-11-17) replaced that
  row: §5.7 now defines the display-only watch (SYS-007…010), and
  OUT-014 reads "the app never merges them and never writes a file
  because of a watch event", accepted by "An external edit flips the
  state without any dialog; a sync still overwrites the file and makes
  a backup". The landed service is that watcher (`file_watch.rs`,
  T-102/D-137).

  Reading: the spec is the authoritative source (§1.4), and the brief
  itself defers to it ("a test/inspection pin per OUT-0xx as the spec
  assigns"). A literal "no watcher code" pin would assert against an
  implemented P0 requirement and be red by construction; a source scan
  for the absence of watcher tokens would be the pseudo-test Project
  Rule 11 forbids. The suite therefore pins the clause the spec
  assigns today, per scheme, with the real service live: after the
  run's own writes the settled service reads every project clean and
  the files hold what the run left; after an external edit the verdict
  flips, the `state://file-changed` wire carries exactly the flips, the
  files still hold exactly the external bytes (nothing merged, nothing
  written back), and no run row, copy or stamp moves.

  Follow-up for the board: the card's text is stale (v1.0 wording).

- _Where the suite registers._ Both layouts the brief envisioned need
  `lib.rs`. `src-tauri/tests/` cannot reach the pipeline — every module
  of `lib.rs` is `pub(crate)` (only `specta_builder` and `run` are
  `pub`), and `ipc_tests.rs`'s module doc already records that command
  handlers are crate-private. A new in-src `*_tests.rs` module needs a
  `mod` line in `lib.rs`'s test block — T-077's frozen zone in this
  batch. The brief's line for that case: do not edit `lib.rs`;
  narrowly-scoped test-support additions in `sync_phase*.rs` are in
  zone when strictly required; stop only when a `lib.rs` change is
  unavoidable. It is not: the suite is declared as a
  `#[path = "sync_pipeline_tests.rs"]` child module of
  `sync_phase4_tests.rs` — the finish phase's suite, a test file, so no
  production byte moves. A `#[path]` on a module declared at the top
  level of a non-`mod.rs` file resolves against that file's directory;
  the compile confirms it (the tests run as
  `sync_phase4_tests::sync_pipeline_tests::*`). No `#[path]` attribute
  existed in the tree before (a grep finds none) — this is the first.

  Follow-up: once `lib.rs` is free, move the declaration into its test
  block (`#[cfg(test)] mod sync_pipeline_tests;` after
  `mod sync_phase4_tests;`) and delete the `#[path]` block — two
  lines, no test change.

  **2026-11-24 addendum (T-341):** the follow-up landed exactly as
  written — the `#[path]` block is gone from `sync_phase4_tests.rs`,
  `lib.rs`'s test block registers `mod sync_pipeline_tests;` beside
  the phase suites, and the suite's file and test bodies are
  unchanged (13 tests before and after). The module's qualified path
  moved with the declaration, `sync_phase4_tests::sync_pipeline_tests`
  → `sync_pipeline_tests`; nothing in the tree referenced the nested
  path, so no call site changed. A `db_tests.rs` pin keeps the tree
  free of `#[path]` module registrations (T-341).

- _What counts as a library operation._ The §7.10 library commands are
  not landed (the command tasks ahead). The seven operations of the
  DoD-7 test go through the store writers those commands will call over
  the same `Db::run` executor (`update_variant`, `assign`, `unassign`,
  `hide_item`, `move_item`, `update_item`, and `create_item` +
  `create_variant` + `assign`), each in its own transaction; the run
  itself is always the real `sync_run`. Vacuity is excluded twice: the
  library is read back in its new order (MAIN-011), and the next sync
  must produce the hand-derived new content of all three schemes.

Solution: `src-tauri/src/sync_pipeline_tests.rs` — thirteen tests over
one harness: real `.git` repositories from
`eunomia_fs::temp_repos::TempRepos`, a real database in a temp data
root, the mock app in the state `setup` produces (the `ipc_tests.rs`
`sync_watch_app` shape), and the real watch service spawned in every
test — a run awaits the after-sync refresh's ack with no budget (the
D-137 hang note) — at the ipc suite's 40 ms test debounce.

- _Creation and overwrite (OUT-005, §7.5, T-F4, T-F12, D-22, D-24)._ A
  missing target is created in A and C and never in B
  (`skipped`/`E_MARKERS_INVALID`, the run `partial`, nothing backed up
  or stamped); an existing A/C file is fully replaced and its
  hand-written bytes survive as exactly one copy; in B only the block
  is rewritten — a refused marker pair stays byte for byte, and the
  outside of a BOM + CRLF file is kept and reads back `unchanged`.
- _Order (DoD 5, OUT-001…004, ALG-020…022)._ The file follows the
  library `position` after a `move_item`, not the creation order.
- _The marker (DoD 13, 14; ALG-030…032; D-23; D-065; D-01)._ The ALG-032
  template field by field; the marker as the last line of A and C and
  the line before the end marker in B; exactly one per file; one line
  for every project of a run, naming the run's own instant; scheme A's
  full build with the reading lines in their positions.
- _External edits (T-F13, OUT-015, OUT-014)._ The state flips, the next
  sync overwrites without a dialog and backs the external bytes up; in
  B only the block is the app's — a line after the end marker survives.
- _A deleted target (SYS-009, OUT-005, OUT-020)._ Files a sync once
  wrote are deleted outside the app: the hint flips, the watcher
  recreates nothing itself, the next sync recreates the A and C targets
  (nothing to back up) and skips B with `E_MARKERS_INVALID` — and the
  skipped B keeps the sync state of the run that wrote it.
- _Library operations (DoD 7, OUT-011, 012, MAIN-011, OUT-010, D-11,
  ALG-020)._ Seven operations: same bytes, same modification time, no
  run, no copy — until the next sync applies every one of them.
- _Unchanged runs and the sync times (T-F9, D-24, DoD 17, OUT-020,
  DB-024, MAIN-024, MAIN-027)._ A no-change run leaves bytes and
  modification times alone and makes no copy while stamping the
  `unchanged` projects; `written` and `unchanged` are stamped, `skipped`
  and `failed` keep their previous state — for a project that WAS
  stamped, not only for one that never was — and a `partial` run moves
  nobody's overall time.

The oracle posture: no expectation is rebuilt through the builders
under test (`eunomia_core::target_file`, `assembly_b`, `marker_clock`,
`hash`) — the bytes are spelled from ALG-020…022, ALG-030…032 and
decisions D-19, D-21, D-22 and D-23, and the D-19 marker lines are
re-spelled in the suite (the fixtures are user files: a drifted
production constant must fail the suite, not follow it). The error
mappers are the consolidated seams only (`library_seed_error_for_tests`,
`sync_runs_app_error_for_tests`, `projects_store_to_app_error`,
`sqlite_error_to_app_error`) — no new spelling (D-161, D-162, D-171).

Four smaller rulings inside the suite:

- _A `written` stamp is asserted inside its run; an `unchanged` one
  equals `finished_at`._ Phase 3 stamps the write instant and phase 4's
  `finished_at` is a later one; DB-002 carries milliseconds, so
  equality is not the `written` contract. §9.4 phase 4 step 1 makes it
  the `unchanged` one.
- _Waits are condition polls with a 30 s ceiling, never pass-count
  slots._ D-140's rule: the bound is a failure ceiling, a healthy run
  returns early. The one `sleep` is the lower bound of a "nothing
  further happens" check — a late write can be missed, never invented.
- _Expectations ride the fixture's canonical roots_ (`TempRepos`
  canonicalizes — D-160), and the one injected write refusal uses
  `io::Error::other`: no raw OS code in a test (Project Rule 3).
- _The primary claim is asserted first._ The mutation pass moved two
  assertions: the refused-marker test now leads with "nothing is
  written into the file", and the watch test gained an explicit
  precondition — after the run's own writes the settled service reads
  every project clean — so a write-back is caught by the direct claim,
  not by a missing later flip.

Falsifiability (Rule 4; mutations applied with an exact-once driver,
observed red, reverted — `git diff` clean after every batch): nineteen
batches, twenty-one mutants, across `sync_phase1.rs`, `sync_phase3.rs`,
`sync_phase4.rs`, `file_watch.rs`, the core `body.rs`, `assembly_b.rs`,
`extra_files.rs`, `target_file.rs` and `marker_clock.rs`, and the
store's `list_items`.

- _The mutants._ The whole-file blank line dropped (A1); a missing
  scheme-B target falling to the whole-file plan (A2); the marker's
  second shifted per project (A3); phase 4 not stamping `unchanged`
  (A4); the ALG-033 comparison short-circuited (B1); a failed write
  stamping (B2); an invalid pair spliced at offset 0 (B3); the same
  with the `skipped` verdict kept, the file written anyway (B4); the
  watcher writing on an event (C); the body in reverse order (D1); the
  splice normalizing CRLF (D2); the reading-line tie swapped (D3); the
  store listing by creation time (D4); scheme C splicing reading lines
  (E); a hidden instruction selected (F1); a heading written with
  nothing assigned in its section (F2); a missing A/C target skipped
  instead of written (I); a skipped project's stamps cleared (J); the
  scheme-C main file written too (K); the extra files written too (L2);
  the run clock shifted uniformly by +90 s (W — run once under each
  marker slack, the point of round 2's P3-1).
- _The result — every test red, each on one of its own assertions._ The
  table is the record the round-1 review asked for; every row was
  observed on the committed test file (the combined batches A and B and
  the single-mutant batches B4 and D23 were re-run after the round-1
  edits).

  | test                  | mutant → the assertion that fired                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
  | --------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
  | creation              | A2 → "§9.4 phase 4 step 3: a skipped project beside written ones"; B4 → "§7.5: the app does not create a scheme-B file"; K → "scheme C leaves the existing main file byte for byte"; A3 → "ALG-032: one marker for every project of the run"               |
  | overwrite             | A1 → "the scheme-A target: exactly one empty line between the managed block and the marker"; E → "ALG-030's reading lines are scheme A's alone"; B1 → the statuses (`unchanged` × 3)                                                                       |
  | refused marker pair   | B4 → "project 1: nothing is written into a refused scheme-B file"; I → "§9.4 phase 4 step 3: five skipped projects beside a written one"                                                                                                                   |
  | BOM + CRLF            | D2 → "the T-F12 target after the sync: the bytes before the begin marker changed"; B1 → the statuses (`unchanged`)                                                                                                                                         |
  | order                 | D4 → the second run's statuses (`unchanged` × 3 after a reorder); D1 → "the baseline: the creation order"                                                                                                                                                  |
  | the marker            | A3 → "ALG-032: one time per run, the same for all projects"                                                                                                                                                                                                |
  | scheme A's full build | D3 → "scheme-A project 0: ALG-030's composition" (the `.local.md` line first); L2 → "D-01: the app does not change an extra file that already exists"                                                                                                      |

  | library operations    | F1 → the second sync's content (the hidden instruction's text in the build); B1 → the second run's statuses (`unchanged` × 3)                                                                                                                              |
  | no-change run         | A4 → "§9.4 phase 4 step 1 stamps the unchanged project"                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
  | the sync times        | B2 → "OUT-020: a failed project keeps its previous sync state"; J → "OUT-020: a skipped project keeps its previous sync state" (the fourth run); A4 → "§9.4 phase 4 step 1: an unchanged project is stamped with the run's time"                           |
  | deleted target        | I → the second run's statuses (`skipped`, `written`, `skipped`); B3 → "the skipped scheme-B project beside two written ones"; J → "OUT-020: a skipped project keeps the sync state of the run that wrote it"; C → the `file_deleted` verdict never settles |

- _Three predictions were wrong, and each said something._ The
  refused-marker test stayed green under the short-circuited
  comparison — an invalid file is refused at step 4 and never reaches
  step 5, so that mutant could not reach the pin (it got its own). The
  watch test went red under two mutants predicted harmless, both
  indirectly — that is why the precondition above exists. And the first
  per-project-marker mutant indexed the date field, so phase 3 itself
  panicked and every red came from the mutant's own bug: a red run is
  evidence only when the panic site is the suite's assertion. The
  runner prints every failure's site and message; a batch counts only
  when they are the suite's own. The round-1 additions brought four
  more, all explained: the refused-marker test also went red under the
  missing-target mutant (its scheme-A project has a missing target
  too); the watch and library-operations tests died in the suite's own
  `read` helper on that same mutant; a first form of the extra-files
  mutant (L) clobbered the own target of a scheme-C project whose stem
  is `AGENTS` — that target is named `AGENTS.project.md` — and was
  tightened into L2; and a runner bug that printed MATCH for a batch
  in which nothing had compiled was caught before it could hide a
  missing mutant (a "not run" is a mismatch unless a filter asked for
  it).
- _Two would-be no-ops never ran, and one batch was split._ The
  exact-once guard stopped a failed-write arm four columns deeper than
  assumed and a `String` moved into a loop closure (and, in round 1, a
  missing-target arm at the wrong indentation and two mutants that
  returned a `WrittenFile` where a `Result` was due). The first
  combined batch masked two of its four mutants behind earlier failing
  assertions — a mutant behind another's assertion proves nothing — so
  each got a batch of its own.

Honest boundaries: Linux only, locally — the three-OS green is CI's on
the merge push (the card's own "done when"). Platform facts are
analysed here, not executed:

- _The macOS startup race of D-181 (main's entry for CI 45235995817;
  not in this entry's base)._ FSEvents can deliver a fixture write made
  BEFORE `spawn_service` after the stream starts, as one extra, silent
  partial pass; the pre-fix ipc batteries broke on absolute pass-count
  slots. This suite has none. Its only pass-count wait is `>= 1` in
  `go_live`, where the startup `Refresh` is the first command on the
  bus (a pre-startup event routes through an empty table and never
  counts as a pass). Its one event assertion is a SET of flips,
  collected after a condition wait that guarantees all three were
  already emitted (emit-then-record), and every straggler pass is
  verdict-neutral: it re-reads files whose verdicts only the test's own
  acts change. D-181's own second iteration shows how subtle this
  family is, so the macOS legs are the ones to watch on the merge push.
- _Teardown is best-effort on every OS — not "the `Db` first"._
  `tauri::App` (2.12.6) has no `Drop` and holds its state in an
  `Arc<AppManager>`; the live watch service task owns an `AppHandle`
  and loops on the bus for the process's life, so the managed `Db`
  outlives every world, and `TempDir::drop` is
  `let _ = remove_dir_all(…)` (tempfile 3.27.0). A temp root with a
  file still open can therefore survive the drop — a leak, never a
  failure — and every sibling suite that spawns the service shares it.
  Whether Windows refuses that removal is not executed here. Measured
  on Linux after round 2, because leaked roots turned up in `/tmp`
  while this task ran: this suite's worlds were removed in 78 of 78
  runs (four clean runs and two with failing tests under mutants), and
  so were the sibling watch batteries' (144 tests, twice); the one root
  each whole-workspace run leaves comes from `recovery_tests` (21
  tests) — one 8-KB, freshly migrated, empty `db/eunomiasync.sqlite3`
  per run, the file its `db_recreate` round trip writes. Thirteen such
  roots had accumulated across that day's sessions before the count
  started. The open-handle leak is therefore not this suite's on
  Linux; a board follow-up carries the pointer.

Three more boundaries are stated rather than implied. The creation
marker's zone NAME is checked for shape only — that it names the system
zone is `marker_clock`'s own suite's pin. OUT-014's display half (the
MAIN-028 column, no dialog) is UI: the suite pins the service's half
and the manual smoke checklist owns the rest. The library operations
run through the store writers, not through §7.10 commands (not landed).
DoD 9 — the dirty flag after a library edit — is deliberately not
pinned: its §15.4 row is not this card's. D-179… D-182 were issued to
parallel sessions and are not in this entry's base (`fd00673`).

Checks: `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2 cargo fmt --all -- --check`,
`CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2 cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D
warnings` and `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2 cargo nextest run --workspace
--no-fail-fast --test-threads=4` — all exit 0 on Linux (1652 tests,
1652 passed, none skipped; the suite's thirteen among them) — and
`pnpm run format:check` exit 0.
