### D-193 — T-125: the `backups_list` contract — the "sync run number" is the run's id, all four statuses are listed, and the row shape is every column the tab can reach — 2026-11-24

Problem: T-125 lands spec §7.10's Backups-module read (BKP-004,
§7.6): in project settings, the "Backups" tab shows "the date, file,
size, and sync run number"; the card's field list adds "status". Four
readings were open before any code: what a "sync run number" is (the
`sync_runs` schema of §6.2 has no numeric column — `id` is a UUIDv7
TEXT), which of the four §6.2 CHECK statuses a "list of copies" lists,
the row's ordering, and the shape of the "file" field.

Question and chosen readings (recorded before implementation, Rule 1):

1. **"Sync run number" = `sync_run_id`, the run's UUIDv7 TEXT id.**
   §6.2's `sync_runs` carries no ordinal, and the wire already names a
   run this way — `ActivityEntry.sync_run_id` is "the sync run
   involved" (T-027's precedent). A derived per-project ordinal was
   declined: the §6.4 run cleanup keeps the last 500 runs, so any
   numbering derived from surviving rows silently renumbers under
   retention, and nothing in the store owns such a column. The field
   is `Option<String>`: the `backup_records.sync_run_id` foreign key is
   `ON DELETE SET NULL`, and §6.4's run cleanup can legitimately
   orphan a row whose run was swept — `None` is the honest cell, not
   an error.
2. **All four statuses are listed.** §6.4's "Backup | File deleted by
   limit | the record gets the `pruned` status" and "rows are never
   deleted — §6.4 keeps the history as status" make the table the
   copy's lifecycle log, and the card's own field list includes
   "status": a list filtered to `ok` would carry a constant column in
   v1 (§10's `missing` detection has no v1 producer), and S11's "the
   copy is missing on disk (status `missing`)" requires non-`ok` rows
   to survive into the P1 restore's pick list. The D-122 ok-only set
   is the dedup/retention window's rule over LIVE copies, not the
   visible history's.
3. **Ordering: newest first — `created_at DESC, id DESC`.** The same
   "newest" D-122 fixed for the retention window and the BKP-010 dedup
   lookup (the same-millisecond id tiebreak included), and the order
   every house list already serves (activity, revisions, DB copies).
4. **The row shape: every `backup_records` column the tab can reach
   except `project_id` and `sha256`.** `created_at` is BKP-004's date
   (DB-002 UTC), `source_path` is the "file" (the §9.4 phase-1
   RESOLVED target path — one stable spelling per file, D-122),
   `backup_path` is the copy's own §5.5 relative layout name
   (BKP-001's "the backup name shows the project, file, and time" —
   and the P1 restore's pick handle), `size_bytes` is the
   BKP-010-checked size, `status` the stored literal, `id` the row's
   own UUIDv7 id (the house row-DTO handle), `sync_run_id` reading 1.
   `project_id` is deliberately absent: the list is scoped by the
   caller's project, so the column is the scope, not per-row data —
   the `RevisionSummaryRecord` precedent of omitting what the view
   cannot vary. `sha256` is deliberately absent as well: the tab shows
   no digest — the BKP-010 check is Rust-side, and the P1 restore
   re-hashes the copy it reads, so the column is the dedup's input,
   not the tab's data. `size_bytes` is `u32` saturated at `u32::MAX`
   on the wire (D-049, the `DbBackupInfo` decision; a real target
   file never approaches 4 GiB).
5. **Scoping: unknown project id = the typed `E_VALIDATION` refusal**
   (field `project_id`, reason "no project has this id") — the
   `revisions_list` precedent: an unknown id is a caller bug, never
   silently "no backups". A KNOWN project with no rows answers `[]`
   (the tab's empty state). The validation lives in the command layer
   through `projects::get` (a projects fact, not a backup-records
   fact — the store read stays a pure per-project keying, the
   `last_checked` shape), and the read is state-agnostic: an archived
   project's history lists too (DB-014 keeps an archived project's
   data; a read never branches on state).
6. **Volume: the whole history, no paging.** The tab loads the
   project's every row in one answer — BKP-004 names no page or limit
   (the card's field list is date, file, size, run, status), and the
   row count grows one row per copy ever made (rows are never
   deleted, §6.4), so the payload is bounded by the project's real
   sync volume, not by a `MAX_PAGE_LIMIT`. `activity_list` paginates
   because the journal mixes every project's events; this read is one
   project's copy history, the retention's own scale. If a real
   project ever makes the tab heavy, paging is a future task with its
   own card.
7. **No-database answer:** the `answer_honestly_without_a_database`
   battery's refusal — `E_DB_LOCKED` with `details.os_kind
"NoDatabase"` from `managed_db`, exactly the history reads' posture
   (T-331).

Solution: `eunomia_store::backup_records::list_for_project` (the
store's per-project read, joined to the caller's transaction, statuses
decoded through `BackupRecordStatus::from_member` — a corrupt cell is

(`backups_list`, the T-331 revisions module shape: one `Db::run` read

### D-194 — T-108: the `project_archive` command's contract — the exclusion row's moment and key, double-archive convergence, and DB-014's dirty flag decided by the row, never written — 2026-11-24

The card's spec text (PRJ-013…018, §6.4, DB-014, D-10, SYS-005) leaves five
points open to more than one reading; the chosen readings were written here
BEFORE the implementation (the rule-1 discipline). The command is
id-addressed (`Result<(), AppError>`, the `exclusion_remove` shape — §7.10
names no payload, and the D-10 screens re-read through the already-landed
widened `projects_list` and `exclusions_list`); an id no row matches is the
typed `E_VALIDATION` refusal naming `project_id` (a stale screen's re-send;
nothing was written).

1. **The `project_exclusions` row (PRJ-017).** Written in the SAME
   `Db::run` transaction as the row update, only when the row's
   `added_via = scan` — §6.4's "if the project was found by a scan" is the
   row's own origin column, not a filesystem fact — keyed by the row's
   `path_key` (the DB-030 identity), storing the row's `path` verbatim with
   reason `removed_scanned`. A manual-born project writes NO exclusion row
   (PRJ-001's picker is its way back). **Convergence, not conflict:** the
   store lets a project and an exclusion share one `path_key`, so an
   exclusion may already exist (a manual exclusion of the same path, or a
   prior archive's row that a later restore leaves behind — T-109's
   restore, not this command, removes it). The archive leaves the existing
   row untouched: its own reason and date are facts of their own, and
   PRJ-017's end state ("its path goes to `project_exclusions`") is already
   true. The `DuplicatePathKey` arm is therefore unreachable at this
   boundary by construction, and the pre-read makes the whole write
   idempotent.
2. **Double archive.** A second `project_archive` on an already-archived
   row is a converging no-op: `Ok(())`, no journal entry, `archived_at`
   not restamped (the store's own idempotence rule), no exclusion churn
   even if the exclusion row was since removed by hand — the removal is
   the user's explicit §6.4 act ("the path is found by a scan again") and
   a re-send of the archive does not override it. The `assignment_set`
   precedent: a same-state re-send writes/journals nothing.
3. **The dirty flag (DB-014, the card's "не dirty" DoD).** The command
   writes NOTHING beyond the row (plus the exclusion and the journal):
   no clearing of `last_synced_hash`, no assignment churn — both stay for
   T-109's restore ("Restoring brings the project back with its
   assignments"). "Not counted as dirty" is decided where it is counted:
   `projects_list`'s `dirty_verdict` returns `false` for an archived row
   BEFORE consulting the cache (D-128's row-decidable arm — a stale cache
   `true` cannot leak onto an archived column), and the `state://dirty`
   service's next pass computes over ACTIVE projects only and prunes the
   leaver silently (the landed prune rule, `dirty_recalc.rs`'s own
   "archived project has no column to mark anymore"). The DB-022 commit
   hook fires on the archive's row change automatically; the command adds
   no recalculation of its own. The same construction keeps the project
   out of the sync set: `read_build_snapshot` (ALG-001) reads
   `ListScope::Active` — the DoD's "does not take part in syncs" holds by
   the store's read, not by any sync-side special case.
4. **The journal.** ONE `project.archived` entry (info/user/ok) whose
   entity columns name the project and whose `project_id` is set — no
   details (the `register_project` shape: the row itself holds the path).
   No separate exclusion-add member: the closed LOG-001…004 vocabulary has
   none (only D-106's `exclusion.removed` exists, added for the removal
   because that command's entry had NO entity to attribute), and the
   archive's entry is attributable — the exclusion row is a DB fact the
   D-10 screen reads through `exclusions_list`, not an event of its own.
5. **No file I/O at all.** §6.4's "the project folder is not touched" is
   total: no availability probe, no folder check — `projects_list`'s own
   docs keep "Archive" an available action on an unavailable column, so
   archiving a project whose folder died must succeed, and the command's
   complexity stays trivially stated (one transaction, indexed by-id and
   by-key store reads/writes).

SYS-005's gate runs as the first act (`reject_during_sync`, before the
database is resolved — the `exclusion_remove` ordering); recovery mode
answers the honest `NoDatabase` fallback, the flag being down there by
construction. The T-109 restore is NOT implemented here (not in flight);
this entry's restore-compatibility choices (kept assignments, kept
`last_synced_hash`, the exclusion row left for the restore to remove) are
its foundation. T-279's `refresh_after_sync` retrofit is likewise out of
scope: the card does not ask for it, and a file-watch refresh would be
file I/O this reading deliberately has none of.

**Round-1 review addendum (same task, 2026-11-24; model
`opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash`, report
`.opencode/reviews/t108-round1-report.md`: REQUEST CHANGES, 0×P0/P1,
2×P2, 7×P3 — all taken in the amend).** The two P2s: the rollback
claim now has its falsifiable proof
(`a_failed_journal_insert_rolls_back_the_row_and_the_exclusion_together`,
the `reject_every_journal_entry` trigger shape), and the SYS-005 gate
doc's "the mutation commands that exist" list names `project_archive`.
The P3s: the kept-hash oracle seeds a real `record_last_synced` value
(was `None` to `None`); three stale doc claims ("no command exists
yet") were corrected; the unknown-id refusal's `value` echo is bounded
(`bounded_echo`, D-115's cap — now `pub(crate)`); the mock's
`toColumnEntry` serves the row-decidable DB-014 arm (`dirty: false`
for an archived row whatever its own flag) with a spec pin. Three
record-only notes:

- _The count sentence is a landing-rebase trap (P3-5)._ T-125
  (`backups_list`, same base) rewrites the same `ARCHITECTURE.md`
  "thirty-eight commands" line to its own "thirty-nine"; both edits
  are textually identical, so the three-way merge resolves SILENTLY
  and the merged prose undercounts a `collect_commands!` of 40. No
  test pins the prose. The landing rebase — only when the orchestrator
  calls it — must set the sentence to the merged truth (forty once
  both siblings land) by hand.
- _T-109's restore will delete a row this command did not create
  (P3-6)._ The convergence arm deliberately leaves a pre-existing
  `manual` exclusion with the archived row's `path_key` untouched; the
  D-10/PRJ-013…018 restore "removes the path from the exclusions", so
  T-109's `project_restore` will delete that manual row too, silently
  undoing the user's own exclusion of the path. The reading is
  consistent (the restore half owns the composition); T-109's own
  decision record must name the choice. Follow-up card material.
- _SYS-005-as-a-check leaves a one-run window (P3-7)._ The gate is
  deliberately a check, not an acquire, so an archive that commits
  just after a run's phase-0 snapshot read (the one connection
  serializes them, but in either order) can still have its project's
  file written and its `last_synced_*` stamped by that one
  already-snapshotted run — one run in which DB-014's "does not take
  part in syncs" is not literally true. The same window exists for
  every gated command (e.g. `exclusion_remove`); it is inherent to
  SYS-005's one-directional rule, recorded here so it is not
  rediscovered. No action in this task.

### D-196 — T-344: `scan_commit` answers a typed partial success when the post-commit probe's join fails (rows stay committed), and a commit over an excluded path lifts the exclusion and adds the project — 2026-11-24

Problem: T-077's follow-up (the card, triaged 2026-11-24, owner
ruling variant 2): (1) the §6.9 write-access probe's join failure
surfaces as `Err` AFTER the transaction committed (the manual add's
posture, inherited by construction) — for a batch that reads as "the
command failed" while every row is merged; (2) a commit whose
selection holds an excluded path answered the typed `"excluded"`
outcome and wrote nothing, so the scan's "Skipped" row had no way
back into the registry through the commit (the manual re-add never
removes an exclusion either — the store's own doc names the removal
the caller's composition).

Readings chosen (Rule 1, recorded before implementation):

- **The partial success is one result-level field, `probe_failed`**
  (`ScanCommitResult { entries, probe_failed }`). The probe runs ONE
  `spawn_blocking` over every created row's target, so a join failure
  kills all verdicts at once — the fact is about the batch, not about
  a row, and a per-row outcome spelling (`"added_probe_failed"`) would
  duplicate it per row. `true` means: the rows ARE committed, the
  entries are the committed truth, and the `"added"` rows carry
  `write_access_warning: None` because UNCHECKED, not because
  writable — the field's own doc states this, and how the UI presents
  the two live kinds of answers stays open question (3), UI-002's to
  design. The failure is logged once through the new class-only edge
  `logging::scan_commit_probe_degraded` (the same mapped fields the
  `scan_commit_failed` edge carries: code, params, os_code, os_kind,
  os_message — a join failure has no stored user content, Rule 8).
- **The excluded branch becomes delete + register + journal.** Inside
  the same transaction: `find_exclusion_by_path_key` answering a row
  now deletes it (`delete_exclusion`), registers the project
  (`register_project`), and THEN journals ONE `exclusion.removed`
  entry (the D-119 shape: entity = the exclusion row, `File` detail =
  its stored path — with one deviation, recorded here: `project_id`
  names the row created moments earlier in the same transaction,
  which is why the journaling follows the registration — here a
  project row IS involved and the Activity window's project filter
  should attribute the lift to it; `exclusion_remove` itself keeps
  its no-project shape). The journal order is therefore the row's
  `project.added` first, then the lift's `exclusion.removed` — the
  entry outcome is `"added"`. The answer's outcome vocabulary
  shrinks to `"added"`/`"already_added"`/`"archived"`: `"excluded"`
  can no longer occur. D-179's "typed non-add outcomes journal
  nothing" narrows accordingly — the still-typed outcomes
  (`already_added`, `archived`) journal nothing; the excluded case is
  no longer a non-add outcome.
- **Boundary — which exclusions the commit lifts.** Only the
  no-project-holds-the-key case (the old typed-`excluded` branch). An
  exclusion row coexisting with a project row — the archive flow's
  by-design pair (§6.4: archiving adds the path to
  `project_exclusions`; DB-015 keeps the archived row) — is
  untouched: the commit answers `"archived"` with the restore offer,
  and the restore owns that removal. The SEC-003 gate is unchanged:
  excluded-class repositories are published into the discovered set
  like every reported class (D-179), so the commit admits them.
- **Scope boundary.** The manual add keeps its `Err`-after-commit
  posture: its probe covers one row and the card's ruling is about
  the batch command; changing the single-add contract is not this
  card's. The mock twin models the lift (state exclusions shrink,
  `exclusion.removed` journaled) and answers `probe_failed: false`
  always — no filesystem, no probe half (the D-108 limits posture its
  header records).

Tests (BDD, red first, mutation-verified below): the T-077 battery
`registered_and_excluded_paths_answer_typed_outcomes_and_the_rest_are_added`
is rewritten — the excluded path now commits (`"added"`, row created,
exclusion row gone, journal carries the new row's `project.added` plus
the `exclusion.removed` entry naming it); two unit pins cover the
probe halves the end-to-end path cannot reach without a fault-injection
seam: the join mapping with a REAL `JoinError` (a panicking
`spawn_blocking` task, awaited) answers the empty verdicts and the
marker, and the result assembly carries `probe_failed` with the
warnings still aligned to their rows.

Checks: `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2 cargo fmt --check`; `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2
cargo clippy -p eunomia-sync --all-targets -- -D warnings`; targeted
`cargo nextest run -p eunomia-sync scan_tests logging`; prettier +
eslint + targeted vitest over the mock chain; the full suite runs once
after the flash batch (owner instruction). One review round.

### D-197 — T-346: the abort's clock becomes a command-level seam (`SyncRunSeams.abort_clock`), an interrupted run's non-movement of MAIN-027 is an executable pin, and the phase-1 abort gets a real oracle — 2026-11-24

Problem: T-325's follow-up (the card, triaged 2026-11-24, owner
ruling variant 1 — all three points closed in one task): (1) a
pipeline-level abort test with a measurable pause needed a clock seam
on the COMMAND (`sync_run_with`), the zone T-325 froze then being
merged; (2) "an interrupted run does not move MAIN-027" was pinned
only by grep-verification, never executed; (3) phase 1's abort reads
its clock correctly but its test asserted only
`finished_at.is_some()` — no oracle for the value.

Readings chosen (Rule 1, recorded before implementation):

- **The seam sits in `SyncRunSeams`, typed like its siblings.**
  `abort_clock: AbortClock`,
  `Arc<dyn Fn() -> jiff::Timestamp + Send + Sync>`, production
  `jiff::Timestamp::now` — the same instant family phase 2's own
  abort parameter uses, so one type answers for both consumers. The
  command feeds it to the abort paths it drives ITSELF: the D-25
  gate's stop, the cancel checkpoint's stop (both through
  `stop_run`, whose signature gains the caller-supplied
  `finished_at` stamp), and phase 2's abort (`run_with_abort_clock`
  instead of the wrapping `run`). The post-phase-0 `Err` wrapper
  (`pipeline_refusal`/`stop_run_if_running`) keeps the real clock:
  it is the best-effort corpse cleanup on a path whose FIRST error
  is the answer — no test measures that instant, and its semantics
  (the abort's own instant, D-185) stay true with the real clock.
  The conversion for `stop_run`'s stamp reuses phase 2's
  `db002_stamp`, now `pub(crate)` — the fourth private copy the
  command would otherwise have grown.
- **The characterization pin is pipeline-level through the cancel
  checkpoint.** Run 1 succeeds (production seams); run 2 enters with
  a PRE-LATCHED cancel token — steps 1–3 consult nothing, step 4 is
  the one check point, so the pre-latch is the deterministic way to
  reach it — and `abort_clock` answering a FIXED later instant. The
  assertions: the run row is `aborted` with `finished_at` equal to
  the seam's instant in the DB-002 spelling (the measurable pause,
  deterministic — the abort's own instant, D-185's semantics now
  observable through the command), `last_success_finished_at`
  (MAIN-027's derived read, §9.4 phase 4 step 4) is UNMOVED at run
  1's stamp, and the project's `last_synced_at` is unmoved (OUT-020's
  aborted half).
- **Phase 1's oracle is a clock parameter, the phase-2 shape.**
  `sync_phase1::run_with_abort_clock(app, phase0, free_probe, now,
abort_clock)` with `abort_clock: impl FnOnce() -> String` — the
  DB-002 spelling, phase 1's native stamp type (its abort writes
  `values::now_utc()` directly, no jiff conversion anywhere in the
  phase); `run` wraps it with the real clock. The upgraded shortage
  battery drives the twin with a FIXED stamp and asserts
  `finished_at ==` that stamp exactly — the oracle the `is_some()`
  assertion lacked. The read POINT (after the probe, before the
  verdict transaction) stays documented, not pinned: phase 1's abort
  has no side effect before the stamp for a two-instant clock to
  discriminate (phase 2's read-point pin uses the swept copy — phase
  1 has no sweep), and a `FnOnce` clock answers once.

Honest boundaries: the D-25 gate and the cancel checkpoint are the
only command-driven aborts the seam reaches in this task's tests; the
phase-2 abort through the command inherits the seam by construction
(the same `Arc`), but no pipeline-level test injects a failing copy
AND a fixed clock together — phase 2's own suite pins that abort's
clock semantics. The seam's construction sites: the pipeline suite's
struct literal and SIX struct literals in `ipc_tests.rs` (all taking
the production clock beside their injected backup/write arms) — the
compiler found the six after a wrong "grep-checked, no sibling
sites" draft claim, and grep then confirmed the census.

Checks: `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2 cargo fmt --check`; clippy
`-p eunomia-sync --all-targets -- -D warnings`; targeted nextest
`sync_pipeline_tests sync_phase1_tests`; mutation checks recorded in
the task report. One review round.

### D-198 — T-348: the `variant_get` contract the editor and the MAIN-006 tooltip will code against — 2026-11-24

Problem: the T-329 batch landed the variant WRITE commands
(`variant_create`/`variant_update`/`variant_set_main`/`variant_delete`/
`variant_restore`), but no §7.10 command carries a variant's TEXT —
the instruction editor's body (§7.3 LIB-002, 009…016's field rules —
MAIN-006 only opens the editor and owns the tooltip) and the name
tooltip's text half (MAIN-006: "A tooltip with the text (first 600
characters, 400 ms delay)") have no source to read. The owner split the follow-up
out of T-083's card and ruled it spec-only (this task describes the
contract; the implementation is its own future card).

Readings chosen (Rule 1, recorded before the spec edit; the card
delegates every contract detail not fixed by a ruling to this
record):

- **One parameter, `id`** — the variant's row id (DB-002), the same
  identity every variant command addresses and the id
  `library_get`'s inline entries already serve the UI.
- **The answer is the stored row plus the derived emptiness.** The
  §6.2 row columns exactly as the landed variant commands' answer
  carries them (the `VariantRecord` wire shape: `id`,
  `instruction_id`, `name`, `content`, `is_main`, `state`,
  `created_at`, `updated_at`, `deleted_at` — checked field for field
  against `src/bindings.ts`'s `VariantRecord_Serialize`,
  `deleted_at` nullable) — the row body reuses that shape with ONE
  derived addition: `is_empty`, LIB-014/D-13's "outputs no
  text" flag, computed by the build's own oracle (ALG-002's
  normalize), exactly the flag `library_get`'s inline entries carry
  (D-187; the oracle's identity checked against
  `LibraryVariantEntry`'s own doc in the same file). The field is DERIVED — the schema has no column for it —
  so the two readers of a variant (the inline list, the by-id read)
  cannot disagree about what "empty" means.
- **Any state is answered as stored.** The read serves the row
  whatever its §6.4 state (`active` or `deleted`): it is a read, the
  state column rides the answer, and a stale screen re-reading an
  id that was soft-deleted in another window sees the truth instead
  of a refusal (the convergence posture of D-179's typed outcomes).
  An unknown id is the typed refusal of the `exclusion_remove`
  unknown-id shape (`E_VALIDATION` naming `id`;
  `src-tauri/src/commands.rs`, `exclusion_remove_impl`) — §10 has no
  not-found code, and the frozen registry keeps that shape.
- **The command never truncates.** `content` is the full stored text
  (DB-006's 262,144-character bound); the MAIN-006 tooltip's "first
  600 characters" is the UI's own clamp over the returned text, not
  a command parameter — the same full text feeds the editor's body,
  and a server-side truncation would make the tooltip's source
  useless for the editor (two commands where one read suffices).
- **§7.10 placement, no count drift.** The command joins the Library
  module's row and gains a sentence in §7.10's command notes. The
  registered-command counts (ARCHITECTURE.md's 38,
  `mode.spec.ts`'s shipped-set pin) stay untouched — the spec
  describes the contract, the implementation card lands the command.

Checks: md-only diff (docs/spec.md, this file) — prettier and a
factual re-read of every cited line (rule 2/11), the md-only regime
(no test suites run), ONE review round.

### D-199 — T-349: the heading record carries `from_level`, the skipped-from level, beside the LIB-032 skip flag — 2026-11-24

Problem: LIB-032 / T-083's follow-up — the boolean `level_skipped`
flag answers "is this a skip", but a UI that wants to show WHICH
level is skipped needs the pair's other half: the level the heading
arrives FROM. `eunomia-core`'s gaps module already computes it
(`HeadingLevelGap::from_level`, the pair's previous heading's level);
`library_get`'s heading entry just never surfaced it. Owner ruling
(triage 2026-11-24, variant 1): add `from_level` to the heading
record now — wire, backend, mock twin, spec — and the battery gains
the assertions, mutation-verified.

Readings chosen (Rule 1, recorded before implementation):

- **Type: `Option<u8>` on the wire (`from_level: number | null`).**
  `Some(from_level)` exactly when the row IS the `to` half of a gap
  (the same rows `level_skipped` is true for — the flag and the
  level answer one pair, never disagreeing); `None` for every other
  heading (the first heading, closes, siblings) — a skip-fact-less
  row has no skipped-from level, and `0` would be a level value no
  heading can carry while looking like data. The heading entry's
  other numeric field (`level`) is already `u8` on the wire, so no
  new numeric convention is introduced.
- **One gaps pass, two facts.** The existing
  `heading_level_gaps` call gains a second index map
  (`to_index → from_level`); `level_skipped` keeps its exact
  semantics (membership in the `to` set) and `from_level` reads the
  new map — the two fields are built from one report, so a gap the
  report missed (or invented) fails both, not one.
- **The mock twin mirrors the backend, not core.** The mock computes
  its own skip set (it has no core); it now computes the same pair
  map, so the mock's contract matches the backend's on both fields.
- **Spec: the contract rides §7.10's command notes.** The spec's
  only existing LIB-032 wording is the requirement row's "warning
  icon"; `library_get`'s payload is described in the command notes
  since T-348's sentence shape. A `library_get` clause names both
  skip facts — the boolean and the skipped-from level (`2`–`6`,
  null when the row is not a skip).

Checks: BDD red-first (the field added with a deliberately constant
empty map — the shape battery's positive assertion and the dedicated
battery went red on it — then the real map, green); mutation-verified
twice, both observed: the empty-map red above, and the post-green
poisoning of the map's values to garbage, which the dedicated
battery caught (the shape battery's `None` rows cannot see it). fmt,
clippy `-p eunomia-sync`, targeted nextest (library_tests), the
bindings export pin, prettier/eslint/targeted vitest over the mock
chain, and the D-195 doc-test pass. The full suite runs once after
the flash batch. One review round (run 2026-11-25 after the batch's
transport/limit interruptions: APPROVE WITH NITS, 4×P3 — the
fixture's second skip now arrives from H3, killing the constant-2
mutant class; the 2–6 range wording narrowed to the real 2–4; the
skip set folded into the map; this record's mutation wording aligned
with both observed runs).

### D-200 — T-350: `library_get`'s answer widens to a struct carrying `hidden_count`, the UI's D-14 number, computed over the served transaction — 2026-11-24

Problem: D-14's "Show hidden" toggle shows "the current number of
hidden instructions", and the default (hidden-excluded) answer cannot
supply it — the widened read serves the rows themselves, so the only
client-side route is fetching the widened tree and counting it, a
round trip the UI should never need. Owner ruling (triage 2026-11-24,
variant 1): the count lands in the DEFAULT answer now; deferring or
client-side recounting is not wanted.

Readings chosen (Rule 1, recorded before implementation):

- **The answer widens to a struct, both scopes.**
  `LibraryGetResult { tree: Vec<LibraryTreeItem>, hidden_count: u32 }`
  replaces the bare vector — a field cannot ride an array, and one
  command keeps one answer shape under either scope. The name `tree`
  is D-187's own word for the payload ("one flat position-ordered
  vector"). This is a breaking wire change; the UI has no callers yet
  (the editor tasks are queued), and the tests are this change's
  callers.
- **`hidden_count` counts HIDDEN INSTRUCTIONS** — the rows only the
  widened scope serves (`state = 'hidden'`; headings are always
  active, so the count is the toggle's number exactly). Scope-
  independent: both scopes carry the same count, computed by one
  `COUNT` in the SAME read transaction (D-037) — the default answer
  knows its hidden half without serving it.
- **The store gains the query, not the command.**
  `eunomia_store::library::count_items(conn, scope)` — the COUNT
  lives where the list lives (the module that owns the table's
  read vocabulary); the command maps the i64 through the wire's
  saturation rule (`u32::MAX`, the `variant_count` precedent —
  specta forbids 64-bit integers).
- **The mock twin computes the same number from its own rows**
  (hidden fixtures), and the spec's §7.10 library_get clause names
  the field.

Checks: BDD red-first (the struct widened with a deliberately
constant zero, the new battery red, then the real COUNT — green);
mutation-verified (the count poisoned to zero turns the battery red).
fmt, clippy `-p eunomia-sync`, targeted nextest (library_tests), the
bindings export pin, prettier/eslint/targeted vitest over the mock
chain, and the D-195 doc-test pass. The full suite runs once after
the flash batch. One review round.

### D-201 — T-106: the `project_update` command's contract — the four editable fields as an id-addressed patch, the warning-not-refusal duplicate name, and T-279's refresh declined for fields no watch input reads — 2026-11-25

The card (§7.10 Projects module `project_update`; PRJ-008/009/011/021,
§6.9, SYS-005, LOG-001…004) leaves seven points open to more than one
reading; the chosen readings were written here BEFORE the
implementation (the rule-1 discipline). The command follows D-194's
module shape: `project_update.rs` + `project_update_tests.rs`,
`reject_during_sync` first, `managed_db`'s honest `NoDatabase` answer,
then ONE `Db::run` transaction carrying the store update and the
journal insert.

1. **The wire: id-addressed patch, flat optional args.**
   `project_update(project_id, name, label, color, description)` →
   `Result<(), AppError>`, each field `Option<String>` — the D-194
   id-addressed reading for the project family (`exclusion_remove`'s
   shape), with the patch semantics the store's own `ProjectUpdate`
   already chose ("`None` leaves the field unchanged"; "PRJ-008 saves
   the whole modal at once, but the repository does not force a full
   overwrite" — `crates/eunomia-store/src/projects.rs:737-784`).
   Absent field = unchanged: a stale screen that re-sends one field
   cannot wipe the other three, and the future PRJ-008 modal (T-160)
   sending all four is the same contract. The screen re-reads through
   the already-landed `projects_list` (name/label/color on the
   column), so the answer is `()` — no echo payload. Flat args, not a
   payload struct: the `instruction_update(id, name)` form is the
   update family's precedent, and tauri-specta maps each arg to one
   invoke key.
2. **The duplicate name is saved, not refused (§6.9/PRJ-011).** §6.9's
   name row is explicit: "Duplicates are allowed with a warning" — a
   UI-level field warning, never a store refusal, so the command saves
   a duplicate name like any other. The warning is the modal's live
   field validation (T-160), computable client-side from the names
   `projects_list` already serves — unlike the add flow's
   `write_access_warning` (a Rust-only filesystem fact), it needs no
   wire arm; `Result<(), AppError>` carries nothing and no journal
   difference exists between a duplicate and a unique name.
3. **"The path cannot be changed" is answered by contract, not
   refusal (PRJ-008's AC).** The command's args ARE the editable
   field list — no `path`, no `scheme`/`base_name`/`extra_*` (those
   are T-107's own card, DB-023's watch-set inputs) — and the store's
   `ProjectUpdate` has no `path`/`path_key`/`added_via` members at
   all. There is no wire surface a path could ride, so no typed
   refusal exists to test; the oracle pins the row instead: after an
   update, `path`, `path_key`, `added_via` (and `state`, `sort_order`,
   `last_synced_*`) are verbatim. The spec §7.10 note says so.
4. **The archived row is a stale screen's refusal (D-115's reorder
   precedent).** PRJ-008's modal opens from an ACTIVE column's pencil
   icon; an id that names no row, or a row archived since the modal
   opened, is the same stale-screen re-send reorder refused
   ("unknown OR archived"). The refusal is the typed `E_VALIDATION`
   naming `project_id`, reason "no active project has this id", the
   caller's id echoed bounded (`bounded_echo`, D-115's cap); nothing
   is written, nothing journaled.
5. **The journal: ONE `project.changed` entry, only for a real
   change.** D-119 recorded `ProjectChanged` for exactly this family
   ("the future update family will use the same member"); LOG-001's
   "changing projects" is its category. Info/user/ok, entity and
   `project_id` naming the row, no details (the `register_project`/
   `project_archived` shape — the row itself holds the facts). A send
   whose present fields all equal the stored values — including the
   all-`None` send — is the D-188 verified no-op: the equal fields are
   stripped BEFORE the store call (no `updated_at` restamp — the
   store's own empty/no-op rule), nothing written, nothing journaled.
6. **Validation order (§6.9 all-or-nothing).** SYS-005 gate first
   (the family's first act), then every PRESENT field through the
   shared core validators in §6.9 table order (name, label,
   description, color — the first invalid field answers with the
   `E_VALIDATION` envelope naming it, `rejected_field`; the
   description's NUL-strip is §6.9's own silent rule), then
   `managed_db`, then the one transaction. An entity is never saved
   partly: a refused field means NOTHING was written (the card's DoD).
   The echo split inside that envelope (the `rejected_text_field` vs
   `rejected_title_field` precedents): the name, label and color echo
   the caller's field bounded (D-115's cap — identity fields); the
   description echoes NO value — stored prose is the one thing SEC-008
   keeps out of envelopes, and the validator's reason already carries
   the measured length. The color refusal also states its class
   itself instead of the validator's Display: that Display
   interpolates the sent value, and a caller-supplied string must not
   ride the envelope whole.
7. **T-279's `refresh_after_sync` declined for this card (the D-144
   cross-reference the board asks for).** SYS-007's own list ties
   watch-set changes to a project's addition, scheme or file-name
   change and its archival — name, label, color and description touch
   none of those inputs, so a refresh pass would be file I/O with NO
   observable change (D-194 declined the retrofit for `archive`, a
   command that actually REMOVES watches, on the same basis). The
   wiring belongs to T-107's scheme arm and to T-279's own retrofit
   when it lands (its card lists this arm); PRJ-008's "saving updates
   the column header right away" is the UI re-reading `projects_list`,
   not a watch fact.

Tests: `project_update_tests.rs` — the happy path (four boundary-legal
fields — name 100, label 6, description 1000 code points — saved, the
immutable columns verbatim, one attributable journal entry), the
card's DoD battery (each invalid field: row verbatim + journal

Frontend: the mock twin + `commands.spec.ts` (the same batteries over

### D-202 — T-119: the `sync://progress` event — k-of-N over terminal verdicts, §9.4's phase words, the rate limit as a `SyncRunSeams.progress_clock` seam, and per-write emissions riding the injected write operation — 2026-11-25

Problem: SYS-003 (spec.md:163) and §7.10's events line (spec.md:585)
name `sync://progress` — "progress … no more than 10 times per second"
— but the registry (`collect_events!` in `lib.rs:316-321`; the card's
"lib.rs:224-229" line numbers are stale, verified Rule 2) carries four
events and zero code occurrences of the fifth. The card's own note
(project review 2026-11-23, P2-3): emit at meaningful phase
boundaries, at most 10 emissions per second, behavioral tests of
delivery and rate. MAIN-026 (spec.md:494) is the consumer: a live
"k of N" region while the sync runs.

Readings chosen (Rule 1, recorded before implementation):

- **k and N are §9.4 verdicts, not files or phases.** `done` (k)
  counts the run's projects with a TERMINAL §9.4 verdict —
  `skipped`/`unchanged` from phase 1's transaction on, plus
  `written`/`failed` as phase 3 stamps them — a monotone 0 → N
  counter (a write attempt decides its project: success and failure
  both produce a row). `total` (N) is the run's active project count
  (phase 0's snapshot), constant for the whole run, so MAIN-026's
  region reads one scale per run and never rescales mid-run. Files
  are not counted (a project is one file); phases are not counted
  (four steps make a poor progress scale).
- **One emission immediately before each of phases 1–4 begins, only
  when the run reaches the phase.** `preflight` 0/N right before
  phase 1 (after the DB-032 checkpoint — an emission for a phase a
  refused run never reached would lie), `backups` decided/N right
  before phase 2 (after the D-25 gate and the cancel point — a gated
  or cancelled run has already answered), `write` decided/N right
  before phase 3, `finish` N/N right before phase 4 (phase 3 decided
  every remaining project). NO terminal flush after phase 4 — the
  scan `ProgressTracker` precedent (scan.rs:457-463): the terminal
  state lands in the command's ANSWER, the summary.
- **The phase vocabulary is §9.4's own words, lower-case on the
  wire:** `preflight`, `backups`, `write`, `finish` — the
  `ScanClassWire` serde-rename shape. No `start` member: phase 0 is
  instantaneous (flag + snapshot + row) and its completion IS
  preflight's start; the first emission announces `preflight`.
- **The seam is command-level; no phase module is rewritten.** The
  event DTO, the phase enum, `SYNC_PROGRESS_MIN_INTERVAL` (SYS-003's
  100 ms twin of scan's `PROGRESS_MIN_INTERVAL` — scan's own const
  stays scan's, its doc ties it to ALG-053; two literals for one
  SYS-003 bound is the honest split, each pinned by its own literal
  test) and the shared `SyncProgressReporter` live in `commands.rs`'s
  sync-run region. Per-write emissions — the only place k moves
  WITHIN a phase — ride the injected `seams.write` operation wrapped
  at the command level (a facade phase 3 already calls, the brief's
  own option), so the wrapper's counter and base live where the
  pipeline composition lives. Honest boundaries, recorded: phase 1's
  per-project preflight loop has no injectable seam (adding one
  rewrites the phase — its progress is the boundary pair 0/N →
  decided/N), and phase 2's per-project backups change no verdict,
  so k is static there — neither loop emits per-project events.
- **The rate limit is a `SyncRunSeams` clock member, D-197's
  pattern:** `progress_clock:
Arc<dyn Fn() -> std::time::Instant + Send + Sync>`, production
  `Instant::now` — the throttle's time source is one injectable fact
  (the abort-clock posture, D-197/D-140: deterministic tests over
  simulated instants, never fixed sleeps). The reporter is shared
  (command task + phase 3's blocking-pool closure), so its
  `last_emit` lives behind a `Mutex` whose guard covers exactly the
  rate decision; the EMIT is the caller's (outside the lock — the
  scan callback holds its lock across the emit, this design does
  not need to: the payload is already built). The throttle rule is
  scan's coalescing rule verbatim: the first report emits
  immediately, a later report emits iff ≥ 100 ms passed since the
  last emission, and a suppressed report's state is simply not sent
  — the next emission carries ITS OWN newest state. A refused
  emission is display-only: `logging::sync_progress_emit_failed`
  (the `scan_progress_emit_failed` twin, one minimal widening
  outside the owned pair — the D-147 logging-edge precedent), never
  fatal to the run.
- **The mock side follows the scan twin, exactly:** `IpcEventMap`
  gains `'sync://progress'` typed over the generated payload, and
  `mockEvents.syncProgress` is the typed accessor — but NO mock
  source drives it (the mock `syncRun` emits nothing, the posture
  `scan://progress` itself has on the mock side: the accessor and
  the bus registration are the mock contract; the emitting backend
  task is this one). The event-only rule: `collect_commands!` stays
  40, `mode.spec.ts`'s command pin is untouched (it pins commands,
  not events — verified).

Tests: `commands.rs`'s inline suite — the interval literal
(SYS-003's own arithmetic: 10/s = 100 ms), the wire-name literal,
the immediate first emission, the in-window suppression with
newest-state coalescing, and the rate battery (10_001 reports at
1 ms spacing over a simulated clock → exactly 101 emissions at
0, 100, …, 10_000 ms, consecutive spacing ≥ 100 ms, every sliding
one-second window ≤ 10 — the scan battery's shape). `ipc_tests.rs`
— the delivery test over the REAL phases through `run_sync_with`
(3 projects: one `unchanged` from a first run, two rewritten after
an external edit each) with a JUMPING injected clock (each call ≥
200 ms apart, so every report emits): the exact ordered payload
sequence [(preflight,0,3), (backups,1,3), (write,1,3), (write,2,3),
(write,3,3), (finish,3,3)] and nothing after; the fixed-clock rate
pin (a frozen instant, 6 reports → exactly ONE delivered event —
the pipeline consults the throttle, mutation: bypassing it delivers
all six); the D-25 gate path (a gated run emits only `preflight` —
the emissions stop where the run stopped); and the registration
census marker (`commands::SyncProgressEvent` exactly once in
`lib.rs`, the scan registration-pin shape). `events.spec.ts` — the
`syncProgress` accessor twin over the mock bus. `logging.rs` — the
`sync_progress_emit_failed` line pin (the scan edge's twin: WARN,
the message, the error's Display form). Mutation groups: M1 the
throttle gate removed → the rate battery + the fixed-clock pin
red; M2 the write wrapper's report dropped → the delivery sequence
red; M3 a boundary emission dropped → the delivery sequence red;
M4 the registration dropped → the census pin red (and the export
pin rewrites the bindings); M5 the decided-count base broken →
the delivery sequence red. All five were run red-then-reverted,
M1 twice — once in the red-first round, once on the final
(let-chain-refactored) code.

Verified on the way (Rule 2): tauri-specta's `Event::emit` PANICS
over an unmounted event on the mock runtime ("Event sync://progress
not found in registry!") instead of answering `Err` — so EVERY
harness that drives `sync_run_with` must mount the event, which is
why `sync_pipeline_tests`' World harness gained the registration
line beside `ipc_tests`' `sync_watch_app` (the display-only
emit-failure posture holds for the real runtime; the mock runtime's
panic is the mount wiring's own loud failure, the
reasoning-panic posture). Clippy's `collapsible_if` forces the
let-chain spelling at both emission sites (edition 2024). The
process note: one mutation revert used `git checkout --` on the
still-uncommitted `commands.rs` and wiped the round's work — fully
rebuilt from the session's edit history with no residue, but the
shape to avoid is real: mutation reverts on uncommitted files go
through the same surgical apply/revert they came in with, never
`git checkout`.

Checks: `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2 cargo fmt --check` (green after one
`cargo fmt` pass over the new code); `cargo clippy --workspace
--all-targets -- -D warnings`; `cargo nextest run --workspace
--test-threads=4` — 1871/1871; `cargo test --doc --workspace` (86 +
12, the D-195 ruling); `pnpm test` (361/361), `pnpm run
format:check` (green after prettier --write over this entry),
`pnpm run lint`, `pnpm run typecheck`; `src/bindings.ts`
regenerated through the export pin (first run red — the D-034
mechanic — second run green, the regenerated file committed).

- P2-1 (taken, the round's substance): the boundary-truthfulness

the_typed_envelope` asserts a phase-2 abort emits exactly

- P3-2 (taken as this record): "no more than 10 times per second"

- P3-3 (taken): the four phase words had no serialization pin —

- P3-4 (taken): "phase 0 is instantaneous" contradicted §9.4 (the

- P3-5 (taken): the write wrapper now calls the shared

### D-203 — owner commission: the html-pages prototype delta batch — ten features read into the spec, the wire and guard rulings — 2026-11-25

Problem: the refined main-window prototype (branch `html-pages`, the
ten commits `d6f4069`…`cc24a86`) grew UI features the spec does not
describe, several of which need backend work that has no contract yet.
The owner's commission: verify what appeared, write it into the spec
as contracts (§7.10's unimplemented-command pattern), and card the
work. Every feature was verified against its commit's diff and the
prototype code (`pages/`), per rule 2; the readings below were chosen
before the spec text was written (rule 1), and the new requirement
rows and the §7.10 command notes cite this record (presentation-level
rows and error-table cells reference the requirement IDs instead).
All ten map to the
owner's bullet list one to one; the three CSS-only commits
(`d6f4069` header dividers, `90e4410` "⋮" right alignment,
`f8b6033` settings-modal scroll insets) are presentation-level and
land in the spec as two sentences (UI-023, PRJ-008), not as
behavior contracts.

Readings chosen:

- **(1) The empty-main oracle (commit `f717664`).** The prototype
  disables the "Make main" star while the variant has no name or no
  body (`v.name.trim() === '' || v.text === ''`), live as the text is
  typed. The real contract splits by layer: the LIVE EDITOR gate is
  the prototype's (a draft may carry an empty name — the star
  disables until both are filled, the tooltip names the reason); the
  COMMAND gate (`variant_set_main`, landed T-329 with no such guard —
  `src-tauri/src/variants.rs:692-718` verified) uses the canonical
  emptiness only: a variant whose normalized text is empty —
  `is_empty`, the D-13/ALG-002 oracle D-187/D-198 already fixed for
  the wire — cannot be promoted, refused with the typed `E_VALIDATION`
  naming `id` (the LIB-024/025 layering — the typed command surface
  behind a UI-disabled action; LIB-024/025 additionally never fire
  through the UI, while LIB-036's star-disable is the feature
  itself and the refusal serves stale or direct callers).
  The prototype's raw `text === ''` is the demo's narrower twin — a
  whitespace-only variant outputs no text and cannot serve as the
  default replacement either, so the build's own oracle wins. The
  rule gates the PROMOTION action only: create mode still starts with
  an empty `Main` (LIB-002) and an already-main variant keeps its
  badge while empty. New requirement LIB-036.
- **(2) "Buttons for saving backups" is an EXPORT, not a restore
  (commit `4c942d2`).** The per-row action saves the COPY to a chosen
  location (an OS save dialog in the packaged app; the browser
  equivalent is the download). It is deliberately not BKP-007's
  restore — that stays P1 (D-17), untouched, and T-164's "restore
  from UI is P1" line is not crossed. Contract: `backup_save(id)` —
  the id-addressed row from D-193's list; the save dialog opens from
  Rust (the SEC-001 dialog pattern, `dialog_pick_folder`'s sibling —
  the §5.6 sentence gains this command); the suggested name carries
  the backup's file stem and creation stamp
  (`<stem>.backup-<stamp>.<ext>`, the prototype's layout); the file
  is written to the chosen path and verified against the record's own
  `size_bytes`/`sha256` columns (BKP-010's stored oracle — no new
  digest policy), a mismatch or failed write per §9.5's
  `E_VERIFY_FAILED`/`E_WRITE_FAILED` semantics; a row whose file is
  gone from disk (`pruned`/`missing`/`discarded`, D-193's four
  statuses) is refused with `E_RESTORE_SOURCE_MISSING` — §10's row
  widens from its P1-restore-only wording; an unknown id is the typed
  `E_VALIDATION`. No journal entry (an export of stored data, not a
  recorded action; the prototype logs nothing), no SYS-005 gate (it
  writes outside every managed area and changes no sync state).
  New requirement BKP-012 (renumbered from the draft's BKP-011 by the round-1 review: the §7.6 row "BKP-001, 002, 008, 011" already owns that id — the family-max scan missed the compressed listing; BKP-012 is unused everywhere).
- **(3) The variant-texts popover needs no new wire (commit
  `4c7b6f7`).** The per-cell "eye" opens a read-only popover listing
  every variant of the row — main first, full text, the assigned one
  badged, empty ones noted (D-13) — with no 600-character truncation
  (viewport clamp, inner scroll). D-187's ruling stands: `library_get`
  serves no variant content; the popover fetches each variant's text
  through `variant_get` (D-198's landed contract, per variant id) when
  it opens, lazily. No new fields, no new commands. The popover joins
  the column-menu machinery (outside click, Escape, scroll; the eye
  toggles). New requirement MAIN-032.
- **(4) Replace/extend is a new assignment TARGET, not a rendering
  option (commit `0d33a1f`).** The prototype stores the mode per cell
  and composes `base + BLANK_LINE + supplement`. Readings: (a) the
  extend cell keeps a BASE VARIANT reference beside the supplement —
  §6.2's CHECK gains the third arm `(variant_id NOT NULL AND
custom_text NOT NULL)` (migration 0004 over the landed 0003 shape;
  the v3 exactly-one-target rule is superseded for this arm);
  (b) the composition is DYNAMIC — the build reads the base variant's
  CURRENT text (`normalize(base)` joined with `normalize(supplement)`
  by the §9.2 blank line, either half may be empty — ALG-023), so
  library edits flow in; (c) the base is fixed while the cell is
  custom: it is the cell's assigned variant at "+" press (the main
  for an unassigned cell), the disabled select does not re-pick it,
  and changing the base means deleting the custom instruction and
  creating it again (the UI-010 flow); (d) `assignment_set_custom`
  (landed T-331, `content: Option<String>` — verified) gains a `mode`
  parameter (`replace` | `extend`); (e) everything already ruled for
  custom cells carries over — the disabled "Custom" select, bulk
  operations skip, ALG-020's counts-as-assigned, DB-016's
  reserved-marker rule on the supplement; a variant deletion moves an
  extend cell's BASE to the main variant and keeps the supplement
  (LIB-023's move, the supplement is not an assignment). The
  prototype's editor flow (mode radios visible only in the custom
  mode, hint naming the appended-to pair, untouched-draft swap on
  switching, preview composition, dashed "+" chip, "(supplements
  <variant>)" edit title, delete clears the mode) is the UI
  requirement MAIN-034; the cell-states table gains the extend row.
- **(5) The file preview's contract is the REAL build text, not the
  demo's rendering (commit `b52fff0`).** The prototype's code adds
  each instruction's name as a `##` heading and omits the library's
  section headings — its commit message says "mirrors the real sync
  unit", the code does not quite (rule 2: trust the code, record the
  discrepancy). The spec describes the honest contract: the preview
  shows exactly the next sync's managed content (§9.2/9.3, without
  the creation marker; scheme B shows the managed block only),
  rendered as sanitized Markdown (SEC-005/D-15) for reading —
  headings by ALG-020, no instruction names (ALG-022), effective cell
  text with the ALG-023 composition. New command
  `project_build_preview(project_id)` computes it from the current DB
  state (a read: no SYS-005 gate, like `library_get`); the modal
  renders through the existing `markdown_preview`; the active-project
  scoping follows `project_update`'s typed refusal (unknown or
  archived id → `E_VALIDATION` naming `project_id`). Empty column →

  icon, first item of the column "⋮" menu) are described as they
  stand; picking one is an explicit open point for the owner.
  New requirement MAIN-033, the modal joins UI-002's list.
- **(6) The section picker realizes S3, no new backend (commit
  `53a2819`).** The create dialog gains a Section select (create mode
  only): headings indented by depth, the FIRST TOP-LEVEL SECTION
  preselected (the spec fixed no default — now it does), "(no
  sections)" disabled when the library has no headings and the
  instruction then lands at the table end. The wire is D-188's
  `section: Option<String>` unchanged — the picked heading id places
  the instruction at that heading's section end (the LIB-032
  drop-on-heading target D-188 already chose); the prototype's
  picker lists headings only (no explicit root entry — the root
  placement stays a wire capability of the landed command, not a
  picker option). Requirement text joins LIB-002's row.
- **(7) The root-section deletion rule is mirrored in the command
  (commit `cc24a86`).** The prototype disables the trash on a level-2
  section while its section holds anything (instructions, nested
  headings; hidden rows count), with the tooltip naming LIB-033's

  nested and empty root sections stay deletable; every membership
  mutation refreshes the buttons and a stale click never opens the

  `src-tauri/src/headings.rs:723-733` verified) deletes
  unconditionally — it gains the defensive refusal: a level-2 heading

- **(8) The three CSS commits land as presentation requirements.**
  UI-023: adjacent project header cells carry a visible divider

  column "⋮" button sits at the header cell's right edge, the same

Scope and honesty boundaries (rule 11): every UI feature is written
as the prototype behaves it; every backend piece that does not exist

`heading_delete` guards, the extend schema and command shape) is

### D-204 — T-107: `project_update`'s scheme, file-name and extra-file arm — the watch-verdict inputs as a patch, extra files stored under every scheme (store-anyway), and the DB-023 dirty clause decided by the row, never written — 2026-11-25

The card (§7.10 Projects `project_update`; PRJ-012, DB-023, D-01, D-03,
§7.5, SYS-005, SYS-007, LOG-001…004) extends T-106's landed command
(D-201, commit df6ef88) with the settings modal's write-configuration
half: `scheme`, `base_name`, and the two extra-file options. The card
leaves nine points open to more than one reading; the chosen readings
were written here BEFORE the implementation (the rule-1 discipline).
The command keeps D-201's contract whole — the same id-addressed patch
surface (`Result<(), AppError>`), the same `reject_during_sync` first,
the same `managed_db` honest `NoDatabase` answer, the same ONE
`Db::run` transaction carrying the store update and the journal insert,
the same module (`project_update.rs` + `project_update_tests.rs`,
extended — no second command, the registry stays at 41).

1. **The wire: four more flat optional args, two of them a typed
   object.** `project_update(project_id, name, label, color,
description, scheme, base_name, extra_local, extra_project)` —
   D-201's flat-args reading extended (tauri-specta maps each arg to
   one invoke key; `base_name`→`baseName`, the extras→`extraLocal`/
   `extraProject`). `scheme` and `base_name` are `Option<String>`:
   closed vocabularies the command itself parses, so an off-list
   literal answers the TYPED `E_VALIDATION` envelope naming the field
   (the color's own precedent — a specta-typed enum arg would move the
   refusal to Tauri's arg-deserialization boundary, an untyped string
   error with no `message_key` for UI-011 to localize). The extras are
   `Option<ExtraFilePatch>` — a new wire DTO
   `{enabled: bool, position: String}` (the §6.5 JSON object shape,
   the core `ExtraFile` serde twin, both members required and unknown
   members refused at the invoke boundary, the D-003 typed-IPC
   reading): `position` stays a `String` for the same typed-refusal
   reason; `enabled` is a `bool` (a non-boolean shape is an
   invoke-level deserialization failure, exactly as a non-string
   `name` already is — the boundary's own behavior, not a field
   refusal). The store's `ProjectUpdate` already carries all four
   fields (`crates/eunomia-store/src/projects.rs:747-765`) — the
   command fills them; the store is untouched.
2. **Validation order: the §6.9 fields first, then the PRJ-012 half in
   its own sentence order.** §6.9's table carries only ONE of the new
   fields (File name, near the table's end); scheme and the extra
   positions are §7.5/§6.5 closed vocabularies, not §6.9 rows. The
   order: name, label, description, color (D-201's table order,
   unchanged), then scheme, base_name, extra_local, extra_project
   (PRJ-012's own sentence — "its own scheme, file name, and extra
   files"). The two-fault ordering precedent extends: an invalid name
   plus an invalid scheme answers about `name`; an invalid scheme plus
   an invalid base_name answers about `scheme`. The vocabulary
   refusals echo the caller's literal bounded (D-115's cap — the wire
   string is unbounded by definition) with a class-only reason: "the
   scheme must be one of A, B, C (spec 7.5)" / "the file name must be
   AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md (spec D-03)" / "the position must be start
   or end (spec 6.5)". Case-sensitive, like every schema CHECK
   literal (`settings::Scheme::from_member`'s own posture).
3. **Extra files under schemes B/C: STORE-ANYWAY — the spec's own
   words, not a refusal and not a silent ignore.** The §6.2 columns
   are NOT NULL on every row (every scheme); §6.5's `default.extra_*`
   seeds EVERY new project whatever `default.scheme` is, so a scheme-B
   row carries extra values by construction; the builder ignores them
   under B/C (ALG-030's "(A only)"; the core `ExtraFile` doc's own
   "under schemes B and C the builder ignores them, mirroring the
   spec"); DB-020's formula hashes "extra-file flags and positions"
   with NO scheme qualifier (`hash.rs`'s recorded reading — the hash
   fingerprints the build configuration), so an extra flip under B/C
   changes the hash and dirties the row; PRJ-008's "extra files only
   in scheme A" names the MODAL's scheme-conditional block (the UI
   hides the controls), never a store rule. A refusal would break the
   B→A switch (the dormant value must survive it — PRJ-012's "a
   project has its own … extra files" is the row's, not the scheme
   window's), and a silent ignore would contradict the hash formula.
   The command therefore stores extra-file fields under every
   scheme, journals the change, and dirties through the hash arm; the
   brief's DoD sketch ("extra fields on a B/C target → nothing
   saved") was written against this unresolved reading — the
   spec-decided oracle is its store-anyway opposite, pinned by a
   test.
4. **base_name and scheme validation (§6.9's File-name row, §7.5).**
   The file name is "a value from the list", D-03's list —
   `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md`, the closed `BaseName` vocabulary
   (`BaseName::from_member`'s two literals); "path and extension are
   not typed in" is why the vocabulary is closed at all. The scheme
   is §7.5's A/B/C. An off-vocabulary literal refuses the whole save
   (§6.9's all-or-nothing, D-201 point 6 extended): row verbatim,
   journal absent.
5. **The DB-023 dirty clause: decided by the row, never written
   (D-194's DB-014 posture).** The command writes the row only — no
   dirty flag, no hash cell, no `last_synced_*` churn (OUT-020's
   fact stays the sync's own). The stored `last_synced_hash` was
   computed over the OLD build configuration; DB-020 hashes scheme +
   target path + the extra flags and positions + the build text; the
   DB-022 service's next pass (the commit hook fires on the row
   change; the tests drive `recalc_and_emit` directly — T-108's
   surface) recomputes over the NEW configuration, the hash differs,
   DB-021 answers dirty. Nothing in the command duplicates that
   decision — the DoD asserts it through the real service's diff and
   `projects_list`'s `dirty` column.
6. **The old file on disk: NO file I/O in the command (the D-194
   posture).** DB-023's "the old file with the previous name is not
   deleted" is a prohibition on the app, and §7.5 assigns no cleanup
   anywhere (scheme C "does not open the main file"; scheme A/C write
   the new target at the next sync; scheme B splices in place) — the
   old file's fate is the user's own. The command changes the DB row
   only; the next sync writes the new target; the watch refresh's
   pass READS target files (its verdicts) and writes nothing. The
   DoD's disk oracle: a real file, a scheme/base_name change, the
   bytes read back verbatim.
7. **The watch refresh: the committed arm carries the four
   watch-verdict inputs (T-279/D-144 — the OPPOSITE arm from D-201
   point 7).** SYS-007's own list ties watch changes to "a project is
   added or its scheme or file name changes" — and the pass's
   `ProjectFact` consumes exactly the four fields this arm can change
   (`file_watch.rs`: scheme, base_name, extra_local, extra_project —
   the set membership through `target_file_name(scheme, base_name)`,
   the VERDICTS through the extras feeding the expected target
   content). So the committed arm — the patch actually changed at
   least one of the four — awaits ONE full watch pass through the
   BOUNDED mutation seam `file_watch::refresh_after_mutation`
   (D-156/T-280: the brief names D-144's `refresh_after_sync`, but
   the interactive-caller one-liner `project_add_manual` itself has
   called since T-280 is the bounded twin; the unbounded seam stays
   the sync pipeline's), never-fatal aftermath —
   `logging::file_watch_mutation_refresh_degraded` on refusal, the
   save stands, the next anchor re-converges the set (D-144's
   convergence). A no-change patch AND a name/label/color/
   description-only change run NO refresh: the pass would be file
   I/O over inputs that did not move (D-201 point 7's own list, the
   boundary this card extends). The refresh runs AFTER the commit
   (the transaction's `Ok` carries whether the watch-input half
   changed — the journal insert stays INSIDE the transaction, the
   refresh strictly after it).
8. **The journal: ONE `project.changed` entry, D-201 point 5's shape,
   NO details.** Entity and `project_id` name the row; the field set
   stays out — the row itself holds every fact this command writes
   (D-201's own reading, extended to the new half), the entry shape
   stays uniform across the command's whole field set (one modal
   save = one entry whatever half changed), and nothing
   user-content rides the entry (Rule 8).
9. **The no-op extension.** A send whose present fields all equal the
   stored values writes, journals and refreshes nothing (D-201 point
   5 extended): the extras compare as whole values (enabled and
   position together — a disabled-but-different position is a REAL
   row change: the column changes and DB-020 hashes it), and the
   store's own empty-update rule still refuses to churn `updated_at`.

Tests: `project_update_tests.rs` extended — fifteen new tests and
three extended ones. The card's DoD battery: the scheme-change and
base-name-change dirty+untouched-file pins (DB-023's both halves,
through the real `recalc_and_emit` pass and `projects_list`'s column
over a clean baseline spelled through the public core `build_hash`
seam), the extra-file dirty pin (DB-020's no-qualifier formula) and
its scheme-B arm (the flags alone move the hash — the managed text
under B gains no reading line), the disabled-position whole-pair pin
(a position-only change with the flag off is a real, journaled,
dirty-making row change), each invalid literal saves nothing (scheme,
base_name, both extras' positions — case-sensitivity and the bounded
echo pinned), the two-fault ordering pins (the §6.9 half first, then
PRJ-012's own order, extra_local before extra_project), the
store-anyway pin under scheme B, the four wiring pins (one awaited
pass on a scheme, a file-name and an extra-file change each; none on
a name-only change or the unchanged re-send — the pass counter over
the quiescent `converge_startup_watch` baseline the deterministic
observable, no sleeps and no absolute pass indexing), the
whole-configuration happy path, and the E_SYNC_RUNNING / NoDatabase /
unknown-id arms re-sent with the new fields. Frontend: the mock
twin's `commands.spec.ts` battery (seven new tests: the happy path,
the vocabulary refusals with bounded echo and both extras' tokens,
the ordering mirror, the scheme-B store-anyway mirror, the
whole-pair position mirror, the no-op mirror, the
valid-scheme-over-unknown-id mirror) and the `mode.spec` surface pin
unchanged at 41 names. Mutation groups are recorded in the review
addendum below.

Checks: BDD red-first (the new tests written against the un-widened
command — the compile failure IS the red state — then green after the
implementation); all runs exit-code-gated under `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2`,
nextest `--test-threads=4`; the D-195 doc-test pass included;
prettier/eslint/typecheck for the frontend half.

### D-205 — T-109: the `project_restore` command's contract — the exclusion deletion is reason-agnostic (the pinned manual-exclusion ruling), the no-existence arm converges, and double-restore is D-194's converging no-op mirrored — 2026-11-25

The card's spec text (PRJ-013…018, §6.4, D-10, DB-015, SYS-005,
SYS-007) leaves six points open to more than one reading; the chosen
readings were written here BEFORE the implementation (the rule-1
discipline). The command is the D-194 mirror: id-addressed
(`Result<(), AppError>`, the `project_archive` wire family — §7.10
names no payload, and the D-10 "Archived projects" screen plus the two
DB-015 offer carriers that already exist (`project_add_manual`'s
`archived_duplicate` arm and `scan_commit`'s `"archived"` outcome,
both naming the row through `existing`) re-read through the landed
`projects_list` and `exclusions_list`. A new module
`src-tauri/src/project_restore.rs` + `project_restore_tests.rs` (the
T-108 shape); `reject_during_sync` first, `managed_db`'s honest
`NoDatabase`, then ONE `Db::run` transaction (D-037) carrying the
store's `projects::restore` transition, the exclusion deletion(s) and
the in-transaction journal insert — commit or roll back together
(D-051).

1. **The exclusion deletion is keyed by `path_key` and is
   reason-AGNOSTIC — the pinned owner ruling, recorded, not
   re-opened.** PRJ-013…018's own words decide the composition:
   "Restoring … removes its path from the exclusions" names the END
   STATE, not a row class, so the restore deletes whatever exclusion
   row holds the row's `path_key` (DB-030's identity, the same key the
   archive wrote): the archive-born `removed_scanned` row AND a
   pre-existing `manual` exclusion the archive deliberately left in
   place (D-194 point 1's convergence — its round-2 P3-6 note: "T-109's
   `project_restore` will delete that manual row too, silently undoing
   the user's own exclusion of the path"; the pinned card comment
   carries the same ruling). The manual row's own reason and date are
   facts of their own, but the restore half owns this composition: the
   restored project's path must come back to the scan's discovered
   set, and a surviving manual row would keep hiding it (D-098's
   classifier would answer `archived`/`excluded` over a row that is
   active again). Pinned by a test where a manual exclusion predates
   the archive and is gone after the restore.
2. **No exclusion at all: converging, not a refusal.** A row whose
   exclusion was hand-removed while it was archived (the §6.4
   physical-delete arm — "the path is found by a scan again") or a
   manual-born row that never had one restores fine: the removal's end
   state is already true, the transition and the journal entry are the
   act. This is D-196's `find_exclusion_by_path_key`-then-delete shape
   (the lift answers nothing when the find answers `None`) and
   D-194 point 2's own mirror sentence ("the removal is the user's
   explicit §6.4 act") read from the restore side: the restore never
   re-adds what the user removed, and its target state needs no
   re-add. A refusal here would trap a hand-removed row out of the
   restore forever — §6.4 assigns no such dead end.
3. **Double-restore: a converging no-op (D-194 point 2 mirrored).** A
   re-send on an already-active row answers `Ok(())` with NOTHING
   written — no journal entry, `updated_at` not restamped (the store's
   `restore` returns an active row unchanged, its own idempotence
   rule), no exclusion churn even if an exclusion row with the same
   `path_key` has since appeared (round 1's P3-6 corrected the
   builder list: this command's own cycle cannot leave the pair — the
   restore deletes the row, and the archive writes no exclusion when
   one already exists — so the reachable builders are a hand-seeded
   row, a `db_restore_backup` landing a mixed pair, or a manual add
   over a still-excluded path (`project_add_manual` lifts no
   exclusion, D-196's boundary); the churn would override a fact the
   re-send did not own, D-194's own no-override posture). The
   `assignment_set` precedent: a same-state re-send writes/journals
   nothing. The stale screen the archived
   screen becomes when the row was restored elsewhere (DB-015's offer
   is one carrier) converges instead of erroring — the exact mirror
   of the archive's already-archived arm, and the OPPOSITE family
   member from `project_update`'s archived-id refusal (D-201 point 4),
   which protects a PATCH from wiping a row that left the modal's
   world: a restore re-send writes nothing the first send did not
   already write, so there is nothing to protect.
4. **Unknown id: the typed `E_VALIDATION` refusal naming
   `project_id`** with the bounded echo (D-115's cap — the
   `project_archive` arm, `bounded_echo`); nothing was written. This
   arm is the stale-screen shape regardless of the point-3 reading.
5. **The watch arm (SYS-007, T-279/D-204): the committed transition
   awaits ONE full watch pass through the bounded mutation seam.**
   SYS-007's own sentence — "removed when a project is archived" —
   read in reverse is the restore's membership half: the row returns
   to the watched set, the ADD arm's shape (D-144's list: the refresh
   belongs to the mutation that moves a row INTO the set or moves its
   verdict inputs), so the committed arm (the row actually transitioned
   archived → active) awaits ONE full pass through
   `file_watch::refresh_after_mutation` (D-156 — the same one-liner
   `project_add_manual` and T-107's arm run; the bounded wait, the
   never-fatal aftermath, `logging::
file_watch_mutation_refresh_degraded` on refusal, the save standing)
   strictly AFTER the transaction — the journal insert stays inside
   it, the refresh never is. A converging no-op arm runs NO refresh (a
   pass over a row that did not move is file reads with no observable
   change, D-201 point 7's own boundary). **The recorded boundary: the
   archive ran no refresh** (D-194: the leaver exits the set at the
   next anchor's pass; the card asked for none) — the asymmetry is
   deliberate and is the add/remove split D-144 itself drew: the ADD
   side's verdict inputs are the user's fresh concern, the removal is
   realized by every later pass's active-only re-derivation. The
   restore is the add side.
6. **The dirty flag: decided by the row and the service, never
   written (D-194 point 3 / D-204 point 5 posture).** The command
   writes NOTHING beyond the row (plus the exclusion deletion and the
   journal): no `last_synced_hash` churn — the stored hash is the one
   D-194 point 3 deliberately kept, covering the PRE-archive build
   configuration, and it stays exactly where the archive left it. The
   next `recalc_and_emit` pass (the DB-022 commit hook fires on the
   row change; the tests drive the service directly, T-107's surface)
   recomputes over the now-ACTIVE row (DB-021 over DB-020): the world
   unchanged since the last sync answers clean, an assignment that
   landed while the row was archived (the store's `assign` is
   state-blind) answers dirty — the DoD pins both halves through the
   real service and `projects_list`'s `dirty` column. The project is
   back in the sync set by the store's read (`read_build_snapshot`
   reads `ListScope::Active` — D-194 point 3's own construction,
   reversed).
7. **The journal: ONE `project.restored` entry, no exclusion member.**
   LOG-001…004's own list puts "restoring projects" in the journal;
   the closed vocabulary's member is `Action::ProjectRestored` →
   `"project.restored"` (verified in
   `crates/eunomia-store/src/action_log.rs`), info/user/ok, entity
   columns naming the project, `project_id` set, NO details (the
   `project.archived` shape — the row itself holds the path). The
   exclusion deletion is NOT journaled separately: D-194 point 4's
   mirror — this entry, unlike `exclusion_remove`'s, names its object,
   and the D-10 "Excluded paths" screen re-reads the table through
   `exclusions_list` (the row's disappearance IS the screen's data).
   D-196's `scan_commit` journaled its `exclusion.removed` because the
   lift was that batch's own typed outcome event with the D-119
   deviation to record; the restore is one PRJ-013…018 act, and the
   pinned ruling's own word for the manual-row deletion is
   "silently". The DB-015 offer carriers need no journal of their own
   either — the restore they invoke is the entry.
8. **No file WRITES; the watch refresh is the one file-system
   interaction (D-204 point 6's posture, mirrored).** §6.4's folder
   guarantee holds through the restore exactly as through the archive:
   the target file's bytes are the user's own until the next sync; the
   one deliberate exception to the command's otherwise complete lack
   of file-system interaction is the point-5 refresh pass, which only
   READS target files (OUT-011). A dead folder restores fine — no
   availability probe, no folder check (`projects_list`'s own docs
   keep the restore path available on an unavailable column's row).
   Complexity stays trivially stated: one transaction, indexed by-id
   and by-key store reads/writes.
