### D-206 — owner commission: the main-window mock-up joins main as the frozen visual reference `docs/prototype/` — the 2026-11-25 rulings on the frontend skeleton, the porting split, and the board↔spec audit — 2026-11-25

Problem: the approved mock-up (branch `html-pages`, 53 commits over the
merge-base `24e745b`, head `cc24a86`) lived only on its branch and on the
Netlify demo (https://es-demo-634.netlify.app), which keeps following the
branch — while D-125 (41 gaps, spec 1.2) and D-203 (ten features) cite its
commits as evidence, and executors work in fresh worktrees that need the
reference locally. Three files, no dependencies, no build step:
`pages/index.html` (3,945 lines), `pages/app.js` (5,143), `pages/styles.css`
(3,136) — 12,224 lines. The owner's commission of 2026-11-25: bring it into
`main` as a frozen visual reference and record the rulings below. The copies
landed as `docs/prototype/{index.html,app.js,styles.css}`, byte-identical to
`cc24a86:pages/*` — verified per file by blob id (`git rev-parse
cc24a86:pages/<file>` equals `git hash-object docs/prototype/<file>`:
`index.html` `30007dda6548e14ea905e44df676e9003f653349`, `app.js`
`4cc26ed4cf9b5bf4e128d23436b39954f6854268`, `styles.css`
`80dd735a527711a1a4e9594227c019ad85abcea7`) — and are never edited
afterwards.

The owner's rulings of 2026-11-25:

1. **The mock-up is a frozen visual reference, excluded from every
   check.** `.prettierignore` excludes `docs/prototype` (this record);
   `eslint.config.js` lists it in the config-level `ignores`; vue-tsc
   never sees it (`tsconfig.json`'s `include` lists only `src/**`); CI's
   `lint` job runs `pnpm run lint`, `pnpm run format:check`,
   `pnpm run typecheck` — none of them walks `docs/`. It is not code to
   check, and nothing is compiled or emitted from it: the one build-side
   reader is Tailwind's automatic content scan (`src/assets/main.css`
   imports `tailwindcss` without an `@source` limit), which reads the
   folder read-only for candidate class names, as it reads every other
   unignored source, and cannot fail. The spec (`docs/spec.md`) stays
   the behavioral truth, the mock-up the visual one — where they
   disagree, the spec wins (the demo deviations are listed in D-125 and
   D-203). AGENTS.md now names the reference and this rule.
2. **The porting split: the JS stays unported; markup and CSS are ported
   as material; UI texts go to the i18n catalog.** Behavior is written
   from the spec, never from `app.js` (126 functions over
   `getElementById`/`querySelector`, demo data tables; 6 ESLint errors
   under the project's config — the demo JS is neither linted nor
   fixed). The texts go to the i18n catalog in temporary per-feature
   files (T-363), where the owner refines them.
3. **The frontend gets a skeleton layer before the feature cards.**
   T-362 theme tokens, T-363 main-window shell on seed data (absorbs
   T-148), T-364 matrix, T-365 library dialogs (absorbs T-186), T-366
   project dialogs, T-367 service dialogs — all in TODO with the labels
   `html` and `flash`. Afterwards the feature cards refine the existing
   components instead of building screens from scratch.
4. **NFR-001's supported floor rises to macOS 12.3.** The spec edit is
   T-361, processed right after this record and landed by D-207 — the
   task commit was first created as `2bc6b84` and then amended in place
   to carry it: three Markdown-only edits — the LIB-024 hint
   exception for single-variant instructions, the floor itself, and a
   note on UI-020's per-feature catalog files. The two code comments
   naming the old floor are updated by T-362.
5. **The i18n catalog is split per feature temporarily and merged
   later.**
6. **The palette is the executor's discretion within `theme.spec.ts`**
   (starting values in T-362).

### D-207 — three owner rulings land in the spec: the LIB-024 hint hidden for single-variant instructions, the supported floor at macOS 12.3, UI-020's temporary per-feature catalog — 2026-11-25

Problem: three owner decisions existed only on the board and in
conversation while the spec said otherwise. The LIB-024 hint — "Make
another variant main first" (the D-125 wording, spec 7.3) — is
meaningless when there is nothing to make main: an instruction that has
only its main variant. NFR-001 said "macOS 12 and newer" while the UI
relies on the native `<dialog>` element (all 23 of its dialogs), which
needs Safari 15.4 = macOS 12.3 — the two claims could not both hold.

rulings 2 and 5) splits the catalog per feature so the owner can refine
texts in small files. The rulings below resolve all three; the spec edit is

(D-206's own snapshot of it, ruling 4, is refreshed by this record).

Sources: card T-333 — the owner triage ruling of 2026-11-24 (the
round-1 review of T-318, finding P3-3, D-176) — and the conversation
with the owner of 2026-11-25.

1. **The LIB-024 hint is hidden when the instruction has only the main

### D-208 — T-110: the `project_relink` command's contract — the Locate flow's gate order (the add flow's mirror with the probe before the transaction), the subfolder resolved to the repository root, and the DB-015 archived collision carrying the restore offer's id — 2026-11-25

The card's spec text (D-09, DB-015, SYS-005, §7.10; the DoD "the
project is available again after the path change, assignments
preserved") leaves eight points open to more than one reading; the
chosen readings were written here BEFORE the implementation (the
rule-1 discipline). The card's pinned cross-link comment (from T-077,
dated before T-109) is TRUE and consumed for this task's own
territory: the restore command it asks for LANDED as T-109/D-205, so
the DB-015 archived-collision refusal this command answers can carry
the row's id for a restore offer with a real consumer already
registered. The named dependencies were verified by grep before any
reliance (Rule 2): the git-root finding
`eunomia_fs::paths::find_git_root` (crates/eunomia-fs/src/paths.rs),
the projects repository with the schema's `path_key UNIQUE`
(crates/eunomia-store/src/projects.rs, migrations/0001_init.sql), and
the `sync_running` flag with `reject_during_sync`
(src-tauri/src/commands.rs) — all landed.

1. **The wire: id-addressed with one path argument,
   `Result<(), AppError>`** (§7.10 names no payload for any project
   command; the D-205/D-194/D-201 family's `()` — the screens re-read
   through `projects_list`). The gate order is the ADD flow's mirror
   (the only family member that also receives a picked folder):
   SYS-005 first (`reject_during_sync` — a check, never an acquire),
   then SEC-003 (`session_paths::validate_ui_path` — the Locate path
   is a UI-named path from `dialog_pick_folder`, so it must be a
   registered project or a session pick; the session half passes
   before any database read, so recovery mode stays consistent), then
   the `.git` check, then `managed_db`, then ONE `Db::run` transaction
   carrying the row transition and the in-transaction journal insert
   (D-037/D-051 — commit or roll back together). The pinned
   cross-link's consumer-facing half: `scan_commit`'s `"archived"`
   outcome and `project_add_manual`'s `archived_duplicate` are the
   ADD flows' own carriers and stay theirs; this command's refusal
   vocabulary is below.
2. **The `.git` check resolves the picked folder to its repository's
   CANONICAL ROOT and relinks there — no `repo_root_offered` arm.**
   D-09's own words ("a new path with a `.git` check") name a check,
   never an offer; the offer is PRJ-003's add-specific reading ("the
   app offers the root, it does not silently register a different
   folder than the one the user picked") about CREATING a row from a
   pick — a relink re-points an EXISTING row whose identity is the
   row (name, label, color, description, origin, position all stay),
   so there is nothing to silently register. The card's dependency
   sentence — find the git repository ROOT for the selected folder —
   is the ruling: `find_git_root` walks up (nearest root wins, D-06),
   and the ROOT's verbatim UTF-8 text plus `path_key(&root)` (the
   identity half of `ProjectFields::derive`, the add's own
   derivation) become the new `path`/`path_key`. The path and the key
   change together by construction — the key IS derived from the
   canonical path (DB-030). The probe runs BEFORE the transaction on
   the blocking pool (SYS-001 and the D-096 ordering: a dead drive
   must not hold the one database lock — the add flow's own
   placement): a folder outside any repository answers §10's
   `E_NOT_A_REPO` ("pick the repository root"); a root whose
   canonical text is not valid UTF-8 is the D-086 addendum's encoding
   rejection. A DEAD new path never reaches the probe: the SEC-003
   gate canonicalizes the sent path first, and an unresolvable path
   answers its own recorded refusal (E_VALIDATION naming `path` —
   "not allowlisted", whatever the OS reason, D-100's recorded cost);
   the probe's own io-refusal belt (`E_PROJECT_UNAVAILABLE` with the
   OS facts — "could not check" is not "not a repo", D-090's split,
   `repo_lookup_failed`) covers the mid-flight race between the two
   canonicalizations. **The OLD path is never probed at all**: the
   common case is the folder MOVED (gone), but a copied
   repository (the old path still alive) relinks identically — the
   old folder's existence is not a fact this command reads, and no
   file at either path is written or read beyond the root probe
   itself.
3. **The transaction: row read → convergence → DB-015 → the store's
   `relink` → ONE journal entry.** The by-id read first: an id no
   ACTIVE row matches — unknown, or archived since the column's
   marking was rendered (the Locate action rides an active matrix
   column, D-09/MAIN-028; the archived screen's own action is
   Restore) — is the typed `E_VALIDATION` refusal naming
   `project_id` with the bounded echo (D-115's cap; the
   `project_update` stale-screen shape, D-201 point 4). Then the
   idempotence rule (make-operations-idempotent): a re-send whose
   resolved root equals the row's stored `path` AND `path_key`
   converges — `Ok(())`, nothing written, no `updated_at` restamp, no
   journal entry, no watch refresh (the D-201 point-5/D-204 point-9
   verified no-op; a screen's retry after any interruption converges).
   Then DB-015 INSIDE the transaction (the add flow's own
   serialization rule: the check and the write share the one
   connection, so the write cannot race past it):
   `find_by_path_key` over the NEW key, the row itself excluded —
   a collision is refused (point 5). Then the store's new
   `relink(conn, id, path, path_key)` writer: ONE `UPDATE` setting
   `path`, `path_key` and `updated_at` (the DB-002 stamp — the row's
   own edit clock; the sync facts deliberately NOT restamped), with
   the store-level convergence guard
   `WHERE id = ? AND (path <> ? OR path_key <> ?)` — the
   `archive`/`restore` shape (a matched-rows count of 0 reads the row
   back: `None` is `NotFound`, `Some` is the converging no-op), and
   the `duplicate_or_sql` belt mapping the schema's `path_key UNIQUE`
   violation to `DuplicatePathKey` (unreachable past the command's
   pre-check on the one connection — the D-103 convergence rule; if
   it ever fires anyway it reaches the `projects_store_to_app_error`
   fallback, never a masked conflict). The journal: ONE
   `project.changed` entry — the closed vocabulary's own recorded
   member ("A project's row changed (update, relink, reorder)",
   `crates/eunomia-store/src/action_log.rs`; LOG-001…004 lists
   "changing projects" with no relinking member of its own),
   info/user/ok, entity and `project_id` naming the row, NO details
   (the `project_update` shape: the row itself holds every fact this
   command writes).
4. **What the transition does NOT move: the family posture, mirrored
   from D-205 point 6.** The assignments stay verbatim (DB-014 — the
   DoD's second half; the store's assignment rows are keyed by the
   project id, which does not move), and so do `sort_order`,
   `added_via`, `state`, every §6.9/PRJ-012 field and — the load-
   bearing keep — `last_synced_hash`/`last_synced_at` (OUT-020's
   cells are the sync's own; the command writes no hash of its own).
   The DB-020 formula covers the TARGET PATH
   (`sha256('v1' + scheme + target path + …)`, the core's
   `content_build` spelling `<root>/<base_name>`), so the stored
   pre-relink hash and the next recomputation differ by construction:
   the dirty verdict is decided by the row and the DB-022 service,
   never written here (the D-194 point-3/D-204 point-5/D-205 point-6
   row-decidable posture — the DoD pins it through the real
   `recalc_and_emit` pass and `projects_list`'s `dirty` column: clean
   before over the old target, dirty after over the new one).
5. **The DB-015 refusals: `E_VALIDATION` naming `path`, the caller's
   path echoed bounded, class-only reasons — and the archived arm
   carries the restore offer's id.** §10's `E_VALIDATION` row owns
   this ("the operation's own state forbids it": another row, active
   or archived, holds the resolved key). Both arms refuse the whole
   operation with the `rejected_field` shape (`field: "path"`, the
   bounded echo of the caller's path, D-115's cap): an ACTIVE
   collision — "an active project already has this path (DB-015)"
   (the user's action is §10's own: fix the field, pick another
   folder); an ARCHIVED collision — the DB-015 offer shape adapted to
   the `Result<(), AppError>` wire: the same refusal plus
   `params.existing_project_id`, the archived row's id (a UUIDv7
   TEXT, DB-002 — machine-generated identity, not user content, so
   Rule 8 does not keep it off the envelope; the add flows' existing
   answer is the precedent). The id is what the offer needs: the UI
   cannot find the archived row itself (`projects_list` serves no
   path column), and the consumer exists — `project_restore`
   (T-109/D-205) takes exactly that id. The refusal names the class
   ("an archived project already has this path (DB-015)"), never the
   stored name or path. Nothing is written in either arm.
6. **The watch arm (SYS-007, T-279/D-204 — the LAST member of
   T-279's list): the path IS a watch input, and the committed arm
   awaits ONE full watch pass.** The pass's `ProjectFact` carries the
   row's `root` (`file_watch.rs` — the watched file is
   `root + target_file_name`), so a committed relink moves the watch
   input exactly the way a scheme/file-name change does (D-204 point
   7): strictly AFTER the transaction (the journal insert stays
   inside it, the refresh never is), the committed arm — the row
   actually moved — awaits ONE full pass through the bounded mutation
   seam `file_watch::refresh_after_mutation` (D-156 — the same
   awaited one-liner `project_add_manual`, T-107 and T-109 run),
   never-fatal: a refused send, a failed pass or an expired budget
   degrades with `logging::file_watch_mutation_refresh_degraded` and
   the relink stands; the next anchor re-derives the set (D-144's
   convergence). A refused arm never reaches the refresh; the
   converging re-send runs none (a pass over a row that did not move
   is file reads with no observable change, D-201 point 7's own
   boundary). With this command landed, every member of T-279's
   refresh list the spec names exists — `project_add_manual` (add),
   `project_update` (scheme/file-name/extra), `project_restore`
   (restore), `project_relink` (relink); the orchestrator can close
   T-279's card.
7. **The availability DoD ("снова доступен"): the command writes no
   availability anywhere — the pin runs the real probe surfaces.**
   Availability is a fact about the machine's current filesystem,
   owned by the D-084 probes (`availability::recheck_and_emit`'s
   diff and `projects_list`'s fresh per-read column, D-09/DB-032);
   a relink that wrote a verdict would freeze a fact the next probe
   re-derives. The DoD is pinned the family way (the dirty tests'
   shape): the world starts in D-09's situation — the row's old
   folder gone, one `recheck_and_emit` pass records the unavailable
   verdict and emits the diff — then the relink lands, and the next
   pass answers the RECOVERY change (`available: true`, the reason
   gone) while `projects_list`'s column reads available over the new
   path.
8. **No file WRITES (the D-194/D-204/D-205 posture).** The old target
   file, wherever it survived, is the user's own (the add's
   "nothing is touched" half mirrored); the new target file is the
   next sync's. The one file-system interaction is READ-only: the
   root probe (point 2) and the watch pass it may await (OUT-011).
   Complexity stays stated: the root probe is the canonical
   walk-up's linear climb (D-090's own bound), the store writes are
   indexed by-id and by-key, and the transaction is one
   statement-plus-journal — untrusted text (the caller's path) is
   probed, echoed bounded, and never interpolated into diagnostics
   (Rule 8).

Problem: the theme shipped only the eight T-145 tokens (page, surface,

adjustment. Two smaller debts rode along: D-207 (ruling 2) raised the
NFR-001 floor to macOS 12.3 and left the two code comments naming the
old floor to this task, and Tailwind's automatic source detection has
been silently reading the frozen mock-up's styles.css.

palette (docs/prototype/styles.css, light block from line 24, dark
block from line 58).

1. **The palette is the card's starting values, unchanged.** Thirteen
   tokens, each in ALL THREE theme.css blocks (light `:root`,
   `[data-theme='dark']`, and the `@media (prefers-color-scheme:
dark)` fallback — the two dark sets identical), six-digit hex.

   | token         | light   | dark    |
   | ------------- | ------- | ------- |

   Deviations from the card: none — every starting value was checked

3. **Decorative values stay out of theme.css.** The row hover tint,

   in the styles of the components that draw them, outside the

4. **`@source not '../../docs/prototype'` in src/assets/main.css.**
   Automatic source detection starts at the Vite project root
   (base = e.root, pattern '**/*') and reads the frozen mock-up's
   styles.css today, leaking stray candidates into the bundle — a
   utility candidate and a theme-variable candidate the app never
   renders. A with/without compile of the stylesheet showed the
   difference in the output bytes, so the directive is not cosmetic;
   it keeps the demo out of the build entirely. (This record names no
   leaked token verbatim on purpose: DECISIONS.md is itself inside
   the scan root, and naming one would re-leak it.)
   The directive's path resolves against the
   directory of the file carrying it, not the cwd — verified in the
   installed tailwindcss 4.3.5: the `@source` handler pushes
   `{base: O.context.base, pattern, negated}`
   (node_modules/tailwindcss/dist/lib.js:32, inside `Wn`); an
   imported stylesheet's nodes carry the base its loader returned
   (lib.js:21, `Or`); the loader returns
   `base: dirname(loaded stylesheet)`
   (node_modules/.pnpm/@tailwindcss+node@4.3.5/.../dist/index.js:10,
   `Kt`); the entry stylesheet is compiled with
   `base: dirname(entry css)` (@tailwindcss/vite/dist/index.mjs:1).
   An empirical probe with the installed compile API confirmed a
   directive in a nested stylesheet resolving `../docs/prototype`
   against that stylesheet's own directory — hence `../../` from
   src/assets/.

6. **The two test files were edited for consistency and NOT run**

### D-210 — T-120: the `sync_cancel` command — the slot's token latched through the command (the pinned path), a point-of-no-return KNOWLEDGE latch beside the token, and the three-state answer — 2026-11-25

The card (SYS-003, §9.4 phase 2 step 3, §7.10's Sync row, §10; the
DoD "отмена в preflight не меняет файлы и время синхронизации")
consumes the D-147/T-258 slot. The pinned card comment (T-284's half

1. is consumed verbatim and NOT re-opened: the command takes the
   token through `SyncCancelSlot::token()` and cancels by latching that
   same Arc — "cancel through the slot" IS the existing check, and no
   second path to the token, no second consultation, and no second
   latch exists after this task. Seven readings were open; the chosen
   readings were written here BEFORE the implementation (the rule-1
   discipline).

1) **Module shape — a NEW module `src-tauri/src/sync_cancel.rs`, the
   battery in `ipc_tests.rs`.** The D-204/D-205/D-208 family
   precedent (one command, one module) holds: a new file keeps
   `commands.rs`'s sync region (already D-138/D-147/D-202's home,
   ~7400 lines) from growing, and the command is a SIBLING consumer
   of the slot, not a pipeline resident. The battery, though, lands
   in `ipc_tests.rs`'s sync-run section — NOT in a self-contained
   family file: the tests are lifecycle-shaped (a run parked before
   the check point, a run parked mid-phase-3, the slot, the census,
   the run rows), and every fixture they need (`sync_app`, the
   gated-database park, `published_cancel_token`,
   `count_empty_run_error_codes`, `run_sync_with`) already lives
   there; the family's self-contained file would duplicate the whole
   parked-run machinery. The command, its wire DTO and the
   `logging::sync_cancel_failed` edge are the module's own; the
   slot, the token and the check point stay in `commands.rs` where
   D-138/D-147 left them.
2) **The answer — `Result<SyncCancelOutcome, AppError>`, THREE unit
   members** (serde-tagged `{"outcome": …}`, the `SyncRunOutcome`
   wire shape): `cancelled` / `tooLate` / `nothingToCancel`. D-138's
   answer-shape discipline mirrored: a state answer rides `Ok`,
   never `Err` — a declined cancel is a state, not a system failure,
   so the typed-refusal reading is declined. §10's vocabulary has NO
   member for it (`E_SYNC_RUNNING` names a second run or a project
   edit; `E_VALIDATION`'s elastic clause names field/state refusals
   whose user action is "fix the field" — neither fits a late
   cancel), and inventing `E_CANCEL_TOO_LATE` is an owner-scope
   decision recorded here as declined (prefer the spec's existing
   words). The flat `()` of the scan twin is declined for a
   structural reason the scan never has: §9.4 phase 2 step 3 gives
   the sync a point of no return, so "will stop", "is finishing
   anyway" and "nothing was live" are three different UI facts; the
   scan's cancel is always eventually honored, one fact, `()`.
3) **No live run — `nothingToCancel`, the converging no-op.** The
   `scan_cancel` mirror (its own words: "the window-close race must
   not error in the loser branch"): §10 names no situation, and a
   cancel arriving after the run answered converges the way
   D-194/D-205's same-state re-sends do. A typed refusal would error
   the stale-click race the twin explicitly protects.
4) **The post-point knowledge — a KNOWLEDGE latch in the slot, never
   a second cancellation channel.** `SyncCancelSlot` gains
   `past_point: AtomicBool`, marked by `sync_run_with`
   immediately after the ONE consultation falls through (the check
   read not-cancelled — the run enters §9.4 phase 2's uncancellable
   tail), and reset by `CancelLease`'s `clear_if_current` together
   with the token: one lifecycle, because only the flag holder marks
   (a losing start never reaches a check), and the flag holder's
   lease always clears — the D-147 interleavings keep their
   meanings (a loser's clear no-ops over the winner's latch, and a
   stale flag cannot outlive its run's token). The pipeline NEVER
   reads it and no branch of the pipeline consults it: it is pure
   knowledge for the command's answer. The run row was rejected as
   the source (no phase column exists; adding one is a schema
   change, an owner decision far heavier than a latch), and
   `backup_records`-presence was rejected (not every run writes
   one, and it costs a database read on a command that owns none).
5) **The command's order — latch first, one behavior, then read the
   knowledge.** `token()` → `cancel()` unconditionally when a token
   exists (the pinned T-284 path; the post-point latch is D-147's
   documented harmless no-op — one behavior, three answers), THEN
   read the latch. The certainty split, recorded honestly: `tooLate`
   read after the latch is CERTAIN (the latch set ⟹ the consultation
   completed ⟹ it read the pre-latch state — a latch before the
   consultation would have stopped the run and left the latch
   unset); `cancelled` is ADVISORY — the round-1 review widened the
   windows beyond the nanosecond consultation-in-flight one: a
   pre-check stop (the D-25 gate's `NeedsConfirmation`, an
   availability-checkpoint or phase-1 `Err`) ends the run before the
   consultation and the latch is never honoured (the confirmed
   re-call is a full new run with a new token), and a run boundary
   between the command's slot read and its knowledge read can leave
   the answer describing a run other than the one latched. The DTO's
   doc states all of them: the run's OWN answer — the `aborted`
   summary D-138's law defines — is the authoritative outcome; this
   answer names the state the command acted on. (Closing the windows
   structurally would require serializing the latch with the
   consultation — a restructuring of the landed D-138/D-147
   mechanism this card is explicitly forbidden from making: the
   pinned path is the plain latch. The card's own wording — "до
   окончания фазы 2" — reads the END of phase 2 as the point; the
   effective point is the single consultation D-138 placed before
   the backups, so a cancel arriving DURING the copies already
   answers `tooLate`: the consultation has passed, and no code will
   perform the stop a `cancelled` would name. §9.4's sentence is
   satisfied a fortiori; recorded here so a later reader does not
   re-open the point.)
6) **No SYS-005 gate, no database access at all.** The command IS
   the escape hatch for a running sync — SYS-005's list is the
   project-CHANGING commands, and a cancel mutates nothing. The slot
   is the only state read (managed in every mode, D-147; recovery
   mode answers `nothingToCancel` — the honest shape there, the slot
   is empty by construction). The missing-slot wiring bug answers
   the `scan_slot_missing` honest fallback shape
   (`SyncCancelSlotMissing`, the D-037 fallback — a diagnostic
   naming the state, not a panic, not a silent Ok).
7) **Registration makes it command #44.** `collect_commands!` gains
   one line (`sync_cancel::sync_cancel::<tauri::Wry>`, beside
   `commands::sync_run` — the path-prefix order), `src/bindings.ts`
   regenerates through the export pin (`syncCancel` over the
   `SyncCancelOutcome` DTO), the mock twin `syncCancel` models the
   `nothingToCancel` arm ONLY — the mock `syncRun` stand-in is
   synchronous, so no live-run window exists for a latch to land in
   (the documented stand-in limit, recorded beside the mock's other
   sync limits: the `cancelled`/`tooLate` arms and the
   `E_SYNC_RUNNING` gate are not modelled), `mode.spec` pins the
   44-name surface, `ARCHITECTURE.md`'s module table and
   "forty-four" count sentence follow, `manual-smoke.md`'s
   registered-command list names it, spec §7.10's command-notes
   paragraph gains the `sync_cancel` sentence, and the stale
   future-tense comments that name the command (`commands.rs`'s
   `CancelToken`/`SyncCancelSlot` docs and the two
   `#[allow(dead_code)]` markers on `cancel`/`token`, `ipc_tests.rs`'s
   three, `lib.rs`'s one, `ARCHITECTURE.md`'s "for the future
   `sync_cancel`") are made true. `logging.rs` gains
   `sync_cancel_failed` (the `sync_run_failed` family shape).

### D-211 — T-363: the main-window shell on seed data — the port split, the BaseModal contract, the DEV-only gallery and its build proof, the decorative tokens, and the range deviations — 2026-11-25

Problem: the approved mock-up (docs/prototype/) and the spec (UI-001,
UI-002, UI-012, MAIN-010, MAIN-025, §11.1) describe the main window,
but the app still renders the Tauri/Vite placeholder. The skeleton
task had to port the reference's markup and styles into Vue
components without porting its demo JS, on mock data only (no IPC),
with the seed and the dev gallery excluded from the production build,
and several brief line-ranges that do not line up with the elements
the range demands.

Sources: card T-363 (absorbing T-148); the owner acceptance ruling of
2026-11-25 (no tests written or run; the visual match is checked by
code review, no screenshots); D-207 ruling 3 (the per-feature
catalog); D-209 ruling 3 (decorative values out of theme.css).

1. **Structure.** `src/components/ui/` — BaseModal.vue and
   useDialog.ts (the dialog contract, see ruling 2);
   `src/components/shell/` — AppToolbar.vue, MatrixFrame.vue,
   SyncPanel.vue (the window's three regions; MatrixFrame exposes the
   `#rows` slot the family cards fill — until a parent fills it, the
   frame shows the UI-012 no-instructions empty state, keyed off
   `$slots.rows`); `src/styles/` — one file per ported stylesheet
   section (ruling 5); `src/dev/seed/` — types.ts, projects.ts,
   library.ts, assignments.ts, settings.ts, index.ts (no component
   imports the seed's runtime values — the only runtime importer is
   App.vue, dynamically behind the DEV guard; the shell components
   take props, whose types come from the seed through `import type`,
   erased at build, so the dist gate holds — a recorded dependency
   direction, so a later card does not turn it into a runtime import);
   `src/dev/screens.ts` and
   `src/dev/DevGallery.vue` (the registry and the DEV-only gallery,
   ruling 3). App.vue is the one shell container: it imports no IPC
   module (App.spec.ts pins that with a raw-source scan, the
   i18n.spec.ts pattern), keeps useOsTheme() (UI-021), and adds a
   visually hidden `<h1>` as the window's accessible level-1 name —
   the visible brand stays the toolbar's `div.brand`, the reference
   element unchanged (the smoke test's `toBeVisible` became
   `toBeAttached` for that reason).

2. **The dialog contract and BaseModal.** BaseModal wraps a native
   `<dialog>` carrying the reference's `.modal` markup and classes;
   `defineModel<boolean>('open', { default: false })`; a watcher maps
   model → methods with both guards (showModal() throws on an open
   dialog, close() throws on a closed one), and the same guarded sync
   runs on mount — a parent may mount the dialog already open (the
   gallery does), a sequence a change-only watcher would miss; the
   dialog's `close` event
   writes the model back to false, so Esc and programmatic close both
   stay truthful. Props: `size` (`md` = bare `.modal`, `lg`/`xl` = the
   reference's width modifiers), and the accessible name (NFR-019):
   `labelledBy` (an id of a title inside the slot) or `label` rendered
   as a visually hidden `<h2>`. What the native element gives for free
   and is deliberately NOT reimplemented (focus trapping, full ARIA
   and tests are T-149's): Esc closes; focus moves inside on open and
   returns to the trigger on close; everything outside an open modal
   dialog is inert; `::backdrop`. Future dialogs wrap BaseModal and
   expose `defineModel<boolean>('open')`; useDialog() hands them the
   state ref.

3. **The registry and the DEV-only gallery, with the build proof.**
   `src/dev/screens.ts` holds `screens: Array<{ id, title, component }>`
   (starts with the shell only — `component: null` means the running
   app itself; selecting it clears the hash); family cards append their
   dialogs there. DevGallery.vue reads `#screen=<id>` on mount and on
   `hashchange`, mounts a screen's component with `v-model:open`, and
   clears the hash when the screen closes from inside. App.vue mounts
   it through `import.meta.env.DEV ? defineAsyncComponent(...) : null`
   — the same statically-replaced guard guards the seed import in
   App.vue (`if (!import.meta.env.DEV) return` before a dynamic
   `import('./dev/seed')`) and, added this round, the dev namespace of
   the catalog (ruling 6). The proof, `pnpm run build` then grep
   `dist/`: `dev.gallery.launcherLabel` (a gallery-only key literal),
   `Dev screens` (a dev-catalog value), `Measure before optimizing`
   (a seed instruction text), `ef4444` (a seed-only palette color),
   `Responde siempre` (a seed variant text), and the names
   `dev/seed`, `DevGallery`, `hiddenInstructionCount` — all absent;
   the production bundle is one 140 kB JS chunk. The gallery's own
   styling is a scoped `<style>` block, not Tailwind utilities:
   Tailwind's source detection would otherwise emit the launcher's
   utility classes into the production CSS while the component's JS
   stayed excluded — component styles ride the same dead import
   branch, so nothing of the gallery reaches the CSS either (round-1
   review finding, fixed).

4. **Where the decorative values live, and the token-swap table.**
   src/styles/base.css declares, once, the decorative custom
   properties of the mock-up's palette block (styles.css 24–82) that
   the ported rules draw with: `--border` (#e2e8f0 light / #2b3a58
   dark), `--row-hover` (#f1f5f9 / #22304e) in the theme.css
   three-block pattern (light, `[data-theme='dark']`, the
   `:root:not([data-theme='light'])` media fallback), and the
   theme-independent `--radius`/`--radius-sm` (6px/4px) and
   `--w-check`/`--w-name`/`--w-proj` (40/300/150px) in the light block
   only (reading: the brief's "same three-block pattern" governs the
   values that change with the theme; constants are declared once).
   The reference's own palette block is not ported — colors live only
   in theme.css. The swap applied to every ported rule:
   `--text`→`--ink`, `--text-muted`→`--ink-muted`,
   `--text-faint`→`--ink-muted` (the D-209 contrast ruling: as text it
   failed AA, as a dashed border it stays ≥3:1), `--bg`→`--page`,
   `--border-strong`→`--line`, `--focus`→`--focus-ring`,
   `--surface`/`--surface-2` unchanged, and accent-as-button-background
   → `--accent-strong` with `--on-accent` text (3.77:1 → 5.48:1).
   Reading kept verbatim: `.btn-primary:hover { background:
var(--accent-strong) }` — the mock-up's hover token maps to the
   same name, so the hover is a no-op under the swapped palette; a
   darker hover shade would be a new color (an owner decision, not
   this card's).

5. **CSS sections ported, and those left to T-364…T-367.** Ported:
   Base 83–136 → base.css; Toolbar 137–237 → toolbar.css; Buttons
   238–281 → buttons.css; the matrix frame 282–381 (table, colgroup,
   the pinned header row and first columns — the row-hover rule keeps
   its inert `.c-cell`/`.c-fill` selectors so the section stays
   verbatim) → matrix.css; Sync panel 899–949 → sync-panel.css; Modal
   base 1099–1159 → modal.css; Motion 3126–3136 → motion.css; all
   imported from src/assets/main.css right after theme.css, and the
   placeholder-era `main { min-height: 100vh }` rule removed (it
   would push the sync panel below the fold — the `.app` column owns
   the fill now). Not ported, with ranges: 382–898 (row/cell/column-
   header internals — T-364's rows and headers), 950–1098 (T-364's
   chip/caret/tooltip styles), 1160–3125 (the 23 dialogs, T-364…T-367),
   minus three forced rides-along in ruling 7. Markup ported: the
   toolbar (index.html 67–158), the matrix frame (159–365), the sync
   panel (2509–2548); rows, cells, column-header internals, every
   dialog and the demo's ICONS-driven glyph injection stay with the
   family cards — the Activity/Settings glyphs are inlined in
   AppToolbar as the ICONS markup facts (app.js ~2590), plain template
   SVG.

6. **The per-feature catalog mechanics.** `src/locales/en.json` is
   untouched (the i18n.spec.ts assertions on it stay true); the
   shell's copy lives in `src/locales/en/shell.json` under `shell.*`,
   the gallery's in `src/locales/en/dev.json` under `dev.*`;
   i18n/index.ts merges them into one catalog at load time with
   explicit imports and a plain spread (the namespaces do not overlap)
   and keeps `MessageSchema` = the merged type. The catalog-coverage
   test keeps working unchanged: it scans `.vue` sources for
   `t('…')` literals and resolves them against the MERGED catalog
   instance. The dev namespace's merge sits behind the same
   statically-replaced DEV guard as the gallery (ruling 3), so the dev
   strings stay out of the production bundle. The files are temporary
   (D-207 ruling 3): merged back into one `en.json` when the skeleton
   phase ends.

7. **The three range deviations the brief's lines forced, and every
   reading chosen.** (a) `.toggle-count` (styles.css 1083–1090) and
   `.empty-state` (1093–1097) are visible at rest in the shell but sit
   inside the excluded 950–1098 — both rules are ported verbatim with
   a file-header note; the REST of the range (`.selected-chip` among
   them) stays with T-364…T-367 (the chip renders `hidden` at rest:
   no selection state exists in the skeleton — UI-010 is the matrix
   card's). (b) `.modal-lg`/`.modal-xl` width rules (styles.css
   1167–1169 and 1545–1547) sit inside the excluded 1160–3125 but are
   the BaseModal size props' widths — the two `inline-size` rules are
   ported into modal.css; the per-dialog layout rules around them are
   not. (c) The sync-progress element (index.html 2515–2521) ports
   hidden with an empty text span and no styles (they live at
   styles.css 2297+ with the sync-behavior card); the add-section
   `.hbtn` button is not rendered (its styles are at 576+, its glyph
   JS-injected — header internals, T-364). Readings chosen: the
   project filter options render the seed project names (data) with
   the copy option through i18n; the "Show hidden" count is the
   seed-derived concealed-row count (2 — the static markup's 0 is the
   demo's pre-JS value; app.js counts the same rows); the sync
   counter derives from the seed statuses (4, matching the mock-up's
   hardcoded footer); `lastSuccessfulSync` is an explicit seed fact —
   the stamps are display strings, not comparable dates; assignment
   cells of an `unavailable` project are not marked disabled in the
   seed — the rendering card derives it from `status`; the demo's
   "empty variant assigned" cell is seeded as a plain `main`
   assignment of a text-less instruction; the "1 variant" chips are
   seeded as `Variant 1` entries carrying the main text (the demo
   materializes them lazily, app.js ~2354), so every displayed count
   is data.

7a. **The round-1 review's corrections and remaining readings (same
commit, amended).** (a) The seed's `dirty` cells are the demo's
EIGHT "(changed)" cells, not three: `data-initial` records the
checkbox's initial checked state, so a cell is changed when its
current state differs from it — three assigned→not-assigned cells
(`data-initial="true"` unchecked) and five not-assigned→assigned
cells (`data-initial="false"` checked: Response tone/docktree,
Comment style/task-id-mcp, Unit tests/moli, Coverage targets/moli,
Bundle size budget/EunomiaSync); the first seed carried only the
three. (b) The badge's and the danger button's text swap the
reference's literal #ffffff for the palette's on-accent token:
white on the dark-theme warning is 2.15:1 and on the dark danger
2.77:1 (AA needs 4.5), on-accent is 6.88 and 5.35, and in the
light theme on-accent IS white, so the light look is the
reference's; a dedicated on-warning/on-danger token pair stays a
palette-owner follow-up. (c) The toolbar's right cluster keeps the
mock-up's order (Activity, Settings, Add project, New instruction,
?) although UI-001's enumeration and the §11.1 sketch list Add
project and New instruction first — the brief ports markup from
the reference, the buttons carry no behavior yet, and the owner
picks the order when they are wired. (d) The UI-012 empty state's
markup is composed (message + "New instruction" button, per
UI-012), not ported — the reference's `.empty-state` div is its
empty-SEARCH state with no button; only the CSS rule is the
reference's. (e) MatrixFrame drops the reference's
`role="region"` on the `<main>`: an explicit role would strip the
element of its implicit main landmark; the aria-label alone names
it (the one element-semantic deviation, like the visually hidden
h1). (f) `openScreen` special-cases the shell entry (component
null) to clear the hash — the comment's claim, previously only the
effect.

8. **Consistency edits to the two test files (none run, none skipped
   or deleted — the owner acceptance ruling).** App.spec.ts rewritten
   to the shell truth: the three regions render, the level-1 heading,
   the seed-fed filter (9 options), the hidden count (2), the sync
   facts (stamp + badge 4), the selection cluster hidden at zero, the
   UI-012 empty state while `#rows` is unfilled, and the no-IPC-import
   source scan; the old placeholder assertions (version line, tracked-
   projects plural, logo alts) are gone with the placeholder — T-212
   restores the IPC round-trip assertions when it wires app_info into
   this window. e2e/smoke.spec.ts: "app shell renders" keeps its
   title, heading text and toolbar/syncbar visibility, with
   `toBeVisible` → `toBeAttached` for the now visually hidden h1 (the
   reason in a comment); the app_info test honestly states the
   skeleton truth — the shell renders its seed content (filter count,
   stamp, counter) — and its comment names T-212 as the card that
   restores the version assertion. Both theme tests stay byte-
   identical (the shell's `main` is `.matrix-wrap`, still
   `var(--page)`); i18n.spec.ts needed no edit (it resolves against
   the merged catalog).

### D-212 — T-364: the matrix skeleton on seed data — the container-agnostic row and cell components, all eight §11.2 states, the header internals, the column menu, the variant popover, the tooltip, and the two bulk dialogs — 2026-11-25

Problem: the shell's frame rendered an empty tbody behind an
unfilled slot, the column headers showed bare project names, and
none of the matrix family's components existed. The card had to port
the reference's rows, cells, column-header internals, column menu,
variant popover, text tooltip and bulk dialogs as behavior-free Vue
components on seed data — with every state of §11.2 present,
distinguishable without color, and named for screen readers — without
breaking the seed's DEV-only bundle gate and without pre-empting the
behavior cards (T-169 virtualization, T-184/T-355 interactions,
T-187 tooltip wiring).

Sources: card T-364 (the acceptance ruling of 2026-11-25: no tests
written or run, the visual match is checked by code review without
screenshots); D-206/D-211's porting rules and token swap; spec
§11.2 (lines 797–813), MAIN-001…032, UI-010, UI-023, NFR-019/020.

1. **Structure.** `src/components/matrix/` — MatrixHeadingRow.vue
   (props `heading`, `columnCount`), MatrixInstructionRow.vue
   (`row`, `projects`, `rowAssignments`), MatrixCell.vue (`row`,
   `project`, `assignment`; hosts the VariantPopover),
   ProjectColumnHeader.vue (`project`; renders the whole `th.c-proj`
   and hosts the ColumnMenu), ColumnMenu.vue (`anchor`; emits
   `close`/`select`), VariantPopover.vue (`entries`, `anchor`; emits
   `close`), InstructionTextTooltip.vue (`text`, `open` only),
   BulkAssignDialog.vue (`open` model + `projects`, `variants`),
   BulkConfirmDialog.vue (`open` model + optional `text`), and
   floating.ts (the shared viewport clamp, the outside-click/Escape
   dismissal, the anchor helper — the demo's positioning formulas
   verbatim per component: the menu right-aligns under the trigger
   with gap 4 (app.js 1110–1112), the popover left-aligns with gap
   6 (app.js 1280–1282); both flip above the trigger's top). MatrixFrame.vue no longer has a slot: it takes `rows`
   and `assignments` props and renders the row components in its
   tbody itself (the empty state keys off `rows.length === 0`); the
   `#rows` mechanism is gone. App.vue passes the seed's `library`
   and `assignments` through the same DEV-guarded dynamic import.
   The CONTAINER-AGNOSTIC rule holds for every row and cell
   component: props in, one row/cell/header of content out, scripts
   never touch DOM order (no `nth-child`, `parentElement`,
   `closest('table')`); the menu and the popover position from their
   own element plus an anchor POINT handed in as data (the trigger's
   bottom-right, taken from the click event's `currentTarget`) —
   T-169 can re-host them in a virtualized container. The menu
   closes on outside click and Escape (the demo's target hit-test
   against the trigger class — `.col-menu-btn` / `.cell-icon--eye`
   — keeps the toggle click from closing what it just opened);
   scroll-close and the real actions are T-184/T-355's. The menu
   moves focus to its first item on open (the demo's fact,
   app.js ~1115).

2. **The eight cell states, each derived from the seed** (the
   union of `src/dev/seed/types.ts` + the row): (a) not assigned —
   `state: 'none'`, a bare checkbox, no select; (b) main variant —
   `state: 'main'`, checked + inline select showing "Main"
   (LIB-002's main-variant name; the demo's "Default" loses to the
   spec, §11.2 row 2); (c) alternative — `state: 'variant'`, the
   select shows the variant's name; (d) custom text — `state:
'custom'`, a DISABLED select showing "Custom" and edit/delete
   icons; (e) extend custom — the same plus the dashed "+" chip
   (`.extend-mark`, title names the base variant, MAIN-034); (f)
   empty variant — NOT a union member: derived (main → the
   instruction's `text === null`; variant → the named variant's
   `text === ''`, LIB-014/D-13), rendered as the dashed-border
   select `.variant-select--empty`; (g) changed — `dirty: true` on
   any state: the dimmed `.cell-changed` shade, the title tooltip
   "Assignment changed — will be written on the next sync" (the
   demo's fact, app.js 219), and a VISIBLE "(changed)" suffix
   (`.cell-changed-mark` — spec §11.2 row 7 wins over the demo,
   whose suffix is screen-reader-only); (h) unavailable project —
   `project.status === 'unavailable'` derived in the component (D-211
   ruling 7): cells disabled, no icon cluster, the header carries
   the warning icon, and the cells' accessible-name state becomes
   §11.2 row 8's "Project unavailable" (round-1 review: the label is
   the column's, but the disabled cells announce it). Every cell
   carries the "+" affordance even when
   unassigned (MAIN-007; the demo's `cell-unchecked` hiding loses to
   spec §11.2 line 810). Each cell's accessible name is
   "instruction — project: state", "(changed)" included (NFR-019),
   through `matrix.cell.name` + the `matrix.cell.state*` keys; the
   empty-variant label is wired into the state derivation for both
   the main and the variant arm (round-1 review: the seeded
   Pre-commit checks cell must announce "Assigned, empty variant"). The
   assigned select always exists when the checkbox is checked —
   including rows the demo left select-less (its chip-driven
   `variantOptionsFor` suppression, app.js 226–231): §11.2's
   main-variant state names the select, and the empty-variant state
   cannot exist without one; the demo's static at-rest look for
   those seven rows deviates accordingly (a spec-wins reading, like
   D-211's).

3. **The seed extension and the added demo cells.** The Assignment
   union gained the brief's custom arm exactly: `{ state: 'custom';
mode: 'replace' | 'extend'; base?: string; dirty: boolean }` —
   `base` names the extend cell's fixed base variant (MAIN-034).
   The demo's STATIC data has no custom cells at all (its JS builds
   them in flows only), so two demo cells were added to
   assignments.ts and are recorded here per the brief: (i) Response
   tone — quotameter, `{ state: 'custom', mode: 'replace' }`; (ii)
   Naming conventions — moli, `{ state: 'custom', mode: 'extend',
base: 'Strict' }` (the variant the demo assigns to task-id-mcp in
   the same row). The empty-variant state rides the demo's own
   "empty variant assigned" cell (Pre-commit checks — EunomiaSync,
   seeded as a plain `main` of the text-less instruction in D-211
   ruling 7). No `matrix.ts` was needed: nothing was missing from
   the seed — the popover's full texts ride `library.ts` through
   props (the real app will fetch them per variant id through
   `variant_get`, MAIN-032; the demo's "Default" option name becomes
   "Main (main variant)" per LIB-002). `src/dev/seed/matrix.ts` is
   therefore not created.

4. **The header internals and UI-023.** ProjectColumnHeader renders
   the reference's `th.c-proj`: `.proj-line` (the color chip via a
   `:style` custom-property binding, the 1–6 char label, the full
   name in the `title` and an sr-only span — MAIN-028) and the
   status sub-line `.proj-sub` per `ProjectStatus`: ok → the short
   last-sync stamp (derived from the seed's long display stamp by a
   local regex — the demo's format fact; the real-data card replaces
   it with Intl per UI-020), dirty → dot + "unsynced changes",
   external/deleted → the warning triangle + text, unavailable →
   the circle-slash + text (icons inlined as the reference's SVG
   markup facts). The edit/preview/"⋮" icons the demo injects with
   JS (app.js 5079–5121) are inlined the same way, with the demo's
   classes and labels. The "⋮" hugs the right edge
   (`.proj-line .col-menu-btn`), and the header divider rule
   (`.c-proj + .c-proj`) had already landed with T-363's frame
   section (matrix.css 97–101). The Instruction column header gained
   the add-section `.hbtn.hbtn--add` button (the `#instruction-header`
   id and the styles.css 618–621 rule are the reference's; D-211
   ruling 7c had left it "header internals, T-364").

5. **CSS sections ported** (one file each, imported from
   src/assets/main.css after the shell's): Project column headers
   382–457 → matrix-columns.css; Tree rows 458–622 → matrix-rows.css
   (`.hide-btn` rides along unused — its behavior is MAIN-012's
   card); Bulk assignment operations 623–679 → matrix-bulk.css;
   Variant contents popover 680–745 → matrix-popover.css; Matrix
   cells 746–898 → matrix-cells.css; Interactive states 950–1098 →
   matrix-states.css (minus `.toggle-count`/`.empty-state`, already
   ported early by T-363 — noted in the file header). Three
   reference ID selectors became classes for instance-reusable
   components, declarations unchanged: `#column-menu` →
   `.column-menu`, `#variants-popover` → `.variants-popover`,
   `#text-tooltip` → `.text-tooltip`. The section's three
   decorative tints (`--row-drop` 874–882, `--row-selected`/
   `--cell-changed` 963–973) moved to base.css's three-block
   pattern beside `--border`/`--row-hover`. Two forced ride-alongs
   outside the brief's ranges: `.extend-mark` (styles.css 1250–1265,
   the excluded dialog zone) — the §11.2 extend chip; and two NEW
   rules, `.variant-select--empty` and `.cell-changed-mark`,
   following the reference's dashed-outline and muted-text idioms
   for the two §11.2 states the demo's stylesheet never drew. The
   checked checkbox takes the accent-as-control-background swap
   (`--accent-strong`, D-211 ruling 4); its check mark is painted
   in the theme's `--on-accent` value — a data URI cannot read a
   var(), so the two theme values ride the three-block pattern
   (light `#ffffff`, dark `#052e22`) instead of the demo's
   hardcoded white, which would have failed AA in the dark theme.

6. **The dialogs and the showcases.** BulkAssignDialog and
   BulkConfirmDialog wrap BaseModal per the T-363 contract
   (`defineModel<boolean>('open')`); their data is props only —
   `projects`, `variants` (`readonly BulkVariantChoice[]`, rendered
   only for the one-selected-row case), and the confirm line `text`
   (absent → the mock-up's "Placeholder." stands in, its static
   fact; its JS fills the count at runtime). The demo's `#bulk-form`
   id and the JS-filled containers are dropped; title ids come from
   Vue's `useId()`. The gallery-side entries show the chrome with
   the defaults (empty project list); the real parent passes the
   seed (the selection card, T-184's family). The `.ps-field`/
   `.ps-check-row` classes stay in the markup with their styles
   left to the project-settings card's section (styles.css 1160+).
   src/dev/showcases/ holds five DEV-only wrapper screens —
   MatrixCellStates (one cell per §11.2 state off real seed rows,
   fabricated assignments), ColumnHeaderStates (the five statuses
   off the seed projects), ColumnMenuShowcase and
   VariantPopoverShowcase (open next to a trigger), TooltipShowcase
   (visible) — all registered in screens.ts together with the two
   dialogs. The registry's seed-free rule is rewritten as its real
   boundary: screens.ts is reachable ONLY through DevGallery.vue,
   which rides the statically-replaced DEV guard, so the registry,
   the showcases and the seed all stay out of the production bundle;
   the build's dist/ grep proves it (checked: the registry titles,
   a showcase hint, the seed texts, the palette hex — all absent;
   the production `matrix` catalog present).

7. **Readings chosen where the brief was open.** (a) The assigned
   cell always carries the inline select (ruling 2's spec-wins
   argument). (b) The main variant's display name is "Main"
   (LIB-002), not the demo's "Default", in the select and the
   popover. (c) The caret button renders with the reference's static
   `aria-expanded="true"` and no handler (collapse is UI-004's
   card); the hide/restore eye button is NOT rendered (the demo
   injects it with JS; MAIN-012's card owns it) — the hidden rows
   render with the reference's static `.row-hidden` + dashed chip.
   (d) The demo's one pre-checked row-sel checkbox ("Secrets
   handling", its staged screenshot state) is not carried: the seed
   has no selection concept, so every row-sel renders unchecked and
   the toolbar cluster stays hidden at zero. (e) The short sync
   stamp is derived from the long seed stamp by a local regex
   (ruling 4); the header tooltip composes per status through
   `matrix.header.title*` (the dirty column keeps the plain
   titleOk line, per the demo). (f) The popover entry derivation
   reads `text === ''` (alternatives) and `text === null` (the main
   of a text-less instruction) as empty, without ALG-002's
   whitespace normalization — the seed holds no whitespace-only
   texts; the build-side composition keeps the rule. (g) The demo's
   pre-JS `variant-btn` cells (alternative assigned) render as the
   spec's checkbox + select, since the select always exists (ruling
   2). (h) `option` values are the markers `main`/`custom` and the
   variant names — no `v-model` exists to read them; the static
   `:selected` bindings carry the state. (i) The card text's "Move
   left / Move right" menu items lose to the reference and the spec:
   the frozen menu (index.html 2811–2828) and §7.4/MAIN-033 name
   "Preview file…" / "Assign all visible" / "Clear column", and those
   three are what the component ports; a move command for columns is
   not in the spec's column menu.

8. **Consistency edits (none run, none skipped or deleted — the
   owner acceptance ruling).** App.spec.ts: one test became untrue
   — "shows the UI-012 no-instructions empty state while the rows
   slot is unfilled" — because the frame now renders the seed's 33
   rows; rewritten minimally to assert the rows render and the
   empty state does not exist. The other tests stay true unchanged.
   One pre-existing T-363 defect is fixed in passing: the toolbar's
   bulk button was visible at rest despite `hidden` — `.btn`'s
   `display: inline-flex` defeats the attribute — and the
   reference's `#bulk-assign-btn[hidden]` rule (matrix-bulk.css)
   plus the reference's own id on the button (index.html 107) is
   the same fix the demo ships; the button's `hidden` attribute
   binding is unchanged.

### D-213 — T-365: the library skeleton on seed data — the two-pane instruction editor, the history panel, the confirmation dialogs — 2026-11-26

Problem: the library family had no screens — the editor, the history
panel and the six confirmation/restore dialogs of UI-003/UI-010 did
not exist, and the structure cards behind them (T-185's create flow,
T-189…T-195's behavior family) need the markup to refine. The card
had to port the reference's `#edit-dialog`, `#history-dialog` and the
small confirmations as behavior-free Vue components on seed data,
with the LIB-036/LIB-024 gates and the D-207 hint exception rendered
from data, without breaking the seed's DEV-only bundle gate.

Sources: card T-365 (the acceptance ruling of 2026-11-25: no tests
written or run, the visual match is checked by code review without
screenshots); D-206/D-211's porting rules and token swap; the D-212
precedents (shared form idioms, the registry's seed-free rule, the
dist/ proof); spec UI-003, UI-010, LIB-002, LIB-009…016, LIB-017…022,
LIB-023/024/025, LIB-026/027, LIB-036, MAIN-007/LIB-018, MAIN-034,
NFR-019; T-186 absorbed (its criterion — a component test of the
editor's structure — is superseded by the owner's no-tests ruling).

1. **Structure.** `src/components/library/` —
   InstructionEditorDialog.vue (the two-pane UI-003 window, size-xl
   BaseModal; props `instruction: LibraryInstruction`, `mode:
'instruction' | 'custom'`, and the custom mode's `projectName`,
   `customText`, `customBaseLabel`; plus `previewBlocks`), with its
   panes as components: EditorVariantList.vue (`variants`,
   `selected`; emits `select`), EditorFields.vue (`instructionName`,
   `variantName`), EditorTextTabs.vue (`text`, `placeholder`,
   `previewBlocks`; the ARIA tablist and both panels); HistoryDialog.vue
   (`instructionName`, `revisions`, size lg), RestoreVariantDialog.vue
   (`variantName`), UnsavedChangesDialog.vue, HideInstructionDialog.vue,
   HeadingDialog.vue (`mode: 'add' | 'rename'` — the title follows it
   like the demo's openHeadingDialog, app.js ~840–845 — and
   `initialName`, the rename prefill),
   HeadingDeleteDialog.vue, VariantDeleteDialog.vue (`variantName`,
   `affectedProjects`). Every dialog is on the T-363 contract:
   BaseModal + `defineModel<boolean>('open')`; title ids from
   `useId()`; the reference's method="dialog" forms make Save/Cancel/
   Close/Delete/Restore/Hide/Discard the dialogs' own return values.
   No component imports the seed's DATA or `src/ipc/**` — types ride
   `import type` from `../../dev/seed` (the D-212 precedent), data
   only through props.

2. **Data-derived states and their sources.** (a) The main variant
   always heads the list: the dialog derives the rows — the implicit
   main first (the seed's `text: null` main), then
   `instruction.variants` in order. (b) LIB-014: a row whose body is
   empty (main `text === null`, alternative `text === ''`) gets the
   matrix's dashed `.empty-mark` and the dimmed `.ie-variant-empty`
   label. (c) LIB-036's UI gate: the "Make main" star is disabled
   when the row is already main or its name is blank or its body is
   empty, with the reason as title/aria-label; the seed's
   "Pre-commit checks" shows the disabled star (its reason is the
   already-main wording — the no-name/no-body reason has no seed
   state, every alternative in the seed library carries a name and a
   body; the same row drives the D-207 hint-less Delete). (d) LIB-024: the
   main variant's Delete is disabled with the hint "Make another
   variant main first — the main variant cannot be deleted"; D-207:
   when the instruction has only the main variant the hint is NOT
   rendered at all — the button keeps its action name as the
   accessible name (an icon-only control must be named), but no
   reason text, and the demo's LIB-025 "last variant" tooltip is
   never ported (the spec: LIB-025 never fires through the UI). The
   seed's single-variant rows drive it. (e) LIB-023: the
   variant-deletion confirmation names the NUMBER of affected
   projects — the spec wins over the demo's static line (the demo's
   requestDeleteVariant text carries no count, app.js ~1889); the
   count arrives as a prop, pluralized 0/1/other. (f) The history
   panel renders op chips keyed by the revision's op, the Restore
   variant button on delete rows (inert), the "Restored" chip on a
   `restored` row (the seed starts with none), and the snapshot body
   per D-16 (instruction: name + state; variant: name + text); the
   empty state shows through the mock-up's own hidden toggling.

3. **Local UI state only** (no side effects, no IPC): the selected
   variant row (switching swaps the fields'/textarea's `:value`
   rendering), the active Edit/Preview tab (click switching; the
   arrow-key/Home/End roving focus is a feature card's), and the
   MAIN-034 replace/extend radio (it moves the placeholder between
   the three mode wordings and toggles the "Appended after" hint —
   the draft-resetting of MAIN-034 is behavior). Everything else is
   NOT done: no validation, no save, no unsaved-changes tracking, no
   restore, no Markdown rendering. The owners: T-185 (the create
   flow, the Section picker, the heading add/rename/delete flows),
   T-189's family (validation, saving, the unsaved-changes guard and
   the change tracking behind it), T-190…T-195 (the variant
   actions — add/Make main/Delete —, the restore flow, the hide
   flow, and the custom-editor semantics of MAIN-034/MAIN-007).

4. **The seed extension.** types.ts gained `HistoryOp`,
   `HistorySnapshot` (the `kind` discriminant), `HistoryRevision`
   (`restored: boolean` required — the demo's runtime feedback flag
   seeded explicitly false everywhere) and `PreviewBlock` (a typed
   union: heading/paragraph/code/list). history.ts stores the demo
   builder's OUTPUT as data — JS is never ported, so
   `buildDemoRevisions` (app.js 2404–2468) is not carried; its
   result for "Commit messages" is: 12 revisions, newest first, with
   `when` stamps precomputed by the demo's histStamp formula
   (HIST_NOW_MS 19 Nov 2026, 14:32 UTC+3; "D Mon YYYY, HH:MM
   (UTC+3)"), including the deleted "Old wording" pair (the delete
   row carries the panel's restore button) and the
   "Conventional Commits" hide/restore pair. preview.ts holds the
   static Preview sample (five typed blocks over the same
   instruction's copy). Both export through seed/index.ts. The
   custom-mode text rides a PROP: the seed's Assignment union has no
   text field (T-364's shape, untouched), and the showcase passes the
   demo's add-flow draft — the base variant's text (app.js
   2680–2692; the edit flow's stored custom text is 2651–2660).

5. **CSS sections ported** (theme-token swap applied; one file each,
   imported from src/assets/main.css after the matrix family's):
   Instruction editor modal 1160–1493 → library-editor.css; History
   modal 1916–2093 → library-history.css (the `--text-faint` and
   `--text-muted` maps to `--ink-muted`, `--focus` to
   `--focus-ring`, `--border-strong` to `--line`; `--accent` as a
   border/badge color stays `--accent`). Not re-ported: the
   `.modal-xl` width (1167–1169) and the `.modal-lg` width
   (1545–1547) — already in src/styles/modal.css (T-363's header
   note says so); `.extend-mark` (1250–1265) — T-364's
   matrix-cells.css. Three editor rules physically sit past the
   File-preview header (1513–1540: `.ie-warnings`,
   `.ie-warnings-list`, the 760px media query) and are ported with
   the editor — they style `#edit-dialog`'s markup. The shared
   markdown selector groups (`:is(.ie-preview, .fp-body) …`) are
   ported verbatim as the in-range rulesets they are; their
   `.fp-body` halves are inert until T-366's file-preview modal
   mounts that class (its own section 1494–1542 stays T-366's). The
   small confirmation dialogs have NO section and NO rules of their
   own: grep by their markup's class names found every class already
   ported (modal.css, buttons.css, toolbar.css); library-dialogs.css
   exists as the documented slot (no rules) — the heading dialog's
   `.ps-field/.ps-input/.ps-error/.ps-hint` and the editor's
   `.ps-tabs/.ps-tab` stay in the markup with their rules left to the
   project-settings section (1543–1915, T-366), per the D-212
   precedent. The history body's scrolling (`flex: 1 1 auto;
overflow-y: auto`) engages once T-366 lands the fixed-height
   `.modal-lg form` rule (~1546); the seed's twelve rows render fine
   without it.

6. **The create-mode decision.** The Section select IS part of the
   reference's `#edit-dialog` form (index.html 2610–2615), so its
   markup is ported — inert: an empty `.ps-select`, the label through
   i18n, `.ie-section-field` staying `display:none` outside
   `.ie-create` (the mock-up's own rule); no picker logic (T-185's).
   No `.ie-create` class is ever applied by this component.

7. **Readings chosen where the brief was open.** (a) The editor-mode
   showcase is split into THREE registry screens — the library edit
   ("Commit messages": main badge + two alternatives + the LIB-024
   hint), the empty single variant ("Pre-commit checks": LIB-014 +
   LIB-036 + the D-207 hint-less Delete), and the custom mode
   ("Response tone" — quotameter, base label "Response tone — Main")
   — so every data-derived state is visible from the gallery.
   (b) The main variant's list name and badge render one i18n key,
   `library.editor.mainVariantName` = "Main" (LIB-002's naming, the
   D-212 "spec wins over the demo's Default" line). (c) The custom
   mode's title composes "Custom instruction — {instruction} —
   {project}" through the two props (the demo's title fact, app.js
   2651). (d) The D-207 suppression removes only the REASON: the
   Delete button's accessible name stays the action name, because an
   icon-only control must be named (NFR-019); the hint-as-tooltip
   disappears with the title. (e) The variant rows' key is the row
   name (names are unique within an instruction, §6.9). (f) The
   radio group keeps the reference's static `name="ie-custom-mode"`
   (one editor instance renders at a time). (g) The registry lists
   the three prop-less dialogs (unsaved, hide, heading-delete)
   directly, like T-364's bulk dialogs; the prop-ful ones ride small

### D-214 — CI 45782298320: T-110's DB-015 echo oracle was platform-blind — the macOS temp root pushed the picked path over D-115's cap; the fixture is deliberately over-cap on every platform now and the expectation is computed from the documented arithmetic — 2026-11-26

Problem: CI run 45782298320 (push of `3b800ca`, T-120's landing) was
red on BOTH macOS legs — macos-15 and macos-15-intel — and only
there (windows-latest, ubuntu-24.04, the deny job, both builds and
e2e green; the known watcher flake did not fire this run),
deterministically on one test:
`project_relink_tests::a_path_key_collision_with_an_active_project_is_refused`
panicked at project_relink_tests.rs:655 —
`assert_eq!(error["params"]["value"], json!(picked))` with left
`"/private/var/folders/9d/l02zfgrs7c16twd3wbpdmhkc0000gn/T/.tmpTpx
(+12 more code points)"`, right the verbatim 76-code-point picked
path (848 passed, 1 failed — the same single failure on both legs).

The verified diagnosis (every claim re-checked against the code
before this entry, Rule 2):

1. **The production code is correct.** `bounded_echo`
   (src-tauri/src/commands.rs:5762-5771) caps the echo at 64 code
   points and names the rest — D-115's ruling. The DB-015 refusal
   (src-tauri/src/project_relink.rs:234-242) echoes
   `bounded_echo(&path)` — the caller's raw path — exactly as D-208
   point 5 pins the contract ("the caller's path echoed bounded",
   DECISIONS.md:25373-25392, both arms sharing the one call site).
   The macOS CI observed the SPECIFIED behavior; nothing in
   production changes.
2. **The test's oracle was platform-dependent.** It asserted the
   echo equals the verbatim fixture path under the recorded
   assumption "short here, verbatim" — true on Linux
   (`/tmp/.tmpXXXXXX/new-repo` ≈ 25 code points, under the cap),
   false on macOS: the system temp root alone
   (`/private/var/folders/9d/…/T/` = 56 code points) plus
   tempfile's `.tmpTpxyPs` (11) plus `/new-repo` (9) = 76 code
   points — 12 over the cap, hence "(+12 more code points)". The
   T-110 executor ran the suite on Linux only: D-181's class
   (macOS-only breakage invisible on the dev machine), with a
   deterministic arithmetic cause this time rather than a race.

The sibling sweep (the whole suite grepped for `params"]["value"]`
and `params"]["path"]` oracles — 26 + 9 sites, every one read):
**no other test compares a `bounded_echo`-shaped value against a
verbatim path built under a system temp root.**

- `bounded_echo` is the ONLY bounded seam a PATH rides in
  production (project_relink.rs:236); every other call site
  (commands.rs:5778/5844/5849/5888/5892/6007, project_archive.rs:111,
  project_restore.rs:142, project_update.rs:241/247/275/320/423/440/457,
  project_relink.rs:209) receives ids, names, labels or literals.
- The tests over those seams ARE the healthy precedent:
  deliberately-sized strings with independently computed
  expectations (project_update_tests.rs:556/1222/2000,
  project_restore_tests.rs:908, project_relink_tests.rs:1035 (in
  `project_relink_refuses_an_unknown_id_with_the_typed_envelope`) —
  the
  T-106/T-109 `"x"`×70 → `"x"`×64 + "(+6 more code points)" pins;
  the TS mock twin's spec pins at
  src/ipc/mock/commands.spec.ts:732/902/1001/1232/1454/1601) or
  short closed-vocabulary literals ("ABCDEFG", "purple", "middle",
  "BETA", `\u{7}REPO`, "no-such-row").
- Every other path-echo oracle compares a VERBATIM seam against
  the same verbatim string on both sides (no cap involved, so no
  platform's temp-root length can flip it): the scan commit's
  `rejected_unreported_path` (scan.rs:1400-1406) and
  `field_rejection_of` (scan.rs:1411-1421), the D-086
  `rejected_non_utf8_path` (commands.rs:3844-3851),
  `repo_lookup_failed`'s `params.path` (commands.rs:3869-3887,
  SEC-008's "paths may ride params"), and the DB-init/recovery
  wires (recovery_tests.rs, db_tests.rs).
- The mock spec's DB-015 batteries (commands.spec.ts:1058/1082)
  assert no `value` at all — code/field/reason/offer id only; the
  TS fixtures are synthetic in-memory paths, no OS temp root.
- Empirical cross-check: both macOS legs failed exactly ONE test
  each (848/1), deterministic — no second sibling fired anywhere
  in the matrix.

Solution (the service commit, referencing T-110): the oracle is now
platform-independent BY CONSTRUCTION, the healthy precedent's
shape, in `project_relink_tests.rs`:

1. **The fixture's name is deliberately 64 code points long**
   (`"new-repo-with-a-name-that-puts-the-picked-path-over-the-echo-cap"`),
   so every ABSOLUTE picked path is over D-115's cap by construction:
   the name alone IS the cap, and any temp root contributes at least
   the separator before the name. The prefixes including that
   separator: Linux `/tmp/.tmpXXXXXX/` = 16 (80 total, 16 over —
   measured locally, "(+16 more code points)"); the macOS runner's
   canonical `/private/var/folders/…/T/.tmpXXXXXX/` = 68 (132
   total); Windows `%TEMP%\.tmpXXXXXX\` ≈ 50 (≈ 114 total). The
   echo always takes the bounded arm, and a `total > ECHO_CAP`
   precondition assert fails LOUDLY on any unforeseen platform
   instead of silently passing the verbatim arm.
2. **The expectation is computed from the documented arithmetic
   ALONE** — D-115's 64-code-point cap and the "(+N more code
   points)" suffix, applied with the test's own
   `chars().take(64)` / `count() - 64` — never a call to
   `bounded_echo` (a circular oracle would mirror the
   implementation instead of testing it). A cap change, a suffix
   change, or an unbounded regression reddens the assertion.
3. **Mutations verified (Rule 4), each reverted byte-for-byte.**
   M1: reverting the oracle to verbatim (`json!(picked)`) — the
   original bug's shape — fails locally on LINUX with left
   `/tmp/.tmpXXXX/new-repo-… (+16 more code points)` vs right the
   verbatim path: the original blindness (green on Linux whatever
   the oracle) is removed, the failure now reproduces on the dev
   machine. M2: removing the cap in `bounded_echo` (verbatim echo)
   fails the FIXED test — the oracle pins the BOUNDING itself, not
   the input's shape.

Checks (the full chain, real exit codes, `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2`):
`cargo fmt --check` 0; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --
-D warnings` 0; `cargo nextest run --workspace --test-threads=4`
1953/1953; `cargo test --doc --workspace` 86+12, 0 failed (D-195);
`pnpm test` 395/395; `pnpm run format:check` 0; `pnpm run lint` 0;
`pnpm run typecheck` 0. Honest boundary: the local machine is
Linux-only — the macOS proof rides CI (the next push's run), which
the construction no longer depends on: the test pins the bounded
arm everywhere rather than wherever the temp root happens to be
long. No follow-up cards: the production shape was never wrong, and
the sibling sweep found nothing to card.

**Round-1 review addendum (same task, 2026-11-26; model
